members.text: In the reify repo, `cargo fmt --check` is NOT part of the verify gate — neither `scripts/verify.sh` nor `hooks/pre-commit` invokes rustfmt, and the tree carries ~165 pre-existing `cargo fmt --check` diffs under the pinned 1.96.0 toolchain (no rustfmt.toml exists, so default `use_small_heuristics` chain-width 60 disagrees with the hand-written style in many files). Do not "fix" fmt diffs you did not introduce, and do not treat a fmt diff as a gate failure; match surrounding file style and rely on `cargo clippy --all-targets` instead.

Reify's Rust crates carry pervasive PRE-EXISTING rustfmt drift: cargo fmt -p reify-core --check and -p reify-ir --check both report diffs in many untouched files (diagnostics.rs, dimension.rs, kernel.rs, ty.rs, value.rs imports/enums) on the pinned 1.96.0 toolchain, and no script in scripts/ invokes cargo fmt, so the verify pipeline does not gate on it. Never run cargo fmt --all to satisfy a "fmt clean" plan step — it produces a huge unrelated diff. Check only your own regions instead: cargo fmt -p CRATE -- --check 2>&1 | grep 'FILE:YOUR-LINE-RANGE', then hand-apply just those hunks.

The reify repo is NOT rustfmt-normalized and `scripts/verify.sh` does not gate on `cargo fmt --check` (grep for "cargo fmt"/"rustfmt" in verify.sh returns nothing). Measured on 2026-07-27 at base commit aa858e10a9: `cargo fmt -p reify-compiler --check` reports ~150 diffs across expr.rs, geometry.rs, scope.rs, type_compat.rs, annotations/* and several tests/ files, with no rustfmt.toml in the tree (default config, rustfmt 1.9.0 from the pinned 1.96.0 toolchain). So a red `cargo fmt --check` is a PRE-EXISTING repo-wide condition, not a regression you introduced. Do not "fix formatting" to make it green — that reformats files far outside your task scope and blows up the diff. To check whether a violation is actually yours, confirm the flagged construct is absent from `git diff <base>..HEAD` (line numbers shift when you add lines above pre-existing violations, which makes old violations look new).

Reify has NO rustfmt gate: no rustfmt.toml exists, `git grep 'cargo fmt'` returns nothing tracked, and scripts/verify.sh's lint pass is only `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (fmt-agnostic) — i.e. the lint action is clippy-only and never runs `cargo fmt --check`/rustfmt. The codebase is intentionally NOT rustfmt-clean under the pinned toolchain (rustc 1.96.0 / rustfmt 1.9.0-stable, edition 2024 per workspace Cargo.toml) — pre-existing diffs are widespread across nearly every crate: reify-stdlib (~946 diffs), reify-audit (~728KB), reify-eval (149 files/~37k lines, incl. engine_eval.rs ~25 sites, engine_build.rs, elastic_static.rs, deps.rs, dynamics_ops.rs, engine_admin.rs), reify-lsp, reify-solver-elastic (incl. loop_closure_value.rs, loop_closure_solver.rs), reify-kernel-occt (lib.rs, ffi.rs, handle.rs, build.rs — ~150 diffs), reify-ir + reify-kernel-manifold (geometry.rs, constraint.rs, kernel.rs), reify-kernel-gmsh (build.rs, kernel.rs, kernel_real.rs, lib.rs, mesh_boundary.rs), and gui/src-tauri (commands.rs, debug.rs, debug_server.rs, types.rs, main.rs, tests/rpath_smoke.rs, watcher.rs/watcher_tests.rs). This is a hand-maintained house style that deliberately diverges from rustfmt defaults, not an oversight. Because rustfmt is not part of the enforced gate, pre-existing rustfmt-disagreement in tracked files (e.g. multi-line macro-arg wrapping style) never fails the lint gate on its own — amendment/review passes should not "fix" such drift unless it was explicitly flagged in the task, since touching it is unrelated scope creep.

Rule: do NOT run `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt -p <crate>`, `cargo fmt --all`, or any crate-wide/whole-file fmt for a targeted fix — it reformats the ENTIRE crate/file (observed up to 149 files/~37k lines) even when only one function needed a change, producing massive unrelated churn on every affected task.

Verifying your OWN edits introduce no NEW drift:
- The correct edition is 2024 (NOT 2021) — passing the wrong `--edition` flag flips rustfmt's style-edition defaults (import ordering etc.) and produces spurious diffs unrelated to your change.
- Preferred: `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` (auto-reads edition from Cargo.toml). Flag ORDER matters: `cargo fmt --check -p <crate>` (flag before `-p`) has been observed to non-deterministically error "Unrecognized option: 'p'" or behave inconsistently (likely lock contention from concurrent cargo processes across worktrees) — put `-p <crate> --` before `--check`.
- Alternative: `command rustfmt --check --edition 2024 <single-file>` per file. Note `cargo fmt -- --check <file1> <file2>` does NOT actually scope to just those files in this workspace — it still reports drift across the whole crate.
- CAUTION: bare `rustfmt --check <path-under-repo>` (not /tmp) can be intercepted by a shell wrapper/shim that prints a canned "LINT OK | rustfmt | 0 issues" regardless of actual state — untrustworthy. Also, the locally-installed rustfmt version can differ from whatever formatted the repo, producing whole-workspace false-positive diffs (confirmed by diffing a pristine base-commit file copy) — this is a local-toolchain artifact, not a real regression.
- To isolate a genuine semantic change from incidental reflow noise in the same diff (e.g. an accidental broad `cargo fmt` got mixed into WIP): normalize BOTH old and new file versions through `rustfmt --edition 2024` and diff the normalized versions (collapses formatting-only hunks to nothing), then splice that delta by line-range onto the real unformatted original file rather than committing the fully-reformatted file.
- Real gate: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (or `--tests`) scoped to the touched crate. Rely on `cargo test` + this clippy invocation for verification, not fmt-check.
- Confirm no NEW drift from your edit: diff `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check | grep "^Diff in"` site counts before/after your change, or check your changed line ranges are disjoint from reported dr [cut]

The reify workspace is NOT rustfmt-clean on main: `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` reports dozens of pre-existing diffs (e.g. reify-constraints has ~90 across solver.rs, registry.rs, relate_solve.rs, and most tests/). It is therefore not a verify gate, and running `cargo fmt -p <crate>` would reformat large amounts of unrelated code. To format only your own new/edited files, invoke rustfmt directly: `rustfmt --edition 2024 <paths...>`. The real style gate is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (scripts/verify.sh:2010-2012), which makes rustc lints like dead_code hard errors — so an unused pub(crate) helper or struct field added ahead of the step that consumes it needs a targeted `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment, not a bare declaration.

members.text: reify-gui debug-MCP transport has TWO distinct dispatch systems: (1) mcp_context.rs::mcp_tool_call_impl handles engine-locked `reify_*` tools (tested in tests/mcp_dispatch_tests.rs); (2) debug_server.rs::dispatch_tool handles the `:3939/mcp` debug tools — its default arm delegates frontend-mediated tools to DebugBridge::query_frontend (debug.rs), which emits a `debug-request` Tauri event, awaits a oneshot keyed by id, and is completed by DebugBridge::resolve(id, json) when bridge.ts (gui/src/debug/bridge.ts buildHandlers/initDebugBridge) invokes `debug_response`. To unit-test the query_frontend↔resolve round-trip you need tauri::test::mock_app() (MockRuntime), which requires DebugBridge to be generic over R:Runtime (it currently pins AppHandle<Wry>) and the tauri `test` feature enabled.

Scripting reify-gui retests over the debug MCP (verified 2026-07-22): (1) The reify-debug HTTP MCP (port from the worktree's .mcp.json, e.g. 127.0.0.1:59469/mcp) answers tools/call via plain curl WITHOUT an initialize handshake or Mcp-Session-Id header — stateless POSTs work fine for health/open_file/engine_state/wait_for_idle/demand_dispatch. (2) wait_for_idle ≠ settled: it can return idle_after_ms≈28 for a file whose async tessellation/geometry-query passes are still running — bottom_deck_split.ri returned idle then SIGSEGV'd the process ~6s later. After wait_for_idle, confirm via engine_state values + process aliveness before concluding anything. (3) engine_state's `values` field is a LIST of {id,value} dicts, not a dict — a .get('mass') extraction silently reads None and fakes a "mass missing" result (this produced one false alarm in-session). (4) Native-crash capture recipe: relaunch the GUI under `gdb -batch -ex "set pagination off" -ex "handle SIG33 SIG34 SIGPWR SIGXCPU nostop noprint pass" -ex run -ex "thread apply all bt 12" --args target/debug/reify-gui <file.ri>` with REIFY_DEBUG=1/REIFY_DEBUG_PORT set, then trigger via MCP open_file — MCP stays reachable under gdb (~5s startup lag). Stack-overflow signature to recognize: SIGSEGV at a function's ENTRY line with reference args reading 0x0 in a deep recursion on "tokio-rt-worker" (2MB stack) — that's the guard-page stack probe, not a null deref; CLI evading it only proves the main thread's 8MB stack, not correctness. (5) A detached setsid launch has no shell to print "Segmentation fault", so a signal death leaves the captured stderr log EMPTY — silence + missing process = native signal; use a wrapper that echoes $? (139=SEGV, 134=ABRT, 137=OOM-kill) to a log for the exact signal.

members.text: Procedure (2026-05-27): committing a batch of PRD markdown files to main while the orchestrator is stopped — use an EXPLICIT pathspec (`git add docs/prds/v0_6/<each file>`, never `git add .` on main which scoops orphan dirs) and `git commit --no-verify` (the main pre-commit hook runs the full workspace verify, slow and can fail on unrelated red; doc-only changes can't break the build so --no-verify is the vetted-safe path when contained). PRDs MUST be committed to main BEFORE flipping their tasks to pending, because task workers branch from main and need the PRD on disk. The full "flip" of a planning batch is: commit PRDs → bulk `set_task_status(ids, "pending")` (comma-separated handles ~120 ids in one call; already-pending are no-ops) → restart the orchestrator.

To land a small edit (e.g. a PRD doc fix) directly on the local `main` ref while the orchestrator + other sessions are actively churning main, use an ATOMIC CAS rather than `git commit` (which would clobber a concurrent advance because its working-tree/tree is stale). Recipe: edit the file in the primary working tree; then in a retry loop: X=$(git rev-parse refs/heads/main); build the tree = X's tree with the one file replaced (git hash-object -w FILE; a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE via git read-tree X + git update-index --cacheinfo + git write-tree); NEW=$(git commit-tree TREE -p X -m ...); `git update-ref refs/heads/main NEW X` (CAS — fails if main moved, then retry from the new X); finally `git reset -q` to sync the primary index to the new HEAD. This refuses to clobber concurrent main-advances and avoids the orchestrator dirty-start guard (never leave loose uncommitted tracked changes on main). Do NOT push (local main leads origin by design). Foreground `sleep` is blocked, so retry without backoff. Used 2026-05-31 to land commit 8de0eb13d2 (trajectory PRD §11 doc edit) on attempt 1.

Procedure (Reify): to land a pure-docs commit (e.g. a PRD + capability manifest) directly on local main while the orchestrator is running and the main-gate is enforcing, use `REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS=1 git commit --no-verify -F <msgfile> -- <file>` scoped to the single file (the bypass is proportionate for pure docs; --no-verify avoids the --include-infra pre-commit verify holding .git/index.lock ~30min behind the test semaphore). Two gotchas hit this session: (1) the `-F <msgfile>` option MUST come BEFORE the `--` pathspec separator, else git parses the message-file path as a pathspec ('outside repository'); (2) a NEW untracked file must be `git add`-ed first — `git commit --only -- <path>` cannot commit an untracked path ('did not match any file(s) known to git'). The main-gate logs a sanctioned 'bypass main move <old> -> <new>' line.

Reify: committing a PURE-DOCS change directly on main under the ENFORCING main-gate is fast and safe even with the orchestrator running — confirmed the mechanism 2026-06-24. The pre-commit hook (hooks/pre-commit → hooks/project-checks) delegates to `scripts/verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra`; because `--scope staged` scopes by `git diff --cached`, staging ONLY docs/*.md files yields an empty plan and prints "verify.sh: nothing to verify ... no commands in plan" → exits 0 in seconds (no Rust build, no long .git/index.lock hold). On success the hook calls main_gate_mark, so hooks/reference-transaction records the refs/heads/main move as SANCTIONED ("main-gate ...: sanctioned main move <old> -> <new>"). So: `git add <docs.md...> && git commit -F msg` works for PRD commits — no land.sh, no merge-queue, no REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS needed. Confirms feedback_docs_commit_direct_on_main_under_enforce with the underlying scope-picker reason.

The pre-2026-07-06 belief that "docs changes hit the merge worker's trivial-pass and land in seconds" was true when written and is FALSE now. By contrast a plain commit on main runs hooks/pre-commit -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE unset (role 'task', so no C2 force), and decide_scope classifies `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml` as no-heavy-checks: seconds.

IT IS SANCTIONED, NOT A VIOLATION: hooks/pre-commit runs project-checks on main and then calls main_gate_mark, so hooks/reference-transaction logs the ref move as SANCTIONED. The CLAUDE.md main-gate invariant forbids moving main WITHOUT a gate (merge --no-verify / update-ref / reset / commit-tree plumbing) — a hook-gated commit on main is not that.

SEQUENCE:
1. Write the artifacts as untracked files in project_root at their canonical paths (PRD docs/prds/<vM_N>/<slug>.md, manifest <slug>.capability-manifest.md, sidecar <slug>.capability-manifest.yaml).
2. File the batch with planning_mode=True, wire deps, then commit_planning — it stamps the on-disk sidecar IN PLACE and copies delivered_checks into producer metadata. Flip FIRST, commit the STAMPED sidecar once; never land an unstamped sidecar and stamp afterwards.
3. `git add <each exact file path>` — never `git add -A` and never a directory. project_root is a shared hot checkout with concurrent /prd sessions and the orchestrator; a directory add sweeps foreign untracked files into your commit.
4. `git commit --only <same exact paths> -F <msgfile>` — `--only`/`-o` with an explicit pathspec ignores foreign staged state. (A pathspec commit alone fails on untracked files, which is why step 3 exists.)

HARD TRAPS:
- NEVER `--no-verify` on main. `reify.mainGate.enforce` is true; --no-verify skips pre-commit, so no sentinel is marked, hooks/reference-transaction sees an UNSANCTIONED main move and HARD-ABORTS the transaction. (This is dark-factory's docs-only-commit habit; it is fatal in reify.)
- NEVER `git checkout -b` in project_root — it moves the running orchestrator's checkout off main.
- Confirm HEAD == main before committing (the offline lane can leave project_root on another branch).
- pre-commit can exceed a default 2-minute tool timeout; pass timeout >= 300000.

OBVIATED BY THIS SOP: the branch-landing sidecar-serialization dance (copying commit_planning's yaml.dump-rewritten sidecar back into a landing branch and cmp-ing every to-be-tracked file, to avoid leaving a dirty tracked file in project_root that trips the orchestrator dirty-start guard). Committing in place makes the on-disk copy and the committed copy identical by construction — nothing can diverge.

COST EVIDENCE: on 2026-07-25 the resolution-unification and stdlib-namespace PRD .md files landed via `Merge task/task/prd/...` branches through the merge queue while their capability-manifest .m [cut]

claim: For PRD artifacts, follow the current canonical, hook-gated direct-on-main SOP with exact paths, and verify all earlier conflicting procedures are accounted for.

members.text: reify-compiler's CompiledModule.functions is USER-SOURCE-ONLY: compile_builder/functions_phase.rs:100-105 routes prelude/stdlib fns to ctx.resolution_functions (compile-time overload dispatch only) and leaves ctx.functions user-only as the stored output. So `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)` after `reify_test_support::compile_source_with_stdlib` evaluates against a table with ZERO prelude fns — a name+arity intercept in reify-expr eval_expr cannot be "beaten" by the stdlib .ri body in such a test; removing the intercept yields Value::Undef (the eval_user_function_call lookup-miss value, reify-expr/src/lib.rs:1625), never the .ri placeholder's value. The production path differs: reify_eval::merge_functions (reify-eval/src/lib.rs:1425-1432, pub(crate)) unconditionally appends prelude fns into the runtime dispatch table. reify_compiler::merge_prelude_functions (lib.rs:332) is pub but there is no public accessor exposing the compiled prelude's CompiledFunction slice to feed it.

reify test-harness contract (measured 2026-07-26, task 5410): `reify_test_support::compile_source_with_stdlib` returns a CompiledModule whose `.functions` is USER-SOURCE-ONLY — prelude/stdlib .ri function bodies are NOT in it. The compiler routes prelude fns to `ctx.resolution_functions` (used for compile-time overload dispatch only) and stores only user fns in the module (crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/functions_phase.rs:100-105, ctx.rs:201, reify-compiler/src/lib.rs:274-275). Probe: a fixture with zero user `fn` items compiles with 0 Error diagnostics and `module.functions.len() == 0`.

CONSEQUENCE for tests using `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)`: the function table is EMPTY, so no stdlib .ri body ever executes. On a lookup miss `eval_user_function_call` returns `Value::Undef` (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:1625). Therefore such a test CANNOT observe a stdlib .ri body's return value, and a test asserting `Value::Undef` is a no-op guard (it agrees with the fallthrough). The rule: under this harness a fixture discriminates iff the INTERCEPT's expected value is NOT Undef.

Production differs: reify_eval::merge_functions (crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs:1425-1432) DOES merge prelude functions into the runtime dispatch table, so stdlib .ri bodies genuinely compete there. Tests that need a .ri body to actually shadow/compete must go through reify-eval (Engine/merge_functions), not `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)`.

This invalidated the "placeholder .ri body would return X" framing in crates/reify-expr/tests/option_recovery_eval_tests.rs (incl. the "coincidentally correct" note at :575-584) and in the task-5410 drift-guard doc comments.

In reify, `CompiledModule.functions` is USER-SOURCE-ONLY: `compile_source_with_stdlib` does NOT put the stdlib/prelude `pub fn` bodies there. `functions_phase.rs:105` routes prelude fns into `ctx.resolution_functions` (used for resolution only, then discarded at `ctx.rs:201`, whose comment says "ctx.functions (user-only) remains the output stored in CompiledModule"). Consequence: a test doing `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)` has an EMPTY function table for a source string that declares no `fn` items, so `eval_user_function_call` misses and returns `Value::Undef` silently (`reify-expr/src/lib.rs:1625`) — the stdlib `.ri` body never runs. The production path differs: `reify_eval::merge_functions` (reify-eval/src/lib.rs:1425-1432) DOES merge prelude fns, so only an Engine-level test reproduces stdlib-body-shadowing behaviour.

claim: `CompiledModule.functions` contains only user-defined functions, so tests using it with `EvalContext` cannot exercise stdlib bodies; use the Engine/runtime merge path to test their behavior.

members.text: Warm-lane seeding defeats cargo's `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for TRACKED files: scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh:745-749 bulk-stamps every non-target/ file to 2020-01-01, while `target/` is reflinked with `cp -a` (mtimes preserved) and the seed's sed -i relocation (seed-warm-lane.sh:892-898) bumps build-script `output` files to seed-time. Cargo reruns a build script only when a watched path's mtime EXCEEDS that build dir's `output` mtime, so a 2020-stamped tracked file can never trigger a rerun and the base's compiled artifact is linked verbatim. Measured in _lane-37 (2026-07-27): tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js at 2020-01-01 vs four target/debug/build/tree-sitter-reify-*/output at 2026-07-27 01:14. The `_touch_git_delta` rescue (seed-warm-lane.sh:388-409) only re-touches TRACKED files differing from EFFECTIVE_BASE_COMMIT and is skipped when that resolves empty, so it is a conditional mitigation, not a guarantee. Any build script whose correctness depends on rerun-if-changed of a tracked source is exposed; prefer content-hash staleness plus republishing the watched path's mtime when outputs actually change. Context: task #5629 / esc-5392-1.

Cargo decides whether to re-run a build script by comparing each `cargo:rerun-if-changed` path's mtime against the mtime of `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>-<hash>/output` (strict `>`, nanosecond resolution) — that `output` file, not a timestamp file, is the freshness reference. Consequence: anything that bumps an `output` file's mtime silently suppresses the rerun and links the previously compiled artifact. Verified empirically 2026-07-27 with a throwaway crate: change a watched file, then `touch` its `output` 5s newer → build script does NOT run (stale artifact, no warning); restore `output` 5s older → it runs. Relevant to any tooling that rewrites files under `target/**/build/*/` (e.g. scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh's links-metadata/OUT_DIR `sed -i` relocation sweep, which rewrites `output`/`root-output` in place and therefore advances their mtimes).

claim: Cargo suppresses build-script reruns when watched paths are not newer than the build directory’s output file, so seeding or rewriting timestamps can silently preserve stale artifacts.

members.text: When a Reify task description references a cfg-gate location like "gate at crates/reify-eval/build.rs:59-63" (e.g. has_openvdb), that is almost always a REFERENCE to pre-existing shared build-script infrastructure that the task CONSUMES via #[cfg(has_openvdb)] / #[cfg(not(has_openvdb))] attributes in source/test files — NOT a directive to modify build.rs. The has_openvdb cfg is already emitted by reify-eval/build.rs:59-63 (rustc-check-cfg + rustc-cfg when OpenVdb native libs are found). Architects should NOT list build.rs in a plan's files unless the gate logic itself is changing, or the phantom-done gate will later flag it as declared-but-untouched.

Architect convention for the plan `files` write-set: a file whose existing functions are merely REUSED read-only (called/imported) by this task — but not edited — must NOT be listed in the plan's `files`. Only files the task actually creates or modifies belong there. Listing a reuse-only file trips the pre-merge "declared but not touched" narrowing gate. Example: task 4232 (generic-user-fns γ) reused entity.rs's `check_type_param_bounds`/`satisfies_trait_bound` from entities_phase.rs without editing entity.rs (INV-1: "reused from the structure side, not reinvented"); entity.rs was over-declared and had to be dropped during the narrowing pass.

Architect gotcha: tree-sitter parser artifacts `tree-sitter-reify/src/{parser.c,grammar.json,node-types.json}` and `src/.grammar_hash.stamp` are gitignored (see tree-sitter-reify/.gitignore) — generated from grammar.js by `tree-sitter generate` and auto-regenerated by build.rs at build time; committing the ~63K-line parser.c causes merge conflicts. NEVER list these in a plan's `files` array: they can never be touched by a commit, so they trip the plan-narrowing/phantom-done gate. Declare only `grammar.js` (+ test/corpus + lib.rs) for grammar changes.

Architect plans must declare in `files` only paths the task will WRITE, not paths it merely reads or calls into. The pre-merge phantom-done gate flags any declared file untouched by branch commits and forces a narrowing pass. Task 5334 (δ cluster formation) declared crates/reify-eval/src/structural_query.rs defensively, but its expansion helpers (build_trait_registry, enumerate_descendants, expand_structural_query, apply_trait_filters, apply_cost_aggregation) are already `pub(crate)` on main and callable from resolve_order.rs with no visibility widening — so the file was consumed read-only and had to be dropped from the plan.

Architect plan `files` lists must include only files this task CREATES or MODIFIES — not files reused read-only. A Rust integration test that pulls in a shared harness via `#[path = "common/foo.rs"] mod foo;` and only READS its constants/helpers does NOT modify that harness; listing it triggers the pre-merge "declared but not touched" narrowing flag. Record such harnesses as reuse items, not in `files`. Concrete case: task 4738 wrongly listed `crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs` (96KB shared differential harness, built up by prior tasks incl. dep 4737 which added `SELECTIVE_DEMAND_MULTIBODY_SRC`); the branch only touched `engine_build.rs` + the new `selective_demand_beta.rs`, so differential.rs was dropped from the files list.

Plan `files` list convention: only list files a task will CREATE or MODIFY — not files consumed read-only (reused unchanged). The `files` array drives concurrency locks and the phantom-done/pre-merge gate, which flags any declared file untouched by branch commits. If a plan step says "in X.rs (or Y.rs)" or a reuse item says to use a substrate "unchanged", that file is a read-only dependency and must be kept out of `files`. Example: task 3392 (MITC3+ shell) declared shell_kinematics.rs but only consumed shell_kinematics::shell_kinematics() read-only; the new interior-tying shear helper landed in mitc3_plus.rs, so shell_kinematics.rs was correctly dropped during the architect narrowing pass.

When authoring a TDD plan, the `files` list is create/modify-only — it drives concurrency locks and the phantom-done pre-merge gate. Files that a plan only READS or reuses (e.g. an existing helper like `Engine::dispatch_compute_node` in engine_admin.rs that a new method calls) must NOT be declared in `files`; record them in the `reuse` section instead. Likewise, do not declare crate root `lib.rs` for "make the new pub method reachable from integration tests" — inherent `pub fn` methods on an already-`pub struct` are reachable without any re-export. Declaring read-only/reuse files triggers a post-implementation narrowing pass.

claim: Plan files lists should include only files the task creates or modifies; keep read-only dependencies and reused infrastructure out of the write-set.

members.text: Gotcha for testing tracing-event levels/counts in the reify workspace: call `reify_test_support::prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of any test that asserts exact event counts via `tracing::subscriber::with_default`. Without it, a sibling parallel test thread can poison the per-callsite Interest cache to `never`, silently bypassing the per-test subscriber so it captures nothing. reify-test-support hand-rolls its tracing Subscriber impls (CapturingSubscriberBuilder / CountingSubscriberBuilder), so no `tracing-subscriber` crate dependency is needed — only `tracing`.

For Rust tracing tests in reify, use `reify_test_support::CountingSubscriberBuilder` (registers any subset of {INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ...} + optional `target_prefix(...)` filter) for count-only assertions. For field-level capture, the only existing primitive is `WarnCapturingSubscriber` which is WARN-only and private — for INFO/DEBUG field capture, define a small inline subscriber within the test module mirroring the `MessageVisitor` + `Arc<Mutex<Vec<...>>>` pattern from tracing_support.rs:615-684. ALWAYS call `prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of any test using `with_default` to count exact events — without it tracing-core's per-callsite Interest::never cache can silently poison the callsite under parallel test runs.

Gotcha: in Rust `tracing`, callsite `Interest` is cached PROCESS-GLOBALLY but `tracing::subscriber::with_default` is THREAD-LOCAL. So a unit test that installs a capturing subscriber via `with_default` and asserts a `tracing::debug!` event fired will FLAKE if any sibling test in the same test binary reaches that same callsite first with no subscriber installed — interest gets cached as `never` and the event is silently dropped. Measured in reify-eval (task 5075): 6 of 12 runs failed, and two consecutive identical `cargo test` invocations gave opposite results; it passes in isolation with `-- --exact`. Do NOT fix with `serial_test`/global mutex/`--test-threads=1` (that couples unrelated tests to a log line) — instead assert on a deterministic non-global observable. Applies to reify's widespread `CapturingSubscriberBuilder` + `with_default` idiom (engine_purposes.rs, kernel_registry.rs, engine_edit.rs, compute_targets).

claim: Tracing callsite interest is process-global but `with_default` is thread-local, so event-capture tests can flake when parallel tests cache a callsite as disabled.

members.text: Gotcha for mesh-contract (INV-GEO-1) enforcement work: `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` (crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs:1794) returns a single OPEN triangle (verts [0,0,0,1,0,0,0,1,0], indices [0,1,2]), which `Mesh::validate()` REJECTS under `MeshInvariant::Closed` (open_edges=3) — identical to the manifold γ test's `bad_mesh`. So flipping the tessellate→ingest handoff (engine_build.rs site 1) to fail-closed enforce breaks any cross-kernel BRep→Mesh handoff test routing that mock through the conversion executor (e.g. cross_kernel_handoff.rs). Site 1 only fires on CROSS-kernel Mesh handoffs, not single-kernel tessellate-for-export, so the blast radius is bounded to cross-kernel-handoff tests. Real OCCT tessellations (examples/, prj/) are valid, so the .ri corpus is expected clean.

Gotcha for mesh-contract (INV-GEO-1) work: `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs returns a SINGLE OPEN TRIANGLE (vertices [0,0,0, 1,0,0, 0,1,0], indices [0,1,2]) with a comment that misleadingly calls it "a minimal valid mesh". `Mesh::validate` (crates/reify-ir/src/geometry.rs) REJECTS it under MeshInvariant::Closed with open_edges=3. Any change that makes a mesh-contract check fail-closed on a path fed by this mock will break the cross-kernel BRep→Mesh handoff tests that route it; fix by emitting a closed mesh or setting the contract mode to warn per-test.

claim: MockGeometryKernel::tessellate emits an open triangle that violates the closed-mesh invariant, so fail-closed mesh-contract checks break cross-kernel handoff tests unless the mock mesh or test contract is adjusted.

members.text: Running reify-audit's PTODO detector against a linked git worktree needs two overrides: (1) pass `--runs-db <writable-path>` (e.g. /tmp/x.db) or the CLI exits 125 trying to open the absent data/orchestrator/runs.db; (2) set `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=<main-repo>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` (the main checkout, not the worktree) to activate the liveness lane — otherwise it looks for a worktree-relative ./.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, can't find it, and degrades to structural-lane-only (prints "tasks.db unreachable ... liveness (β) and inverse (ζ) lanes degraded"). Keep `--project-root .` so file/git scanning still targets the worktree. PTODO marker keywords are only TODO|FIXME|HACK immediately followed by `(` or `:` (regex `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b\s*[(:]`); `RESOLVED(...)` lines are NOT treated as markers. A canonical cite is `#` + 1..5 nonzero digits anywhere on the marker line; terminal owners (is_terminal_status = done|cancelled) yield orphan findings, blocked/pending/deferred are LIVE.

To self-check the CLAUDE.md PTODO hard gate (untracked/orphaned/bare-ignore task cites) from a reify task worktree BEFORE committing, run the detector directly: `cargo build --release -p reify-audit && ./target/release/reify-audit --pattern PTODO --runs-db "$(mktemp)" --no-jcodemunch --project-root .` (exit 0 = no High findings; exit N = High-finding count). A bare `./target/release/reify-audit --pattern PTODO` fails with "error opening runs-db 'data/orchestrator/runs.db': unable to open database file" because data/ is git-untracked and therefore absent in every worktree — an empty 0-byte file is an acceptable --runs-db for PTODO (see tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh), and --no-jcodemunch skips an MCP connection PTODO does not use. This manual run is the only per-task feedback for that gate: scripts/verify.sh only runs the tests/infra run_all.sh pool (which owns test_reify_audit_ptodo*.sh) when DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, so a per-task verify will NOT catch a bad #[ignore] cite.

Running the PTODO audit from a worktree (reify-audit --pattern PTODO): worktrees lack both `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` and `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, so the bin exits 125 unless you pass `--runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db` (it opens runs.db during setup even for --pattern PTODO). To run the LIVENESS lane (which detects `orphaned`), also set `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db`; without it the liveness lane degrades to "tasks.db unreachable" and only the structural lane runs. KEY: the actual tests/infra verify gate (`tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh`) runs `ptodo-baseline-gen` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded-structural only) and ratchets live structural fingerprints ⊆ the committed (empty) ptodo-baseline.txt — so liveness-lane `orphaned` findings do NOT block the worktree verify gate; only structural untracked/bare-ignore/malformed-cite do.</content>

members.text: To hermetically simulate a nextest-less host for a tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh suite (without PATH gymnastics or scratch files in the repo), sed a TEMP COPY: `sed -e 's|^SCRIPT_DIR=.*|SCRIPT_DIR="'"$PWD"'/tests/infra"|' -e 's|\*"nextest=1"\*)|*"nextest=1-SIM-NEVER-MATCHES"*)|' -e 's|cargo nextest run |cargo nextest-SIM run |g' tests/infra/<f>.sh > "$(mktemp -d)/sim.sh"`. Sed 1 pins SCRIPT_DIR so the copy can live outside tests/infra yet still source test_helpers.sh and resolve REPO_ROOT; sed 2 forces the suite's NEXTEST_AVAILABLE probe to 0 so nextest-gated asserts SKIP (crisp signal, no expected-FAIL noise); sed 3 makes the plan-line greps unmatchable, mimicking the `cargo test` plan such a host gets. Hiding cargo-nextest from PATH does NOT work: verify.sh probes `cargo nextest --version` first (scripts/verify.sh:1343) and cargo also resolves subcommands from $CARGO_HOME/bin, so you either still get NEXTEST=1 or trip the loud hard-fail at :1366-1375 instead of the graceful NEXTEST=0 fallback. Copying a patched verify.sh is also poor — verify.sh (:249-250) and the suites (:49-53) derive REPO_ROOT from their own BASH_SOURCE dir, forcing scratch files into scripts/ and tests/infra/ where run_all.sh may pick them up.

To simulate a nextest-less host for tests/infra plan-oracle suites (e.g. test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh, test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh, test_verify_semaphore_wiring.sh, test_verify_offline_partition.sh, test_verify_compile_gate.sh — task 5599): use a symlink farm mirroring ~/.cargo/bin MINUS cargo-nextest, prepended to the real PATH with the real ~/.cargo/bin element filtered out, plus HOME=<tempdir> so verify.sh (~line 877) skips sourcing ~/.cargo/env (which would re-prepend the real ~/.cargo/bin and un-hide cargo-nextest). Two traps: (1) CARGO_HOME must NOT be exported to the real ~/.cargo — cargo resolves `cargo-<subcmd>` from $CARGO_HOME/bin in addition to PATH, so cargo-nextest reappears and the plan flips back to nextest=1; (2) the naive recipe PATH="$STUB:/usr/bin:/bin" strips ~/.cargo/bin wholesale, which also removes the tree-sitter CLI and makes test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh's suite-start ensure_tree_sitter_ready gate fail 5 execute-mode sections (A/B/C/F1/H) for reasons unrelated to nextest.

Since task 4971, any test fixture that must simulate cargo-nextest being genuinely absent (to exercise scripts/verify.sh's NEXTEST=0 fallback) needs BOTH a stubbed `cargo` on PATH AND an empty temp $HOME with a restricted PATH excluding ~/.cargo/bin — a stub alone is insufficient. verify.sh's nextest probe (verify.sh:933-970) disambiguates "genuinely absent" (`command -v cargo-nextest` also fails) from "present but probe failing" (hard-fails after 3 retries instead of falling back); if ~/.cargo/bin stays on PATH, `command -v cargo-nextest` resolves the real binary and verify.sh takes the hard-fail branch instead. apply_env() (verify.sh:626) also re-sources ~/.cargo/env (re-prepending ~/.cargo/bin) unless $HOME/.cargo/env doesn't exist, so the temp HOME must be genuinely empty. The canonical idiom (WORKDIR/SHIM_DIR/TMP_HOME + `HOME="$TMP_HOME" PATH="$SHIM_DIR:/usr/bin:/bin"`) lives in tests/infra/test_verify_nextest_probe.sh and was retrofitted into tests/infra/test_verify_semaphore_wiring.sh's (1q) block by task 4984. Exception: for `--scope all --print-plan` alone, an exit-1-for-all cargo stub suffices on its own (no non-nextest cargo call is made), so the empty-HOME/restricted-PATH rig is only required when the fixture goes past plan-printing into an actual nextest-vs-test execution branch.

claim: To test the nextest-absent fallback reliably, ensure the real cargo-nextest cannot reappear through PATH, CARGO_HOME, or ~/.cargo/env; tailor the harness to the test.

members.text: Architect resume gotcha: when re-invoked on a task branch that already has a complete TDD commit sequence but is missing .task/plan.json, and those commits are NOT yet on main (unlanded on the task branch), reconstruct a faithful plan mirroring the committed steps and confirm_plan() — do NOT call report_task_already_done (it requires the commit be reachable from main and would fail that validation for unlanded task-branch work). Observed on task 4971 (verify.sh nextest-probe fix): 4 commits a70958eb80..0eb2201908 present, plan.json absent.

An architect can be re-invoked on a task branch that ALREADY carries complete committed work: `.task/plan.json` is untracked, so a warm-lane re-seed (tracked-files-only + `git clean -xfd`, e.g. when the branch is rebased onto a new main tip) wipes it while the commits survive. Diagnose with `git log --oneline main..HEAD`. The correct response is to reconstruct a plan whose steps map to the existing commits — NOT `report_task_already_done`, which requires the commit to be on main (verify with `git ls-tree main -- <path>`; a branch-only commit does not qualify).

Architect resume gotcha (warm lanes): when re-invoked on a task/NNNN branch, the prior run's .task/plan.json can be gone (.task/ is gitignored, wiped on warm-lane re-seed) while its committed TDD work PERSISTS on the branch. Always `git log --oneline main..HEAD` first — if commits already implement part of the task, plan ONLY the remaining gap (don't re-plan already-green RED tests), but still list the full task footprint in create_plan files[] so locks/phantom-done see all branch-vs-base diffs. Seen on task 5031 (gui-state-sync L2): diff.rs + L1 lint + bridge.ts were committed; only engineStore.ts frontend transport remained.

Architects re-invoked on a reify task worktree should first run `git log main..HEAD` and `ls -la .task/`: an already-implemented branch (test(NNNN)/impl(NNNN) commits present) combined with a DANGLING `.task/plan.json` symlink (target `worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/plan.json` missing) means plan metadata was lost on a lane reseed while branch refs survived. Do NOT call report_task_already_done in that state — that exit requires the commits to be on main, and they are not. Author the plan by deriving the steps from `git diff main...HEAD` so the step list matches the committed work, then confirm_plan and file an escalate_info(category='infra_issue') noting the metadata loss.

CONSOLIDATED (merged 11 near-duplicate entries total: 5 in the 2026-07-05 partial merge + 6 residual near-duplicates folded 2026-07-05 per task 5022): Warm-lane task resume / requeue-rebase loses `.task/plan.json` (gitignored, filesystem-only per CLAUDE.md — never survives a lane re-seed) while the branch's committed TDD step commits (`test(NNNN): step-K RED` / `feat(NNNN): step-K GREEN`, sometimes prereq tags like `pre-1`) survive intact on task/NNNN. Trigger signatures: task metadata `reblock_guard` reading like "warm-lane acquire fault for branch 'NNNN' (seed/worktree...)"; an architect re-invoked and finding branch commits but no plan.json; branch annotated "RESUME CONTEXT: this is a re-queue"; or a requeued task surfaced with a DIFFERENT task's plan.json attached (a prior lane-occupant's, or an adjacent sibling task's — verify plan.json.task_id actually matches the dispatched task before trusting it). Correct action: RECONSTRUCT a faithful plan.json mirroring the committed step structure — `git log --oneline main..HEAD` (or against the branch's merge-base) plus per-commit `--stat`/diff to map each commit to its step by touched files — then call mark_step_done per commit and let the executor re-verify the already-GREEN steps rather than redoing them. Do NOT call report_task_already_done: that path requires the commit be reachable from main, and task-branch WIP is not. Verify premises against the live worktree diff (`git diff <base_commit>..HEAD`) before reconstructing; don't trust old commit-message "green" claims or a plan's analysis narrative blindly — re-run the actual tests/clippy first.

Task-specific gotchas to check every time (kept separate as they carry unique detail):
- A "chore: save WIP before rebase" commit can contain a REAL step's full implementation, not just noise — always `git show --stat`/`git show` each WIP-labeled commit before dismissing it (task 4168, memory a5e8b6b4-10f5-4d43-8b7e-f0cadd54e7bb).
- TDD commits can be directly S1..SN-labelled enabling 1:1 mapping, with a WIP commit occupying the slot of the step whose label was stripped during rebase (task 4870, memory b28158fb-2bdf-408b-979c-03f71cc11520).
- Interleaved WIP-save commits and step-pairs that share one commit SHA both occur — use the last commit in such a sequence as the step's recorded commit (task 4954, memory 17b3b5aa-39b0-4750-b6b5-d552081ac563; also task 3965, memory 1ccfce69-dec1-4a6d-ad1a-81e0440107f9).
- Trailing WIP commits beyond the last clean step commit can be folded into one clean commit via `git reset --soft <last-clean-step-sha>` + recommit — verify `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` is unchanged before/after to prove no content was lost (memory 57af0b70-d339-49ea-a203-6732b588bf47).
- Extra WIP commits after the last named step can contain legitimate additional task-scoped hardening already absorbed into an existing step's description — these don't need a new plan step, just re-verification that they still pass (task 4942, memory a7e90820-babc-4d09-9a27-05a81222ed24).
- A prior LANE OCCUPANT's stale plan.json can be shown for the current task (task 4019 shown task 3932's plan) — verify plan.json.task_id matches the dispatched task (memory e44cd1f5-0696-4fa2-899b-842fc61368e6).
- A SIBLING task's plan.json can be shown instead (task 4855 shown task 4854's plan) — verify actual branch state (git log/rev-list) before trusting the shown plan (memory 7b0d9518-e1ee-4f3e-b86c-f62a399b709a).
- After an INFRA-failure requeue mid-implementation, a rebase during "save WIP" commits can rewrite SHAs, so a reconstructed plan's recorded SHAs for already-"done" steps can point at the wrong (later WIP/amend) commit — don't trust recorded SHAs at face value; cross-check `git log --format='%H %s' main..HEAD` against the plan's file list (task 4906, memory fe1e9c21-0b65-49a5-88b5-bed9225037fa).

Warm-lane recovery gotcha: a task's full implementation can already be committed on its task/NNNN branch when the architect is (re-)invoked, because `acquire_lane` re-seeds the worktree from base and wipes the gitignored `.task/plan.json`. In that case the architect should reconstruct a plan matching the existing TDD commits (git log main..HEAD shows the test/impl pairs) rather than call report_task_already_done — that tool requires the work be on main, but here it is on the unlanded branch. Reconstructing plan.json regenerates the artifact the orchestrator state machine needs so the task can proceed to verify/land.

claim: When task-branch commits survive a warm-lane reseed but `.task/plan.json` is lost, inspect the branch diff and reconstruct a plan matching existing work; don’t report the task done until it’s on main.

members.text: `pkill -f <pattern>` and `pgrep -f <pattern>` match against the FULL command line, which INCLUDES the running shell's own command containing that pattern string — so `pkill -f phase0-run.sh` or `pkill -f load-sampler.sh` self-matches and kills your own bash (observed twice jun9 2026, exit 144). Always kill background helper scripts by PID (capture from pgrep output, then `kill <pid>`), not by `pkill -f <name>` when <name> appears in your command. Also note: multi-statement Bash tool commands occasionally get mangled by the harness's eval-wrapper collapsing newlines between statements (e.g. `tail -8` invalid, echoes concatenated); prefer one logical command per call or `&&` chains, and `tail -n N` not `tail -N`.

OPERATIONAL GOTCHA (killing background builds from an interactive Claude Bash tool): broad process-killing patterns can match the harness's OWN command subshell and truncate the command (observed as exit 144 = 128+SIGTERM, or "Killed" mid-output). Specifically `kill -TERM -<PGID>` where the PGID is shared by the tool's subshell, and `pkill -f 'cargo build --workspace'` (matches the literal pattern string inside your own running command line). Safer: kill explicit PIDs, or pkill on a path unique to the target (e.g. the lane's absolute target dir) that cannot appear in your own command. The actual build processes still died correctly each time; only the reporting command self-terminated. The persisted log files survive, so just re-read them in a follow-up command.

Shell gotcha (cost ~40 min wasted wall-clock 2026-07-25): checking background-build liveness with `pgrep -f "cargo build -p reify-cli"` SELF-MATCHES — the checking shell's own command line contains the pattern, so the check reports "still running" forever (the build had finished in 2m35s). Same family as the probe-exit-pipe gotcha. Robust alternatives: grep the build log for `Finished`/`error`, test the target binary's mtime, or pgrep with a pattern the checker doesn't carry (e.g. `pgrep -x cargo` scoped by cwd, or `pgrep -f 'carg[o] build'` bracket trick). Also applies inside `until pgrep ...` watcher loops — the loop matches itself and never exits.

claim: Avoid broad `pgrep`/`pkill -f` patterns that appear in your own shell command, since they can self-match; use explicit PIDs or safer independent checks.

members.text: Sibling-geometry consumption edges are already encoded in the compiler output: a `let` that references a sibling geometry `let` lowers to `GeomRef::Sub(bare_name)` inside `RealizationDecl.operations`. Bare names (0 dots) mean same-structure siblings; dotted names ("sub.member") mean cross-sub — a namespace split that is safe by construction since DSL identifiers never contain '.'. The authoritative enumeration of which `CompiledGeometryOp` variants carry consumption edges is the private `extract_realization_edges` in crates/reify-eval/src/deps.rs: Boolean{left,right}, Modify|Transform|Pattern{target}, Sweep{profiles}, Isosurface{grid}; GeomRef::Step(_) is intra-node and skipped; Primitive/Curve/Profile carry none. It is not re-exported through `pub mod deps`, so consumers outside reify-eval (e.g. gui/src-tauri) must mirror its match arms rather than call it — cite it in a comment so the two cannot drift.

Reify compiler: a sibling-let geometry reference lowers to `GeomRef::Sub(name)` ONLY on the Modify/Transform/Pattern argument path (the #4668 bare-Ident pre-check, crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:1377-1385). Boolean operands go through `resolve_boolean_arg` (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_boolean.rs:28-60), which has no bare-Ident pre-check and INLINES the operand's initializer as sub-ops referenced by `GeomRef::Step(n)`. Measured: for `param geometry = difference(body, holes)` the names "body"/"holes" appear nowhere in the compiled realization's operations (only `Sub("hole")`, from the Pattern arg, survives). So `RealizationDecl.operations` — and `reify_eval::deps::extract_realization_edges`, which shares the blind spot — is NOT a complete oracle for "which sibling realizations are consumed downstream". The complete name-level source is the value-cell layer: `TopologyTemplate.value_cells[*].default_expr` carries `ValueRef(ValueCellId{entity, member})` for every sibling reference. Caveat when using it: a `: Rigid` structure's auto-derived mass/centroid/moment_of_inertia lets also hold `ValueRef(geometry)`, so a consumption scan must count only Geometry-typed cells as consumers.</content>
</invoke>

members.text: reify-debug MCP expansion: a frontend-mediated debug tool (reads DOM or Solid stores, not the OCCT engine) needs ONLY a tool_defs() entry in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs plus a handler in gui/src/debug/bridge.ts buildHandlers — NO new Rust dispatch match-arm. dispatch_tool()'s default arm (debug_server.rs ~:481) already delegates any unmatched tool name to debug_bridge.query_frontend(). Frontend store fields read by such tools must also be added to the DebugStores type in gui/src/debug/types.ts (it exposes a structural subset of the real engineStore, e.g. it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297).

Adding a frontend-mediated reify-debug MCP tool requires only (1) a ToolDef in debug_server.rs tool_defs() and (2) a handler in bridge.ts buildHandlers(). No new Rust dispatch_tool arm is needed: dispatch_tool's default match arm forwards any unrecognized tool name to state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params). A new Rust dispatch arm is only required when the tool needs engine/disk access (run_on_engine), e.g. open_file/load_fixture. Image-returning tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must ALSO be listed in is_image_tool() so tools/call strips the data-URL prefix and emits an MCP image content block.

Reify has NO rustfmt gate: no rustfmt.toml exists, `git grep 'cargo fmt'` returns nothing tracked, and scripts/verify.sh's lint pass is only `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (fmt-agnostic) — i.e. the lint action is clippy-only and never runs `cargo fmt --check`/rustfmt. The codebase is intentionally NOT rustfmt-clean under the pinned toolchain (rustc 1.96.0 / rustfmt 1.9.0-stable, edition 2024 per workspace Cargo.toml) — pre-existing diffs are widespread across nearly every crate: reify-stdlib (~946 diffs), reify-audit (~728KB), reify-eval (149 files/~37k lines, incl. engine_eval.rs ~25 sites, engine_build.rs, elastic_static.rs, deps.rs, dynamics_ops.rs, engine_admin.rs), reify-lsp, reify-solver-elastic (incl. loop_closure_value.rs, loop_closure_solver.rs), reify-kernel-occt (lib.rs, ffi.rs, handle.rs, build.rs — ~150 diffs), reify-ir + reify-kernel-manifold (geometry.rs, constraint.rs, kernel.rs), reify-kernel-gmsh (build.rs, kernel.rs, kernel_real.rs, lib.rs, mesh_boundary.rs), and gui/src-tauri (commands.rs, debug.rs, debug_server.rs, types.rs, main.rs, tests/rpath_smoke.rs, watcher.rs/watcher_tests.rs). This is a hand-maintained house style that deliberately diverges from rustfmt defaults, not an oversight. Because rustfmt is not part of the enforced gate, pre-existing rustfmt-disagreement in tracked files (e.g. multi-line macro-arg wrapping style) never fails the lint gate on its own — amendment/review passes should not "fix" such drift unless it was explicitly flagged in the task, since touching it is unrelated scope creep.

Rule: do NOT run `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt -p <crate>`, `cargo fmt --all`, or any crate-wide/whole-file fmt for a targeted fix — it reformats the ENTIRE crate/file (observed up to 149 files/~37k lines) even when only one function needed a change, producing massive unrelated churn on every affected task.

Verifying your OWN edits introduce no NEW drift:
- The correct edition is 2024 (NOT 2021) — passing the wrong `--edition` flag flips rustfmt's style-edition defaults (import ordering etc.) and produces spurious diffs unrelated to your change.
- Preferred: `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` (auto-reads edition from Cargo.toml). Flag ORDER matters: `cargo fmt --check -p <crate>` (flag before `-p`) has been observed to non-deterministically error "Unrecognized option: 'p'" or behave inconsistently (likely lock contention from concurrent cargo processes across worktrees) — put `-p <crate> --` before `--check`.
- Alternative: `command rustfmt --check --edition 2024 <single-file>` per file. Note `cargo fmt -- --check <file1> <file2>` does NOT actually scope to just those files in this workspace — it still reports drift across the whole crate.
- CAUTION: bare `rustfmt --check <path-under-repo>` (not /tmp) can be intercepted by a shell wrapper/shim that prints a canned "LINT OK | rustfmt | 0 issues" regardless of actual state — untrustworthy. Also, the locally-installed rustfmt version can differ from whatever formatted the repo, producing whole-workspace false-positive diffs (confirmed by diffing a pristine base-commit file copy) — this is a local-toolchain artifact, not a real regression.
- To isolate a genuine semantic change from incidental reflow noise in the same diff (e.g. an accidental broad `cargo fmt` got mixed into WIP): normalize BOTH old and new file versions through `rustfmt --edition 2024` and diff the normalized versions (collapses formatting-only hunks to nothing), then splice that delta by line-range onto the real unformatted original file rather than committing the fully-reformatted file.
- Real gate: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (or `--tests`) scoped to the touched crate. Rely on `cargo test` + this clippy invocation for verification, not fmt-check.
- Confirm no NEW drift from your edit: diff `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check | grep "^Diff in"` site counts before/after your change, or check your changed line ranges are disjoint from reported dr [cut]

Verifying a Reify GUI observable programmatically (no eyeballing screenshots): launch `REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<port> scripts/run-gui-dev.sh <file.ri>` and drive the reify-debug MCP listener over plain HTTP with curl — `POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` with headers `Content-Type: application/json` AND `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` (the Accept header is required; omitting text/event-stream fails), body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":N,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{}}}`. This works even when the reify-debug MCP server is NOT registered in the agent session (the session's .mcp.json entry only binds if the port was already listening at session start — a GUI you launch mid-session never registers, so curl is the only route). Useful tools: `store_state` → `viewports["design-main"].meshCount` is the single best assertion for "how many bodies actually render"; `mesh_stats` → every mesh the engine emitted with entity_path (compare against meshCount to prove hidden != absent); `open_file` {path: ABSOLUTE} + `wait_for_idle` → load a DIFFERENT example into the ALREADY-RUNNING GUI, so checking N examples costs one build, not N. Result JSON is nested: `result.content[0].text` is itself a JSON string needing a second json.loads. Cost note: the cold debug build (feature `gui`) took ~25 min in a warm lane, so launch it detached early and poll while doing other verification.

Scripting reify-gui retests over the debug MCP (verified 2026-07-22): (1) The reify-debug HTTP MCP (port from the worktree's .mcp.json, e.g. 127.0.0.1:59469/mcp) answers tools/call via plain curl WITHOUT an initialize handshake or Mcp-Session-Id header — stateless POSTs work fine for health/open_file/engine_state/wait_for_idle/demand_dispatch. (3) engine_state's `values` field is a LIST of {id,value} dicts, not a dict — a .get('mass') extraction silently reads None and fakes a "mass missing" result (this produced one false alarm in-session). (139=SEGV, 134=ABRT, 137=OOM-kill) to a log for the exact signal.

WHY (both branch paths are now the SLOW ones): reify's merge gate stamps DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, which makes scripts/verify.sh force --scope all (contract C2, verify.sh:778) and --profile both (verify.sh:602); dark-factory's INV-1 (task 2883, verify.py:5499) additionally REFUSES the docs-only trivial pass at merge role and escalates it to the full global gate, because an adoptable merge verdict must never be stamped from zero evidence. So a docs-only merge costs the same cold debug+release workspace build as landing a compiler change (reify budgets merge_verify_cold_command_timeout_secs: 10800 = 3h). scripts/land.sh is equally expensive — its pre-merge-commit hook runs `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge verify.sh all --profile both --scope all`. The pre-2026-07-06 belief that "docs changes hit the merge worker's trivial-pass and land in seconds" was true when written and is FALSE now. By contrast a plain commit on main runs hooks/pre-commit -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE unset (role 'task', so no C2 force), and decide_scope classifies `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml` as no-heavy-checks: seconds.

IT IS SANCTIONED, NOT A VIOLATION: hooks/pre-commit runs project-checks on main and then calls main_gate_mark, so hooks/reference-transaction logs the ref move as SANCTIONED. The CLAUDE.md main-gate invariant forbids moving main WITHOUT a gate (merge --no-verify / update-ref / reset / commit-tree plumbing) — a hook-gated commit on main is not that.

SEQUENCE:
1. Write the artifacts as untracked files in project_root at their canonical paths (PRD docs/prds/<vM_N>/<slug>.md, manifest <slug>.capability-manifest.md, sidecar <slug>.capability-manifest.yaml).
2. File the batch with planning_mode=True, wire deps, then commit_planning — it stamps the on-disk sidecar IN PLACE and copies delivered_checks into producer metadata. Flip FIRST, commit the STAMPED sidecar once; never land an unstamped sidecar and stamp afterwards.
3. `git add <each exact file path>` — never `git add -A` and never a directory. project_root is a shared hot checkout with concurrent /prd sessions and the orchestrator; a directory add sweeps foreign untracked files into your commit.
4. `git commit --only <same exact paths> -F <msgfile>` — `--only`/`-o` with an explicit pathspec ignores foreign staged state. (A pathspec commit alone fails on untracked files, which is why step 3 exists.)

HARD TRAPS:
- NEVER `--no-verify` on main. `reify.mainGate.enforce` is true; --no-verify skips pre-commit, so no sentinel is marked, hooks/reference-transaction sees an UNSANCTIONED main move and HARD-ABORTS the transaction. (This is dark-factory's docs-only-commit habit; it is fatal in reify.)
- NEVER `git checkout -b` in project_root — it moves the running orchestrator's checkout off main.
- Confirm HEAD == main before committing (the offline lane can leave project_root on another branch).
- pre-commit can exceed a default 2-minute tool timeout; pass timeout >= 300000.

OBVIATED BY THIS SOP: the branch-landing sidecar-serialization dance (copying commit_planning's yaml.dump-rewritten sidecar back into a landing branch and cmp-ing every to-be-tracked file, to avoid leaving a dirty tracked file in project_root that trips the orchestrator dirty-start guard). Committing in place makes the on-disk copy and the committed copy identical by construction — nothing can diverge.

COST EVIDENCE: on 2026-07-25 the resolution-unification and stdlib-namespace PRD .md files landed via `Merge task/task/prd/...` branches through the merge queue while their capability-manifest .m [cut]

Landing a NON-task docs artifact (e.g. a PRD capability manifest) via the orchestrator merge queue, learned 2026-06-19: works fine from the MAIN checkout with no numeric task id. Procedure used: create a task/<slug> branch in /home/leo/src/reify, stage ONLY the new file (leave pre-existing untracked files alone), commit, then `git checkout main` in the main checkout for hygiene (the branch ref persists; keeps project_root on main as the orchestrator's dirty-start guard expects). Then mcp__escalation__merge_request(task_id="<descriptive-slug>", branch="<slug-WITHOUT-task/-prefix>", worktree="/home/leo/src/reify", wait_secs=100). The worker forms task/<slug>, resets its own _merge-verify worktree, and the docs-only diff takes the trivial-pass fast path → returned {status:"done", push_status:"pushed", commit:<sha>} within the bounded wait (no poll round-trip needed). task_id need not be numeric; branch param must omit the task/ prefix (worker prepends it); worktree can be the main checkout since the worker merges in _merge-verify, not in the passed worktree.

CONSOLIDATED (merged 11 near-duplicate entries total: 5 in the 2026-07-05 partial merge + 6 residual near-duplicates folded 2026-07-05 per task 5022): Warm-lane task resume / requeue-rebase loses `.task/plan.json` (gitignored, filesystem-only per CLAUDE.md — never survives a lane re-seed) while the branch's committed TDD step commits (`test(NNNN): step-K RED` / `feat(NNNN): step-K GREEN`, sometimes prereq tags like `pre-1`) survive intact on task/NNNN. Trigger signatures: task metadata `reblock_guard` reading like "warm-lane acquire fault for branch 'NNNN' (seed/worktree...)"; an architect re-invoked and finding branch commits but no plan.json; branch annotated "RESUME CONTEXT: this is a re-queue"; or a requeued task surfaced with a DIFFERENT task's plan.json attached (a prior lane-occupant's, or an adjacent sibling task's — verify plan.json.task_id actually matches the dispatched task before trusting it). Correct action: RECONSTRUCT a faithful plan.json mirroring the committed step structure — `git log --oneline main..HEAD` (or against the branch's merge-base) plus per-commit `--stat`/diff to map each commit to its step by touched files — then call mark_step_done per commit and let the executor re-verify the already-GREEN steps rather than redoing them. Do NOT call report_task_already_done: that path requires the commit be reachable from main, and task-branch WIP is not. Verify premises against the live worktree diff (`git diff <base_commit>..HEAD`) before reconstructing; don't trust old commit-message "green" claims or a plan's analysis narrative blindly — re-run the actual tests/clippy first.

Task-specific gotchas to check every time (kept separate as they carry unique detail):
- A "chore: save WIP before rebase" commit can contain a REAL step's full implementation, not just noise — always `git show --stat`/`git show` each WIP-labeled commit before dismissing it (task 4168, memory a5e8b6b4-10f5-4d43-8b7e-f0cadd54e7bb).
- TDD commits can be directly S1..SN-labelled enabling 1:1 mapping, with a WIP commit occupying the slot of the step whose label was stripped during rebase (task 4870, memory b28158fb-2bdf-408b-979c-03f71cc11520).
- Interleaved WIP-save commits and step-pairs that share one commit SHA both occur — use the last commit in such a sequence as the step's recorded commit (task 4954, memory 17b3b5aa-39b0-4750-b6b5-d552081ac563; also task 3965, memory 1ccfce69-dec1-4a6d-ad1a-81e0440107f9).
- Trailing WIP commits beyond the last clean step commit can be folded into one clean commit via `git reset --soft <last-clean-step-sha>` + recommit — verify `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` is unchanged before/after to prove no content was lost (memory 57af0b70-d339-49ea-a203-6732b588bf47).
- Extra WIP commits after the last named step can contain legitimate additional task-scoped hardening already absorbed into an existing step's description — these don't need a new plan step, just re-verification that they still pass (task 4942, memory a7e90820-babc-4d09-9a27-05a81222ed24).
- A prior LANE OCCUPANT's stale plan.json can be shown for the current task (task 4019 shown task 3932's plan) — verify plan.json.task_id matches the dispatched task (memory e44cd1f5-0696-4fa2-899b-842fc61368e6).
- A SIBLING task's plan.json can be shown instead (task 4855 shown task 4854's plan) — verify actual branch state (git log/rev-list) before trusting the shown plan (memory 7b0d9518-e1ee-4f3e-b86c-f62a399b709a).
- After an INFRA-failure requeue mid-implementation, a rebase during "save WIP" commits can rewrite SHAs, so a reconstructed plan's recorded SHAs for already-"done" steps can point at the wrong (later WIP/amend) commit — don't trust recorded SHAs at face value; cross-check `git log --format='%H %s' main..HEAD` against the plan's file list (task 4906, memory fe1e9c21-0b65-49a5-88b5-bed9225037fa).

members.text: Adding a NEW top-level standalone `tests/*.rs` integration binary to one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) turns the merge gate RED via `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` (the anti-re-accretion kLOC-cap guard, rule b) with `HARNESS_KLOC_CAP FAIL ... reason=unsanctioned-standalone`, even though the test itself compiles and passes. Fix: in the SAME diff, add the canonical path `crates/<crate>/tests/<file>.rs` to the grandfather baseline `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest` (a "conscious row addition" IS the sanctioning mechanism), inserted in ambient-locale `sort` order. Exempt names that skip this: `harness_*.rs` files (governed by the kLOC cap instead) and the 7 override binaries. The manifest header's per-crate/total counts are a frozen base-commit snapshot, already stale vs the live file, and must not be edited.

Adding a NEW top-level crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) fails the early verify gate scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git with "HARNESS_BASELINE_REG FAIL ... reason=unregistered-standalone". Preferred remediation is NOT to add a row to tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest (a shrinking ratchet whose header pins per-crate snapshot counts) but to land the file as a module under the crate's existing harness_<subsystem>.rs C1 compile unit: git mv it into tests/harness_<subsystem>/ and add `#[path = "harness_<subsystem>/<f>.rs"] mod <f>;` — the explicit #[path] is mandatory in an integration-test crate root, and the test's module path stays <f>::<test> so filtersets resolve unchanged. This is the precedent harness_engine.rs documents for task #5056.

reify harness-layout gate — REFINES memory ad415479-f6b6-441b-b95f-6bf1d4168804 (which says the fix for a new standalone crates/<c>/tests/<file>.rs is always "add a grandfather baseline row"). That is WRONG for a crate already FULLY consolidated. Check first: `grep -c '^crates/<crate>/' tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest`. If the count is 0 the crate's consolidation leaf has LANDED (reify-kernel-occt since task #5277, 51 rows removed; reify-cli since #5274) and adding a row un-ratchets a finished consolidation — the manifest header says it is "a RATCHET, NOT A PERMANENT ALLOW-LIST" and PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md §5 C2(b) says "no new gratuitous standalone binary re-accretes". Correct fix there: `git mv` the file into tests/harness_<sub>/<file>.rs and add `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` to the harness root (explicit #[path] mandatory at an integration-test crate root). Even in a still-grandfathered crate (reify-eval, 357 rows), prefer the existing subsystem harness when one fits (harness_sweep/harness_geometry/harness_engine/harness_mechanism/harness_kernel_realization) — it costs one line, adds no link unit, and keeps the ratchet monotone. The diff-scoped gate scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh only inspects TOP-LEVEL crates/<c>/tests/*.rs (harness_layout_in_scope_standalone rejects anything nested below tests/), so the moved file is out of scope and the gate goes green with no manifest edit at all. Verified task #5342 commit 894377054c: both new helix-sweep tests moved (0 content bytes changed), gate PASS added=2 violations=0, kloc-cap 16/16, clippy 0 warnings.

Harness-consolidation (PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md W1) anti-re-accretion guard tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh (task 5265, leaf B1) uses a checked-in GRANDFATHER BASELINE tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest (867 rows at creation: reify-cli 73, reify-syntax 61, reify-kernel-occt 48, reify-eval 395, reify-compiler 290; the 2 in-scope overrides tensegrity_t0a/representation_within_assertion excluded). Rule (b): a top-level crates/<c>/tests/*.rs is sanctioned iff it is harness_*.rs OR one of the 7 override binaries OR listed in the baseline. This is why the guard is GREEN on the pre-consolidation tree. CONSEQUENCE for every consolidation leaf (C-cli/C-syntax/C-occt/C-eval-*/C-compiler-*): when you move former tests/<file>.rs into tests/harness_<subsystem>/<file>.rs, you MUST delete those files' rows from harness-layout-baseline.manifest IN THE SAME DIFF (the baseline ratchets down; empty == fully consolidated), else the guard stays green falsely OR (for a genuinely new stray) goes red. Cap is 20000 raw wc -l lines per harness_*.rs. Guard is classified `pool` in run-all-classification.manifest and runs in the merge-tier run_all suite every merge_request.

reify-eval test-harness consolidation (task #5278, PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md C1/leaf EVAL-1, "1/3" of 3) verified pattern for sibling leaves 2/3 & 3/3: move standalone crates/reify-eval/tests/<file>.rs into tests/harness_<sub>/<file>.rs and declare each in tests/harness_<sub>.rs via `#[path="harness_<sub>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` (explicit #[path] REQUIRED — a bare `mod` at an integration-test crate root resolves to the sibling tests/<file>.rs, not the subdir). This prefixes every test's nextest name with `<file>::`, so `test(/^<file>::/)` selects exactly that former binary's tests; consolidation is selection-neutral because NO .config/nextest.toml or tests/infra filterset references reify-eval test files by name (only the 7 override binaries use binary()). Three gotchas confirmed: (1) source-relative include_str!/include_bytes! need exactly one extra `../` when moved one dir deeper (e.g. fixtures/ -> ../fixtures/, ../../../examples/ -> ../../../../examples/); concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),...) loads are move-safe and must NOT be touched. A successful `cargo nextest list -p reify-eval` already PROVES include-path correctness since include_str! resolves at compile time. (2) Files installing a process-wide #[global_allocator] (common::alloc_counter::CountingAllocator) must stay STANDALONE + grandfathered in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest — two in one binary is a "multiple global allocators" compile error, one shared corrupts sibling alloc-count deltas. (3) Ratchet: remove each moved file's `crates/reify-eval/tests/<file>.rs` row from the baseline manifest IN THE SAME DIFF. Cost gotcha: alternating `cargo nextest list --workspace` and `-p reify-eval` triggers full ~7min recompiles (feature unification differs) — pick ONE invocation form and stick to it. Layout-only: BT-1 total #[test]-fn count must be unchanged (reify-eval was 4690).

CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (Stage 1 recon; supersedes Mem0 5d4d7853-5673-4ff2-b733-b403baee48e2, now deleted, whose census premise went stale within ~24h). reify harness-layout gate — which remediation applies when a diff adds a new top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler) and trips `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` (reason=unregistered-standalone) or `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` (reason=unsanctioned-standalone).

RULE: prefer folding the new test into one of the crate's EXISTING `harness_<subsystem>.rs` units over adding a grandfather row to tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest — adding a row un-ratchets a shrinking ratchet. Adding a baseline row is correct ONLY for a crate that genuinely has no harness unit yet.

CENSUS IS VOLATILE — DO NOT TRUST A DATED SNAPSHOT. The per-crate consolidation leaves land continuously, so any hardcoded "crate X has zero harness files" claim rots fast (the superseded entry asserted reify-compiler had ZERO harness_*.rs on 2026-07-24; four — harness_langcore / harness_patterns / harness_traits / harness_auto_binding — landed overnight via task 5283, merged commit 0360b1c25fc105c2dbb6fc9bc62dde78dbb596f4, falsifying it by 2026-07-25; corroborated independently by Mem0 60239edb-8fc6-48f6-bc07-e27041e92ccc). ALWAYS re-derive the census live at the time you need it, with:
  ls crates/<crate>/tests/harness_*.rs        # does a harness unit exist?
  grep -c '^crates/<crate>/' tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest   # 0 => consolidation LANDED, never add a row
A count of 0 means that crate's consolidation leaf has landed and grandfathering is forbidden.

members.text: Architect resume gotcha (warm lanes): when re-invoked on a task/NNNN branch, the prior run's .task/plan.json can be gone (.task/ is gitignored, wiped on warm-lane re-seed) while its committed TDD work PERSISTS on the branch. Always `git log --oneline main..HEAD` first — if commits already implement part of the task, plan ONLY the remaining gap (don't re-plan already-green RED tests), but still list the full task footprint in create_plan files[] so locks/phantom-done see all branch-vs-base diffs. Seen on task 5031 (gui-state-sync L2): diff.rs + L1 lint + bridge.ts were committed; only engineStore.ts frontend transport remained.

When a Reify task description references a cfg-gate location like "gate at crates/reify-eval/build.rs:59-63" (e.g. has_openvdb), that is almost always a REFERENCE to pre-existing shared build-script infrastructure that the task CONSUMES via #[cfg(has_openvdb)] / #[cfg(not(has_openvdb))] attributes in source/test files — NOT a directive to modify build.rs. The has_openvdb cfg is already emitted by reify-eval/build.rs:59-63 (rustc-check-cfg + rustc-cfg when OpenVdb native libs are found). Architects should NOT list build.rs in a plan's files unless the gate logic itself is changing, or the phantom-done gate will later flag it as declared-but-untouched.

Architect plan `files` lists must include only files this task CREATES or MODIFIES — not files reused read-only. A Rust integration test that pulls in a shared harness via `#[path = "common/foo.rs"] mod foo;` and only READS its constants/helpers does NOT modify that harness; listing it triggers the pre-merge "declared but not touched" narrowing flag. Record such harnesses as reuse items, not in `files`. Concrete case: task 4738 wrongly listed `crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs` (96KB shared differential harness, built up by prior tasks incl. dep 4737 which added `SELECTIVE_DEMAND_MULTIBODY_SRC`); the branch only touched `engine_build.rs` + the new `selective_demand_beta.rs`, so differential.rs was dropped from the files list.

Architect plans must declare in `files` only paths the task will WRITE, not paths it merely reads or calls into. The pre-merge phantom-done gate flags any declared file untouched by branch commits and forces a narrowing pass. Task 5334 (δ cluster formation) declared crates/reify-eval/src/structural_query.rs defensively, but its expansion helpers (build_trait_registry, enumerate_descendants, expand_structural_query, apply_trait_filters, apply_cost_aggregation) are already `pub(crate)` on main and callable from resolve_order.rs with no visibility widening — so the file was consumed read-only and had to be dropped from the plan.

Plan `files` list convention: only list files a task will CREATE or MODIFY — not files consumed read-only (reused unchanged). The `files` array drives concurrency locks and the phantom-done/pre-merge gate, which flags any declared file untouched by branch commits. If a plan step says "in X.rs (or Y.rs)" or a reuse item says to use a substrate "unchanged", that file is a read-only dependency and must be kept out of `files`. Example: task 3392 (MITC3+ shell) declared shell_kinematics.rs but only consumed shell_kinematics::shell_kinematics() read-only; the new interior-tying shear helper landed in mitc3_plus.rs, so shell_kinematics.rs was correctly dropped during the architect narrowing pass.

When authoring a TDD plan, the `files` list is create/modify-only — it drives concurrency locks and the phantom-done pre-merge gate. Files that a plan only READS or reuses (e.g. an existing helper like `Engine::dispatch_compute_node` in engine_admin.rs that a new method calls) must NOT be declared in `files`; record them in the `reuse` section instead. Likewise, do not declare crate root `lib.rs` for "make the new pub method reachable from integration tests" — inherent `pub fn` methods on an already-`pub struct` are reachable without any re-export. Declaring read-only/reuse files triggers a post-implementation narrowing pass.

Gotcha: in Rust `tracing`, callsite `Interest` is cached PROCESS-GLOBALLY but `tracing::subscriber::with_default` is THREAD-LOCAL. So a unit test that installs a capturing subscriber via `with_default` and asserts a `tracing::debug!` event fired will FLAKE if any sibling test in the same test binary reaches that same callsite first with no subscriber installed — interest gets cached as `never` and the event is silently dropped. Measured in reify-eval (task 5075): 6 of 12 runs failed, and two consecutive identical `cargo test` invocations gave opposite results; it passes in isolation with `-- --exact`. Do NOT fix with `serial_test`/global mutex/`--test-threads=1` (that couples unrelated tests to a log line) — instead assert on a deterministic non-global observable. Applies to reify's widespread `CapturingSubscriberBuilder` + `with_default` idiom (engine_purposes.rs, kernel_registry.rs, engine_edit.rs, compute_targets).

Gotcha for testing tracing-event levels/counts in the reify workspace: call `reify_test_support::prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of any test that asserts exact event counts via `tracing::subscriber::with_default`. Without it, a sibling parallel test thread can poison the per-callsite Interest cache to `never`, silently bypassing the per-test subscriber so it captures nothing. reify-test-support hand-rolls its tracing Subscriber impls (CapturingSubscriberBuilder / CountingSubscriberBuilder), so no `tracing-subscriber` crate dependency is needed — only `tracing`.

For Rust tracing tests in reify, use `reify_test_support::CountingSubscriberBuilder` (registers any subset of {INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ...} + optional `target_prefix(...)` filter) for count-only assertions. For field-level capture, the only existing primitive is `WarnCapturingSubscriber` which is WARN-only and private — for INFO/DEBUG field capture, define a small inline subscriber within the test module mirroring the `MessageVisitor` + `Arc<Mutex<Vec<...>>>` pattern from tracing_support.rs:615-684. ALWAYS call `prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of any test using `with_default` to count exact events — without it tracing-core's per-callsite Interest::never cache can silently poison the callsite under parallel test runs.
