Orchestrator test config-loading (updated by task 2719, commit 02e2d43cd2): the two transitional top-level symlinks `orchestrator.yaml` and `orchestrator/config.yaml` (which pointed at the canonical `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml`) are RETIRED. The autouse `_isolate_orch_config` fixture (orchestrator/tests/conftest.py) NO LONGER deletes ORCH_CONFIG_PATH + relies on the CWD-relative `Path('config.yaml')` symlink fallback; it now PINS `ORCH_CONFIG_PATH` to the absolute `REPO_ROOT / "dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml"` (plus ORCH_PROJECT_ROOT=tmp_path as before). Consequences unchanged in spirit: (1) a bare `OrchestratorConfig()` in an orchestrator test still loads OPERATIONAL overrides (e.g. merge_verify_breadth='full', merge_train_former_enabled=True), NOT defaults.yaml code defaults — a test asserting a config-sourced CODE DEFAULT must still opt into `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("code_default_config")` (conftest.py), which points ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at a guaranteed-absent file so only defaults.yaml loads. (2) A test can still load the committed config by its own later `monkeypatch.setenv("ORCH_CONFIG_PATH", str(path))` (wins over the autouse fixture, same function-scoped monkeypatch); the DF_CONFIG_PATH constants in test_fleet_staleness_composition.py / test_harness_service_restart.py / tests/scripts/test_fallback_verify_config.py / test_orchestrator_watchdog.py now point at `dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml`. Gotcha the pin guards against: with the symlink gone, a bare `OrchestratorConfig()` from the orchestrator/ cwd with ORCH_CONFIG_PATH UNSET silently returns defaults ('scoped'/False), NOT an error — so the fixture's ORCH_CONFIG_PATH pin is load-bearing to keep operational config loaded across the suite. NOT breakers (verified during the pre-removal gotcha investigation, task 2719 cleanup of 2698): `dashboard/src/dashboard/config.py`'s legacy-spelling discovery list and `scripts/run_vllm_eval.py`'s `.is_file()` candidate resolver do not depend on the removed symlinks and stay unchanged.

CONCRETE TRIP-UP (task 3513, 2026-08-06): a plan wrongly assumed OrchestratorConfig's field default for `test_command` ('pytest') would apply in-test; instead the autouse pin serves the real fleet-wide operational value (a `cd shared && uv run pytest ...` chain) — the config-sourced value bullet (1) above warns about. Any test helper that depends on a config-sourced default should assert that premise explicitly so a future drift fails loudly instead of silently passing on the wrong value.

orchestrator/tests: as of task 2545 (routing sigma gate), the repo's live top-level dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml defines no `routing:` key at all, so `OrchestratorConfig()` built under just the autouse `_isolate_orch_config` fixture already resolves `cfg.routing.rules` to the full shipped defaults.yaml rule list (large-plan-steps, large-plan-modules, simple-saturated-full-path, retry-tier-up) — confirmed empirically by constructing OrchestratorConfig under that fixture's env and inspecting `cfg.routing.rules`. Do not rely on this for a test whose premise requires a specific shipped rule to be live, though: it is incidental (the operational yaml could add a `routing:` key later and silently break the premise). Use the opt-in `code_default_config` fixture (conftest.py:286) instead, exactly as test_routing_retry_tier_up.py and the byte-equivalence scenarios already do, whenever a test's correctness depends on a specific defaults.yaml routing rule being present.

GOTCHA (dark-factory orchestrator tests, measured task 4481): a bare `OrchestratorConfig()` in a test does NOT give you code defaults. The autouse `_isolate_orch_config` fixture (orchestrator/tests/conftest.py) pins ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at the OPERATIONAL dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, so a bare config reads whatever that file declares and falls back to the package default only for keys it does NOT declare. Measured: 390 config leaf fields exist, the operational yaml declares 41, so 349 keys are silently supplied by the code default. Any test asserting one of those 349 passes BY ACCIDENT and goes red the moment an operator declares that key — a landmine armed by an ops edit, in a file nobody thought to pre-check.

THE HATCH: `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("code_default_config")` (conftest.py) re-points ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at a guaranteed-absent file so only the package-bundled defaults.yaml loads. It runs AFTER the autouse fixture and wins. It must never be made autouse (that would strip config.yaml from ~10k tests that legitimately want it). Two ad-hoc equivalents are already widespread and count as isolation: monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', '') (154 uses) and monkeypatch.delenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', raising=False) (29 uses).

TWO DISTINCT FAILURE CLASSES, needing different detection — do not assume one method finds both:
(A) STATIC — asserts a field EQUALS its code default. Found by AST scan. A committed ratchet now holds this at zero for the whole suite: orchestrator/tests/test_code_default_hatch_guard.py + _config_default_scan.py.
(B) BEHAVIOURAL — exercises default-only behaviour with no literal assertion anywhere, so NO static scan can see it. Typically a section's `enabled` flag defaulting True is what makes a code path run at all. Found ONLY dynamically: perturb every undeclared key at once (constraint-aware — several fields carry pydantic `le` bounds and model validators), swap the yaml in, run the suite, and take adversarial_failures MINUS baseline_failures. Measured over a 41-file union: baseline 0 failed / 2986 passed; adversarial 97 failed. Class (B) outnumbered class (A) roughly 3:1.

REPAIR RULE THAT HELD UP IN PRACTICE: for class (A), the one-line hatch. For class (B) where the root key is a section `enabled` flag and the test is about BEHAVIOUR rather than defaults, prefer the knob-agnostic pin (set the one flag explicitly in the fixture that builds the config) over the hatch — the test then keeps reading operational values for every other key. Where a test hard-codes a threshold literal, read it live off the config under test instead.

ALWAYS BISECT THE ROOT KEY BEFORE REPAIRING; the obvious guess is wrong often enough to matter. Measured counterexample: test_harness_deterministic_recon_sweep.py's 18 adversarial failures look like they must come from `deterministic_recon_sweep_enabled` — perturbing that key ALONE leaves the file fully green (95 passed). The actual root key was `recovery_emission.enabled`, a different config section. One root key producing 18 failures needs one decision, not 18.

TOOLING NOTE: the adversarial-config harness must `cp` the real yaml aside and restore it under a shell `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and you must verify `git status` clean and the yaml byte-identical afterwards — you are mutating a tracked, operator-owned file in the live tree.

claim: Tests relying on package defaults must explicitly use `code_default_config`; bare `OrchestratorConfig()` reads operational config and can make default-dependent tests pass accidentally.

GOTCHA (orchestrator/tests/test_session_hooks.py, discovered task 4662): adding an optional keyword to a session_hooks helper can break a pre-existing test WITHOUT that test calling the helper directly — because the suite's dominant idiom is `monkeypatch.setattr(sh, '_helper', lambda: <value>)`, replacing the WHOLE function with a zero-arg stub. A new `probes=` keyword forwarded from the caller then raises `TypeError: <lambda>() got an unexpected keyword argument`.

MEASURED: threading a per-event memo into `_nested_claude_liveness_pid` broke `test_forked_inheritor_record_gets_a_pid_that_dies_with_it` (1 failed / 168 passed) even though the function's own signature stayed backward-compatible with a `None` default. The two tests that call it DIRECTLY (`sh._nested_claude_liveness_pid()`) were unaffected — only the setattr-stub site.

SO: before planning "add an optional kwarg, no test edits needed", grep `monkeypatch.setattr(sh, '<name>'` for every helper you intend to forward INTO, not just for direct calls to it. Fix is a one-token arity change on the stub (`lambda **_kw: 424242`) that leaves its return value and every assertion identical — but it is still a test-file edit, so a plan that promises "no existing test edited" needs the exception recorded (filed as esc-4662-1).

Note the asymmetry that makes this easy to miss: a helper whose call sites all pass the new kwarg is safe if tests only call it directly, and unsafe if any test stubs it out. The two look identical when you grep only for the bare function name.

When adding a keyword parameter to a function that tests monkeypatch with a hand-written stub, widen the stub's signature in the SAME commit — and assert on the caught exception's identity, not just that some error was recorded. In dashboard, `_index_escalations` calls `load_queue_escalations(dir, skipped=...)`; the existing stub `def _boom(_dir: Path)` then raised an arity `TypeError` instead of the intended `PermissionError`. Because `TypeError` is in `memory_evals._ARTIFACT_ERRORS`, the degradation test stayed GREEN while silently ceasing to exercise the read boundary at all. The fix is `def _boom(_dir: Path, **_kwargs: Any)` plus an assertion that the recorded issue detail contains the injected error text ('Permission denied'), which is what makes an arity mismatch distinguishable from a real read failure. This failure mode is distinct from the bare-MagicMock one: a hand-written stub is stricter than the real callee, and a broad `except` tuple upstream converts that strictness into a false pass.

AMENDMENT to the task-4292 kwarg-threading blast-radius gotcha (memory 9b2b0d32-e99f-4063-9f02-863c3cff4634, "enumerating the blast radius by grepping for `call.args ==` UNDERCOUNTS it"). Task 5364, 2026-09-18 — a THIRD breaking idiom, and the specific misreading that produces the undercount.

THIRD IDIOM. A plain positional `async def` stub wired in via `patch.object(obj, '_method', side_effect=stub)` where the subject under test is NOT a retry/timeout loop. Unlike idiom 2 (which the 4292 entry warns fails misleadingly as a TimeoutError), this one fails LOUDLY and correctly: `TypeError: ...<locals>.fake_llm_batch() got an unexpected keyword argument 'withheld_list'`, naming the new parameter. Measured: 10 tests across two files. Same fix — give the stub `**kwargs` when the test is about behaviour rather than call shape; all six positional arguments stay inspected, nothing is weakened.

THE MISREADING THAT CAUSED IT. Task 5364's plan analysis grepped the CALL SHAPE `fake_llm_batch(cands, pools, ps_list, start, proj_id, proj_root)`, found it at three cited line numbers, and concluded in a frozen design_decision that "keyword-only-with-default leaves all of those untouched". The grep was right and the inference was wrong, because it conflated two different things a positional shape can be:
- a positional CALL SITE of the real method — genuinely transparent to a new keyword-only parameter, because the caller simply never passes it;
- a positional STUB DEFINITION patched over that method — NEVER transparent, because the production code now passes a keyword the stub's signature does not accept.
A keyword-only-with-default parameter is additive for callers and breaking for doubles. Those are opposite directions, and the same grep hits both.

PRE-FLIGHT. Before threading a kwarg through `<method>`, grep for `def ` stub DEFINITIONS (not call sites) bound to it: `grep -rn "def fake.*<method-ish-name>\|patch.object(.*'<method>'" tests/`, then check each hit for `**kwargs`. Count the definitions, not the call shapes.

(Filed as an amendment, not a replacement: 9b2b0d32's two idioms and its `assert_awaited_once_with` guidance are unchanged and still correct.)

dark-factory dashboard gotcha (measured task 4884, 2026-09-07): threading a NEW keyword argument into an existing `fetch_tasks`/`fetch_statuses` call site inside `active_tasks._shape_one_project` breaks every test stub that hard-codes the old signature — 44 test failures from a single added `timeout=` kwarg, and the tracebacks read as unrelated shaping assertions ("deferred task T-30 was dropped by the active-status filter") with the real `TypeError: _statuses() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout'` buried below.

WHERE THE STUBS LIVE (all three must be patched together, they are not centralised): `dashboard/tests/test_active_tasks.py::_register_fetch_tasks`'s inner `_narrowed` and `_statuses` closures; three local `_fake_fetch_statuses` definitions in the same file; and `dashboard/tests/test_task_runtime_boundary.py::_fake_fetch_statuses`. `_narrowed` already accepted `timeout=None` and `_statuses` did not, which is why only the `fetch_statuses` leg broke.

FIX SHAPE: give the stub `*, timeout=None` (accepted-and-ignored) rather than `**kwargs` — the explicit keyword keeps the stub's signature a readable statement of the production contract, and `**kwargs` would silently swallow a future fourth kwarg the stub should have been updated for.

DIAGNOSIS TIP: when a batch of dashboard shaping tests fail together with assertions about MISSING ROWS, grep the captured output for `unexpected keyword argument` before reading any individual assertion — a stub TypeError inside `asyncio.gather` surfaces as an empty/short row set at the assertion site, not as an error at the call site.

Gotcha (task 2847): adding a new keyword arg to orchestrator.evals.runner.build_eval_orch_config silently breaks orchestrator/tests/test_eval_memory_isolation.py::test_run_eval_forwards_memory_endpoint_to_build_eval_orch_config, whose monkeypatch stub `def _rec(config, task, base_config=None, *, memory_endpoint=None, judge_config=None)` (~line 199) is keyword-only with no **kwargs and rejects any unknown kwarg with a TypeError at run_eval's call site — even though the stub's docstring claims it is "not a signature lock". Any change to build_eval_orch_config's signature must update that stub in the same commit.

orchestrator/tests/test_eval_memory_isolation.py::test_run_eval_forwards_memory_endpoint_to_build_eval_orch_config monkeypatches build_eval_orch_config with a rigid-signature stub `def _rec(config, task, base_config=None, *, memory_endpoint=None, ...)`. run_eval calls build_eval_orch_config UNCONDITIONALLY forwarding all its knobs (memory_endpoint, and now judge_config as of task 2825), so any NEW keyword param added to build_eval_orch_config must also be added to this `_rec` stub or the test breaks with `TypeError: _rec() got an unexpected keyword argument '<param>'` — even though the test only asserts on memory_endpoint. Same test-double-pins-signature class as the test_liveness_boundary_gate.py write_agent_session spy. It is the only test that shadows build_eval_orch_config; other callers (run_eval/run_end_to_end/run_architect_eval) use the real function. Fix is a one-line signature widen (add `<param>=None` to _rec), not a behavior change.

claim: When adding a keyword parameter, find and update every rigid test stub that replaces the function; additive parameters can still break those doubles.

members.text: In reify, `cargo test` output is intercepted by a hook that replaces stdout/stderr with a one-line "PASS: n | FAIL: n | SKIP: n" summary — `--nocapture`, `2>&1`, and redirecting to a file all still lose `eprintln!`/`println!` diagnostics. To extract measurements from a throw-away probe test, have the test itself write to a path outside the repo (e.g. `std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open("/tmp/probe.txt")`) and `cat` that file afterwards. Remember to `rm` the probe file from `crates/<crate>/tests/` and confirm `git status` is clean before finishing.

In the reify worktree Bash sandbox, `cargo test` output gets auto-summarized to a single "PASS: N | FAIL: N | SKIP: N" line with no per-test detail whenever the invocation matches/runs multiple tests (even with --nocapture). To see full detail (panic messages, assertion diffs) for a specific failing test, run it with a fully-qualified name plus `-- --exact` so exactly one test matches — that yields the complete libtest output including panic backtraces.

reify eval-worktree gotcha: `cargo test` stdout/stderr reaching the agent is silently replaced by a one-line summary ("PASS: n | FAIL: n | SKIP: n") — even when redirected to a file and `cat`ed, and even for `--nocapture`. Panic messages and eprintln! output are therefore invisible, which makes probe/debug tests useless by default. Workaround: pipe the output through `base64 -w0` (`cargo test ... 2>&1 | base64 -w0`) and decode mentally — the full raw output survives. Alternatively encode the answer in PASS/FAIL by writing one assert-per-hypothesis test and running each with a name filter.

When running `cargo test`/`cargo nextest` in a reify worktree, a Bash-tool hook often collapses test output to a single `PASS: N | FAIL: N | SKIP: N` line and swallows per-test failure detail (and piping it through grep loses even that line). To see WHICH test failed and why, build the test binary (`cargo build -p CRATE --test NAME`) then run the compiled binary directly from `target/debug/deps/<name>-<hash>` with `--test-threads=1`, redirecting to a file. Also: reify-eval CLI e2e tests like `cli_reify_eval_prints_inspectable_structure_values` require the `reify` bin at `target/debug/reify` — `cargo test -p reify-eval` alone does NOT build it; run `cargo build -p reify-cli --bin reify` first or the test fails with a spawn error (not a real regression).

In the reify repo, `cargo test … -- --nocapture --show-output` produces only a one-line summary `PASS: N | FAIL: N | SKIP: N` and drops actual test stdout — some wrapper in the harness chain swallows it (NOT the `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh` runner, which just sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH). Workaround when a smoke test relies on `println!` for human-readable per-item output: build via `cargo test`, locate the test binary at `target/debug/deps/<test-name>-<hash>` (use `find target/debug/deps -name "<name>*" -executable`), and execute it directly with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/snap/freecad/current/usr/lib`. Test-harness flags work normally on the direct binary.

claim: In reify, test-runner hooks may hide cargo test details, so use a workaround such as running one exact test or invoking the test binary directly to inspect failures.

members.text: verify.py::_build_fallback_config is reached only on the no-module_configs path and filters task_files to .py first (py_files). So root-level pyproject.toml/uv.lock are dropped and a `[pyproject.toml, uv.lock, cockpit/...]` diff already scopes to cockpit alone (post task 2344). The fleet-wide fallback for a single-subproject diff fires ONLY when a root-level .py file (most commonly repo-root conftest.py) is present, because that makes _single_subproject_prefix return None (via `any('/' not in f)`), and the code then returns config.test_command verbatim. This is the exact residual gap task 2368 fixes.

Orchestrator verify test-scoping: a task whose modules have no per-subproject orchestrator.yaml gets module_configs=[] from workflow._resolve_module_configs, so run_scoped_verification (verify.py) routes to _build_fallback_config, which historically set test_command = config.test_command verbatim — the fleet-wide `cd shared && uv run pytest tests/ && cd ../escalation && ...` chain — dragging unrelated subprojects' red tests into the task's verify (false-blocked task 2293/cockpit at esc-2293-13). Lint/type are already scoped to touched files via _scope_command; only TEST had the stale fleet-wide fallback. Fix: derive a subproject-scoped `cd

&& uv run pytest ` in the fallback when all touched .py files share one top-level dir P that has its own pyproject.toml in the worktree.

claim: In the no-module-config fallback, scope tests to a touched subproject when all changed Python files belong to one; a root-level Python file prevents scoping and can trigger the fleet-wide test command.

members.text: Mutation-testing a reify tests/infra/*.sh suite must be done IN PLACE (back up the file, mutate, run, restore), never on a copy under /tmp. These suites derive the repo root and the artifact-under-test's path from their own BASH_SOURCE location, so a mutated copy run from /tmp cannot find $JC_INDEX/etc and EVERY assertion fails (e.g. "0 passed, 47 failed", with rc=127 buried in the capture). That reads as "the mutation was detected" and silently certifies a non-vacuity proof that never ran — a FALSE POSITIVE, the opposite direction from the false negative in memory 4193f200 (mutant missing its sourced siblings) and complementary to 654dd5b3 (verify.sh derives REPO_ROOT from BASH_SOURCE, not cwd). The discriminator that catches it: a valid mutation proof fails ONLY the targeted assertion(s) — "46 passed, 1 failed" — so always read the pass count, not just the presence of a FAIL line. Hit 2026-08-21 in task 6107 while proving Test 14's identity-seam assertions non-vacuous; the /tmp run produced a confidently wrong claim that had to be corrected in a later commit message.

Mutation-testing a reify shell script (flip a flag, run the mutant, confirm a test goes red) must copy the script's sourced siblings alongside it. scripts/warm-lane-audit.sh does `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib_portable.sh"` (line 145), so a mutant copy alone in /tmp dies there and emits NO stdout at all — which reads as "the assertion still passed", a false negative that silently invalidates the discrimination proof. Copy both files into the temp dir (keeps the worktree provably clean, unlike an in-place sed/revert).

Reify infra-test mutation validation: a mutated COPY of a tests/infra/*.sh member must be run from INSIDE tests/infra/, not from /tmp. These scripts resolve their helper library as "$SCRIPT_DIR/test_helpers.sh" and hard-exit with "ERROR: test_helpers.sh not found" from any other directory, which reads like a broken mutation rather than a path problem. Workflow that works: cp the member to tests/infra/zz_mut_probe.sh, apply the mutation, run it, then rm the probe before staging (it is not gitignored).

To mutation-probe a reify tests/infra/*.sh member that reads repo files through REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/../..", don't drop a copy into tests/infra/. Sandbox the tree instead: `d=$(mktemp -d); git archive HEAD .config scripts tests/infra <any crate files the member checks> | tar -x -C "$d"`, then cp the working-tree member over the archived copy, mutate it, and run `bash "$d/tests/infra/<member>.sh"`. SCRIPT_DIR and REPO_ROOT then resolve inside the sandbox, so test_helpers.sh, sourced libs and config reads all work. The worktree stays clean, no sibling *.sh scan sees a scratch file, and several probes can run in parallel. Verified 2026-09-23 (task 7791) on test_nextest_slow_priority.sh: ~10MB archive, ~21s per run.

claim: Mutation probes must preserve the script’s expected paths and dependencies, and confirm only the targeted assertions fail rather than trusting any FAIL output.

members.text: Architect-time gotcha for dark_factory: when EXTRACTING a shared helper out of orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py, the destination MODULE is constrained by the existing tests, not by taste. Both test_verify_merge_flake_suppression.py and test_verify_preexisting_main_break.py seam exclusively via `patch.object(verify_module, 'run_verification'|'_group_node_ids_by_subproject'|'logger', ...)` after a lazy in-test `from orchestrator import verify as verify_module`. So an extracted function that MOVES to a sibling module and does `from orchestrator.verify import run_verification` holds its own binding, those patches silently miss it, and the pre-existing tests break — while a function that STAYS in verify.py and resolves those names as verify module globals keeps every existing patch working. This is the placement corollary of the known "patch the importing module's binding, not the defining module" rule: if the tests patch module M's globals, callee code that must observe the patch has to live in M and look the names up unqualified at call time. Check the test files' patch targets BEFORE choosing where an extraction lands — a PRD code block's file-path header is not authoritative against them.

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/evals/reviewer_trial/__main__.py, every click CLI command's async `_run()` body does local `from .runner import run_trial` / `from .scorer import score_panel_run` / `from .report import ...` imports inside the closure rather than at module top level. This means tests must patch these at their SOURCE module (e.g. `orchestrator.evals.reviewer_trial.runner.run_trial`, `orchestrator.evals.reviewer_trial.scorer.score_panel_run`), not at `orchestrator.evals.reviewer_trial.__main__.run_trial` — patching the latter has no effect since the CLI re-imports the name fresh from the source module on each invocation. `_load_corpus` and `_select_original_corpus` are the exception: they're defined directly in `__main__.py`, so patch those at `orchestrator.evals.reviewer_trial.__main__._load_corpus`.

In orchestrator/src/orchestrator/cli.py, command functions that call into a module whose functions get monkeypatched in tests (e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr(routing_module, 'probe_models', fake_fn)`) must reference that module qualified (`from orchestrator import routing` then `routing.probe_models(...)` looked up at call time) rather than `from orchestrator.routing import probe_models` — a name-bound import would capture the original function at cli.py import time and silently ignore the test's monkeypatch on the source module's attribute.

When extracting a merge_queue drive-path into a test helper in a SEPARATE module (e.g. orchestrator/tests/_merge_queue_harness.py), reference merge_queue module-level symbols via dynamic attribute lookup (`import orchestrator.merge_queue as _mq`; use `_mq.run_scoped_verification`, `_mq.LocalRunner`, etc.), NOT `from orchestrator.merge_queue import ...`. Many merge-queue tests do `patch('orchestrator.merge_queue.run_scoped_verification', ...)`; a from-import binds the name in the helper module at import time, so the patch never reaches the helper and the pass-mock is silently ignored, breaking those tests. In-class methods (like the old _verify_and_advance shim) worked because Python resolves module globals at call time — a from-import in a new module loses that.

Testing a `scripts/` module loaded via importlib: a FUNCTION-LOCAL import (`from x import helper` inside the function body, `# noqa: PLC0415`) re-resolves the module attribute on every call, so `monkeypatch.setattr(x, 'helper', spy)` in a test genuinely intercepts it. A module-level `from x import helper` binds the name at import time and makes that same spy a silent no-op — patch the SCRIPT module's own attribute instead. This makes the import form load-bearing for the test, not just a lint preference: it is what lets a "this script must delegate to the one sanctioned helper" invariant be asserted as an observed CALL (spy that delegates to the real function, so the caller still behaves correctly) rather than as a grep over the script's source text.

claim: For monkeypatches to intercept calls, resolve patched names from the module attribute at call time, respecting the tests’ patch target rather than binding imports early.

members.text: In a reify warm lane, `cargo test -p reify-gui --lib` runs directly with no manual LD_LIBRARY_PATH: `.cargo/config.toml` sets `target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.runner` to `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh`, which provides the OCCT/deps library path to the test binary. You only need LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu when invoking the built test binary by hand.

Running a reify workspace TEST binary directly (e.g. ./target/debug/deps/reify_compiler-<hash> <test_name_filter> --nocapture --test-threads=1) requires `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin:/opt/reify-deps/lib`, otherwise it fails with "error while loading shared libraries: libopenvdb.so.13.0: cannot open shared object file". This is because the tbb-pin/OCCT/OpenVDB RUNPATH treatment (mechanism A″) is applied only to the workspace BINARIES (reify, reify-gui) — NOT to test deps binaries. `cargo test` sets this env automatically; running the prebuilt binary directly does not. This direct-run path is very useful for iterating on a single test (esp. a crash/SIGSEGV-reproducing one) without paying cargo's rebuild, which under warm-lane build contention can be 1-6 min even for an incremental reify-compiler change.

Running a reify test binary DIRECTLY from target/debug/deps/ (e.g. to repeat one test many times under induced load, which `cargo test` makes awkward) fails with "error while loading shared libraries: libopenvdb.so.13.0". Cargo injects the prebuilt native-dep search path via build-script link directives, but a bare exec does not: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu" first. Keep that OCCT-before-deps ordering — reify wants system OCCT 7.8 while /opt/reify-deps ships 7.9 transitively via gmsh. Also note libtest prints a trailing BLANK line after "test result: ok. ...", so `| tail -1` in a pass/fail harness yields an empty string and reports every round as failed; grep for '^test result:' instead.

Running a compiled reify test binary DIRECTLY out of target/debug/deps/ (e.g. `./target/debug/deps/struct_ctor_field_conformance_tests-<hash> --list` to enumerate test names without a rebuild) fails with `error while loading shared libraries: libopenvdb.so.13.0`. `cargo test` sets the loader path itself; a direct invocation does not. Prefix with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/opt/reify-deps/lib64` and it works. Useful when you need the test-name roster of an already-built binary and do not want to pay another cargo invocation.

To see WHICH reify-gui test failed, run the test binary directly — the skim wrapper condenses `cargo test` to `PASS: N | FAIL: M | SKIP: K` with no failure names. Get the path via `env cargo test -p reify-gui --lib --no-run --message-format=json` (parse the `compiler-artifact` line whose `target.name` is `reify_gui` and `profile.test` is true), then run it with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` — without that the binary dies with `error while loading shared libraries: libopenvdb.so.13.0`.

When running a reify test binary directly out of target/debug/deps/ (the standard way to see WHICH test failed, since the skim wrapper condenses cargo test to PASS/FAIL counts with no names), do NOT hand-maintain LD_LIBRARY_PATH — exec through the repo's own cargo runner instead: `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh ./target/debug/deps/<bin> --test-threads=8`. That script is what `.cargo/config.toml`'s `runner=` key already points cargo at, so it is the single source of truth for the native-dep loader path and cannot drift from what `cargo test` itself uses. Evidence this matters: at least six separate procedural memories record this same gotcha and each spells the path differently and incompletely (`/opt/reify-deps/lib:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`, `/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin:/opt/reify-deps/lib`, `/opt/reify-deps/lib:/opt/reify-deps/lib64`, `/opt/reify-deps/lib:/opt/reify-deps/manifold/lib:/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin`) — the wrapper makes the list unnecessary to know. It conditionally prepends the snap-OCCT dir and /opt/reify-deps/lib only when each actually exists and holds libTKernel.so*, so it is also correct on hosts where a hardcoded path would not be.

claim: For reliable direct execution of reify test binaries, use `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh` instead of maintaining `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` by hand.

members.text:
dark-factory's root pyproject.toml sets `addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"`. Under importlib mode pytest does NOT insert a test file's own directory onto sys.path, so a shared non-test helper module placed next to tests (e.g. tests/scripts/systemd_unit_invariants.py) is UNIMPORTABLE from sibling test files unless that directory's conftest.py explicitly inserts `Path(__file__).parent`. tests/scripts/conftest.py already does this for `scripts/`; extend the same idempotent guard rather than relying on pytest's rootdir behaviour. Symptom of getting it wrong is a collection-time ImportError, not an assertion failure.

SEE ALSO 02b9371f (measured 2026-09-02, task 4345): this claim is ASYMMETRIC by invocation shape, not a blanket rule — `cd <subproject> && pytest tests/...` DOES put the tests dir on sys.path[0] (a bare sibling import works there), while a repo-root multi-package run does not. Read 02b9371f before assuming a sibling import that works in a single-subproject run will also work in a multi-package/repo-root run.

In tests/scripts/, test modules cannot import each other: there is no __init__.py, pytest runs with addopts="--import-mode=importlib" (pyproject.toml), and tests/scripts/conftest.py only inserts the repo's scripts/ dir onto sys.path — not tests/scripts/ itself. So reusing a helper like test_orchestrator_service_files.py::_parse_sections from a sibling test module requires a local copy (or moving the test into that module), not an import.

In tests/scripts/, a sibling non-test HELPER module IS importable from a test module (`from systemd_unit_invariants import ...`) because tests/scripts/conftest.py:26-28 inserts that directory onto sys.path — pytest's --import-mode=importlib (root pyproject addopts) does not do it, the conftest does. Several inline "copied because a sibling cannot be imported" helper duplicates in this directory rest on the false half of that claim (only sibling TEST modules are un-importable); extract shared helpers into systemd_unit_invariants.py instead of copying.

REFINEMENT (measured 2026-09-02, task 4345) of the existing note that "--import-mode=importlib does not put a test file's own directory on sys.path". The truth is ASYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the trap:

* `cd escalation && uv run pytest tests/...` — the tests dir IS `sys.path[0]`. A bare `from _sibling import X` WORKS. Conftest is named `'conftest'`.
* Repo-root MULTI-package run (`pytest escalation/tests/x.py orchestrator/tests/y.py`) — `sys.path[0]` is some OTHER subproject's tests dir; escalation/tests is absent entirely. The same import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at COLLECTION time. Conftest is named `'escalation.tests.conftest'`.

Why this hides: dark-factory's verify `test_command` runs each subproject SEPARATELY (`cd shared && pytest tests/ && cd ../escalation && pytest tests/ && ...`). So a sibling-module import with no conftest sys.path insert is fully green in verify and breaks only for a human running pytest from the repo root. Never conclude "the sibling import works" from a single subproject-scoped run — test both shapes.

THE FIX IS AN ENFORCED HOUSE CONVENTION, not an ad-hoc insert. `tests/scripts/test_pytest_workspace_collection.py` states it ("each subproject exports its non-fixture helpers under a uniquely-named sibling module") and enforces it: `test_subproject_conftests_add_tests_dir_to_sys_path` iterates `_SUBPROJECTS_WITH_CONFTEST` and requires `sys.path.insert(0, str(_TESTS_DIR))` (Path form) or `sys.path.insert(0, _tests_dir)` (os.path form) — the regex accepts ONLY those two spellings, positioned after the `_SRC` insert and before the first non-stdlib import. Existing sibling helpers: `_fm_helpers.py`, `_orch_helpers.py`, `_dashboard_helpers.py`, `_dt_helpers.py`, `_merge_queue_harness.py`.

`_SUBPROJECTS_WITH_CONFTEST` is a HAND-MAINTAINED registry and was `['dashboard', 'fused-memory', 'orchestrator', 'shared']` — escalation had a tests/conftest.py but was absent from the list AND missing the insert. So "escalation can't use a sibling helper" was never a property of importlib mode; it was an un-enrolled subproject. If you hit this for a subproject, check the registry before concluding the option is closed. Adding the insert to escalation left the full suite green (1511 passed, 2 xfailed, 84s).

Corollary for planning: "a conftest helper is reachable only as a fixture, so folding it needs a fixture parameter on every test" is only true when the sibling-module route is genuinely unavailable. Check the registry first — it can turn a ~90-call-site mechanical conversion into a 6-file edit with zero test-signature changes.

In dark-factory, a shared non-test helper module for tests/scripts/ is importable by BARE NAME (e.g. `from setup_host_parsing import ...`, `from systemd_unit_invariants import ...`) because tests/scripts/conftest.py explicitly inserts that directory onto sys.path. That insertion is load-bearing, not redundant: pyproject.toml sets `addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"`, and under importlib mode pytest deliberately does NOT add a test file's own directory to sys.path — without the conftest line a sibling helper fails at COLLECTION with a bare ModuleNotFoundError. Put shared parsing/assert helpers in a uniquely-named sibling module there rather than duplicating them across test modules.

claim: Under pytest importlib mode, sibling imports depend on invocation shape, so explicitly add the tests directory via conftest and share helpers from non-test modules, not test modules.

members.text: Cross-repo tasks whose deliverable is dark-factory source must be filed with project_root=/home/leo/src/dark-factory, NOT /home/leo/src/reify. Reify worktrees track ZERO files under orchestrator/ (verified: `git ls-files 'orchestrator/*'` = 0, and zero hits for git_ops.py/workflow_types.py/merge_queue.py/merge_liveness.py anywhere in reify), so a DF-side task filed against reify's project_root is structurally unactionable — the architect can never write a plan. Diagnostic tell: the task record carries metadata.repo="dark-factory" while project_root points at reify, and files_tagged_at is stamped with NO files key (the file-tagger ran and found nothing to tag). Reify tasks 5608 and 5735 both hit this, 5735 being a re-file of 5608 into the same wrong project_root.

Cross-repo misfile detection for reify architects: before planning a task whose title starts "dark-factory:", check whether its target files are tracked in reify (`git ls-files`/`git grep` in the worktree). dark-factory (/home/leo/src/dark-factory) is a separate repo with its OWN taskmaster tree (.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json, project_id "dark_factory"), so such a task cannot be implemented from a reify worktree — the commit lands in the wrong repo, yields an empty task-branch diff (phantom-done), skips reify's verify gate, and dirties the running orchestrator's project_root. The established disposition is refile-into-dark_factory-then-cancel: reify 5575 was cancelled with metadata refiled_as="dark_factory:3102" + refile_reason, approved 2026-07-27 via interactive /unblock (esc-5575-3). Report these with report_unactionable_task, not report_blocking_dependency — nothing is missing, the task is just in the wrong tree. Genuine cross-repo work is tracked the other way round, via `external_deps: ["dark_factory:NNNN"]` on the reify task.

Architect check before planning a reify task whose title starts "dark-factory:" — read `metadata.repo` first. If it says `dark-factory` while `project_root` is `/home/leo/src/reify`, the task is mis-routed and NO reify-side plan exists: confirm with `git ls-files 'orchestrator/*' | wc -l` (0 in reify) and then cross-check `search_tasks(project_root="/home/leo/src/dark-factory", ...)` for an existing duplicate before rejecting. Two corroborating tells: `metadata.files_tagged_at` stamped with no `files` key (the tagger found zero local files), and a prior sibling carrying a `reblock_guard` signature "architect reported task unactionable: filed against project_root=...". Observed twice on the same seam — reify 5608 and its child 5735 both blocked this way, while the real work was already filed and at review as dark_factory task 3003.

Reify tasks titled "CROSS-REPO (dark-factory merge_queue.py)…" (e.g. task 4851: post-merge equivalence false-positive on stale/detached worktree HEAD) have NO reify-side deliverable: the entire fix (in `_check_post_merge_equivalence`/`_finalize_advanced_merge`/`_maybe_auto_chain_generation`/`resolve_queued_branch_ref`) and its regression test live in dark-factory's `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py` + `git_ops.py`, which are absent from the reify repo. The reify architect should call `report_unactionable_task` (no reify test/impl can be written). Distinguish from seams like the trivial-pass guard / main-gate / warm-lane D8 / cpu-gov α-β-γ, where reify DOES ship an oracle/script/primitive and only the wiring is dark-factory's — those are plannable; a pure dark-factory bug-fix dispatched as a reify task is not.

The reify repo tracks the orchestrator's CONFIG only (`dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml`) and none of its source: `git ls-files | grep -c '^escalation/'` returns 0, and reify has no orchestrator/src tree. So a task filed from reify about escalation detail/summary building, review aggregation, verdict caching, or workflow state must be retargeted to the dark-factory repo (/home/leo/src/dark-factory/orchestrator/src/orchestrator/) — no reify-side plan can carry the fix. Run that git ls-files check before planning any task whose description says "ORCHESTRATOR/DARK-FACTORY INFRA, not reify source".

For Reify tasks whose described code changes live in the dark-factory repository (orchestrator, fused-memory, etc.), the architect cannot produce a viable plan: the Reify worktree contains no orchestrator code, plan-tools `files` lock paths must be relative to the worktree, the verify pipeline runs Rust/npm tests on Reify (not pytest on dark-factory), and any commits would not deliver fixes to the orchestrator. Such tasks should be re-filed in the dark-factory task tree. Escalate via category=scope_violation when encountered.

members.text: Convention for a multi-stream /prd program run by agent seats (established 2026-10-10/11 on the /review-all program, after the deliberation reference's "one /team, each seat authors and decomposes" proved unworkable): seats author the PRD, manifest and YAML sidecar and return a structured block, never committing and never editing the program doc; the lead commits all PRDs in ONE `git commit --only`; the lead orders decompose by the seam-dependency graph (on dark_factory S14 shared leaves → S18/S21 → S25 → S23) and hands each seat the filed task ids it depends on plus its rulings; seats decompose under planning_mode, add their high/critical leaves as dependencies of the trigger-chain gate, commit_planning their own batch, write the stamped sidecar to disk without committing; the lead commits all stamped sidecars and the FILED rows in one closing commit. Reasons: decompose needs other streams' ids for real dependency edges (S14's scripts-adoption leaf had to wait on S25's bootstrap while S25's leaves wait on S14's shared leaves, resolved only by the lead choosing the direction), and six concurrent `git commit` in the machine-operated main checkout would contend on the index lock. Two companion conventions: a HELD leaf for a dependency on a later-wave stream is filed in planning mode, wired in-batch, excluded from commit_planning, and stamped metadata.x_seam_wait = {stream, contract} for the owning stream's session to release; and the seat brief carries the report's actual mechanical-filings rows for its keys rather than the lead's claims (the lead was wrong twice).

Convention (review-all program docs, codified in skills/review-all 2026-10-11 from what the first run's S14→S18/S21→S25→S23 wave did): /prd decompose under a /review-all program is LEAD-SEQUENCED. (a) seats author PRD + manifest + sidecar and return a structured block, never committing and never editing the program doc or another stream's PRD; (b) the lead commits all PRDs in one `git commit --only`; (c) the lead orders decompose by the seam graph and hands each seat the filed ids it depends on plus the lead's rulings on its open questions; (d) seats decompose under planning_mode, add their high/critical leaves as dependencies of the trigger-chain gate, commit_planning their own batch, write the stamped sidecar to disk and do not commit it; (e) the lead commits all stamped sidecars and the FILED rows in one closing commit. Two program-doc conventions: a HELD LEAF (`metadata.x_seam_wait = {stream, contract}`, filed in planning mode, wired in-batch, EXCLUDED from commit_planning, released by the owning stream's session — e.g. S25 ι 6764 waits on S20/C3, S25 ξ 6770 on S2/C5), and "a seat never edits the program doc; it returns the FILED row and cross-reference lines for the lead to apply". Why: seats needed each other's task ids for seam dependencies, and six concurrent git commits in the machine-operated main checkout would have contended on the index lock. Seat briefs must carry the report's Mechanical filings rows VERBATIM and the seat re-runs contract §8 step 1 before filing regardless — the lead's briefs twice asserted a Phase-5 task that did not exist.

claim: A multi-stream /prd program run by agent seats is lead-sequenced: only the lead commits, and it orders decompose by the seam-dependency graph.

members.text: In dark_factory, adding a new import line that carries a `# noqa: ...` (for example the `# noqa: E402` imports after load_dotenv() at the top of fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/main.py) fails merge verify. scripts/tests/test_inline_suppression_ratchet.py::test_the_live_tree_passes_the_gate_once_the_baseline_is_seeded fails because scripts/inline_suppression_baseline.json is keyed by kind+codes+sha256 of the stripped line, and may only shrink. Do not add to the baseline. Either avoid the suppression, for example with a local import inside the function that uses it as main.py's run_server already does, or give the marker an owner: `# debt: task <id>`, `# debt: ticket tkt_<id>` or `# ratified: <row id>`. The owning task must be a follow-up that removes the suppression, never the task that adds or rewords the line. To check before merging, run `uv run --project scripts python scripts/inline_suppressions.py --check --root <worktree>`. Found in task 7397 (esc-7397-7).

INV-12 inline-suppression ratchet trap: scripts/inline_suppressions.py keys an unowned `# noqa` by (kind, codes, sha256 of the stripped physical line) with NO path, and the baseline is a global multiset that only shrinks. Copying an existing suppressed line verbatim into N more files therefore overruns that key's count, and the failure lists EVERY site, including the pre-existing one. Task 3932 hit this twice in the merge gate (7 copies of `_df_no_leaked_drain_processes,  # noqa: F401  — the binding IS the wiring`), as task 6966 had before it with the client-feed conftest. Before landing, run `scripts/inline_suppressions.py --check` on the integrated tree, and prefer a wiring that needs no suppression at all. Slack (headroom the tree no longer uses) is not a failure; `--tighten` is separate maintenance.

claim: The INV-12 inline-suppression ratchet fails merge verify on any new unowned suppression key, and its baseline may only shrink.

History: task 2878 added Scheduler.is_actively_held (dispatched/lock/cancel-grace), task 2931 added _has_fresh_dispatch on metadata.routing.latest.decided_at, and task 2991 added _has_fresh_merge_phase on metadata.merge_phase_liveness.entered_at. Task 3541 then made liveness a filing-incarnation question. When the task is in _escalation_events or is_actively_held, escalation.pins::classify_pins is consulted and the L0 is promoted only if it lands in dead_l0 (the filer is known and differs from the current claimant). Otherwise it is deferred, not dropped. Pattern for the next recurrence: do not add another freshness disjunct. Fix the live signal (_escalation_events / is_actively_held) or the filing-incarnation classification instead. Note dispatch gating keys on has_open_l1 (level 1), not L0 — so deferring the reaper promotion is what unblocks re-dispatch of a wedged task.

Orphan-L0 reaper liveness (task 3002, merged at commit 065fae12b2 on 2026-11-13): do NOT model a reviewer_comprehensive / resettled_adjudicator dispatch's liveness with an elapsed-time freshness window or with a role-aware routing.latest.role check. members.text: reify-audit's jcodemunch MUNCH decoder (crates/reify-audit/src/jcodemunch_client.rs): a 3-colon-segment `__tables` spec — `prefix:table:cols`, type list OMITTED, which jcodemunch-mcp 1.108.54 emits for find_references (`r:__rows__:file|specifier|match_type`) — decodes EVERY column as ColType::Str, so numeric columns arrive as JSON strings. Any wire adapter reading them with a bare `row.get(k)?.as_u64()?` / `.as_f64()?` inside a `filter_map` then silently DROPS the whole row instead of erroring. Use the tolerant `row_u64` (and its float twin) helpers, which accept a JSON number or a parseable string. Related gotcha in the same file: `decoded` is a `serde_json::Map`, i.e. a BTreeMap (the crate does not enable `preserve_order`), so a "first table carrying column X" scan visits tables ALPHABETICALLY, not in wire order — `"Aux"` sorts before `"__rows__"` ('A' 0x41 < '_' 0x5F).

In reify-audit's jcodemunch MUNCH decoder, accepting a TYPE-LESS 3-segment `__tables` spec makes every column decode as `ColType::Str`, which silently breaks any adapter that reads a numeric column with a bare `as_u64()`/`as_f64()` inside a `filter_map` — the row is dropped and the caller gets an empty Vec instead of a loud `LoadError::Protocol`. Widening the spec grammar therefore REQUIRES rewiring every mandatory numeric column through a number-or-string tolerant reader (`row_u64`/`row_f64` in crates/reify-audit/src/jcodemunch_client.rs). Optional numeric columns read with `unwrap_or_default()` are safe and deliberately left alone.

jcodemunch-mcp 1.108.54 emits 3-segment MUNCH `__tables` specs (`prefix:table:cols`, e.g. `r:__rows__:file|specifier|match_type`) with the trailing type list OMITTED, and its `find_references` rows carry no `line` column at all. In reify-audit's `jcodemunch_client.rs`, a type-less spec decodes EVERY column as `ColType::Str`, so any wire adapter reading a numeric column with a bare `?.as_u64()` / `?.as_f64()` inside its `filter_map` silently drops the whole row — turning a grammar drift into a silently-empty `Vec` (an audit reporting a clean corpus) instead of a loud `LoadError::Protocol`. Read mandatory numeric columns through `row_u64` / `row_f64` (number-or-string-parse), and treat `line == 0` as the documented "wire did not report one" sentinel rather than a drop condition.

claim: Type-less MUNCH specs decode numeric columns as strings, so adapters must use number-or-string tolerant readers to avoid silently dropping rows.

members.text: Procedural norm for committing PRD/manifest artifacts during CONCURRENT /prd decompose sessions in dark-factory (observed repeatedly 2026-07-06 across W1/W3/W4/W6/W7 streams): all sessions share ONE working tree and ONE .git/index, and the live merge queue plus sibling commits create heavy contention. Symptoms: (a) `.git/index.lock: File exists` (another commit mid-flight), and (b) `fatal: cannot lock ref 'HEAD': is at X but expected Y` (a concurrent commit advanced HEAD during your ~3-min pre-commit pyright run, so your commit loses the ref race). Consequence: your staged file gets SWEPT INTO another session's commit (content lands on main, commit MESSAGE is misattributed) — so ALWAYS locate a PRD/manifest by PATH (`git cat-file -e HEAD:plans/<slug>-prd.md`), never by commit message. Effective workaround for a markdown-only artifact: it needs no pyright, so commit with `git commit --no-verify -F <msgfile> -- <pathspec>` (pathspec-scoped so you don't sweep others' half-staged files) in a retry loop that first waits for `.git/index.lock` to clear — the --no-verify commit is near-instant and wins the race. Being swept is harmless (content is correct on main); the real risk avoided is a partial/garbled index.

dark_factory git discovery (2026-07-09): the pre-commit hook runs 3× pyright on EVERY commit regardless of what changed — even a docs-only/markdown commit to plans/ exceeds the Bash 2-min timeout and gets SIGTERM'd (exit 143). Cleanest fix in Claude Code is the Bash tool's run_in_background:true flag (detaches the commit, survives the 2-min limit, fires a completion notification) — simpler than setsid ... &+poll. Confirmed: a capability-manifest markdown commit timed out twice foregrounded, then succeeded backgrounded (exit 0). Complements the known 'setsid git commit + poll' feedback.

Git gotcha (2026-07-06): to commit ONLY specific UNTRACKED files while leaving unrelated modified/staged files out (e.g. a PRD + manifest committed to main amid other sessions' live WIP), `git commit -F msg -- <path1> <path2>` FAILS on untracked paths with 'error: pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git' — git commit with a pathspec only sees tracked/staged paths. Correct sequence: `git add -- <paths>` FIRST, THEN `git commit -F msg -- <paths>` — the explicit pathspec still commits ONLY those paths (the --only default when paths are given), so other concurrently-staged content stays out of your commit. This composes with the existing df convention: run it as `setsid git commit ... &` + poll the log, because pre-commit runs the full 3× pyright (fused-memory/orchestrator/dashboard) and exceeds the 2-min Bash ceiling even for a docs-only commit.

Committing even a docs-only file under plans/ in dark-factory triggers the FULL pre-commit hook (3× pyright over fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard), which exceeds the Bash tool's 2-min ceiling and gets SIGTERM'd (exit 143) mid-hook — the commit does NOT land. Fix: run it detached — `setsid bash -c 'git commit -F <msgfile> > <log> 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> <log>' &` then poll <log> for the EXIT= marker (pyright takes ~3-5 min total). Second gotcha observed this session: while the first (timed-out) commit sat blocked, the live merge queue landed an unrelated merge (task/2040) and advanced HEAD, leaving the staged file still staged (status `A`) — re-run `git add <file>` before the detached retry. Confirms and extends the feedback that the harness may ignore timeout/run_in_background for `git commit` and that pre-commit 3× pyright exceeds the 2-min ceiling; use -F for the message (heredocs get flattened).

Committing a docs-only file (e.g. a plans/*.md PRD) directly to main in the dark-factory checkout while the orchestrator merge queue and 2-3 concurrent /prd sessions are all committing: a background loop that pre-checks for a fully-free index (no .git/index.lock AND no live 'git commit' process) STARVES — it never finds a free window because the merge queue commits nearly continuously (observed: gave up after 40x10s). Meanwhile a normal commit runs the pre-commit hook = full-repo pyright (fused-memory + orchestrator, ~2 min) holding index.lock the whole time. Robust approach for a markdown/docs-only commit: `git commit --no-verify --only -F <msgfile> -- <paths>` in a tight attempt-and-retry loop (each attempt is sub-second — git fails fast when the lock is held — so retry on failure; do NOT pre-check). It won the lock on attempt 1 where the polling loop failed for 400s. --no-verify is safe here (pyright/ruff/mock-checks are no-ops on markdown) AND courteous (minimizes lock-hold, unblocking the merge queue). Reserve the pre-commit hook for CODE commits. Gotcha: put -F <msgfile> BEFORE the -- pathspec separator, else git reads -F/- as pathspecs; and write the message to a file (heredoc -F - trips the Bash eval-flatten bug).

Operational gotchas for committing to the dark-factory repo from another project's session (observed 2026-07-09): (1) DF's pre-commit hook runs lint + asyncmock checks + FULL pyright over fused-memory/orchestrator/dashboard — even a docs-only plans/*.md commit takes ~3 minutes; use a >=10min Bash timeout and don't diagnose a "hang". (2) Concurrent Claude sessions committing to DF main are common — a .git/index.lock encounter should be triaged with `pgrep -a git` (the holder's command line shows which session/file), NOT deleted; live commits hold it for minutes because of the hook. (3) PRD convention: plans/<slug>-prd.md + plans/<slug>-prd.capability-manifest.md committed directly to main with a `docs(prd):` message.

claim: In dark-factory’s shared checkout, commit docs-only artifacts with path-scoped commands and account for slow hooks and concurrent commits without disturbing another process’s lock.

STAMPED PEER under topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth` — what task 3226 ACTUALLY landed, correcting this topic's canonical prediction.

The canonical entry says "Task 3226 is the code fix that would make this whole gotcha class moot by making the guard hermetic." That is NOT what shipped, and the difference matters for triage.

WHAT 3226 DID (landed 2026-08-25, base main f38463508e):
1. Added `scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` — the cross-repo α/γ comparison run EXPLICITLY, out of suite. Three outcomes, NO skip state: EXIT_OK=0 / EXIT_DRIFT=1 / EXIT_UNAVAILABLE=2, so an absent or unrunnable sibling reports as loudly as real drift and can never read as a pass. Run it as `uv run --project shared python scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` (also `--reify-repo`, `$REIFY_ROOT`, `--json`). ATTRIBUTION: DRIFT is a cross-repo mirror gap owned by a mirror task, NEVER a fault in the dark-factory branch under test; UNAVAILABLE means nothing was compared. Documented in OPERATIONS.md §9a.
2. Closed the skip-vs-pass conflation IN THE PROBE, which is the general half of this gotcha. `verify._BASELINE_SKIPPED_IDS_CACHE` is a parallel per-main-SHA cache of SKIPPED test ids, seeded from the SAME single bare-main probe that seeds the failing baseline (a None `skipped_test_ids` seeds EMPTY, so the two caches never disagree about which shas were probed). `verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main`'s id-diff fast path now intersects its new ids with that cache and, on any hit, FALLS THROUGH to the (category, cause_hint) signature comparison instead of returning the confident task-fault `(False, '')` — one unattributable id invalidates the whole diff. `merge_queue._run_post_merge_verify` partitions the same way, so "N new failing test(s) not present on main" counts only tests main actually RAN, and skipped-on-main ids get their own clause. Both are CACHE-ONLY peeks (no probe on the critical path, G4/task 2564), so a cold cache degrades to the pre-3226 behaviour exactly.

WHAT 3226 DID NOT DO: it did not make the guard hermetic and did not delete the in-suite gates. As of this landing the real /home/leo/src/reify checkout is still executed during an ordinary dark-factory run by 5 gates in fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py and 4 in shared/tests/test_locking.py (plus TestReifyCheckoutPlantedLayout, ~250 lines whose purpose is to assert those gates are ARMED — task 4080). So a reify-side allowlist change with no dark-factory change involved CAN STILL red this repo's suite. Recorded as esc-3226-5.

REVISED TRIAGE RULE: the parents[5] arithmetic that made bare-main and worktree disagree is gone (tasks 3843→3978 replaced it with a marker-bound nearest-ancestor walk single-sourced in shared/src/shared/reify_checkout.py; a fixed parents[N] index is now a REGRESSION, not a fix). Bare main and a worktree therefore reach the SAME reify root, so probe and branch agree and a drift failure classifies as MAIN_HEALTH_RED rather than blaming an innocent task. When you do hit one: run `scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` to get the answer without the full suite, and treat a DRIFT verdict as mirror work, not as the merging task's diff.

The canonical entries under this topic prescribe "hold the merge until the mirroring task lands" — that is the right move only when the dark-factory-side mirror has NOT landed yet. There is a second, distinct arm: the mirror already landed on main and the lane is simply BEHIND it. Then nothing needs to be held or authored — a rebase clears it.

GOTCHA — a bare-main health probe can report "green" on a test that merely SKIPPED, not passed. fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py::test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script resolves its target as Path(__file__).parents[5]/'reify'. From a WORKTREE (/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.worktrees/<n>/fused-memory/tests/) it expands to /home/leo/src/reify, which DOES exist, so the test RUNS — and currently FAILS. Merge verification always runs in a worktree, so verify sees the failing branch while a bare-main probe sees a skip. members.text: NORM for SATISFYING a capability-manifest `expect: absent` delivered_check: purge the forbidden literal from TEST FIXTURE INPUTS in the scoped paths too, not just production code — a mechanical grep cannot tell a live default from a test argument. Sighting 2026-08-21, task 6108 (jcodemunch gamma): the legacy leodearden/reify default was fully removed from production sites in crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs, yet the manifest check (pattern leodearden/reify, paths crates/reify-audit/src, expect absent) still FAILED on one hit at jcodemunch_index.rs:561, where the literal was only the INPUT to an index_db_path slash-flattening assertion. Fix: substitute a neutral same-shaped literal (owner/project yields owner-project.db); behaviour under test unchanged. Corollary making an absence-guard TEST compatible with the manifest check rather than contradictory (raised as unachievable in esc-6108-3, dismissed): give the guard test a strictly SHORTER needle than the manifest pattern — the guard asserts help text lacks the bare owner token with no slash, which cannot match the manifest's slashed pattern. A non-matching-prefix needle is what lets both hold at once.

In reify capability manifests, `grep:` is a binding-KIND token in the evidence taxonomy, NOT a durability convention, and its trailing `wired` is a verdict word — not a greppable anchor. Per ~/.claude/skills/prd/references/gates.md and decompose-mode.md:48, `grep:file:line wired` / `producer:task-N upstream` / `grammar-fixture:path parses` / `floor:bound>X` are the same `<kind>:<locator> <verdict-word>` grammar, and grep:/producer: are two alternative PASS routes for the SAME anti-orphan check. So `grep:git_ops.py:789-809 wired` carries no anchor at all. The durable payload already sanctioned under that same kind is `grep:<file> <symbol> wired` (see warm-lane-pool-activation-seam.capability-manifest.md:59 and v0_6/differential-field-operators.capability-manifest.md:7). De-numbering a binding is gate-safe: the `binding` string is never machine-parsed (shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py takes it as free text) and the enforced artifact is the .yaml `delivered_check`, which is pattern-only and contractually forbidden from using file:line.

CAPABILITY MANIFESTS ARE FAILING IN A SPECIFIC, REPEATING WAY IN REIFY — two independent instances surfaced on 2026-08-07 alone, in unrelated subsystems. The failure is a row marked PASS on evidence that ROUTES AROUND the capability it claims. Instance 1, `docs/prds/v0_6/io-export-import-completion.capability-manifest.md:67`: `| version param reaches export | via δ driver (reads version off STEPOutput) | PASS (δ upstream) |` — a leaf's capability marked PASS on the strength of a SIBLING LEAF'S FUTURE WORK. The manifest also had NO row at all asserting the thing that actually broke ("demanded tolerance reaches OcctKernel::export()"), and its header dates all evidence to a pre-flight snapshot never re-checked after the leaves landed. Instance 2, the predecessor jcodemunch PRD: its live-serve bindings all route around the Rust client — `L-SERVE` binds a curl smoke, `L-CLIENT` a static decode of captured fixtures, `L-WIRE` a construction-site substitution — and the one binding that would have caught the real defect, `L-SMOKE`, names `scripts/smoke-jcodemunch-audit.sh` WHICH DOES NOT EXIST; what shipped instead is `#[ignore]`-gated AND graceful-skips on a bare TCP-connect probe. RULES THAT FOLLOW, for anyone authoring a manifest: (a) never mark a row PASS on a sibling leaf's future work — that is the phantom-completion vector in pure form; (b) never bind a row to a script or test that does not exist — verify the path; (c) a binding that exercises the seam from the OUTSIDE (curl, captured fixtures, a construction-site substitution) does not evidence that the PRODUCTION client works — bind to the production path or say the row is unevidenced; (d) beware bindings that graceful-skip, since a skip-erasing helper reads as PASS when the thing is broken. Also note the structural gap: NOTHING IN REIFY PARSES `*.capability-manifest.md` — only the `.yaml` sidecar's `delivered_check` rows are mechanically evaluated, and that happens downstream in dark-factory's merge queue, with `kind: manual` rows excluded. reify's own literature already names this: `docs/prds/prd-gate-executable-substrate-verification.md:19` — "it only converts free-text promises into tabulated promises that nothing executes".

When a task removes a legacy identifier/default from production code, the capability-manifest `expect: absent` grep is typically scoped to that crate's source path (e.g. `paths: ["crates/reify-audit/src"]`) and is therefore STRUCTURALLY BLIND to the same token surviving in docs, skills and test fixtures. Before declaring such a removal complete, run the absence grep REPO-WIDE (`git grep -n "<token>"` with no path filter) and route each surviving hit to whichever task owns that file — widening that task's `metadata.files` if the file is not already in its list. Two real instances on task 6108 (γ, jcodemunch identity removal): the in-crate live capstone `tests/jcodemunch_live.rs` still pinned the retired identity and broke deterministically (esc-6108-6, outside the `src`-scoped grep), and `.claude/skills/audit/references/cli-invocation.md` still advertised it as the default while the owning doc task μ (6117) listed only `SKILL.md` (esc-6108-7). members.text: In reify-compiler, a `trait` body compiled with NO conformer is not dimension-checked at all. Inside a bare trait, `constraint material.density > 1m` (mismatched dimensions) and even `constraint material.no_such_field > 0` (undefined field) both compile with ZERO diagnostics; the same expressions inside a `structure` correctly emit DiagnosticCode::DimensionMismatch. Consequence: any compile-level "assert_no_error_diagnostics" probe written against a bare trait is VACUOUS and passes regardless of the behaviour it claims to pin. To pin trait-body semantics, either restate the shape as a `structure`, or use the eval-level signal (check_source_with_stdlib + assert the injected constraint's reify_ir::Satisfaction on a conforming structure). Measured on task 6038; the eval-level trait pins live in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_engine/polymorphic_zero_trait_eval.rs.

In reify-compiler, a `trait` body compiled standalone (no conforming structure) emits NO dimension diagnostics: `constraint material.density > 1m` (Density vs Length), `let bad = mass + 1m` on a plain identifier, and even a reference to a wholly undefined member field all produce zero error diagnostics. The identical expressions inside a `structure` DO produce `DimensionMismatch`. Consequence: any test asserting the ABSENCE of a diagnostic (e.g. `assert_no_error_diagnostics` in polymorphic_zero_tests.rs) is VACUOUS if written against a bare trait body — it passes regardless of the behaviour under test. Write such probes as a `structure`, and pair them with a non-vacuity guard asserting that a deliberately-mismatched NON-ZERO literal still errors. Measured task 6038 at HEAD 5370e7a13f; see `member_access_mismatched_non_zero_still_errors` in crates/reify-compiler/tests/polymorphic_zero_tests.rs.

CORRECTION (task 6038 amendment pass, re-measured) to the reify "trait bodies are not dimension-checked" cluster — memories ddf80608-8462-41c7-99c5-0306c6059506, 06e35691-b09f-4d7e-bbdc-18bedc5fcba7 and eea5b075-42f6-4b7f-b417-a0e65ef7a133 state the trap correctly but give INCOMPLETE guidance ("write the probe as a `structure`" / "use the eval-level signal"), implying trait-body shapes are unreachable at compile level. They are not. THE VACUITY CONDITION IS "NO CONFORMER", NOT "TRAIT BODY": `trait T { param material : Material  constraint material.density > 1m }` alone yields ZERO diagnostics, but adding `structure Widget : T { param material : Material = Material(...) }` makes the SAME trait-body expression emit DiagnosticCode::DimensionMismatch. So the preferred fix is ADD A CONFORMER — it keeps the probe faithful to the stdlib site being pinned — rather than restating the shape as a structure. (Memory 10c6eb04-d6ce-4e28-9928-961ecc100593 from task/6143 already had this right.) Two corollaries: (a) the dimensioned-Scalar-vs-Int arm (`density > 1`) errors with `code: None`, so assert on the message there, not on a DiagnosticCode; (b) reify_test_support::check_source_with_stdlib asserts a clean compile before evaluating, so eval-level pins PRESUPPOSE the compile signal and never substitute for it — use eval only for the genuinely runtime Satisfied-vs-Violated discrimination.
