members.text: Shared main-checkout commit discipline (learned 2026-07-02): /home/leo/src/dark-factory's main working tree is used CONCURRENTLY by multiple live interactive sessions plus the orchestrator merge queue, so plain commits race. Observed failure shapes, all benign but confusing: (a) `fatal: cannot lock ref 'HEAD': is at X but expected Y` = another actor advanced main between your pre-commit hook and the ref write — just retry; (b) another session's mixed `git reset HEAD~1` (their commit-rework flow) UNSTAGES your `git add` mid-flight, so your retry says "nothing added to commit" and your file is back to untracked — re-add and retry; (c) the pre-commit hook runs pyright over 3 projects (~2 min) even for docs-only commits, which widens the race window substantially. Discipline: ALWAYS commit path-scoped — `git add <file> && git commit <file> ...` — which both survives concurrent index resets gracefully and never sweeps another session's staged WIP into your commit (found plans/interactive-warm-worktree-prd.md staged by a sibling session; a bare `git commit` would have stolen it). Also: the Bash tool flattens embedded newlines in `git commit -m "multi-line"` (not just heredocs) — commit message paragraphs collapse to one line; use `git commit -F <msgfile>` when the message matters.

ADDITIONAL SYMPTOM under NEWLINE FLATTENING (mode a) of git-commit-message-mangling: if the flattened heredoc body contains a bare `>` following a word (e.g. prose like "Memory Usage > When to write memory" inside a `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` message), the collapsed single-line command reinterprets that `>` as a live shell redirection operator once outside real heredoc protection. Observed on task 4786: this created a stray empty file named after the word right after the `>` (literally a file named `When` appeared in the repo root), and the commit aborted with "here-document at line 1 delimited by end-of-file (wanted `EOF')" plus "No such file or directory" on the following line (the Co-Authored-By `<noreply@...>` line was then misparsed as an input redirect once the heredoc/eval structure broke down). The commit itself aborted cleanly with no garbled content landed — but the stray redirection-target file is left behind as untracked debris in the repo root and must be manually `rm`'d before the next `git add`. Confirms the existing fix in this topic cluster: write the message to a file and use `git commit -F <file>`, which sidesteps this `>`-triggered variant entirely (not just the backtick/newline variants already recorded here).

In this harness, passing a multi-line git commit message via `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` can silently mangle: bash reports "unterminated here-document" / "delimited by end-of-file", the heredoc body leaks as separate `cat: <word>: No such file or directory` errors, and the commit still succeeds but with a garbled one-line message (verify with `git log -1 --format='%B'`). Workaround: write the commit message to a temp file with the Write tool and commit with `git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt` (or `--amend -F` if the garbled commit was just created and nothing depends on it yet) instead of a `-m "$(cat <<EOF ...)"` heredoc.

git-commit-message-mangling peer (task 5870, 2026-09-25): mode (a) newline flattening is INTERMITTENT for a plain double-quoted multi-line `git commit -q -m "subj

body

Co-Authored-By: ..."`. In one session, 2 of 4 such commits kept their layout and 2 SUCCEEDED as a single 700-900-char subject line with the trailer inside it. The two that flattened had `git status --short &&` in the same chain; the cause was not diagnosed. DETECT after every commit: `command git log -1 --format=%B HEAD | wc -l` (2 means flattened). REPAIR without `rebase -i`: write each message to /tmp with a plain heredoc, then `new=$(git commit-tree "<old>^{tree}" -p <parent> -F msg)` for each flattened commit in order (chain -p through the new SHAs). Then run `git reset --soft <newest>`, confirm `git diff --stat <old-tip> HEAD` is empty, and re-call mark_step_done with the new SHAs.

Harness quirk confirmed 2026-07-12 (extends the known heredoc-flattening issue): the Bash tool's eval flattens ALL multi-line constructs, not just heredocs — a multi-line `for … do … done` loop collapses to one line and errors with "syntax error near unexpected token `do`". Also observed: a bare `cd <dir>` on its own line got joined with the next command ("cd: too many arguments"). RELIABLE workaround: write the whole sequence to a script file (scratchpad) and run `bash /path/to/script.sh`.

CORRECTED 2026-08-02 per esc-3249-1's resolution (canonical account: Mem0 8e09d0ea-9def-43e1-8d56-db654b7969af). The original claim that `git commit -F <file>` requires the message file to be INSIDE the repo tree was FALSE — `-F <file>` accepts any readable path regardless of location. The real constraint is ARGUMENT ORDER: `-F <file>` must appear BEFORE the `--` pathspec separator, or git parses the value as a pathspec and, if it resolves outside the repo, fails with `fatal: <path>: is outside repository at '<repo>'` — the error previously misattributed to file location. Also corrected: the claim that a docs-only commit still triggers the full pre-commit hook (~40s pyright) is stale — since task 2551, hooks/project-checks path-filters pyright to packages with staged .py changes, so a docs-only commit prints "pre-commit: pyright skipped (no Python changes)" and finishes in seconds. The working pattern `cp msg.txt <repo>/.commit-msg.txt; git commit --only -F .commit-msg.txt -- <paths>; rm .commit-msg.txt` still succeeds, but the in-repo-copy step is unnecessary cargo-cult, not a requirement — putting `-F <file>` before `--` is what actually matters.

Tooling gotcha (confirmed 2026-05-30, cost real time): the Claude Code Bash tool wraps commands in a zsh `eval '...'` that COLLAPSES NEWLINES TO SPACES. So `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` arrives as one line — the heredoc never terminates, giving `syntax error near unexpected token '('` (exit 127) or a junk message capturing literal EOF/backticks. FIX: write the message to a file with the Write tool, then `git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt` (or `--amend -F`). Never use multi-line `$(...)` in a single Bash call.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20, Stage 1 consolidation]: this entry's original final sentence claimed docs-only commits currently need `--no-verify` because the repo-wide pre-commit hook blocks all commits on pre-existing bare-MagicMock debt in unrelated test files. That claim is stale and now actively wrong: mem0 239885dc-6fb1-474e-9e6f-055bb0c16d9d (2026-07-08) and d40bfdb0-18b5-48af-aeba-4c790d9b810e (2026-07-30) both record that hooks/pre-commit explicitly FORBIDS `--no-verify` and silently strips `.task/` from staging regardless of branch, with the project-checks/ruff+pyright arm running only on main. Do not use `--no-verify` to route around this hook. For a slow-pyright-timeout commit, background/detach the commit instead (see mem0 56c00b29-0a18-4a74-ab11-149eaae0c91e / 39b84e1d-0849-46f9-a8d5-dfbae412ec80); for a hook that silently doesn't seem to run at all, see mem0 c1657903-afe2-4f3d-b733-39ddc3cf9ca4 (core.hooksPath duplicate-key gotcha).

claim: Because the Bash tool may flatten multiline commands, use script or message files instead of multiline inline shell constructs, and verify commit messages after committing.

members.text: The `scripts/` tree (incl. scripts/legibility/) is NOT in the project's `[tool.pyright]` include/extraPaths in pyproject.toml — pyright only covers `conftest.py` plus the package `src/` dirs. So running `uv run pyright scripts/legibility/foo.py` in isolation surfaces spurious import-resolution errors (e.g. `Import "httpx" could not be resolved`, `"load_config" is not a known attribute of module "config"` from the flat `import config`) that the real per-package pre-commit gate (hooks/project-checks) never checks. When verifying a scripts/ change, rely on the pytest suite + `ruff check`; treat isolated-pyright import errors as environment artifacts, not real defects (confirm they pre-exist at the base commit before chasing them).

scripts/tests/ (e.g. scripts/legibility/*.py) is verified via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/...` — this scopes execution to shared/pyproject.toml's own dependency set (pydantic, pydantic-settings, aiosqlite, pyyaml, python-dotenv only). Packages like jsonschema, ruamel.yaml, etc. that are only transitive deps of other workspace members (fused-memory, orchestrator, escalation per their uv.lock) are NOT importable there, even though they may appear available in an ambient/full-workspace venv. When writing a scripts/ module, verify package availability against `uv run --project shared python -c "import X"`, not the interactive dev shell's venv. This convention is load-bearing: see `_FALLBACK_UV_PROJECT = 'shared'` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py and the comment in shared/pyproject.toml (task 2070).

In scripts/legibility/, a bare sibling `import config` (e.g. in census.py) resolves correctly at real runtime (pytest via conftest.py's sys.path insert, and `python scripts/legibility/census.py` via Python's own script-dir-as-sys.path[0]) but is a FALSE POSITIVE under `pyright scripts/legibility/<file>.py` run from the repo root: pyright picks up the unrelated top-level `<repo-root>/config/` directory (an implicit PEP 420 namespace package holding usage-accounts.yaml) instead of scripts/legibility/config.py, producing a spurious "X is not a known attribute of module config" error. Harmless — the root pyproject.toml's `[tool.pyright] include = ["conftest.py"]` doesn't cover scripts/ at all, so this never gates a real merge; verify actual behavior via `python scripts/legibility/<file>.py` directly rather than trusting a standalone pyright run.

Tests under the repo-root `tests/scripts/` directory run via `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/` (scripts/orchestrator.yaml), so they can only import what `shared/pyproject.toml` declares — `escalation`, `dashboard`, and `fused_memory` are NOT importable there. When a scripts/ test needs a first-party package, put that test in a subproject whose pyproject already declares it (e.g. `dashboard/tests/` can import `escalation`, since dashboard/pyproject.toml has `escalation = { workspace = true }`) and load the hyphenated script by absolute path with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, rather than adding a test-only dependency to shared.

Repo-root test files under tests/scripts/ (e.g. tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_watchdog.py) are not owned by any subproject's own [tool.pyright] config, so the verify fallback path type-checks them file-scoped using the ROOT pyproject.toml's [tool.pyright] (extraPaths = the various <subproject>/src dirs only). That root-scoped pyright run has no visibility into conftest.py-driven sys.path mutations (e.g. tests/scripts/conftest.py inserting scripts/ onto sys.path so `import drain_check` resolves at pytest runtime) and reports a spurious reportMissingImports. The established fix in this codebase is an inline `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` on the import line (see tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_watchdog.py:18's `import pytest` for the pre-existing precedent) rather than restructuring the import -- confirm the affected test still passes at runtime before suppressing.

In orchestrator/tests/, a deferred `from dashboard.data.orchestrator import read_task_artifacts` (or any cross-subproject import not among orchestrator/shared/escalation) raises ModuleNotFoundError/reportMissingImports even though the root conftest.py wires all workspace subprojects' src/ onto sys.path. Cause: verify.py runs `uv run --project orchestrator pytest orchestrator/tests/...`, which makes pytest resolve rootdir/confcutdir to orchestrator/ (via orchestrator/pyproject.toml's [tool.pytest.ini_options]) — pytest never ascends above confcutdir to load the repo-root conftest.py, and orchestrator/tests/conftest.py only sys.path-inserts orchestrator/shared/escalation src dirs, not dashboard's. Fix pattern (used in test_lane_lifecycle_integration.py, task 2260): add a module-local sys.path.insert for the needed subproject's src/ directly in the test file (mirroring conftest.py's own idiom but scoped to that file), plus a `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` comment on the import line (pyright doesn't execute runtime sys.path mutations, and orchestrator/pyproject.toml's [tool.pyright] extraPaths also omits dashboard/src). This same `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` convention for cross-subproject deferred test imports is already established in dashboard/tests/test_costs_data.py and escalation/tests/test_*.py.

claim: For scripts and cross-subproject tests, verify imports in the owning project’s runtime and dependency scope; treat isolated pyright import errors caused by missing path context as artifacts, not defects.
