In reify-eval, `Engine::default_kernel_name.is_none()` is an exact test for exactly one thing: "this ENGINE INSTANCE holds no geometry kernel". `default_kernel_name` is a field on the Engine INSTANCE (`crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs:455`), not a property of the linked binary.

Constructor mechanism (unchanged and still correct): `Engine::with_prelude` sets `default_kernel_name = geometry_kernel.map(...)`, so a `None` kernel yields `None` (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_admin.rs:231-236`); `with_registered_kernel{,s}` derive it from `pick_lexmin_brep_kernel`, whose helper `pick_lexmin_brep_kernel_in` (`crates/reify-eval/src/kernel_registry.rs:211-219`) ends in `.or_else(|| registered.values().next())` and therefore returns `None` if and only if the static inventory registry is empty.

CORRECTED 2026-09-08 (curator sitting; verified against reify main @ efbc0932bd). This entry previously framed the predicate as an EXACT test for "this BINARY registered no geometry kernel at all (i.e. stub mode)". That binary-level reading is FALSIFIED, and it fails in BOTH directions:
- It can never be TRUE on a shipped binary. `crates/reify-kernel-manifold/src/register.rs:62-69` emits its `KernelRegistration` via `inventory::submit!` with NO `#[cfg]` gate, and `crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:20`'s `extern crate reify_kernel_manifold as _;` is likewise unconditional, so the "manifold" key is always present in a shipped CLI's registry, the empty-inventory branch is unreachable, and even a stub (no-OCCT) build gets `Some("manifold")` — a Mesh-only kernel. (Refinement first recorded 2026-08-26 from mem0 9d0b91b6-aed7-4b3e-a63c-9e2c3a60b7f3; now promoted from caveat to correction.)
- It is routinely TRUE on a fully kernel-equipped binary. `Engine::new(checker, None)` is PRODUCTION CLI code (`crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:947, 1100, 1983, 2127, 2287`) and is the shape behind the test helper `make_simple_engine` (`crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs:106-108`). Those instances have an empty kernel map and `default_kernel_name == None` on a fully OCCT-equipped build.

Read it therefore ONLY as an instance guard — which is what its legitimate call sites do, e.g. `measure_dfm_rules`'s "C1 guard: no default kernel → nothing to measure" (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_constraints.rs:1603-1606`), correct precisely because it asks about the instance. To ask instead "can this build produce or tessellate a BRep", the honest predicate is CAPABILITY, not presence: `Engine::has_repr_capable_kernel()` (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_constraints.rs:894`; the discriminator `unmeasured_reason` uses at :812), i.e. `CapabilityDescriptor::supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep)` read off the `KernelRegistration`. Conflating the two produces user-facing diagnostics that falsely tell an OCCT-enabled user to rebuild with OCCT.

The normative form of this rule, and the instance-vs-linked-binary distinction spelled out, live in the preferences_and_norms peer under topic `reify-engine-default-kernel-name-predicate`.

In reify-eval, `Engine::default_kernel_name.is_none()` can be read as "this BINARY has no geometry kernel" — not merely "this engine instance has none" — but only on code paths reached via constraint dispatch. `Engine::eval()` never calls `dispatch_constraints` (only `check()`, `build()`, `check_snapshot`, `tessellate_snapshot`, `build_snapshot` do), so the CLI's deliberately kernel-free eval engines (`cmd_eval` plain branch, `cmd_bom`, `cmd_provenance`, all `Engine::new(checker, None)`) cannot reach constraint code. Every surface that both dispatches constraints and can carry a RepresentationWithin builds its engine with `Engine::with_registered_kernel` (`cmd_check`'s assertion branch, `cmd_build`, the GUI session), which yields `Some(..)` iff the binary was compiled with a kernel. This is what makes kernel-absence a safe discriminator for user-facing diagnostics that recommend building with OCCT.

Reify, capability direction of the synthetic-kernel-key gotcha (task 6169, cost two review cycles): you cannot answer "does THIS engine hold a BRep-capable kernel?" by looking the engine's own `geometry_kernels` names up in the static inventory registry. Because `Engine::with_registered_kernel` (the constructor every production constraint-dispatching surface uses — reify-cli main.rs:604/999/1564, gui EngineSession) files its pick under the synthetic `Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME`, that lookup MISSES on every shipped binary and silently degrades to whatever the unregistered-kernel default is (a benefit-of-the-doubt `true` in 6169's case), making any arm gated on the answer dead code on exactly the surfaces it was written for. The fix shape that works: record the answer at CONSTRUCTION, where the `KernelRegistration` is still in hand (`(reg.descriptor)().supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep)` stored into an `Option<bool>` field), and keep the registry scan only as a fallback for `Engine::new(_, Some(stub))` test seams. Note the divergence is invisible on an OCCT build — both answers coincide — so the gate that makes it observable everywhere is a structural pin asserting the engine's own kernel names are ABSENT from the registry, not a behavioural test.

[CORRECTED 2026-08-26]: A prior append to this entry claimed "CONFIRMED 2026-08-26: task 6169 landed this fix as `Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>` (recorded at construction time from the `KernelRegistration`)." That claim was FALSE, verified this stage: a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `repr_capable_kernel` across the reify repo returns zero matches (the field does not exist in the codebase), and task 6169's live status is `pending`, not `done` — no fix has landed. Treat this gotcha as UNRESOLVED. Do not re-assert completion until task 6169 reaches status=done AND the field is confirmed present in the codebase via grep. This entry previously absorbed a same-day near-duplicate note (mem0 3ae219c3, deleted, consolidated here) that restated the same gotcha with less detail.

[RESOLVED 2026-09-09]: Both conditions the 2026-08-26 correction set are now MET, each re-verified first-hand this sitting rather than taken from another record. (1) Task 6169's live status is `done`, with `done_provenance.kind = merged`. (2) The field EXISTS: `Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>` is declared in crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs, and the wiring matches the fix shape prescribed above exactly. It is initialised to `None` in the plain constructor in `engine_admin.rs` — whose own comment says the caller-supplied-kernel seam "leaves it None and gets the benefit-of-the-doubt scan" — and overwritten with `Some(..)` by BOTH inventory-driven constructors in that same file: the single-pick path stores `picked.is_some_and(|reg| (reg.descriptor)().supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep))` right after `with_prelude`, and the multi-kernel path stores the `any(..)` of the same descriptor predicate across the registry. It is consumed by `Engine::has_repr_capable_kernel` in `engine_constraints.rs`, which returns the construction-recorded answer when present and falls back to the registry scan only when it is `None`; `engine_build.rs` destructures the field explicitly so a later field addition cannot silently skip it, and the structural pin lives in crates/reify-eval/tests/representation_within_assertion.rs. The gotcha in the body above is therefore RESOLVED on main — keep it as the design precedent for the synthetic-key class (record the answer where the registration is still in hand), not as a live defect. Cite by SYMBOL (`Engine::repr_capable_kernel`, `Engine::has_repr_capable_kernel`), never by line number: this entry's own `main.rs:604/999/1564` anchors are the kind that rot.

claim: Distinguish an engine instance’s default-kernel state from its BRep capability; determine capability from the registered kernel’s descriptor, recorded at construction.

members.text: The copy-list-drift preflight for verify.sh sandbox meta-tests (tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh, test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh) is factored into a shared helper tests/infra/copy_list_preflight_lib.sh. Any new `--print-plan` sandbox fixture that cp's a subset of scripts/ must, after its cp block and before `git init`, call: `assert_source_closure_copied "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$dir/scripts" verify.sh || exit 1`. It walks verify.sh's FULL transitive `source`/`.` closure (not just direct sources) and fails loudly with "copy-list drift: missing <lib>". Wiring is proven behaviorally (not source-grep) via the fault-injection seam REIFY_COPY_LIST_PREFLIGHT_INJECT_PHANTOM (inert by default). Pure-variable-indirection libs like lib_clock_stop.sh (`source "$var"`) are a documented parser exclusion and stay hand-copied.

Writing a synthetic scripts/verify.sh fixture: a bare `cp scripts/verify.sh $tmp/verify.sh` is READABLE but NOT RUNNABLE. verify.sh resolves its libs relative to its own directory, so a lone copy hard-fails immediately with "verify.sh: ERROR — scripts/occt-scope-lib.sh not found next to verify.sh" (measured: exit 1 in 0.028s, empty stdout). That is fine for a test that only greps the copy's source text, but any test that actually EXECUTES it (e.g. --print-plan) must materialize $dir/scripts/ with the whole sibling set plus $dir/.config/nextest.toml. Do NOT hand-roll the file list and do NOT trim it to verify.sh's seven DIRECT `source` lines — several entries are transitive under an already-copied lib. The maintained list lives in tests/infra/test_verify_throughput.sh's make_branch_fixture, and its companion guard is assert_source_closure_copied from tests/infra/copy_list_preflight_lib.sh, which turns a future source-line addition into a precise "copy-list drift: missing <lib>" error instead of an opaque downstream failure. Reuse both together rather than forking a second copy that can drift. Add scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt on top if the fixture needs select_infra_tests(): verify.sh READS it without sourcing it, so the source-closure preflight cannot discover it.

In reify, tests/infra/test_verify_throughput.sh and test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh auto-discover every `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/..."` lib line in their fixture copy of scripts/verify.sh and HARD-FAIL if that lib was not copied into the throwaway repo. So adding a new sourced *-lib.sh to verify.sh forces updating those fixtures' copy lists. Reading a non-sourced .txt config inline (guarded by `[ -f ]`, degrading to empty when absent) avoids this entirely and is the preferred pattern for new verify.sh config data.

Adding any `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/<lib>.sh"` line to scripts/verify.sh reds SIX infra suites at once with `copy-list drift: missing <lib> (transitive source closure of verify.sh)`: test_verify_scope.sh (2 cp-sites), test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired.sh (2), test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_throughput.sh, test_verify_pipeline_guard.sh, test_verify_release_delta_skip.sh. Each builds a throwaway --print-plan fixture by cp-ing verify.sh's lib closure and calls assert_source_closure_copied (tests/infra/copy_list_preflight_lib.sh); the fix is one `cp "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/<lib>.sh" "$dir/scripts/<lib>.sh"` per cp-site, and the guard's own error prints the exact command. Budget those 6 files into the plan's scope BEFORE writing the source line. Note copy_list_preflight_lib.sh's parser only captures double-quoted literal `/<name>.sh"` paths, so sourcing via a bare variable or a child `bash -c` silently evades the guard — that is evasion, not a fix.

verify.sh sources sibling lib scripts (occt-scope-lib.sh, release-scope-lib.sh, and now affected-crates-lib.sh) and HARD-FAILS with "ERROR — scripts/<lib> not found next to verify.sh" if any is missing in $SCRIPT_DIR, aborting before it prints a plan. Every infra test that builds a verify.sh fixture via a make_fixture/make_branch_fixture helper (tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh AND tests/infra/test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh) must `cp` ALL of these sibling scripts into the fixture's scripts/ dir. So when you extract a new required lib from verify.sh, you must update the cp list in EVERY such fixture, not just one — otherwise the un-updated test goes red. Task 4058 hit this: it added affected-crates-lib.sh to test_verify_scope.sh's two fixtures (lines 47 & 205) but missed test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh's make_fixture, leaving it red on main (esc-3974-200).

Copy-list drift datapoint (task 8685, 2026-10-16): a TRANSITIVE new source line also triggers the drift class. Making scripts/lib_slot_acquire.sh source scripts/lib_event_log.sh (verify.sh -> lib_test_semaphore.sh -> lib_slot_acquire.sh -> lib_event_log.sh) required a cp line in 8 tests/infra files, 9 cp-sites: test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired.sh, test_verify_pipeline_guard.sh, test_run_all_tiering.sh, test_scope_boundary.sh, test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh, test_verify_release_delta_skip.sh, test_verify_scope.sh (2 sites), test_verify_throughput.sh. Discovery recipe that worked: grep tests/infra for files that already cp lib_slot_acquire.sh or lib_clock_stop.sh into a fixture. Whole-tree copiers (cp -R scripts, Python copytree) self-heal. Use a double-quoted literal `source "$dir/lib_x.sh"` path so copy_list_preflight_lib.sh's closure parser sees the new lib.

claim: When changing verify.sh’s sourced library closure, update every sandbox fixture’s copied closure and guard it with the shared preflight to prevent copy-list drift.

members.text: When adding a second ref arm to hooks/reference-transaction, do NOT copy the refs/heads/main arm's zero-OLD housekeeping filter (`[ -z "${_old//0/}" ] && continue`, hooks/reference-transaction:79). Measured on git 2.43.0: `git stash push` presents old=0000000000... on refs/stash even when the stack is already NON-empty (a 2nd push onto a 1-entry stack logged old=0000000 new=c213482). Copying that filter into a refs/stash arm makes the guard silently never fire while still logging as installed — a dead instrument that reads as protection. The zero-OLD filter is correct ONLY for refs/heads/main, where an all-zero old genuinely means pack-refs/gc ref creation.

git's reference-transaction hook sees only SOME refs/stash writes: `git stash push` fires it in the 'prepared' state (and refusing there aborts with rc 128 while leaving the working tree AND the stash stack untouched), but `git stash drop`/`pop` of a non-last entry fire NO hook at all because git rewrites the stash reflog rather than the ref -- only a last-entry drop and `git stash clear` reach a ref-deletion transaction. Two further gotchas: `git stash push` always reports old=0000000 on refs/stash even when the stack is non-empty (so a zero-OLD "housekeeping" filter silently disables any refs/stash guard), and `git stash create`/`git stash apply <ref>` open no refs/stash transaction at all. Verified on git 2.43.0 including from a linked worktree, where refs/stash is shared with the main checkout.

git's reference-transaction hook can only guard the PUSH direction of refs/stash, never pop/drop. Measured on git 2.43.0 in throwaway repos (task 5981): `git stash push` fires the hook on ref=refs/stash in both "prepared" and "committed", and exiting non-zero in "prepared" aborts it with rc 128 while PRESERVING the working tree and leaving the stash stack unchanged. But `git stash pop` and `git stash drop` of a NON-LAST entry fire NO reference-transaction hook at all (git rewrites the stash reflog instead of the ref); only a last-entry drop, a last-entry pop's trailing drop, and `git stash clear` reach a ref DELETION transaction — and in the pop case the working-tree apply PRECEDES the deletion, so refusing it cannot prevent WIP injection. `git stash create` and `git stash apply <ref>` never touch refs/stash at all, so a private-ref park path (dark-factory's refs/dark-factory/merge-park) keeps working with such a guard armed.

claim: A refs/stash reference-transaction hook is not a complete stash guard: it can block pushes, but zero-OLD filtering disables it and most pop/drop paths bypass it.

members.text: Premise-verification gotcha for orchestrator-dispatched worktrees: a run's worktree can be pinned at a stale base (task 2324's run-a4336a9a sat in detached HEAD at an April commit that was a strict ANCESTOR of an August main — 14 crates present vs 33 on main). Grepping only the worktree tree then makes already-landed symbols look missing and inverts the premise check, tempting a from-scratch plan that duplicates landed code. Always cross-check a "missing" file/symbol against the main ref with `git grep -l <sym> main` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD main` before concluding a premise fails. Note `git log --all -S<sym>` pickaxe is too slow here (times out at 2 min); `git grep` on the ref is fast.

PEER (direction (e)) of topic `worktree-stale-base-premise-verification` — the FRESH-BASE direction, the mirror image of (a). In (a) the base is stale so already-landed symbols falsely read as MISSING. Here the base is EXACTLY current main and the symbols are genuinely missing, because the TASK WAS AUTHORED AGAINST A SIBLING TASK BRANCH'S TIP instead of against main.

MEASURED (task 5193, architect, 2026-09-08). Task 5193 asked to fix a residual TOCTOU in `reap_dead_leases` in fused-memory/scripts/cleanup_test_collections.py, quoting the function body verbatim. Its worktree base was 29737babc5 = main tip exactly (`git rev-list --count main..task/5193` = 0 — NOT stale, so every (a) remedy returns "base is fine" and tempts you to trust the premise). But a tree-wide `git grep 'def (hold_lease|live_leases|reap_dead_leases|lease_dir|_is_held|_still_linked)' main -- '*.py'` returned ZERO matches; the worktree's copy of that script was 125 lines with no flock code, and its test file had zero occurrences of 'lease'. All 14 lease functions existed only on branch task/4775 (tip 5b2e95020d, task status `pending`, not an ancestor of main).

THE TELLS, in the task record itself — check these BEFORE grepping, they are cheaper:
  * the description cites a BRANCH TIP SHA rather than a main sha ("measured against task/4775's tip (5b2e95020d)", "amendment 21c1985469"). A premise measured against a branch tip is only true on that branch.
  * `metadata.spawn_context` = 'steward-sweepup' (or agent-followup) with `metadata.spawned_from` naming a task that is NOT `done`. A steward filing a residual-defect follow-up measures it where it found it — on the sibling's worktree — and there is nothing in the filing path that rebases the premise onto main.
  * `dependencies: []` despite `spawned_from` naming that sibling. The follow-up filing path does NOT register the dependency, so the scheduler dispatched 5193 with nothing gating it. Do not read an empty dependencies array as evidence the prerequisite has landed.

THE EXIT: `report_blocking_dependency(depends_on_task_id=<spawned_from>)`, not `report_unactionable_task` (the spec is fine, its base just has not landed) and not a from-scratch plan. Writing the plan anyway would have had the implementer author a THIRD independent copy of the ~350-line lease machinery, after task/4775's and task/4502's, colliding textually with whichever landed first.

COMPOUNDING WRINKLE worth checking: the named remedy may already exist on ANOTHER branch. Here the fix was commit c4ba4c5f52 on task/4502, and a pending L1 (esc-4502-7) was deciding whether 4502's duplicate copy or 4775's original would land — under one outcome task 5193 becomes already-done rather than actionable. When the missing-premise sibling is itself contested, say so in the blocking-dependency reason so the re-queue re-checks instead of blindly re-planning.

PEER of topic `worktree-stale-base-premise-verification`, direction (a) STALE BASE — the VERIFY/DEBUG-time variant, and the one-command diagnostic that settles it in seconds.

SHAPE. A task branch's verify goes red on a test the branch never touched, because the base predates a fix main already landed. Sibling peer 001acf5d records this for the scripts/ LINT gate (task 3614); this peer records it for a repo-wide META-TEST, where the mechanism is nastier: the test's verdict depends on the whole repo's content, not on the changed files, so "my diff doesn't touch that file" feels like a weak argument and agents talk themselves into hand-fixing it.

MEASURED (task 4286, debugger, 2026-09-09). `scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py::test_every_enumeration_site_is_pinned` failed: `docs/code-quality.md` restates 4+ invariant slugs but is not in PINNED_SITES. The branch's diff was 4 .py files, no markdown. merge-base 3470f61ae2 was 99 commits behind main; main (bf23ca33dd) ALREADY registered the file. Fix commit: d2459bd9a7 "fix(5230): register docs/code-quality.md in PINNED_SITES (fix-forward RED main)", landed 2026-09-08, i.e. the RED had been a genuine main-health event that main repaired forward.

THE DIAGNOSTIC, in order — each cheap, and the second one usually ends the investigation:
1. `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` — is the failing artifact even in your diff?
2. `git log --oneline $(git merge-base HEAD main)..main -- <failing-file>` — the killer. It lists exactly the main-side commits your base is missing FOR THAT FILE. A subject line containing "fix-forward", "RED main", or the test's own name is a confession; read the commit message, which often states which test it turned green.
3. `git show main:<path>` to confirm the repaired content, and `git rev-list --count <merge-base>..main` for the staleness magnitude.

DO NOT HAND-PORT THE FIX, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong. The upstream fix is often one step of a multi-commit chain, so the obvious-looking single commit is not self-contained. Here d2459bd9a7 (8 insertions — irresistibly cherry-pickable) only ADDS the registry entry; the pair-wise assertion that entry advertises lands separately in 1964555b6d (77 lines). Cherry-picking d2459bd9a7 alone would have registered a site with no actual pin — silencing the guard while hollowing it out, a strictly worse state than the red. Before cherry-picking anything, run `git log --oneline <merge-base>..main -- <file>` and look at how many commits the fix spans.

CORRECT EXIT: escalate for a BASE REFRESH (merge/rebase main), which brings the chain in as a coherent unit, and say so with the fix commit named. `git merge-tree --write-tree main <branch>` (peer ab747acb) prices the refresh without touching the tree.

COROLLARY for the same investigation: separate the deterministic red from the flakes before escalating. Two sibling failures in that run (`test_restart_all_orchestrators.py`, wall-clock bash-subprocess tests with a 15s cap) passed on isolated re-run — they had failed on an xdist worker while the sibling orchestrator suite burned 3438s of CPU. A verify attempt that fans out across two module prefixes is a load event, so timing-sensitive tests failing there are load flakes until an isolated re-run says otherwise.

A worktree based at the `chore(tasks): auto-commit after set_task_status(<id>=in-progress)` commit does NOT guarantee the task's declared dependencies have merged — the orchestrator stamps in-progress at dispatch, and a task can be re-dispatched (or rescoped via escalation) hours later after deps land. Before planning, verify each dep's landing commit with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <dep_merge_sha> HEAD`; the dep merge commit is in `metadata.done_provenance.commit` from `get_task`. Observed on reify task 2573 (base 4e12e7a06d @ 2026-04-28 20:07) whose dep 2590 landed at 0ea924cc4e @ 2026-04-29 01:54 — five hours later.

Architect premise-verification must check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-commit> main`, NOT just read the file in its own worktree. Task 2778's worktree was based on a HEAD 9 days stale (5d07e3818b) that predated the fix, so the stale "Interim reality: hand-stamp" blockquote still appeared locally in skills/prd/references/decompose-mode.md even though it had been removed on main (02ee855dee, merged via 492f8bda2b "Merge task/2778 into main"). Reading the worktree file falsely CONFIRMS a stale premise and leads to re-planning already-landed work. Contradicts the older assumption that a new worktree's HEAD equals main — verify with `git rev-parse HEAD` vs `git rev-parse main` and inspect `git show main:<path>` / `git grep <token> main` before trusting local contents.

An architect worktree can be seeded on a base that PREDATES its own task's merge, making already-landed work read as missing. Observed on task 4370: worktree HEAD=264ee8cd20 carried task/5273 content and did NOT contain the task's own merge (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 1d886f3f45 HEAD` => NO), while main=db3caf593c DID. Verify premises with `git ls-tree`/`git grep` against the literal `main` ref, never against the worktree HEAD or working tree; a HEAD-relative probe would have falsely justified re-implementing a done task.

claim: Before acting on a task premise, verify its code and dependencies against the relevant landed ref—not the worktree—since stale or sibling-based snapshots can make done work look missing.

members.text: gmsh 4.15.2 deadlocks inside gmshModelMeshGenerate(3) when a PostView background mesh-size field is evaluated from many mesher threads. The threshold is fixture-dependent, so a single measurement does not generalise: on a clean process meshing a unit cube, General.NumThreads=8 completes in ~4s while 32 hangs indefinitely; in tests/mesher_poison_recovery.rs, whose gmsh has already been through a finalize/initialize recovery cycle, 8 already hangs. It is a true block, not slowness (CPU time frozen, all threads in futex_do_wait), and Mesh.MaxNumThreads3D=1 does not avoid it. reify's fix (task #7447) pins General.NumThreads=1 unconditionally in refine_volume_with_size_field. Consequence for test authors: a regression guard for this must ask for a thread count measured to hang ON ITS OWN FIXTURE — copying a count that hangs a different binary silently yields a test that is green on both sides of the fix.

ROOT CAUSE of the gmsh 4.15.2 PostView background-field deadlock (task #7706, supersedes the 'finalize/initialize cycle' hypothesis): gmsh 4.15.2's PViewData::searchScalar/Vector/Tensor (src/post/PViewData.cpp ~L323-415) build the view's OctreePost LAZILY behind an orphaned `#pragma omp barrier` + `#pragma omp single`. 1D/2D meshing run `#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic)` over curves/surfaces (Generator.cpp ~L431/L590), so when General.NumThreads exceeds the number of classified curves, idle threads sit at the loop-end barrier while working threads hit the octree barrier -> futex deadlock. Measured with a Python repro of refine_volume_with_size_field's FFI sequence: unit cube (14 curves after classify_surfaces PI/12) passes at 14 threads and hangs at 15; open triangle (3 curves) passes at 3 and hangs at 4. That is the whole 'fixture-dependent threshold'. FIX (measured 0 hangs in 48 runs at 2..32 threads, both fixtures): call gmshViewProbe once on the calling thread after view_add_list_data and before mesh_generate. Outside a parallel region the orphaned barrier/single bind to a team of one, so the octree gets built single-threaded; `_octree` is only deleted in the PViewData destructor. Upstream master (gmsh-git snapshot 2026-09-29, versioned 5.0.0) replaced it with `_getOctree()` under `#pragma omp critical(PViewDataOctree)`. No release past 4.15.2 existed on PyPI or conda-forge on 2026-10-01.

ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED (task #7706 architect, 2026-09-29, libgmsh 4.15.2 from /opt/reify-deps) for the PostView background-field deadlock: gmsh's PViewData::searchScalar (src/post/PViewData.cpp ~L326) builds its search octree lazily as `if(!_octree){ #pragma omp barrier / #pragma omp single { _octree = new OctreePost(this); } }`. That is a CONDITIONAL OpenMP barrier, so when the FIRST field evaluation lands inside a parallel region, the team's barriers mismatch. gdb thread dump of a hung 32-thread run: 14 threads in gomp_team_barrier_wait_end under PViewData::searchScalarClosest <- PostViewField::operator() <- BGM_MeshSize <- Mesh1D._omp_fn.0, and 18 threads in gomp_team_barrier_wait_final. It fires in the parallel 1D curve stage, which is why Mesh.MaxNumThreads3D=1 never helped. WORKAROUND, measured: one serial gmshViewProbe on the view after gmshViewAddListData builds `_octree` outside any parallel region (view::probe calls data->searchScalarClosest), and `_octree` is only freed in the PViewData destructor, so the barrier is never reached again. Python A/B against the same libgmsh, unit cube, "SS" Kuhn-lattice field: at 32 threads without the probe, 3/3 runs hung; with it, 41/41 meshes completed (at 3, 8, 16 and 32 threads). No newer gmsh release exists: 4.15.2 is the latest on PyPI and conda-forge as of 2026-09-29. Obtaining stacks: ptrace_scope=1 permits gdb only as the PARENT, so run `gdb -batch` with `handle SIGALRM stop print nopass`, `run`, `thread apply all bt`, and have the inferior call signal.alarm(N).

gmsh 4.15.2 gotcha (measured task #7447, reify-kernel-gmsh): a PostView-backed BACKGROUND mesh-size field plus multi-threaded meshing DEADLOCKS inside gmshModelMeshGenerate(3) — the call never returns, CPU time frozen, every thread in futex_do_wait. Measured on a 32-core host with the field installed via view_add/view_add_list_data("SS")/field_add("PostView")/field_set_as_background_mesh: General.NumThreads 1 and 2 pass, 8 and 32 hang. It is not confined to unmeshable input (a valid unit cube hangs too), and Mesh.MaxNumThreads3D=1 does NOT avoid it, so the stall is not only in the 3D HXT stage. Practical consequence: any gmsh entry point that installs a background size field must pin General.NumThreads=1 (what MeshingOptions{deterministic:true} resolves to) or it hangs forever with no error and no timeout.

claim: Gmsh 4.15.2 can deadlock when multithreaded meshing evaluates a PostView background field; serialize meshing or build the field’s octree before meshing.

members.text: To tell whether a `reportMissingImports` pragma on a cross-workspace-member import is load-bearing, measure under a NARROW env as well as the all-packages one. After `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --all-packages`, every member is editable-installed in the root .venv, so the import resolves and the pragma looks vestigial. To simulate the member's own minimal env (what `uv run --directory <member>` builds on an unsynced tree), temporarily move `.venv/lib/python3.*/site-packages/_editable_impl_<other_member>.pth` aside, rerun the member's declared pyright gate, then restore the file. Measured in task 5090: shared/tests/test_task_statuses.py's orchestrator/fused_memory imports gave 0 errors under all-packages and 3 with the .pth files hidden, so those pragmas are load-bearing. Note the trap: `(root/'orchestrator').is_dir()` is true at the repo root, but pyright does NOT resolve `orchestrator.task_status` through that namespace-package partial.

A pyright pragma is vestigial only if BOTH type gates agree. A green run of a member's declared gate (`uv run --directory <member> pyright src/ tests/`) is not enough. Task verify scopes that gate to the changed files: verify_cmd.py::promote_cwd_to_project and strip_cwd render it as `uv run --project <member> pyright <member>/tests/x.py`, run from the REPO ROOT, so it reads the ROOT pyproject's [tool.pyright]. Measured in task 5090: fused-memory/tests/test_cgl_eta_finalize_gate.py imports the fused-memory/scripts module `cgl_eta_finalize_gate`. That path is in fused-memory's own extraPaths ("scripts") but not in the root's. Removing its `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` passed the declared gate (0 errors) and failed scoped verify with 1 reportMissingImports. So before calling a pragma vestigial, re-run the scoped root-cwd form as well: `uv run --project <member> pyright <member>/tests/<file>.py` from the repo root.

GOTCHA (peer under pyright-extrapaths-completeness): a STATIC `import X` / `from X import` of a repo-root scripts/-only module (e.g. `_task_db_scan`) inside ANY workspace member's files (including fused-memory/tests/) fails tests/scripts/test_fallback_verify_config.py::TestMembersImportingScriptsResolveScriptsOnTheirPyrightPath unless that member's [tool.pyright] extraPaths resolves repo-root scripts/. fused-memory's extraPaths does NOT (orchestrator's does). The failure appears only in the scripts gate (`pytest tests/scripts/ scripts/tests/`), not in the fused-memory suite where the test lives. In-scope fix used in task 5335: look the module up dynamically after the scripts/ sys.path insert (`importlib.import_module('_task_db_scan')`), the same way the script under test is already loaded by path. Both pyright scopes then see Any, so the parity the guard protects still holds. Adding '../scripts' to fused-memory extraPaths is the alternative, but it widens that member's whole search path.

A script under fused-memory/scripts/ needs NO sys.path insert to import shared.* — fused-memory/pyproject.toml declares dark-factory-shared as a uv workspace dependency, so it resolves natively (this supersedes older notes suggesting shared/src conftest path inserts). Importing fused_memory.* also works directly (census_memory_metadata.py:101 precedents a module-level import). Repo-root scripts/ is the genuine exception: scripts/ and scripts/legibility/ contain no __init__.py and are installed nowhere, and fused-memory's pytest pythonpath is only ["src", "../orchestrator/src"], so importing legibility.* requires inserting <repo>/scripts on sys.path as a namespace package.

Gotcha (found in task 3355): when a subproject's tests/conftest.py imports a REPO-ROOT module reached via sys.path.append, pyright cannot resolve it and every subproject fails type-check with reportMissingImports. Every workspace member has its own type_check_command that pyrights tests/ (e.g. `uv run --project X --directory X pyright src/ tests/`), plus the stock chain in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml runs npx pyright in fused-memory, orchestrator and dashboard — so ALL of them break, not just the three in the stock chain. Fix: add ".." to each subproject's [tool.pyright] extraPaths, placed LAST so "src" and "../<sibling>/src" still win and the project folders don't shadow their own src/<pkg>/ (the same ordering argument as sys.path.append vs insert(0, ...)). Related: `pytest --fixtures` (even with -v) HIDES underscore-prefixed fixtures, so it cannot be used to verify that an autouse `_`-prefixed fixture is registered in a suite — write a throwaway probe test that asserts the fixture's observable effect instead.

fused-memory's FILE-SCOPED verify type gate runs `uv run --project fused-memory pyright <fused-memory/... files>` from the REPO ROOT (no --directory), so it reads the ROOT pyproject.toml [tool.pyright], whose extraPaths include fused-memory/src but NOT fused-memory/scripts. A fused-memory/tests file that imports a fused-memory/scripts module by bare name, even only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (e.g. `from write_triage_stats import StratumUnit`), passes `cd fused-memory && pyright` but fails verify with reportMissingImports. Bare-name imports between scripts/ siblings still resolve, because pyright falls back to the importing file's own directory. Fix that works under both configs and keeps the real type (measured task 7157, 2026-10-21, pyright 1.1.408): `if TYPE_CHECKING: from ..scripts.write_triage_stats import StratumUnit`. pyright resolves the relative import by filesystem location (reveal_type -> StratumUnit). To reproduce verify, run it from the root: `uv run --project fused-memory pyright fused-memory/tests/<file>.py`.

claim: Before judging Pyright import pragmas or fixes, test both the member-local and root-scoped gates, since their environments and extraPaths can differ.

members.text: When running `cargo test` (or any long command) via the Bash tool's `run_in_background`, do not pipe through `| tail -N`: the persisted output file only contains what was written to stdout after the pipe, so `tail` truncation is permanent — earlier test binaries' pass/fail results are discarded, not just hidden from the immediate view. Redirect/capture full output (no trailing `| tail`) and grep the resulting output file afterward instead.

When confirming test results in a reify warm lane, capture cargo's OWN exit code — `cargo test ... 2>&1 | tail -N` run in background returns `tail`'s status (always 0), so the harness completion notification reports "exit code 0" even when the test run failed. Use `{ cargo test ... > /tmp/log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"; }` and grep the log for `test result:` lines instead. Separately, a targeted `cargo test -p <crate>` in a lane can take 15+ minutes of wall clock when the merge/verify pipeline's full-workspace `cargo nextest run` is concurrently active, since both contend on the same lane `target/` and CPU — size timeouts accordingly rather than assuming a hang.

Harness gotcha (hit 2026-07-19): a background Bash of the form `cargo nextest run ... | tail -N; echo EXIT=$?` reports "completed (exit code 0)" in the task notification even when nextest FAILED — the shell's exit is the trailing echo's, and without pipefail `$?` after the pipe is tail's. The failure was only visible inside the captured output file (nextest printed "2 failed ... error: test run failed"). SOP: for background verification commands, use `set -o pipefail` and capture `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` (not `$?` after a following statement), and ALWAYS read the output file's tail/summary rather than trusting the notification's exit code before declaring a regression green. This nearly passed a red regression as green during the break-glass recovery.

Verifying a Rust suite in a warm lane: `cargo test ... | tail -N` MASKS cargo's exit code (bash reports the last pipeline stage, i.e. tail), so an aborted run can look green — cargo halts at the first failing test binary and the "error: test failed" line can be scrolled past by the tail window. Capture the status explicitly (`cargo test ... > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"`) when the result gates a merge. Separately, a SIGKILLed cargo run (e.g. one hitting the 300s background-task ceiling) can leave `target/debug/deps/<test>-<hash>` missing while cargo still considers it fresh; the rerun then fails with exit status 127 / "No such file or directory" via `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh`. That is an artifact-integrity failure, NOT a test regression — re-run that single `--test <name>` target to rebuild it before diagnosing any code cause.

In this Rust workspace, verifying a full `cargo test -p <crate>` run by piping through `tail -N` inside a backgrounded Bash command (`cmd | tail -250`) can silently mask cargo's real exit code: without `set -o pipefail`, the shell reports `tail`'s exit status (almost always 0), not cargo test's. If any test binary fails, the pipeline still reports success. Always redirect full test output to a file (`cargo test ... > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT:$?"`) and check the captured `$?` directly (or grep the full log for "FAILED"/"^error"), rather than trusting the exit code of a piped-through-tail background command.

claim: When running Rust tests in the background, capture full output and Cargo’s actual exit status rather than piping through `tail`, which can hide failures and discard diagnostics.

members.text:
Recovering reviewer SUGGESTION bodies when a review_issues escalation omits them (verified 2026-08-06, task 5748 / esc-5748-4 / esc-5748-5).

A category=review_issues escalation summarised as "Review cycles exhausted with N blocking issue(s) and M suggestion(s)" carries ONLY the blocking issue bodies in its detail field. The M suggestion bodies are absent from the escalation entirely. Do NOT conclude they are lost or ask for them to be re-surfaced — they are on disk in the lane's task-meta tree.

Canonical path: /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/verdicts/reviewer_comprehensive.json
Note the layout: .task-meta sits under worktrees/, NOT under the lane dir (it is worktrees/.task-meta/_lane-55/..., not worktrees/_lane-55/.task-meta/...). Sibling dirs reviews/, reviews-cycle-N/ and reviews-amend-N/ hold the per-cycle copies.

Structure: {role, schema_version, session_id, emitted_at, verdict:{reviewer, verdict, issues[], summary}}. Every issue — blocking and suggestion alike — is one entry in verdict.issues with severity/location/category/description/suggested_fix. Filter on severity == 'suggestion'. Measured on lane-55: 7 entries = 1 blocking + 6 suggestions, the 6 matching the categories the triage commit acted on.

This corrects an explicit claim I made in the esc-5748-4 resolution ("the suggestion bodies were not included, so they were not triaged; if they matter they need to be re-surfaced with their text"). That was wrong — a later agent recovered all 6 from the verdicts file unaided and triaged them in commit c2cee28de6. The right move on seeing a suggestion COUNT with no bodies is to read the verdicts file, not to escalate for the text.

Related but distinct from the existing note about orphan-reaper category=review_suggestions escalations, which DO bundle the full reviewer JSON in detail behind a #hash:<sha># prefix. The two escalation categories differ in whether the bodies travel with the escalation; only review_issues requires the disk lookup.

Steward: when a dark-factory `review_issues` escalation says "Review cycles exhausted with N blocking issue(s) and M suggestion(s)" but its detail body contains only the blocking findings, the M suggestions are NOT lost — recover them from the on-disk review artifact at `<worktree_base>/worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/reviews/<reviewer>.json` (the `issues` array carries `severity: "suggestion"` entries with location/category/description/suggested_fix; older cycles are archived as `reviews-cycle-N/`). Mechanism, verified 2026-09-07 at orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py:16706-16745: `_escalate_review_issues` sets the summary from `len(reviews.suggestions)` but sets `detail = reviews.format_for_replan()`, whose docstring is "Format blocking issues for the architect to address" and which iterates `blocking_issues` only (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/artifacts.py:281). On that blocking path `_route_review_suggestions_to_curator` is also never called — it runs only on the non-blocking DONE path and the out-of-delta amendment path — so on a cycles-exhausted-with-blocking outcome suggestion text reaches no triage consumer through the escalation queue at all. Read the artifact and triage from it rather than reporting the suggestions as unrecoverable. First hit: esc-6854-2 (task 6854), where 4 suggestions were recovered this way.

When an escalation resumes a reify task after a review, the escalation body may transmit only the BLOCKING findings — a summary saying "N blocking and M suggestion(s)" while the detail body carries just the blocking one. The suggestions are not lost: they are recoverable from the reviewer verdict artifact at <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<lane>/verdicts/reviewer_comprehensive.json (and the per-cycle copies reviews-cycle-N/), where verdict.issues[] holds every finding with severity, location, category, description and suggested_fix. Read that file before concluding the untransmitted suggestions are unactionable.

Handling a `review_issues` escalation: the escalation `detail` carries ONLY the severity=blocking review findings. Non-blocking suggestions are NOT in the record, so a steward reading `get_escalation` alone will silently triage zero of them and hand the task on with them unaddressed.

OBSERVED on esc-5467-16 (task 5467, 2026-08-24): summary said "2 blocking issue(s) and 9 suggestion(s)", and `detail` contained exactly the 2 blocking issues and none of the 9. The full 11-issue `submit_review_verdict` payload was recoverable from the reviewer's own transcript at `data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/<task_id>/<worktree-path-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl` (the resumed implementer found it on line 235 and dispositioned all 9 from there: 4 fixed inline, 5 filed as tickets).

WORKAROUND: when a `review_issues` summary advertises more issues than `detail` contains, pull the verdict payload from the reviewer transcript under `data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/<task_id>/` rather than assuming the suggestions were dropped or are unavailable. Alternatively hand the gap forward explicitly in the `resolve_issue` text so the resuming agent recovers them — that is what closed it here.

MECHANISM IS A HYPOTHESIS, not confirmed: the filing code was never read, so "the filer only serialises blocking items" is inferred from the one observed detail/summary mismatch, not verified. The OBSERVATION (detail held 2 of 11; transcript held 11) is what is measured.

claim: When a review_issues escalation omits suggestion bodies, recover them from the reviewer artifact or transcript and triage them rather than assuming they are lost.

members.text: /unblock false-premise SOP refinement (reify, esc-5211-4): when an escalation's replacement RCA is itself a code claim, VERIFY THE REPLACEMENT PREMISE at the exact code seam before re-scoping the task — the escalation's proposed root cause can be as wrong as the original premise it replaces. In esc-5211-4 an Explore agent re-read the four cited functions and get_shape and confirmed all 5 sub-claims against current main, so the re-scope was safe. Mechanics that worked: (1) rewrite the task via update_task (title/description/details/files/priority) BEFORE resolving, so re-dispatch uses the corrected scope; (2) wire real dependency edges (add_dependency) for the corrected sequencing; (3) resolve_issue(escalation_id, action='restart', resolved_by='interactive') on the L2 cluster escalation set the task to pending AND cascade-resolved its L1 member escalation in one call (pending list went empty) — restart cascades to members like close_only does. For a false-premise escalated task with NO worktree code, the whole disposition is pure task-graph surgery — no merge, no worktree fix, no plan mode.

PROCESS LESSON (L2 design-concern escalations): re-deriving the escalation's empirical numbers independently before the human ruling materially changed the decision. The task-4926 steward reported pinned share_hi=0.659 (margin 0.009 over the 0.65 floor — looked flake-prone) and leaned per-$$ disjoint CPU pairs to avoid cross-run contention. Independent re-measurement with the real machinery got 0.687-0.763 (5x more margin) and showed cross-run same-pair contention IMPROVES the ratio — reversing the sub-decision recommendation. Pattern: for design-concern L2s that hinge on measured values, spend the ~10 minutes to reproduce the measurement in-session (including the contended/concurrent scenarios the steward could not run) before presenting options; steward numbers may be from a single configuration and understate margin or mis-rank alternatives. Reinforces feedback_verify_unblock_rescope_premise_empirically.

An escalation brief's "working hypothesis (unverified, offered as a lead)" must be tested against primary evidence before it shapes the investigation, even when the brief is otherwise excellent and explicitly says "do not re-derive" the rest. In the 2026-07-30 scope-lock-divergence investigation the brief's lead — "metadata.files is written once at task creation and never re-derived when the plan scopes down" — was well-reasoned and wrong: one query against data/orchestrator/runs.db showed the value WAS re-derived and persisted, and was clobbered afterwards. Accepting the lead would have produced a fix at the plan-time re-derivation site, which was already working. The brief's VERIFIED findings (both-directions divergence, branch diff, not-mid-merge probes) were all accurate and correctly saved time — the norm is to separate a brief's verified section from its hypothesis section and re-derive only the latter.

The escalation-watcher's own DecisionRecord/triage notes can propagate a wrong conclusion into the next rotation, so a retraction must be written to the SAME surfaces the claim was written to, not just said in-session. Worked example 2026-07-30: an L2 watcher concluded from get_curator_state().soonest_open_at that the fleet faced a multi-day curation outage, and wrote that into esc-task-curator-3's triage note, its cockpit DecisionRecord text, AND the standing-context block of its own ScheduleWakeup prompt — which would have instructed every later wake to keep re-raising the false alarm and to expect timeouts. When list_tickets refuted it, fixing the record required all four: resolve the escalation with the correction, re-file the DecisionRecord with corrected text, rewrite the wakeup prompt's standing context (explicitly marked as superseding the earlier framing), and tell the human plainly. General rule: when a long-running loop session records a diagnosis in durable artefacts, treat those artefacts as part of the blast radius of being wrong, and enumerate them when retracting.

Convention reinforced by the reify L2 watch session of 2026-07-30/31: an escalation's own stated evidence must be re-probed before acting on it, and doing so repeatedly changed the disposition. Concrete instances from one session — esc-5871-1 claimed task 5785 had "no worktree, no recent commit" and routed it as genuinely stranded; in fact a worktree existed at warm lane _lane-22 and 9 commits sat on the branch, making it complete-but-unmerged, a different remedy entirely. esc-5849-2 recommended cancelling task 5849 as a duplicate; re-running the checks confirmed it, and additionally established there was no '#5849' citation anywhere in tracked source, so the cancel could not orphan a PTODO cite. esc-5859-3 flagged a plan check whose sole expected match turned out to be a COINCIDENTAL substring inside the float 0.665859 in a colormap table. esc-5830-3's own correction over-counted Ok(Value::Null) paths as 3 when there are 2. esc-5377-6 offered "accept the loss, duplicate of 5346" as an option; reading 5346 and 2490 showed they were complementary, so the lost suggestion was genuinely uncovered and was re-filed as task 5895. A stale carry-forward warning also nearly cost real work: a note saying task 5728 was LIVE in _lane-14 and must not be reassigned was false hours later — verified idle with null claimant/heartbeat — and re-checking is what made the re-pend safe.

Unblock/escalation-triage norm: when an escalation declares a task unactionable because "dependency X cannot do Y", independently verify the premise against the ACTUAL pinned crate source AND check crates.io for a newer version before accepting a re-scope/defer. Premises about dependency capabilities are time-bound — the fix may have landed upstream and obsoleted the blocker. Concrete case (2026-06-02, task 3525): the architect's manifold3d-0.2-has-no-provenance-egress premise was correct for the pinned dep but obsoleted the SAME DAY by manifold-csg 0.3.0 adding Manifold::to_meshgl64(); the right move was a dep-bump substrate sibling, not the defer/vendor-patch the escalation framing implied. Also: reject "technically possible but unsound" workarounds (e.g. transmuting a pub(crate) ptr field) — they're quality non-starters in this codebase.

claim: Before acting on an escalation, independently verify its claims against current primary evidence; its diagnosis, measurements, or proposed remedy may be wrong or stale.

members.text: Both headline columns of the E2 bake-off decision table are harness artifacts, in opposite directions, and neither should be read as a retrieval property. (1) b_grouped's canonical-in-top-5 = 0.97 is RECORD-ID ALIASING: the grouped document is emitted with record_id = canonical.record_id (bake_off_storage_shape.py:934) and topic_discoverability scores by record-id match, so any non-contested cluster member surfacing in top-5 scores as "canonical found"; median rank 1.00 follows because the group takes min rank over its members. The tell-tale is that b_grouped scores 0.9886 on canonical-in-top-5 for CLAIM-kind queries, which target amendments and sightings rather than the canonical. Task 3560 owns disclosing this. (2) b_grouped's claim recall IS its crediting ceiling exactly: the grouped render collapses sightings to a bare count and denies them credit, giving (176 - 34 sightings + 6 contested)/176 = 148/176 = 0.8409090909, and the committed JSON reports claim-kind at_10 = 0.8409090909090909 and at_5 = 147/176 = 0.8352272727272727 — matching to the digit. B retrieved every claim it was ALLOWED credit for; the shortfall is a render/credit policy knob, not a retrieval limit. Symmetrically, c_peers' 0.99 on claim queries is fixture saturation (one query per stored claim), NOT an identity lookup — the claim queries are independently authored (0/176 verbatim, SequenceMatcher median 0.09) and were blind-committed before any metric code existed.

The E2 bake-off report's own gloss explaining guard-matched = 0.00 as a category-filter ceiling is WRONG, and it misled at least one reader (the /unblock session of 2026-08-11). The report says a probe of any non-procedural_knowledge category cannot match under any shape, implying the 0.00 is a shape-independent ceiling. But the denominator suffix (n=12/15) means 12 of 15 probes WERE covered, and those 12 still produced no match: max observed score is 0.899 for status_quo and 0.866 for both peer arms, against a 0.92 threshold. So the near-duplicate write guard is dead by THRESHOLD CALIBRATION everywhere, not by category filtering — and the decomposed peer arms move the best score 0.033 FURTHER from firing, which is a real, adverse, shape-attributable write-path signal that the binarised 0.00 column destroys. Consequence: the corpus-shape decision is a read-path decision; none of the three arms addresses the campaign's write-path deduplication problem.

All three headline numbers in the E2 bake-off decision table are measurement artifacts, in different directions. (1) b_grouped's canonical-in-top-5 of 0.97 is record-id aliasing: apply_grouped_read emits the grouped document with the canonical's record_id (bake_off_storage_shape.py near line 934) and topic_discoverability scores by record-id match, so any non-contested cluster member surfacing counts as "canonical found" — on claim-kind queries B scores 0.9886 on canonical-in-top-5, which is the aliasing signature, not a win; task 3560 (in-progress) independently flags this in-tree. (2) b_grouped's claim recall equals its structural crediting ceiling exactly: sightings are collapsed to a count and denied credit, ceiling = (176-34+6)/176 = 148/176 = 0.840909..., and measured claim-kind recall at 10 is 0.8409090909 to the digit — a render/credit policy knob, not a retrieval property; the 28 permanently uncredited claims include falsification records that correct stale canonicals. (3) c_peers' 0.99 claim recall is fixture saturation: the query set authors exactly one query per stored claim, so C's per-claim records sit at ceiling; the queries themselves are genuinely independently phrased (0 of 176 verbatim, char SequenceMatcher median 0.09), so the "identity lookup" critique is wrong in mechanism — the status_quo control scores 0.80 on the same queries, proving the short dedicated record drives the effect. What survives artifact-stripping: decomposition beats status quo 3.2x on tokens (1181/1196 vs 3831) with p under 1e-6, grouping buys zero tokens over flat peers, and a grouped read genuinely wins topic-shaped queries 56/60 vs 46/60 (paired McNemar p 0.002-0.031).

The E2 bake-off's guard-matched-replay column reading 0.00 in every arm is THRESHOLD-bound, not category-ceiling-bound. 12 of 15 probes were category-covered and still no candidate came within 0.02 of the 0.92 threshold: max_observed_score in the committed JSON is 0.899 (status_quo) vs 0.8663 (both decomposed arms). The oft-repeated explanation that the procedural_knowledge category filter caps the column is wrong for these zeros — it explains only the 3 uncovered probes. Two decision-relevant facts the binarised 0.00 destroys: candidate_present_rate discriminates (1.00 status_quo vs 0.933 decomposed arms), and decomposing long entries into short peers moves the guard's best score 0.033 FURTHER from firing — a real adverse write-path signal of the peer shapes. calibrate_write_triage.py records the one genuine rediscovery pair at 0.824, i.e. the 0.92 guard could never have fired on the case it exists to catch. Net: the corpus-shape decision addresses the write-path near-duplicate problem in no arm; the guard is dead by calibration everywhere.

claim: E2 bake-off headline scores confound harness, crediting, and threshold effects, so they cannot by themselves establish corpus-shape retrieval or write-path performance.

members.text: plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json (and its .md twin) is dual-purpose: census_memory_metadata.py treats it as freely regeneratable, but fused-memory/tests/test_memory_metadata.py (task 3195/leaf alpha) pins exact key/kind counts from it as a frozen grandfather oracle for KIND_REGISTRY and BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS. Re-running the census script against live Mem0 stores changes measured counts and kind values (the corpus grows continuously from ongoing agent activity) and will break that oracle test suite. To regenerate only the markdown's presentation (e.g. a header/formatting fix) without invalidating the oracle, load the existing committed JSON and call census_memory_metadata.render_markdown(report) directly (it's a pure function of the report dict) rather than re-running the live scroll. Discovered fixing task 3507, where a prior step's live re-scroll broke 11 tests in test_memory_metadata.py.

plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json is a PINNED ORACLE, not just a report: fused-memory/tests/test_memory_metadata.py reads it directly and asserts exact measured values against it (distinct `kind` count, the KIND_REGISTRY-minus-measured additions set, and 8 blessed key counts in BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS). Regenerating it with scripts/census_memory_metadata.py against the live corpus therefore breaks ~11 tests in that suite even when the regeneration is perfectly valid — the failures are a deliberate tripwire ("census artifact changed — re-derive the registry"), not broken tests. Any task that refreshes the census artifact must be scoped to fused-memory/src/fused_memory/memory_metadata.py and fused-memory/tests/test_memory_metadata.py as well, and must re-derive KIND_REGISTRY/BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS in the same change. Task 3225 hit this and reverted the refresh rather than silence the tripwire.

In dark-factory, `plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json` is read at TEST time by `fused-memory/tests/test_memory_metadata.py` as the frozen "oracle" its KIND_REGISTRY is grandfathered from, asserting exact snapshot equality (distinct-kind count, and per-key census counts). Regenerating that artifact against live Qdrant therefore breaks ~11 tests in a file most tasks do not own, with no code change to blame — measured on task 4006: records 49,628→54,392 flipped distinct kinds 329→385 (70 added, 14 REMOVED — the drift is bidirectional, so a registry grandfathered from a census also needs a policy for values that leave). Before regenerating that artifact, expect to re-derive KIND_REGISTRY in `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/memory_metadata.py` in the same change, or arrange scope for whoever owns leaf β (task 3195).

claim: The census JSON is a pinned test oracle, so never regenerate it from live data without coordinating updates to the metadata registry and its tests.

members.text: MEASURED (2026-09-16, lane _lane-9, HEAD af103dcc53): gmsh `MeshingOptions { deterministic: true }` — which only sets `General.NumThreads = 1` — makes reify's attributed tet producer BIT-reproducible on its own; no `Mesh.RandomSeed` is needed (none exists anywhere in `crates/`). 12 runs across 2 processes under `MeshingOptions::default()` gave 12 DISTINCT meshes (tets 1163..1239); the same 12 under `deterministic: true` were byte-identical, including across process boundaries. This resolves the open caveat in `docs/notes/adaptive-e2e-seed-mesh-drift-measurement.md` ("NumThreads=1 HXT stability is itself unverified absent a Mesh.RandomSeed").

MEASURED (task 7411, 32-core host, gmsh HXT Algorithm3D=10): setting `General.NumThreads = available_parallelism()` — what `MeshingOptions::default()` (deterministic: false) resolves to — is BOTH nondeterministic and SLOWER than `NumThreads = 1` at every tet-mesh scale from ~1.2k up to ~491k tets (0.016s vs 2.2-3.7s at 1.2k; 0.28s vs 11-15s at 33k; 1.0s vs 10-21s at 149k; 3.4-4.3s vs 25-27s at 491k). The speedup narrows with scale (~140x to ~6x) but never inverts, so "pinning threads costs wallclock" is not a reason to leave a reify gmsh meshing call site unpinned — measure before assuming a cost. `deterministic: true` alone gives bit-identical output across processes; no `Mesh.RandomSeed` is needed (none exists in crates/).

MEASURED (2026-09-16, lane _lane-9, 32-core host): pinning gmsh `General.NumThreads = 1` at reify realization mesh scale (~1200 tets) is a large SPEEDUP, not a cost — the opposite of what `docs/notes/adaptive-e2e-seed-mesh-drift-measurement.md` assumed when it deferred the fix for needing "its own benchmark". reify-eval `morph_arm_e2e` over 48 runs at 8-way concurrency: 3m46s wall / 28m21s CPU → 10.4s wall / 22.5s CPU (~22x wall, ~76x CPU). The gmsh attributed-producer reproducibility test: 61-74s → 0.24-0.88s per run. A 32-thread HXT (`Mesh.Algorithm3D = 10`) pool is pure overhead at this mesh size. Do not assume determinism pins trade wallclock at realization scale — measure; the parallel path can be dramatically slower.

claim: For reify’s gmsh HXT meshing, setting NumThreads=1 makes output bit-reproducible and faster than the default parallel setting; no random seed is needed.

members.text: Adding a NEW pass to scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py's _cli timer path, or a new row to its --report branch, silently makes every EXISTING test that calls wdog._cli([]) / _cli(["--bogus"]) / _cli(["--report"]) / _cli() run that pass FOR REAL against the main checkout (REPO_DIR is hardcoded), stamping live clocks and spawning real subprocesses through whatever subprocess.run fake the test installed. Measured task 4883 (2026-10-05): 11 such call sites in tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_watchdog.py, two asserting an EXACT pass list. Sweep with `grep -n '_cli(' tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_watchdog.py` and stub the new symbol at each site (monkeypatch.setattr(wdog, name, ..., raising=False)). Conversely, an UN-FAKED contract test of a sibling script the watchdog shells out to is possible: monkeypatch wdog.REPO_DIR to the test's REPO_ROOT and re-derive the script constant from os.path.relpath(constant, wdog.REPO_DIR) (so a rename still fails), and setenv HOME to tmp_path when the child defaults to ~/.config/systemd/user, keeping the production argv intact (see test_unit_parity_verdict_runs_the_real_checker_and_reads_its_tag).

scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py hardcodes REPO_DIR = "/home/leo/src/dark-factory" rather than deriving it from __file__, so FLEET_DEPLOY_CLOCK_PATH and FM_DEPLOY_CLOCK_PATH default to the LIVE data/ clock files even when tests/scripts/ runs from a .worktrees/<id> worktree. df_pytest_isolation.py + tests/scripts/test_deploy_clock_isolation.py only guard the WRITE side (they fail if a real clock MOVED) and tests/scripts/conftest.py has no read redirect, so any new gate reading those clocks must be explicitly neutralized (monkeypatch the gate to lambda: False) or pointed at tmp_path in every test that reaches it.

PRACTICAL RULE (measured 2026-08-26, task 4754): adding a NEW clock-reading gate to staleness_pass / fused_memory_staleness_pass fails SILENTLY rather than loudly — a green suite is NOT evidence the new gate is isolated. Of the 23 pre-existing staleness tests that neutralize their tier's min-interval gate with `lambda: False`, 21 pin `wdog.time.time` to 2_000_000_000.0 (year 2033), making the live on-disk clock stamp look ~7.7 years old, so a second, unpatched gate reads the LIVE clock and returns False by pure coincidence of the pinned year — isolation that silently expires the moment a new gate is added. The other 2 (test_staleness_pass_noop_when_commit_epoch_none and its fm twin) use REAL time and have purely NEGATIVE assertions, so they pass HOLLOWLY on an incidental gate skip rather than failing visibly. Sweep every existing test that patches a sibling gate and neutralize the new one explicitly before trusting a green run.

Watchdog test-isolation gotcha (task 2396/β, scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py): the standard watchdog test convention drives everything through ONE monkeypatched subprocess.run dispatched on argv shape — but the new fleet-deploy clock gate reads its state via a FILE read (_read_last_fleet_deploy_epoch -> open/read_text of REPO_DIR/data/orchestrator/last_redeploy_orchestrator.json), which bypasses the subprocess.run fake entirely. So a REAL last_redeploy_orchestrator.json present on disk at the hardcoded default path can make _within_fleet_deploy_min_interval() return True and spuriously SKIP staleness_pass in tests that never touched a clock file. Any staleness_pass test that must REACH enumeration/delegation (the unit-level + e2e staleness tests) must neutralize the gate explicitly: monkeypatch wdog._within_fleet_deploy_min_interval -> lambda: False, or setenv ORCH_FLEET_DEPLOY_CLOCK to an absent tmp path BEFORE _load_watchdog() re-execs the module. Same class of footgun applies to any future watchdog helper that reads a file rather than shelling out.

PEER under topic `watchdog-clock-gate-test-isolation` — the REGISTRATION mechanism changed in task 5299, and the older peer 7c61c493's remedy ("point ORCH_FLEET_DEPLOY_CLOCK at a tmp file, per-suite as scripts/tests/conftest.py::_df_fleet_deploy_clock_redirect does") now describes only half of what happens.

MEASURED 2026-09-21 while planning task 4755. `df_pytest_isolation.py::PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_ENV_VARS` is now the SINGLE table that three separate things derive from: (1) `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_RELPATHS = tuple(PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_ENV_VARS)` — no longer a second literal list; (2) the failure message's "set $VAR" remedy, via `deploy_clock_change_report` / `_falsified_message` — the old hand-written `'FM_DEPLOY_CLOCK' if 'fused-memory' in relpath else 'ORCH_FLEET_DEPLOY_CLOCK'` mapping was DELETED and no longer exists anywhere in the file; and (3) a suite-wide autouse REDIRECT inside `_df_deploy_clocks_unwritten` itself, which repoints every listed env var at `tmp_path_factory.mktemp('deploy-clock-redirect')` for the whole session.

PRACTICAL RULE. To bring a NEW cross-process redeploy-coordination file under suite-wide isolation, add ONE entry to that dict. You get the session redirect, the detect-and-fail guard and the correct remedy string together, and all nine conftests pick it up with no edit. Do NOT clone `_df_fleet_dir_redirect` into a parallel fixture and bind it into conftests — that re-creates precisely the second table 5299 folded in (heuristic 11, SPOT), and the derived-tuple comment explains that deriving exists to make an omitted entry unrepresentable rather than a KeyError raised from session teardown at the moment a real clock was falsified.

NON-OBVIOUS, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the file you register need not be a clock. A body with no `source`/`pytest_session` pair makes `clock_stamp_provenance` return None, so `deploy_clock_change_report` classifies FALSIFIED and fails the run — no crash, no KeyError. For a LEASE that is exactly right, because unlike a clock a lease has no benign-external-write case, so every write to the real path during a test run should stay FALSIFIED. `_MAX_CLOCK_BODY_CHARS`'s own comment already contemplates the guard "firing on a file that is not a clock at all". The residual cost is naming only — the table says "clock" — which is answered with a comment, not a rename, since `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_RELPATHS` is imported by name by the watchdog drift test.

Note the session redirect is ONE shared path for the whole session, so a test that needs to control file CONTENTS still does `monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, str(tmp_path / '...'))` per-test. The session redirect is the backstop for tests that forget, not a per-test fixture.

PEER under topic `watchdog-clock-gate-test-isolation` — CORRECTS the "NON-OBVIOUS, VERIFIED" paragraph of peer 00bdff3b (2026-09-21). That paragraph told a future agent that registering a LEASE in `df_pytest_isolation.PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_ENV_VARS` is "exactly right, because unlike a clock a lease has no benign-external-write case, so every write to the real path during a test run should stay FALSIFIED." The premise is BACKWARDS, and task 4755's own review caught it before it shipped.

THE DEFECT. `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_ENV_VARS` drives TWO different jobs, and one entry bought both: the suite-wide REDIRECT, and CHANGE DETECTION (via the derived `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_RELPATHS`). `deploy_clock_guard_roots` deliberately watches the MAIN checkout as well as the worktree — and `scripts/restart-all-orchestrators.sh` creates, per-unit rewrites (`lease_set_current_unit`) and REMOVES the live lease there for the ENTIRE duration of every production sweep. So a real sweep IS a benign external write; that is the only reason the main checkout is watched at all. Any verify run whose session snapshot straddles either end of one fails an innocent branch — before=present/after=rewritten -> REWRITTEN, present/absent -> DELETED, absent/present -> CREATED — re-opening the false-positive class task 4823 closed, with a far WIDER window: a clock moves once, instantaneously, whereas the lease is present for the whole sweep (~15min) against documented 26-41min verify runs.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, stated as a rule for the next file registered here: ask whether a PRODUCTION process writes the file during ordinary operation in a checkout the guard watches. If yes, it is REDIRECT-ONLY. If no (a clock, stamped once on a verified-fresh exit), it gets both halves.

THE FIX (task 4755, `df_pytest_isolation.py`): keep the one table, and derive the change-detected tuple as its COMPLEMENT — `REDIRECT_ONLY_RELPATHS: frozenset[str]`, then `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_RELPATHS = tuple(r for r in PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_ENV_VARS if r not in REDIRECT_ONLY_RELPATHS)`. That keeps 5299's SPOT invariant (no second literal list of files, no `if 'lease' in relpath` string test) while making which HALF each entry gets a named, structured statement.

TWO CONSEQUENCES worth knowing before you touch this: (1) adding provenance (`source`/`pytest_session`) to the body does NOT rescue it — the DELETED case has `after=None` and leaves nothing to attribute — and neither does a benign-rule special case in `deploy_clock_change_report`, for the same reason. (2) Anything deriving from `PROTECTED_DEPLOY_CLOCK_RELPATHS` to reason about the REDIRECT now silently under-covers; `shared/tests/test_deploy_clock_redirect.py` had to switch its `live_paths` construction to the env-var table.

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL, named in the code: a spawner that HARDCODES the lease path instead of reading `$ORCH_FLEET_LEASE` is no longer detected. Nothing in the repo does that; the four-way drift pin and the per-test `monkeypatch.setenv` discipline are what keep it true.

Gotcha: `scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py` HARDCODES `REPO_DIR = "/home/leo/src/dark-factory"` (line 96), so `FM_DEPLOY_CLOCK_PATH` and the `restart-all-orchestrators.sh` it spawns resolve into the MAIN checkout no matter which `.worktrees/<id>` invoked them — unlike the bash script, which derives REPO_DIR from its own path and so follows the worktree. Any test-isolation guard, cleanup sweep, or hermeticity assertion rooted only at `Path(__file__).parent` is therefore BLIND to watchdog-side writes from a worktree run. Measured during task 3797: the worktree root had both protected deploy clocks absent while the main checkout carried the real production ones, i.e. a worktree-rooted guard was watching two paths nothing under a worktree can write. Guard both roots (own root, plus `root.parents[1]` when `root.parent.name` is `.worktrees`/`.worktrees-orphaned`/`.eval-worktrees`).

claim: Watchdog tests must explicitly isolate file-backed gates and writes, accounting for the hardcoded main-checkout paths that bypass subprocess fakes and worktree-rooted guards.
