MERGE_RR.lock trap — removing the LOCK ALONE is not enough; remove `MERGE_RR` too. Short stamped peer to canonical cd34eb91 (topic merge-rr-lock-stale-after-rerere-failure); trigger identical to peer 9ad315f1 (`git merge main` in a warm lane, same `could not write .../rr-cache/<sha>/preimage: No such file or directory`).

MEASURED 2026-08-23, _lane-28, task 5743: after the conflicted merge, commit #1 exited 128 on `MERGE_RR.lock: File exists`. I ran `rm -f MERGE_RR.lock` ONLY — leaving the stale `MERGE_RR` — and the VERY NEXT `git commit` died with `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` and left a freshly recreated 0-byte MERGE_RR.lock. Both commits had in fact landed (correct parent, correct diff, clean status). Only after `rm -f MERGE_RR MERGE_RR.lock` did a `git commit --allow-empty` smoke test exit 0 and leave no lock.

So the stale MERGE_RR — not the lock — is what re-poisons EVERY subsequent commit in the lane; the lock is a symptom regenerated each time. Peer 9ad315f1's remediation names only the .lock, which is why this clause is recorded: follow d3048711 / 6eacf382 and delete BOTH (safe once no merge is in flight — no MERGE_HEAD, no MERGE_MSG, status clean).

Second clause: the SIGSEGV is NOT specific to `git commit --amend`. Peer d3048711 records exit 139 on an `--amend`; here a plain `git commit -F -` segfaulted. Treat a segfault from ANY commit form in a lane that has merged as this trap, and check `git log --oneline -1` before retrying.

Also filed as esc-5743-3 with the suggestion to disable rerere for lane worktrees via scripts/setup-main-gate-worktree-config.sh, since this has now recurred across at least four lanes since 2026-07-30.

MERGE_RR.lock trap — peer sighting via LANE INHERITANCE, not a live rerere failure. Peer to canonical cd34eb91 (topic merge-rr-lock-stale-after-rerere-failure).

MEASURED 2026-08-29, _lane-4, task 6461: a plain comment-only `git commit` (no merge, no conflict, nothing rerere-adjacent in this session) exited with `fatal: Unable to create '.../MERGE_RR.lock': File exists`, yet `git log --oneline -1` showed the commit had landed at HEAD anyway — same lying-exit-code shape as the canonical entry. Distinguishing clause: `stat` on the lock showed mtime ~a full day before this session's plan was even created, and only the `.lock` file existed — no bare `MERGE_RR` alongside it (unlike peer fbd884fc's both-files case). So the trigger here was NOT an in-session rerere write failure; it was a stale lock inherited from the lane's PRIOR occupant that survived warm-lane reseed, because reseed cleans the tracked working tree (`git clean -xfd` etc.) but does not touch `.git/worktrees/<lane>/` per-worktree metadata files, which live outside the working tree entirely.

Procedure followed, confirming the canonical remediation generalizes to this trigger too: (1) `git log --oneline -1` showed the real commit already at HEAD — nothing to redo; (2) confirmed no live git process (`ps aux | grep git`), no MERGE_HEAD/MERGE_MSG, clean status; (3) `rm -f MERGE_RR MERGE_RR.lock` (both, even though only `.lock` existed — `rm -f` on the absent one is a no-op); (4) ran `git commit --allow-empty` as a smoke test — exited 0, no lock error — then removed that smoke commit with a plain `git reset HEAD~1` (safe: the smoke commit was empty, so a mixed reset loses no tree content) to restore the real commit as HEAD. Full sequence confirmed clean after: `git log` shows only the real commits, `git status` clean, both consumer guards (test_harness_kloc_cap.sh, test_harness_baseline_registration_gate.sh) still green.

Implication for the pool-lifecycle docs: this is a candidate gap in warm-lane reseed's cleanup scope (`.git/worktrees/<lane>/` metadata is outside what reseed touches), not just a rerere-during-this-session hazard.

RECOVERY STEP for the warm-lane `git stash` hazard (complements the existing "NEVER use git stash in a warm lane" entry, mem 5fc4ca73-cc2c-4988-9fc5-385ca2092c13, which covers the pop-a-foreign-stash mechanism and the rr-cache risk but NOT this aftermath). After a bad `git stash pop` conflict in a lane, git leaves BOTH `MERGE_RR` and a zero-byte `MERGE_RR.lock` in the per-worktree git dir at /home/leo/src/reify/.git/worktrees/<lane>/. These persist after you resolve the conflict and after `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, and they poison every SUBSEQUENT `git commit` in that lane: observed 2026-07-30 in _lane-22 as one `git commit` dying with "Segmentation fault (core dumped)" and the next failing with "fatal: Unable to create '.../worktrees/<lane>/MERGE_RR.lock': File exists" and exit 128. In both cases the commit object was still CREATED and the branch ref DID move — so check `git log --oneline -1` before assuming the commit failed and retrying (a blind retry would double-commit). Fix: confirm no operation is in progress (none of MERGE_HEAD, MERGE_MSG, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, rebase-merge, rebase-apply exist in that dir), then `rm -f <dir>/MERGE_RR.lock <dir>/MERGE_RR`. Both are regenerated by git on the next real conflict, so removing them when no merge is in flight is safe. Also check whether an rr-cache preimage was written under /home/leo/src/reify/.git/rr-cache/<hash>/ (rerere.enabled is true repo-wide); if the write failed with "No such file or directory" nothing was recorded and there is nothing to clean.

Reify warm-lane git trap (measured 2026-08-06, lane _lane-9, task 5392): `git merge main` inside a warm-lane worktree can leave a STALE 0-byte `<common-git-dir>/worktrees/<lane>/MERGE_RR.lock`, because rerere fails mid-merge with `error: could not write '/home/leo/src/reify/.git/rr-cache/<hash>/preimage': No such file or directory` (the rr-cache subdir is not created in the lane's environment). The merge itself still completes normally. The trap is on the NEXT commit in that worktree: `git commit` exits 128 with `fatal: Unable to create '.../MERGE_RR.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running` — but the commit OBJECT HAS ALREADY BEEN WRITTEN. The fatal comes from git's post-commit rerere cleanup, after the commit lands. Do NOT re-run the commit and do NOT assume failure: run `git log --oneline -1` first (the commit will be there) and `git status` (clean). Remediation is `rm -f <common-git-dir>/worktrees/<lane>/MERGE_RR.lock` after confirming with `pgrep -af '[g]it '` that no git process is actually using THAT worktree (matches in other lanes/repos are irrelevant). Related but distinct from the `&&`-chaining hazard: a `git add X && git commit ... && git log` chain reports the exit-128 and never runs the log, which is what makes the false failure look real.

In a sandboxed reify task worktree, `<common-git-dir>/rr-cache/` is outside the landlock write-set while the per-worktree git dir is writable. Since `rerere.enabled=true` repo-wide, a CONFLICTED `git merge` there fails to create its rr-cache entry but still writes a reference into the writable `MERGE_RR` — after which the next `git commit` fails with `fatal: Unable to create '.../MERGE_RR.lock': File exists` (exit 128) and a subsequent `git commit --amend` SIGSEGVs (exit 139). In both cases the commit object IS still created, so the tree is fine and `git fsck` is clean; the fix is `rm -f <git-dir>/worktrees/<lane>/MERGE_RR <...>/MERGE_RR.lock`, which is pure rerere bookkeeping and safe to delete once the merge has committed. Filed as esc-5467-5.

claim: Stale per-worktree MERGE_RR files can make commits fail or segfault after the commit already landed; verify HEAD before retrying, then remove MERGE_RR and MERGE_RR.lock when no Git operation is active.

GOTCHA — never pin a durable artifact reference to a commit sha created on your own task branch. The merge lane REBASES task/<id> before it lands, so any sha you record for a same-branch commit is an orphan by the time the work reaches main: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` says no, and `git show <sha>:<path>` fails outright once `git gc` prunes the dangling object. This is broken by construction, not bad luck — it is guaranteed for every same-branch sha, and it silently converts a documented recovery path into an unexecutable one.

Where it bites: any committed artifact (investigation report, provenance sidecar, recovery tracker) whose whole value is being auditable evidence. Task 3567's recovery-tracking.json hit exactly this — it pinned the only surviving copy of a deleted memory record to a pre-rebase orphan sha.

DO INSTEAD: pin by repo-relative path + sha256 over the referenced bytes. That survives rebase and is verifiable hermetically (file read + hashlib, no git subprocess), so a test can re-derive it in CI.

TESTING NOTE, the part that is easy to get wrong: a regex that checks a sha's SHAPE (e.g. 40-hex) is not an anti-fabrication gate. A fabricated or stale sha is exactly as well-shaped as a real one. Only re-deriving the digest from the committed bytes actually proves the reference resolves. If a commit sha is still wanted as commentary, label it explicitly non-authoritative and say what it is (run environment vs durability pin).

Reference implementation: fused-memory/tests/test_toolcall_xml_leak_sweep_artifacts.py::TestUnrepairedMutationsAreTracked::test_payload_digests_reproduce, which also rejects reintroduction of the old commit-sha field.

Codebase gotcha (git_ops.py): `is_ancestor(HEAD, main)` returns True TRIVIALLY for a zero-commit branch whose tip equals the main HEAD at branch-create time — documented in find_task_citation_commit (git_ops.py:3331) and find_merge_marker (:3277). So it CANNOT distinguish a landed/merged branch from a freshly-created zero-commit one. To confirm a REAL landing, grep main's history for the canonical merge subject via `_merge_subject(branch, main)` (git_ops.py:578) with `git log <main> --fixed-strings --grep=... --format=%H` (the find_merge_marker pattern). The interactive-worktree reaper (task 2012) relies on this to avoid reaping a just-created _iact-* worktree mid-session.

STAMPED PEER under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` — a SIXTH subcase, plus a CORRECTION to the recommended content check. Observed on dark_factory task 3875 (merge request mr-0ce7a070, landed 2026-08-24T15:50:47Z, main advanced to 7169009858).

NEW, CHEAPEST ATTRIBUTION SOURCE — THE MERGE WORKER LOGS THE REBASED SHA ITSELF. Existing peers reconstruct a rebase landing after the fact by subject-matching. You usually do not have to: the orchestrator journal emits the rebased SHA at gate time. Grep the unit for it:
    journalctl --user -u orchestrator-<project>.service | grep -E 'Task <id>: (verify end|gate cleared)'
On 3875 this gave, verbatim:
    Task 3875: verify end (merge=2251c781, passed=True)
    Task 3875: gate cleared (disjoint or green re-verify); advancing with rebased SHA 71690098 (gate attempt 1/5)
That second line names the landing SHA directly and is authoritative. `merge_status(request_id=...)` returning state='done' confirms terminality but, on the live-snapshot tier, carries NEITHER merge_sha NOR kind — so the journal is strictly more informative here.

THE CORRECTION — DO NOT COMPARE BLOBS; COMPARE DELTAS. A prior peer recommends `git diff main task/<ID> -- <declared files>` and treats EMPTY as proof of landing. That test produces a FALSE "DIFFERS" whenever a declared file is SHARED and has been modified upstream since the branch base. On 3875, `git rev-parse main:<file>` vs `git rev-parse <branch tip>:<file>` gave IDENTICAL blobs for 2 of 3 declared files but DIFFERENT blobs for fused-memory/tests/_fm_helpers.py — not because the task's addition was dropped, but because unrelated upstream commits had grown that file (visible as the hunk header moving from @@ -779 to @@ -781).

THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY WORKS is delta-vs-delta, ignoring hunk offsets:
    # the branch's own contribution
    git diff <branch base> <branch tip> -- <declared files> | grep -v '^index ' > branch.diff
    # the contribution as landed (first landed commit's parent .. landed tip)
    git diff <first landed commit>^ <landed tip> -- <declared files> | grep -v '^index ' > landed.diff
    diff <(grep -E '^[+-]' branch.diff) <(grep -E '^[+-]' landed.diff)
Empty output proves the landed contribution is byte-identical in added/removed lines. On 3875 this was empty (3 files, 201 insertions, 1 deletion, both sides). Hunk headers (@@) and index lines legitimately differ and must be excluded, or the comparison false-alarms.

SAME TECHNIQUE PROVES A REQUEUE REBASE DIDN'T EAT A COMMIT. Before merging, 3875's branch had been requeue-rebased (reflog: `rebase (finish): refs/heads/task/3875 onto 4f58a16fc6`, tip 4242c8c893 -> cb83637836). Running the identical delta-vs-delta comparison across the rebase (376b10cc5c..4242c8c893 vs 4f58a16fc6..cb83637836) showed 237 diff lines on both sides, identical apart from hunk offsets — positive evidence nothing was silently dropped.

FINALLY, done_provenance kind: a prior peer says to use kind='found_on_main' for a rebase landing because kind='merged' "asserts a merge commit that does not exist". That guidance is for the case where you RE-DERIVE the landing from git after the fact. When you hold the merge request id and its terminal 'done', kind='merged' with commit=<the rebased landing SHA> is accepted (the server validates only rev-parse + `merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`, which passes because that commit genuinely IS on main) and preserves the causal truth that the merge lane landed it. Either way, SAY IN THE NOTE that it was a rebase landing and give the rebased SHA — the kind alone is not enough for a later reader.

STAMPED PEER under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` — the PARTIALLY-LANDED subcase, which is the FALSE-NEGATIVE direction the canonical does not yet cover.

`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD main` -> rc=1 does NOT mean "this branch never merged". It proves only that the EXACT TIP is not on main. A branch can have been merged normally at an earlier commit and then had more commits added afterwards — the tip is then correctly not-an-ancestor while most of the work IS on main.

OBSERVED on task 3465 (2026-08-25): main carried `af73e791a3 "Merge task/3465 into main"` (committed 10:23:34 +0100, second parent 8dd3e6fc15, itself committed 10:22:47 — the lane took the then-current tip 47s later, correctly). A steward then committed 156419b8e2 at 10:51:34, i.e. 28 min AFTER that merge had already landed. The steward measured `--is-ancestor HEAD main` -> rc=1 and concluded "Branch task/3465 is NOT on main", which read as "nothing landed" when in fact everything except two commits had.

THE DISTINGUISHING CHECKS (either one, both cheap):
  - `git merge-base main HEAD` — if this returns a commit ON your branch that is NOT the base you branched from, the branch already merged at that point.
  - `git log --oneline main..HEAD` (what is unlanded) together with `git log --oneline HEAD..main` (whether main moved / you have diverged). Two non-empty outputs = diverged, so the next landing is a true merge, not a fast-forward.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: this state strands the residual commits. `report_ready_to_merge` requires main to be an ancestor of the branch tip, which is FALSE once diverged, so the desync fast-path cannot land them; and if the task is marked done on the strength of "it already merged", the post-merge commits are lost silently while main keeps whatever defect they fixed. Check task status is still non-terminal and get a second merge enqueued.

GENERAL RULE, consistent with this topic's canonical: ancestry rc is a claim about ONE sha, never about "the work". Confirm landing by CONTENT on main (`git show main:<path>`), not by testing a ref.

STAMPED PEER under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` — a FIFTH subcase, observed on dark_factory task 4115 (merge request mr-5b8a2168, landed 2026-08-21T12:21:47Z).

THE NEW SUBCASE: `merge_status` returns `state='done'` with NEITHER `merge_sha` NOR `kind`. This is the durable-tier (retention ring / event store) response shape, and it is what the /unblock runbook's polled-done branch calls the "re-derive from git" case. On a REBASE landing that re-derivation chain dead-ends: the runbook says to run `git log main --fixed-strings --grep="Merge task/<ID> into main"`, which returns EMPTY because no merge commit was created, and then to "fall back to {note: ...}" — i.e. record NO commit SHA at all. So the runbook's own fallback silently degrades a perfectly attributable landing into a note-only provenance stamp.

ALL THREE STANDARD SIGNALS READ "NOT LANDED" while the work WAS on main:
  - `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/4115 main` -> rc=1 (not rc=0, not rc=128)
  - branch ref task/4115 still existed at its pre-merge tip 95a16d6cc4
  - exact-subject marker search -> EMPTY

THE DECISIVE CHECK, and the one to reach for: diff the branch against main restricted to the task's DECLARED files.
    git diff main task/<ID> -- <declared file 1> <declared file 2>
An EMPTY result proves the landed content is byte-identical, which is a positive proof of landing rather than the absence of a ref signal. For 4115 this was empty for both declared files while a whole-tree `git diff main task/4115` showed only ONE file (docs/prds/claimant-invariant-enforcement.md, 400 deletions) — main having a newer unrelated commit the branch lacked, which is the expected asymmetry and NOT missing work. Cross-check it with subject matching: all 7 of 4115's commit subjects were findable on main under new SHAs.

STAMPING THE PROVENANCE: use kind='found_on_main' with commit=<the top commit of the branch's landed run on main> (for 4115: 14cfe63892786012b444221e3c4784258929dc7e, found by exact-subject search for the branch TIP's subject). This is legitimate and is NOT the runbook's forbidden "eyeball `git log main --oneline | head -5` and pick a SHA": the SHA is derived by exact-subject match to the branch's own tip commit AND corroborated by the byte-identical content check. The server's only backstop (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`) passes correctly here because that commit genuinely IS on main.

OPERATIONAL TELL: a background poller watching only `--is-ancestor` will run to its ceiling and look like a stall on a SUCCESSFUL landing. On 4115 a Monitor armed on ancestry-or-worker-quiet timed out at 40 minutes while the merge had in fact completed 15 minutes earlier.

When an implementer agent's plan.json records a step commit SHA from BEFORE an inter-iteration rebase (e.g. iterations.jsonl logs commit X, then a later 'rebase' event moves the branch onto a new main), that SHA X becomes unreachable — it is not an ancestor of the post-rebase branch HEAD. Rebasing gives the same-content commit a new SHA. Bisecting regressions by `git checkout <old-logged-sha>` therefore silently compares against a stale main baseline too, conflating the rebase diff with the actual code diff under test. Always confirm ancestry first: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <branch>`; if false, find the rebased equivalent via `git log --oneline <branch>` by commit message instead of trusting the logged SHA.

claim: Rebases make commit SHAs and ancestry checks unreliable evidence; verify durable references and landed work from content or rebased equivalents instead.

Always also measure the unit on BARE main — in both the harness_cli and harness_occt cases main was already within ~100-270 lines of the warn line, so the blocked task was the occasion and not the cause, and that framing belongs in the follow-up task. Precise figure for the harness_cli case (2026-09-10 measurement, folded in from a superseded predecessor entry): bare main was at 17908/20000, only 92 lines under the warn line, before task 6162's growth crossed it.

In reify, you cannot add a new standalone `tests/<name>.rs` integration-test binary to the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler — the `_HL_CRATES` array in tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh). tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh enforces that every top-level tests/*.rs is either a sanctioned `harness_<subsystem>.rs`, one of 7 named override binaries, or grandfathered in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest; anything else fails the merge gate with `HARNESS_KLOC_CAP FAIL ... reason=unsanctioned-standalone`. The reify-kernel-occt grandfather baseline is fully drained (zero entries), so ANY new standalone binary there fails. Per docs/prds/merge-gate-compile-cost.md an over-cap harness is resolved by SPLIT into another harness_*, never by raising CAP_LINES (currently 20000 raw lines). Consequence: "give this flaky test its own test binary for isolation" is not an available fix in these crates — fix the shared state instead. [Corrected 2026-09-16 by the curator sitting per gate task #7568, checked at main 2b9b48e241: the crate set was cited as harness-layout-lib.sh:60-62; it is the `_HL_CRATES` array, at line 123 in that commit.]

members.text: reify HARNESS kLOC SPLIT — WHICH SIDE OF THE tests/common SEAM MOVES. Peer under topic reify-harness-kloc-cap-measurement. When a harness is over/near CAP_LINES and carries external_lines from a bare `mod common;`, the guard's own rule-(a) remedy text (test_harness_kloc_cap.sh, the external_lines-dominates branch) says to "move the including submodules — AND THE INCLUDE WITH THEM — into their own harness". So the movers are the tests/common CONSUMERS, and the new root takes the bare `mod common;`; the original root drops it and measures external_files=0. Verify the single-charge with harness_layout_unit_lines on BOTH roots: external_files must be 0 on one and 1 on the other — if BOTH report 1 the partition is wrong and those lines are being compiled (and charged) twice. Pick the consumer set with `grep -lE '\bcommon::'`, never a bare `grep -c common` (that over-counts prose and identifiers like `boolean_common`). Measured on task #7466 (crates/reify-kernel-occt): 19700 156 18385 56 1159 1 -> harness_occt 10785 128 10657 40 0 0 + harness_occt_measurement 9000 96 7728 16 1176 1. Bonus: the compiler then enforces the seam one-directionally, since the original root has no `mod common;` and any new `crate::common` use there fails to build.

When sizing a new `harness_<subsystem>` compile unit in reify, the real design ceiling is 18,000 lines, NOT the CAP_LINES=20000 hard cap: tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh sets WARN_PCT=90, and its _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN subset ratchet makes a unit ARRIVING in the warn set a GATING red that must be acknowledged with a new allow-row in the same diff — the opposite of a ratchet meant only to shrink. Size a new root to ~13-15k (matching landed roots harness_mechanics 14.5k / harness_langcore 14.3k), and remember the unit total includes the shared tests/common/mod.rs (391 lines) charged in full to every root that declares it.

PEER (topic reify-harness-kloc-cap-measurement), task 7543, measured 2026-09-19 in _lane-4 at 2f7cafa18a. LARGE HEADROOM IS NOT SAFETY — a single leaf can eat 1.8k+ lines of it in one module file. Every prior Section 5d crossing was a near-line base that main would have crossed anyway (harness_cli 17908, 92 under; harness_occt 17737, 263 under; harness_cli again 17954, 46 under), which is why the existing peer's advice is "measure first, and if headroom is SMALL budget for it". Counter-case: crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_compilation_surface measured 16109 at the merge-base (1891 lines under warn_at=18000, 80.5% of cap) and task 7543 alone took it to 18211 (91%) by adding +2102 lines to ONE module file, ctor_conformance_corpus_survey.rs (4850 -> 6952; #[test] count 64 -> 102). So the budget check belongs at PLAN time keyed on the SIZE OF THE PLANNED ADDITION, not only on current headroom: a task whose steps add >1.5k harness lines should measure `harness_layout_unit_lines` against its own projected delta, because there is no in-scope escape once the lines are written. Task 7543's plan had already routed the reusable half correctly (the mini-lexer went to crates/reify-test-support/src/rust_fixture_scan.rs, +419 lib / +566 tests, off-cap) and the survey CONSUMES it without re-testing its primitives — the residue that crossed the line was the generator's own second half plus its pins, which must compile .ri through reify-compiler and drive render_survey and therefore cannot move to a library crate. Relocating survey-specific test code into reify-test-support purely to get under the line would be the same cap evasion (code moved out of the module dir) that the guard's Section 5c non-vacuity check exists to detect, so the correct move is the documented one: escalate, steward files the split task, row added citing it.

To measure a reify test harness against HARNESS_KLOC_CAP, use the guard's own measure — `source tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh` then `harness_layout_unit_lines crates/<c>/tests/harness_<subsystem>.rs`, which prints `<total> <root_lines> <module_lines> <module_files> <external_lines> <external_files>`. Do NOT use `cat harness_X.rs harness_X/*.rs | wc -l`: it omits the external `tests/common/` attribution the cap actually charges (rustc compiles a separate copy of an included helper into every binary), and in a Claude Code session the cargo/skim PreToolUse wrapper intercepts multi-file `cat` and returns 0 lines. Two task descriptions have quoted wrong harness sizes from that `cat` form.

reify harness kLOC cap: `harness_layout_unit_lines` (tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh) measures a compile unit via `_harness_layout_walk_unit`, a transitive `mod`-graph BFS that follows `mod`/`#[path]` declarations ONLY and never a `use` into another crate. So hoisting shared test fixtures into a dev-dependency crate (e.g. crates/reify-test-support) removes their lines from the capped total entirely, while a `#[path]` sibling inside `harness_<subsystem>/` — or `tests/common/mod.rs`, already counted as external_lines — keeps them attributed back to the unit. Always measure with `source tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh; harness_layout_unit_lines <root.rs>`; `cat ... | wc -l` silently omits external_lines.

Reify's harness kLOC cap (tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh rule (a), CAP_LINES=20000) measures the WHOLE compile unit via harness_layout_unit_lines: root .rs + its entire harness_<subsystem>/ module dir + any files #[path]-included from outside it. So moving code BETWEEN member files of the same module dir is line-neutral for the cap — only new file headers/doc and the root's added `#[path]`+`mod` lines count. Measure with `source tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh && harness_layout_unit_lines <root.rs>` (6-field tuple: total root module module_files external external_files), never by hand-summing wc -l.

claim: Plan reify harnesses using harness_layout_unit_lines, which measures the whole compile unit—including shared and external files—and split consumers without double-charging them.

members.text: Scoped merge-verify can emit a false RED (rc=5 "no tests ran") when a task's diff touches a test file whose items are entirely marker-deselected by the subproject's pyproject addopts. `_select_subproject_pytest_targets`/`_is_collectable_test_file` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_plan.py) classify candidates purely by `test_*.py` filename with zero marker/addopts awareness, so e.g. touching orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py (all items marked `warm_lane_bash`, deselected by `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'`) narrows the leg to zero collected items. verify_plan.py's `elif collectable_tests:` branch precedes `elif role == 'task':`, so a source-only diff would have gotten FULL_SUITE — touching the deselected test file is what causes it. Diagnose with `uv run pytest <file> --collect-only -q` (expect "no tests collected (N deselected)"); the real coverage still runs via the offline lane's `-m <marker>` command. Scoper fix tracked as ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN.

Verify false-RED gotcha: the FILE_SCOPED pytest leg in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_plan.py (`elif collectable_tests:` ~:555, before `elif role == 'task':` ~:562) narrows verification to just the touched test files. If every item in those files carries a marker that orchestrator/pyproject.toml addopts deselects (e.g. `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'` at :125), the leg collects zero, pytest exits rc=5, and the task goes RED even though nothing is broken — a source-only diff would have gotten FULL_SUITE instead. Touching the deselected test file is what triggers it. Do NOT work around this by editing addopts, verify_classify.py, or verify_plan.py from inside a task lane; escalate it as a scoped-verify false-RED and merge on independently-verified green (post-merge verify runs the module's unscoped command, which does not hit the empty-selection path). Confirmed on task 3292; the real fix is ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN.

GOTCHA: a task whose only touched .py under a module prefix is a test file whose items are ALL marker-deselected by that module's pyproject addopts gets a scoped verify TEST leg that collects ZERO items -> pytest rc=5 "no tests ran" -> RED, even when the change is entirely correct.

Mechanism. verify_plan.py `_derive_module_runs`, the `elif collectable_tests:` branch, file-scopes the module's test_command to the touched test files. `classify_file` is purely PATH-based (name starts with `test_` => COLLECTABLE_TEST) and has no notion of marker deselection. Note the adjacent branch: a SOURCE-only diff at role='task' gets FULL_SUITE — it is specifically touching the deselected test file that narrows the leg to nothing.

Do NOT try to fix this in the classifier. verify_classify.py `_classify_opaque` pins it: "INVARIANT (task 1852): pytest rc=5 is intentionally classified RED here ... A real test target that unexpectedly collects zero tests must stay RED so the merge gate catches 'tests vanished' regressions — the data-module false-RED is fixed in the SCOPING layer, not here." Task 1852 already closed one instance of this class (test-data modules) at the scoping layer; marker deselection is a second instance the path-based predicate cannot see.

First live instance: orchestrator/pyproject.toml addopts gained `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'` (task 3349, 2026-08-01), moving the bucket to the offline warm-lane-bash lane. Task 3292 was the first task to touch orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py afterwards and redded on 0 items while its real coverage was green (214 passed / 0 failed standalone; 12/12 under `-m warm_lane_bash`; lint + type green). Escalated as esc-3292-1.

Diagnosing it: `uv run pytest <the touched test file> --collect-only -q` inside the module. "no tests collected (N deselected)" confirms it; compare against `uv run pytest tests/ --collect-only -q`. The verify log signature is `16 workers [0 items]` / `no tests ran`, categorised unknown_test_failure, with lint and type both green.

There is NO per-task or per-module scoping override — nothing in docs/task-authoring.md, nothing scope-related in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/defaults.yaml, and no rc=5 retry/widen anywhere in orchestrator/src or shared/src. So a dispatched agent cannot satisfy an obligation like the one at plans/warm-lane-infra-repatriation-prd.md:237 ("leaves must run `-m warm_lane_bash` explicitly on their own verify legs"). Escalate rather than improvising; re-enabling the bucket in addopts would break the addopts<->lane biconditional pinned by orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_bucket_placement.py.

Adding a `-m 'not <marker>'` deselection to a package's pyproject.toml addopts creates a latent verify false-RED: verify_plan._derive_module_runs' arm-4 file-scopes a test-only diff to the touched test files, so a task whose sole touched .py under that prefix is a fully marker-deselected test file emits a pytest run that collects 0 items, returns rc=5, and is classified RED by verify_classify._classify_opaque (the deliberate task-1852 invariant). Note the asymmetry: a SOURCE-only diff under the same prefix takes the role=='task' arm and correctly gets FULL_SUITE — it is touching the deselected test file that narrows the leg to nothing. Task 3494 fixes this in the scoping layer (static addopts `-m` parse + module-level `pytestmark` AST match -> widen to owning-module FULL_SUITE), never in the classifier.

A dark-factory task whose only collectable .py change is a test file wholly deselected by its project's pytest `addopts -m` expression gets a scoped verify command that collects 0 items and exits rc=5 ("no tests ran") — RED no matter what the task's code does. Concretely: orchestrator/pyproject.toml sets `addopts = "... -m 'not warm_lane_bash'"` (landed by task 3349 in merge 8f3f0e4c89), so `pytest orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py` collects "no tests collected (12 deselected)" while `pytest ... -m warm_lane_bash` collects 12 and passes. Diagnose this by re-running the failing verify target with `--collect-only -q` before touching any code; the fix belongs at the verify scoping layer or the module test_command, not in the task's files.

STEWARD DISPOSITION of the marker-deselected-test-file false-RED (esc-3292-1, 2026-08-01). Complements the diagnosis entry b1ee7610-5ef4-4639-8da4-84cc567221bf, which covers the mechanism and how to recognise the signature; this entry covers what to DO once recognised.

That escalation was resolved action='resume', resolution_class='benign' after the steward independently reproduced and confirmed the debugger's diagnosis. The signature — verify TEST leg reporting `[0 items]` / "no tests ran", categorised unknown_test_failure, with LINT and TYPE green — is an ACCEPTABLE false-RED when the checklist below passes. It is not a defect to chase, and the agent that hits it should escalate rather than reach outside its lock scope.

ACCEPT CHECKLIST (the reusable part):
1. Reproduce the empty collection: `uv run pytest <touched test file> --collect-only -q` inside the module, expecting "no tests collected (N deselected)". Contrast with the unscoped module command to show the suite itself is non-empty.
2. Confirm scope: `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` is confined to the task's declared metadata.files.
3. RUN THE TASK'S REAL COVERAGE DIRECTLY and record exact counts — the verify leg never ran it. For warm-lane that means the bash suites plus `uv run pytest -m warm_lane_bash`.
4. Accept on that evidence and send the branch to the merge queue with verified_green=True. Post-merge verify runs the module's UNSCOPED command, so it does not re-hit the empty-selection path that produced the escalation.

Worked example, task 3292: gc suite 214 passed / 0 failed (matching its own ASSERT_FLOORS bump 198->214, i.e. re-measured rather than padded to absorb a red), gc-sweep suite 86 passed / 0 failed, test_lane_state_lib.py 68 passed including the TestProtectGlobFallbackDrift INV-5 pin.

The structural fix is FILED, not dropped: ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN (high) — widen the FILE_SCOPED pytest branch in verify_plan.py to the owning-module full suite when all targets would be marker-deselected, mirroring the shape task 1852 used for test-data modules, preserving both the rc=5-stays-RED invariant and the addopts<->lane biconditional. Its deferred design question: detect "all targets deselected" without paying for a --collect-only probe on every verify plan. Until it lands, expect the remaining warm-lane leaves (δ2, ε, and the task-3298 re-measurement) to red identically and handle them with the checklist above.

claim: When scoped verification touches a test file whose tests are all deselected by pytest addopts, it can falsely RED with rc=5; confirm empty collection, run the real coverage, and escalate for a scoping-layer fix.

members.text: Reify stdlib builtins (`reify_stdlib::eval_builtin(name,args)->Value`) have NO diagnostic sink. Runtime diagnostics from a builtin are emitted POST-call at the reify-expr layer: the `FunctionCall` `_=>` arm (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~502-525) calls helper fns `stackup_diagnose(name,args)->Option<Diagnostic>` / `fea_diagnose(...)` and pushes into `ctx.diagnostics: Option<&RefCell<Vec<Diagnostic>>>` — but ONLY when the builtin returned `Value::Undef`. Emitting a warning on a SUCCESSFUL (non-Undef) builtin return (e.g. W_FlexureYielding, which still returns a valid joint) requires adding a new success-path hook in that arm. The sink ultimately surfaces as `eval_result.diagnostics`.

reify-stdlib `eval_builtin`/`eval_dynamics` builtins return only a `Value` (no diagnostics channel). The ONLY way a stdlib builtin emits a Diagnostic is the `diagnose(name,args)->Option<Diagnostic>` hook pattern: define it in the module (e.g. stackup.rs:280, fea.rs:416, geometry.rs:1168), re-export from reify-stdlib/src/lib.rs as `<x>_diagnose`, and call it in reify-expr/src/lib.rs `emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics` (~L1263) which fires on the `Value::Undef` result path. Note: `@optimized` ComputeNode trampolines (reify-eval, e.g. inverse_dynamics) bypass this hook — their `undef_outcome()` returns empty diagnostics, so a builtin's `diagnose` hook only covers the body-inline/fallback eval path, not the trampoline path.

reify diagnose-wiring architecture: `crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs`'s `emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics` (~lib.rs:1560) is the consolidated home for post-Undef, `Option<Diagnostic>`-returning builtin classifiers — stackup_diagnose, fea_diagnose, geometry_diagnose, and (task 4461) tolerancing_diagnose — each a one-line `if let Some(diag) = reify_stdlib::X_diagnose(name, args) { sink.borrow_mut().push(diag); }` arm gated on `matches!(result, Value::Undef)`. Classifiers that return `Vec<Diagnostic>` and fire on BOTH success+Undef paths (dfm_diagnose, flexure_diagnose) instead get their own `emit_*` fn called unconditionally from the FunctionCall arm. `reify eval` renders eval-time `result.diagnostics` to stderr via `cmd_eval` (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:~754, `eprintln!("{}: {}", severity, message)`), so wiring a classifier into the EvalContext sink is necessary AND sufficient for the user-visible stderr diagnostic — no CLI change needed.

Reify runtime (eval-time) diagnostics flow: EvalContext (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:27-50) carries `diagnostics: Option<&RefCell<Vec<Diagnostic>>>`; emitters use `if let Some(sink)=ctx.diagnostics { sink.borrow_mut().push(diag) }` (see sampled.rs:94-101 FieldOutOfBounds, interp.rs). Engine::eval drains the sink into EvalResult.diagnostics (reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs ~2097). cmd_eval (reify-cli/src/main.rs:571-617) prints each diagnostic to stderr as `{severity}: {message}` and returns ExitCode::FAILURE if any is Severity::Error. Note: stdlib `eval_builtin(name,args)` does NOT receive EvalContext, so a builtin cannot emit diagnostics itself — emission must happen at the eval_expr call site (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:495). The compiler does NOT error on unknown free-function names (reify-compiler/src/expr.rs ~1261-1278 emits at most a Warning), so stdlib builtins like stackup_rss/contributor are callable from .ri without compiler registration.

In reify, a reify-stdlib builtin CANNOT emit a diagnostic directly: `eval_builtin(name: &str, args: &[Value]) -> Value` takes no EvalContext or sink. The only shipped route from a stdlib rejection to a user-visible Error is the post-Undef classifier pattern — the builtin returns `Value::Undef`, a pure `diagnose(name, &[Value]) -> Option<Diagnostic>` in the same module re-derives the cause, and `emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs pushes it (that helper is gated on BOTH `result == Value::Undef` and `ctx.diagnostics` being attached). A reader that COERCES to a default instead of returning Undef is therefore structurally unreachable by the hook and emits nothing. Note the Field-interception match arms earlier in reify-expr's FunctionCall arm (von_mises, principal_stresses, max_shear, safety_factor, fn_field, from_samples, restrict) short-circuit BEFORE the eval_builtin catch-all, so they reach none of the diagnostic hooks and need their own emission site.

Reify runtime stdlib diagnostics (the *_diagnose hooks drained from reify-expr's EvalContext runtime sink) carry no cell name or span, and joints at runtime are anonymous Value::Maps — so a diagnostic that must "name the offending joint/bind" has to put the locator in its own message text (e.g. `bindings[i]`, joint kind + raw axis); the --explain-undef note separately names the undef cell. DimensionedArgRejected messages should be rendered via reify_ir::arg_acceptance::ArgRejection::message (its documented single wording owner), as geometry.rs does.

claim: Because stdlib builtins lack a diagnostic sink, runtime diagnostics must be emitted by reify-expr, with hooks wired to the relevant result and execution paths.

members.text: In fused-memory tests, a sync MagicMock's assert_not_called() will fail the repo-wide style check (tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py, task 525) if any assert_not_awaited() appears in the SAME test function — the checker flags the mix without knowing one of the mocks is sync. Fix by asserting mock.call_count == 0 for the sync mock instead of converting it to an async-style helper.

fused-memory's AsyncMock assertion-style convention (task 525) is enforced by tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py::TestRealTestsDirectoryIsClean, which shells out to scripts/check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py over the WHOLE fused-memory/tests/ directory. A violation you introduce in your own new test file therefore shows up as a failure in that unrelated file, and a targeted `uv run pytest tests/test_your_file.py -k ...` run will never surface it — only a full `uv run pytest` (or running that checker file) does. Rule it enforces: within one test function, don't mix assert_not_called() and assert_not_awaited(); use assert_not_awaited() for every AsyncMock, including AsyncMock attributes on a MagicMock (e.g. conftest's make_graph_mock sets both .query and .ro_query as AsyncMocks).

In fused-memory/tests/, mixing `assert_not_called()` and `assert_not_awaited()` within a SINGLE test function is rejected by the meta-test tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py (task 525 convention) — it reports the offending file:line and fails the whole suite. Either style alone is fine; only co-occurrence in one function trips it. Fix by converting every such assertion in that function to `assert_not_awaited()`. This is easy to hit when a new test asserts across several collaborators at once (e.g. mem0.add + durable_queue.enqueue + journal.log_mem0_intent), and it will NOT show up in a targeted `pytest -k` run of your own test class — only in a full-suite run.

The task-525 AsyncMock assertion-style convention is enforced at TWO different scopes in fused-memory: hooks/project-checks runs scripts/check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py over the STAGED DIFF only, but tests/test_check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py::TestRealTestsDirectoryIsClean re-runs it over the WHOLE tests/ directory. So a test file arriving intact from an older branch (cherry-pick, or a long-lived branch predating the convention) is audited in full and can turn verify red even though the pre-commit hook was silent — on a task branch hooks/pre-commit exits 0 without running project-checks at all. Reproduce locally with `python3 scripts/check_asyncmock_assertion_style.py tests/` (stdlib-only, no uv needed).

claim: Within one test function, avoid mixing `assert_not_called()` and `assert_not_awaited()`; the repository-wide style checker rejects the combination.

members.text:
[CORRECTED 2026-08-23 — see mem 48e2b53d-dc75-4f5a-83f4-4ce14ad504ea] The "STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out below is NOT reliably sanctioned: two independent review blocks (task 3465 — skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md + OPERATIONS.md marker spans, runtime-derived via stdlib ast, loud-failing extractors, STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline; and task 3544, mem0 3c294ce3 — mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test) were both blocked and mandated for deletion by reviewer_comprehensive despite following this carve-out exactly. The reviewer keys on the ASSERTION TARGET being doc prose, a string literal, or an introspected name — not on whether the value is runtime-derived or marker-anchored. Before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's own package already asserts those tokens against real produced output (often making the guard redundant with existing behavioural coverage). Treat the "sanctioned alternative" paragraph below as historical context, not current planning guidance.

---original content---
dark-factory enforces a repo-wide norm AGAINST pytest tests that pin documentation prose, and it is written into the test files themselves: tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_service_files.py:1263, tests/scripts/test_ruff_format_policy.py:48-51, tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py:38-40 and scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py:33-40 each carry a docstring forbidding extension into a wording pin, orchestrator/tests/test_roles_ancestry_check.py:21-36 rejects a proposed "grep skills/*/SKILL.md" test by name as a documentation meta-test, and one such prose pin was actually deleted in review (task 3802 remediation, recorded at test_design_invariants_consistency.py:1167-1170). The sanctioned alternative when a doc genuinely must not drift is a STRUCTURAL drift guard: derive the expected value from live code/config at runtime, anchor the doc side on an HTML-comment marker pair (the lint-command-mirror convention in CONTRIBUTING.md), unit-test the extractor against hand-written fixture markdown rather than the real doc, and make the extractor raise loudly instead of returning empty. Consequence for planning: a prose-only change to a skills/*/SKILL.md is correctly planned as impl-only with no test step — commits 0824cae7a3, 812e186780 and a322d65007 are all single-file, test-free SKILL.md amendments.

CORRECTION to dark-factory memories 48e2b53d and b80b78c4 about the doc-prose guard prohibition, measured 2026-08-29/30 while ruling task 4666. Two things those memories get wrong or incomplete. (1) COUNT: they record TWO reviewer deletion mandates (tasks 3465, 3544). The verified count is ELEVEN landed deletions of prose-pinning test modules/blocks between 2026-04-24 and 2026-08-25, all on main: 4ed37e9367, d53cd62b68, 3e8d369b24, 10978d1ddc, 9427896b8c, fabba102c7, d733c1bdc7, 9c73deb78d, cb6d74359e, c3f8fa0b35, ba7fcffdbc. (2) CAUSE: 48e2b53d concludes the reviewer "keys on the ASSERTION TARGET being doc prose, not on whether the oracle is runtime-derived or marker-anchored". That is not the whole variable — it is CONFOUNDED with redundancy. The operative ground stated in ba7fcffdbc (the task-3465 revert, authored by Leo himself) is "It exercised no runtime behaviour", and the same commit names the behavioural coverage that replaced it (fused-memory/tests/test_scope_violation_escalator.py). Task 3544's second review round likewise rejected on redundancy with shared/tests/test_task_transitions.py, after an EARLIER round had explicitly called its set-equality assertion "a real machine-checkable invariant, not a prose pin". So "targets doc prose" and "redundant with existing behavioural coverage" co-occur in every cited case and were never disentangled. Superseded by INV-10 `guards-exercise-behaviour`, which states the rule in terms of the confound-free variable.

PEER under topic `doc-prose-guard-policy-corrections` (task 5247 review, esc reviewer_comprehensive/test-quality-doc-prose-pin, fix commit 733518914c). A SHAPE the existing peers do not name: the MARKER-PROXIMITY guard, and where it sits relative to the REWORD TEST.

THE SHAPE. tests/scripts/test_reify_closure_staleness_sweep_retired.py sweeps the tracked tree for two retired tokens and excludes an allowlist. Five docs are permitted to keep a token because they record the retirement. To make "records the retirement" checkable rather than taken on trust, the guard asserted that every surviving mention sat within RETIREMENT_MARKER_WINDOW=3 lines of a marker in RETIREMENT_MARKERS=('task 5247','retired'). Deliberately minimal: no sentence wording, no headings, one word in a window.

WHY IT IS STILL A PROSE PIN, and how the reword test reads it. 0f548f86's discriminator (fully reword the sentence, keep the identifier — a wording pin goes red, a referential-integrity guard stays green) LOOKS like it clears this: reword freely and the guard stays green as long as the word survives. But rewording is exactly what deletes it — "no longer runs; removed 2026-09-09" describes the retirement perfectly and goes RED, while "this retired approach is why the sweep runs at 04:30" is live operator prose and passes. It pins the presence of one English word near a line; the window and the small token tuple make it a WEAK pin, not a structural one. GENERALISATION: a proximity/presence assertion over a natural-language word is the same defect as a substring pin, just with a larger blast radius of false negatives — "I only assert ONE word" is not a carve-out. Sharper phrasing of the reword test for this case: ask whether a competent rewrite that PRESERVES THE MEANING can go red. If yes, it pins wording.

THE SANCTIONED SUBSTITUTE, which is what landed. Keep the allowlist dict; delete the marker mechanism. The per-entry WRITTEN REASON is the audit record that the file mentions the thing only historically — human-audited at the moment someone adds an entry, the same shape as tests/scripts/test_atomic_write_regrowth.py::_ALLOWED_RENAMERS. The machine-checked part stays where it is real: every file NOT on the allowlist must carry zero mentions. "Is this exemption honest?" is not mechanizable over prose, and trying to mechanize it is what produced the defect. Also rewrite the comment introducing the dict — the original justified it entirely by the deleted mechanism ("has to be CHECKABLE ... within N lines of a marker"), and leaving it would claim a property the module no longer establishes (same move 461d1a96 records for the comment above a deleted pin block).

THE ENTRY POINT WORTH FLAGGING: the PLAN asked for it. The architect's step said, in good faith, "the allowlist is not enough on its own — make it structural and cheap: assert each surviving mention sits within a small window of a retirement marker." The policy is codified in the ARCHITECT role rules too (roles.py rule 5), so this is a plan that violated its own author's rules and then cost a blocking review round. An implementer executing a step that asks for an assertion over documentation text should check it against the codified policy BEFORE writing it, and escalate the step rather than implement it — the plan is not an exception to the policy.

CORRECTION to the "sanctioned STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out recorded in mem0 b80b78c4 (which cites tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py and its HTML-comment-marker convention as the approved way to pin a doc against live code). That carve-out is NOT reliably sanctioned and should not be planned as a safe pattern. On task 3465 an architect followed it exactly — bare `<!-- name:begin/end -->` marker spans in skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md and OPERATIONS.md, values derived from live producer constants via stdlib `ast` rather than hardcoded, loud-failing extractors that raise instead of returning empty, explicit STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline — and reviewer_comprehensive still blocked the whole 769-line module as a documentation/introspection meta-test and mandated deletion. That is the second such data point: task 3544 (mem0 3c294ce3) had a mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test deleted despite a live in-code oracle. Two independent blocks means the reviewer treats "derived from code at runtime" and "anchored on markers" as insufficient — what it keys on is that the ASSERTION TARGET is doc prose, a module-level/function-body string literal, or a parameter name recovered by introspection. Practical rule for architects: before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's OWN package already asserts those tokens against real produced OUTPUT; on 3465 fused-memory/tests/test_scope_violation_escalator.py already called the real report_rejection() and asserted category/agent_role/severity on the escalation JSON that landed on disk, so the entire guard was redundant with existing behaviour coverage. Same held for its two "premise guard" tests: escalation/tests/test_server.py, escalation/tests/test_queue.py and orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py already cover the granted_files grant end-to-end, so an introspection check on the parameter NAME was both redundant and strictly weaker. Also: when deleting such a guard, the doc-side marker spans and any prose sentence claiming the tokens are "pinned by <test file>" must be deleted with it — a SKILL.md is read verbatim as an LLM system prompt, so a dangling reference to a deleted test tells the executing agent a mechanism exists when it does not.

PEER stamped topic=doc-prose-guard-policy-corrections (per canonical 2821a740's accretion warning). REFINES 92bfe17f ("one operand of an anti-drift assertion must be READ FROM the source of truth at test time") to the case it does not reach: a vocabulary with NO code side at all.

MEASURED on dark_factory task 5723 (blocking reviewer_comprehensive finding, 2026-09-22). tests/scripts/test_shadow_ruling_doc_contract.py added `_CLOSURE_FORMS = frozenset({"owned-successor", "explicit-wont-fix"})` and asserted `documented == _CLOSURE_FORMS` against a marked span in docs/escalation-standing-policy.md. The class it guards is a Leo policy ruling with "no code path changes" by decision, so there is no frozenset to read the expectation off — and the test's own docstring conceded this, arguing the constant "IS the specification". That argument is the defect, not the exemption: 92bfe17f's rule cannot be satisfied when no source of truth exists in code, which means the assertion should not exist, NOT that the test may become the source of truth. A document that claims authority over a vocabulary plus a test constant restating it is two normative homes (heuristic 11, SPOT), and the test-file copy is the one invisible to every reader of the document.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, cheap to apply to any doc-contract guard: for each token in the expected set, name the symbol it resolves to. If every token resolves (a frozenset, an enum, a dataclass field list), the equality is a real two-way drift guard — keep it, and read the operand live. If NONE resolves, the guard's stated failure mode is ABLATION (silent deletion of a ruling from one of its homes), and ablation is fully covered by the marked-span extractor succeeding plus a non-emptiness check. The set equality then buys only locked editorial detail and a forced test edit on any future amendment that adds a token — turning a documentation change into a code change.

THE FIX SHAPE, and the precedent to cite: delete the constant and the equality; keep the begin/end span extractor (which already fails loudly on absent/duplicate/unterminated/inverted) and assert only that the span carries at least one bullet of the expected form. This is what tests/scripts/test_line_pin_policy.py::_marked_body's callers do — "asserts NOTHING about the WORDING inside the markers". Do NOT substitute a looser substring pin, a regex, a length/count bound, or the same tokens relocated into a fixture, a parametrize list, an `ids=` label or a comment. What MAY stay hand-written is the MARKER SLUG itself (`<!-- <slug>:begin`), which is a structural anchor, not a vocabulary — exactly as `_MARKER_BEGIN` is in that precedent.

KEEP THE NAMED ABLATION TEST even when its remaining assertions are a subset of a sibling's preamble. Heuristic 10 (redundant, uniform enforcement): it is the named twin of the other home's guard, mirroring the (a)/(b) pair in test_line_pin_policy.py, and folding it into the sibling makes the ablation guard vanish silently the next time that sibling is narrowed. Rename it if its name pins the dropped count ("...enumerates_both_..." -> "...carries_the_..."). And prove the loosened guard still bites: empty the bullets, confirm RED; delete the span, confirm RED on the extractor's own message; restore before committing.

Do NOT build, keep, or HARDEN tests that assert on docstring/comment PROSE in dark-factory. Codified policy at three enforcement points, all introduced together in commit 7abff876d7, all verified verbatim in-repo on 2026-08-20:

1. ARCHITECT rule 5 "Test scope — skip documentation meta-tests" (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py): do NOT plan test steps that assert on __doc__ strings, docstring prose, comment contents, or module-level string literals, or that "Grep source files for 'did the author mention X' strings". "One-line `assert Foo.__doc__` existence checks inside an API-surface contract test are fine; 50-line substring/regex pins of prose are not."
2. REVIEWER_COMPREHENSIVE (same file): flag as `blocking` any test whose assertions target __doc__ strings, module-level string literals, comment contents, or the prose of another test file. Recommended fix: DELETE the meta-test; if documentation drift is a real concern, fix the source doc once and move on. Explicitly: 'Do NOT propose "harden the docstring-pin regex" as a follow-up — that just deepens the hole.'
3. TRIAGE SKIP rules (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/triage.py): documentation-only wording fixes, AND "Docstring-pin hardening suggestions" — any suggestion to strengthen a regex/substring/AST walk used to assert documentation wording. "The right fix is to delete the meta-test, not to harden it."

THE TRAP, recorded because a steward fell into it on task 4240 and had to reverse itself: when such a guard is found to have a coverage hole (there, a start-anchored regex that missed every path-qualified citation, seeing 45 citations where 64 existed), hardening the regex feels like the obviously-correct engineering fix — it is concrete, measurable and satisfying, and a reviewer's "just delete it" reads like an opinion to be weighed. It is the specifically-banned remedy. A coverage hole in a prose meta-test is evidence for DELETING it, not improving it: the policy's own rationale is that these "frequently ship subtle regex/substring bugs that let real regressions slip through", so finding exactly such a bug CONFIRMS the policy rather than creating an exception to it.

A SECOND ERROR FROM THE SAME EPISODE, worth generalising: do not argue from a NAME-pattern census to a claim about assertion content. "~281 test classes match Test*(Drift|SelfContainment|Completeness|Guard|Contract), therefore prose guards are conventional here" is invalid — those assert on structured config/import/AST drift, not prose. Two guards cited as precedent carry written prohibitions against extension to prose: tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py ("about surrounding prose, and must not be extended to") and tests/scripts/test_ruff_format_policy.py ("It asserts nothing about prose ... and must not be extended to"). main carries zero prose-asserting meta-tests in .py source, and several have been deleted (e.g. 099b1f25cd on task 4236, the near-duplicate sibling of 4240).

CORRECT RESPONSE to documentation drift here: fix the source doc once, at source, and move on — what task 4126 did. Do not build a guard; do not file a follow-up to harden one. Before defending any prose-asserting test against a reviewer, read these three policy sites first: the reviewer is executing codified policy, not offering a preference.

claim: Dark-factory policy forbids tests that pin documentation wording; delete or avoid them rather than hardening them, and rely only on nonredundant checks of real behavior or structural ablation.

members.text: FABRICATED CITATION PROPAGATED THROUGH THREE RECORDS AND WAS HARDENED AT EACH HOP. reify esc-6508-1 (severity CRITICAL) asserted "query timeouts caused by the missing indexes", resting on a documented 1000ms-TIMEOUT causal chain. Verified 2026-08-25: that chain does not exist — zero occurrences of 1000/timeout/timed-out in docs/prds/falkordb-index-provisioning.md, and the string appears nowhere in the dark-factory repo. A recon Stage 2 run (cd53b227, 2026-08-23) INVENTED the citation in dark_factory 3708's `details`; reify task 6508 and then esc-6508-1 hardened it into a causal claim at CRITICAL severity, stripping the hedge the reify canonical memory (12cb03b2) had correctly kept. MEASURED REALITY: reify search runs 0.79-2.83s over 5 queries; a full 24,146-node x 1536-dim cosine scan is 205ms; unindexed label scans are 10-16ms. The real mechanism is FalkorDB's GRAPH.CONFIG TIMEOUT=1000 hard ceiling crossed under contention on a server holding 9+ graphs — missing indexes are a CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, not the cause, and landing 3708 does NOT move the ceiling so it is not guaranteed to eliminate the timeouts. Corrections landed 2026-08-25: dark_factory 3708's details carry an ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION section, and reify canonical 12cb03b2 gained linked child amendment 6797560d. LESSON: a recon-authored citation in a task's `details` is not evidence; check that the cited document actually says it before escalating on it.

OPEN INFRA GAP (surfaced 2026-08-18 by reconciliation run 4c16873a, Stage 1) — the reify Graphiti graph reports a near-empty index set, and until now nothing in either memory store tracked it.

OBSERVATION (as reported by Stage 1's own index_health probe, not independently re-queried against FalkorDB by this record): healthy=false, expected_total=38, actual_total=2 — i.e. 36 of 38 expected indices absent. The missing set spans essentially every FULLTEXT and RANGE index Graphiti provisions: Entity(name/group_id/summary FULLTEXT; name/group_id/created_at RANGE), Episodic(content/source/source_description/group_id FULLTEXT; uuid/created_at/valid_at/group_id RANGE), and RELATES_TO(fact/name/group_id FULLTEXT; valid_at/invalid_at/expired_at RANGE).

LIKELY IMPACT if real: search recall and latency on this graph. Graphiti's hybrid retrieval leans on the FULLTEXT indices for its BM25/keyword arm and on the RANGE indices for temporal filtering (valid_at/invalid_at); without them, keyword-arm results degrade and temporal predicates fall back to scans. This is a plausible contributing factor to the persistently low graphiti relevance_score values seen in reify search results, though that link is NOT established here.

OPEN QUESTION — VERIFY BEFORE REMEDIATING: whether expected_total=38 is the correct expectation for this deployment at all. reify's graph is backed by FalkorDB, not Neo4j (FalkorDB at redis://localhost:6379, graph name == group_id == project_id, i.e. literally 'reify'; see the sibling procedural record on direct FalkorDB/Graphiti graph surgery). FalkorDB's index DDL is not Neo4j's, so a probe whose expected set was authored against Neo4j semantics could be reporting missing indices that this backend never creates and does not need — making healthy=false a probe-side false positive rather than a real provisioning gap. Determine which it is BEFORE running any provisioning: (a) query the live index set directly via GRAPH.RO_QUERY (read-only, per the established safety discipline) and compare against what the FalkorDB driver actually provisions, and (b) confirm whether the probe's expected-set constant is backend-conditional. [SUPERSEDED — see STATUS CORRECTION (3) at the end of this record, added 2026-08-18 by recon run 4c16873a Stage 2: build_indices_and_constraints is KNOWN-HARMFUL on FalkorDB — it silently drops composite index properties when any listed property is already indexed (FalkorDB rejects the composite CREATE INDEX wholesale and swallows the error text). The correct provisioner is dark_factory task 3707's diff-then-create ensure_indices, reached via task 3708's wiring; do NOT run build_indices_and_constraints against this graph.]

ROUTING: the fix almost certainly lives on the dark_factory / fused-memory side (shared server, per-graph index provisioning), NOT in reify's source tree — route any tracking task there rather than filing it as reify source work. Note also that the same question applies to every other graph on this shared server, so treat this as potentially fleet-wide rather than reify-specific.

=== [2026-08-18, Stage 2 of the SAME run 4c16873a] STATUS CORRECTION — ALREADY OWNED; DO NOT FILE NEW WORK; DO NOT RUN build_indices_and_constraints ===

The two open items above are now settled against the live dark_factory task tree. Three corrections to the text above:

(1) THE OPEN QUESTION IS ESSENTIALLY ANSWERED — the expectation is backend-derived, not a Neo4j-shaped constant. dark_factory task 3706 (status=done), "Expected-index-set derivation + list_indices normalizer (FalkorDB index provisioning alpha)", derives the expected set by PARSING graphiti_core's own statement strings via get_range_indices(provider) / get_fulltext_indices(provider) rather than hand-maintaining a list, precisely so it cannot drift from the backend. That task's description ALSO records the exact trap this record hypothesised, as a measured gotcha: GraphProvider is a plain Enum, not a str-Enum, so GraphProvider.FALKORDB == 'fa [cut]

FalkorDB index provisioning: build_indices_and_constraints() is KNOWN-HARMFUL and must NOT be run against the reify (or any) graph. Its composite CREATE INDEX over (uuid, group_id, name, created_at) is rejected WHOLESALE by FalkorDB when any ONE of those properties is already indexed ("Attribute 'uuid' is already indexed") — which is exactly the 2-index starting state every graph on this server is in — and falkordb_driver.py SWALLOWS that error, so it REPORTS SUCCESS while creating nothing. The correct entry point is ensure_indices (per-property RANGE + verbatim FULLTEXT) at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/graphiti_client.py:4065; it is landed on dark-factory main but called from NOWHERE. Wiring it is dark_factory task 3708 (leaf gamma of docs/prds/falkordb-index-provisioning.md), and its gating is DELIBERATE per PRD D10 — restoring BM25 reorders retrieval for every consumer while 3659 concurrently retires 2 of 4 briefing queries, and the current degraded index state is protected evidence for open esc-3375-1 / dark_factory task 3673. A hand rebuild destroys that evidence baseline. Verified 2026-08-25.

claim: Verify evidence, backend behavior, and existing ownership before escalating or changing index provisioning; unvalidated claims and fixes can mislead or cause harm.

members.text: When auditing dark-factory task state, read the sqlite store at `<project_root>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` — NOT `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json`. The JSON file is a dead legacy artifact: it is frozen at max task id 1142, last written 2026-05-02, while the live db held 3457 rows on 2026-08-02. Auditing the JSON silently under-reports and yields false negatives rather than an error. Always open it read-only via `sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)` so a sweep can never touch the running orchestrator's live WAL db. Live columns: tag, id, title, description, details, test_strategy, status, priority, metadata, updated_at, claimant_run_id, heartbeat_at, candidate_key.

STAMPED PEER under topic `tasks-json-is-a-stale-mirror` (canonical 64ae84c2). Two updates the canonical does not carry.

(1) THE FILE IS GONE, NOT MERELY STALE. The canonical reads as though `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` still exists and is just old. As of 2026-08-30 it does NOT exist in /home/leo/src/dark-factory: `/bin/ls -la .taskmaster/tasks/` returns only `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-shm`, `tasks.db-wal`, and `test -e tasks.json` reports ABSENT. It was retired at the 2026-05-06 SQLite cutover and DELETED 2026-08-25 (date independently recorded at `.claude/skills/hotspot-survey/project.md`). Consequence for agents: a read of that path now FAILS LOUDLY instead of silently returning a 4-month-old answer — strictly better than the esc-4659-5 near-miss, where task 4659's architect read it, got a stale answer with NO error, and recorded a false "owned by no live task" claim. If such a file ever REAPPEARS it is a restored backup or a foreign artifact; do not read it and do not migrate from it.

(2) NEVER JUDGE tasks.db's FRESHNESS BY ITS OWN mtime. `tasks.db` runs in WAL mode. Committed writes land in `tasks.db-wal` and the main file's mtime is only touched at checkpoint, so it can lag live writes arbitrarily. Any code or eyeball comparing "which is newer, the db or some other file" must take max(mtime) across `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-wal` AND `tasks.db-shm`. A db-only stat will report an actively-written live store as older than a months-dead snapshot. This is not hypothetical: it is precisely the misread that would let `fused-memory/scripts/migrate_tasks_json_to_sqlite.py --replace` overwrite the live ~30 MB / 4600-row store with a 1152-task May snapshot (task 4682 adds the guard).

Per the canonical: quote no row counts as durable fact — measure them yourself. Open read-only (`file:...?mode=ro` URI). The two zero-byte decoys named in the canonical still apply.

`.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` in dark-factory is a STALE MIRROR and must not be used for task queries. It parses cleanly and holds ~1117 tasks, but contains NONE of the 3000-series ids. The authoritative store is `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` (~3584 rows), with tables `tasks`, `dependencies`, `id_counters`.

This is specifically dangerous because it biases toward the PERMISSIVE answer: a "does anything depend on task N?" query against the json returns "NONE" for every modern task, which reads exactly like a clearance to cancel or re-point it. Caught 2026-08-05 while cancelling task 3104 — the json check reported "no dependents (verified over 1117 tasks)", and the reassuring row count in that message was itself the tell that the corpus was wrong.

Correct probe:
  sqlite3.connect('file:.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
  select * from dependencies where cast(task_id as text)='<id>' or cast(depends_on as text)='<id>'

Sanity-check any task-store query by first asserting a known modern id is present in the rows parsed.

Corpus-forensics: data/orchestrator/runs.db carries NO task metadata — its tables are account_events, events, invocations, runs, scheduler_state, sqlite_sequence, task_results and none has a `metadata` column. So metadata keys (files, files_tagged_at, done_provenance, routing, ...) are answerable ONLY from <root>/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db (column tasks.metadata, JSON), never from runs.db; runs.db answers event/timing/cost questions only. Corollary for cross-project sweeps: <root>/data/runs.db is a 0-byte decoy (confirmed in dark-factory, autopilot-video, pump-web-ui, solar-challenge-platform) — the real event store is <root>/data/orchestrator/runs.db, which scripts/audit_wiped_metadata_files.py:560 runs_db_path() already returns, so import that rather than spelling the path yourself. Measured 2026-08-20 during task 4525 planning. See also the canonical `tasks-json-is-a-stale-mirror` entry for the tasks.db read-only recipe.

GOTCHA (dark_factory, confirmed 2026-08-12): `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` is a STALE artifact — last written 2026-05-02 — and parsing it returns "task not found" for every id filed since. The LIVE task store is the sqlite database `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db`. Two other plausible-looking paths, `.taskmaster/tasks.db` and `data/orchestrator/tasks.db`, are both ZERO BYTES and are decoys.

USEFUL QUERY PATTERN. To get statuses plus real dependency edges plus each dep's own status for a set of tasks in ONE call — far cheaper than N get_task calls, which each return multi-KB descriptions:

  sqlite3 -header .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db "
  select t.id, t.status, t.priority,
   (select group_concat(d.depends_on||':'||coalesce(
      (select s.status from tasks s where s.id=d.depends_on and s.tag=t.tag),'?'))
    from dependencies d where d.task_id=t.id and d.tag=t.tag) dep_status,
   substr(t.title,1,70)
  from tasks t where t.id in (...) and t.tag='master' order by t.id;"

Schema notes: `tasks` is keyed (tag, id) with tag defaulting to 'master'; `dependencies` is (tag, task_id, depends_on) — the column is `depends_on`, NOT `depends_on_id`. This is how to compute "is this task actually READY" (all deps done) versus merely pending, which task status alone never tells you.

When inventorying live consumers of a script/gate across projects, grep the SQLite `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` files, NOT `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json`. The on-disk tasks.json files are stale migration-era snapshots (dark-factory's is dated 2026-05-02, autopilot-video's 2026-05-29) and silently return zero matches for anything filed since — a consumer search that only greps tasks.json will wrongly conclude a surface is unused. Use `grep -rl <pattern> /home/leo/src/*/.taskmaster/` which catches the .db and its -wal, then inspect hits with sqlite3/python.

claim: For task queries and audits, use the live `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` read-only—not stale or decoy JSON/DB files—and verify the data is current.

members.text:
Steward recipe for an orchestrator escalation worded "N reviewer(s) failed with infrastructure errors after retries: <role>" (category task_failure, suggested_action investigate_and_retry): do NOT take the "infrastructure" wording at face value and do NOT retry first. The summary is generated without inspecting why the reviewer failed, so a deterministic turn-cap exhaustion arrives under the same wording as a genuine transient fault, and the harness's own retry loop will burn ~$2-3 per attempt re-deriving it.

Diagnose from the orchestrator run store before acting. Copy it first (never query the live file):
  cp /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db /tmp/runs-ro.db
  sqlite3 /tmp/runs-ro.db "SELECT timestamp,event_type,phase,role,data FROM events WHERE task_id='<id>' AND timestamp>'<cycle start>' ORDER BY timestamp;"
The `invocation_end` rows carry {turns, success, subtype, timed_out}; the `routing_decision` rows carry the {max_turns, model, effort, budget_usd} the role was dispatched with. Compare them. `turns` >= `max_turns` on every attempt (with subtype error_max_turns, or subtype "success" but success:false — the reviewer ran out of turns before emitting its structured verdict) means a budget defect, not infrastructure: retrying identical inputs reproduces it. `timed_out: true` instead means wall-clock, which is a different remedy. The same table's `workflow_verify` row gives the verify verdict plus the exact tip_sha/base_sha it was measured against.

Second recipe, for when a task's review gate fails AFTER a rebase or requeue: check whether the branch's DELTA is unchanged from a delta that already passed review, rather than assuming the new SHAs mean new content. A rebase changes every SHA while leaving the diff identical, so a prior passing review verdict may still apply in full:
  git diff <old_base>..<old_tip> > /tmp/old.patch
  git diff <new_base>..<new_tip> > /tmp/new.patch
  diff <(grep -v '^index ' /tmp/old.patch) <(grep -v '^index ' /tmp/new.patch)
Empty output = byte-identical delta (the `grep -v '^index '` strips blob-hash lines, which differ after a rebase even when content does not). If it is empty and verify is green on the current tip, the review gate is already satisfied on this content and the branch can go to the merge queue via mcp__escalation__merge_request(verified_green=True) instead of through another doomed reviewer lap.

Both recipes were derived handling esc-5481-8 (task 5481, 2026-08-03): reviewer_comprehensive consumed 30/31/31/34/34/34/36/36/42 turns across 9 attempts against a configured max_turns=30, succeeded once, and cost ~$22 across two escalation cycles — while the branch's delta was byte-identical to one that had already passed review and adjudication, and had only failed to land because an orchestrator restart cancelled the merge phase.

Diagnosing "N reviewer(s) failed with infrastructure errors after retries" escalations in reify's orchestrator: that summary is NOT self-evidently an infra fault. The review wrapper writes {"verdict":"ERROR","issues":[],"summary":"Reviewer emitted no/invalid verdict:"} (note the trailing colon and empty payload) into <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<lane>/reviews/<reviewer>.json whenever the reviewer's final message is empty — and it does NOT distinguish a crashed session from a turn-exhausted one. Before treating it as transient, decompress the reviewer's session transcripts under data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/<task_id>/<encoded-worktree>/*.jsonl.gz and read the LAST attachment line of each: {"type":"max_turns_reached","maxTurns":N,"turnCount":N+1} means MAX_TURNS (not transient — a retry reproduces it identically), while the last "budget_usd" attachment tells you separately whether cost was the limiter. reviewer_comprehensive gets default_max_turns=30 from dark-factory orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py (_reviewer_role), and reify's dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml `max_turns:` block overrides only `architect: 120`, so every reviewer specialization runs at 30 turns. On a large branch diff (observed binding at 9 files / +1652/-283 over 21 commits) a comprehensive read does not fit in 30 turns, so the reviewer is cut off mid-exploration before ever calling its verdict tool and the task loops through steward escalations with a green verify. Raising that ceiling is out of steward scope: dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml is load-once (no hot-reload) and needs an orchestrator restart via scripts/orchestrator-redeploy-restart.sh. Instance: task 5891, esc-5891-3 and esc-5891-5, four consecutive sessions all dying at maxTurns=30 with used=$2.03-2.60 of a $5 budget; re-escalated to L1 as esc-5891-6.

PEER (topic reviewer-infrastructure-error-diagnosis) to b08ab18e — two NEW measured facts about the "reviewer verdict discarded" false infra error, from esc-6342-1 (task 6342, _lane-49, 2026-08-21).

FACT 1 — the reviews/ artifact is mechanically RECONSTRUCTIBLE from the sidecar, so the discard is repairable in place, not just diagnosable. On a HEALTHY lane, reviews/<role>.json compares EQUAL (python dict equality) to verdicts/<role>.json["verdict"] — verified on _lane-0. Both are {reviewer, verdict, issues[], summary}; the sidecar just wraps it as {role, schema_version, session_id, emitted_at, verdict:{...}}. So on a discarded lane the repair is a one-liner: write the sidecar's inner "verdict" object over reviews/<role>.json (back the original up as .error-bak first). Cheap, reversible, and harmless if the workflow later re-runs the reviewer and overwrites it. Whether the orchestrator actually re-reads a repaired reviews/ file on resume was NOT verified here — do the repair for the audit trail, but do not rely on it to make the workflow proceed; still go to the merge queue per b08ab18e.

FACT 2 — the discard is CONCURRENT across lanes, not a per-task fluke. At the same wall-clock, _lane-49 AND _lane-15 both showed reviews/=ERROR with 0 issues and the same "Reviewer emitted no/invalid verdict: Verdict submitted: **ISSUES_FOUND** ..." summary prefix, while both sidecars held complete verdicts (5 and 2 issues respectively). Both sidecars carried session_id "". If you find one discarded lane, check the siblings — other tasks are likely sitting on the same false escalation, and each will burn a reviewer lap if resumed.

TIMING SIGNATURE worth pattern-matching: on _lane-49 the sidecar was written 10:43:19Z, the ERROR reviews/ file 40s later at 10:43:59Z, and esc-6342-1 was filed in that SAME SECOND as the ERROR file.
