A sidecar that PREDATES the ERROR record proves the reviewer finished and was discarded — it did not crash and did not run out of turns (which is the OTHER, unrelated cause under this same escalation wording; see canonical index e2a6f1d4 and the transcript/runs.db routes c3cb28f3 / a94bc738).

PROCESS MISTAKE TO AVOID — I made it here: I resolved esc-6342-1 with action='resume' BEFORE searching memory, then found b08ab18e (which says use 'close_only', because 'resume' re-dispatches the reviewer into the same discard) and had to correct course by submitting the merge queue request separately. A resolve_issue call cannot be un-resolved. SEARCH MEMORY FOR THE ESCALATION WORDING BEFORE CALLING resolve_issue, not after. Recovery if you already resumed: check get_task_runtime_state — if the task's phase is DONE (as 6342's was), no reviewer is actually running, and submitting merge_request(verified_green=true) directly still lands the branch.

claim: Reviewer infrastructure-error escalations can mask turn exhaustion or discarded verdicts, so inspect run records, transcripts, and artifacts before retrying or resuming.

members.text: Reconciliation marker GC is split across two stores and the split is easy to misdiagnose. Of the three MARKER_KINDS in recon_ledger.py:89 (stage1_flag_marker, stage2_persistence_marker, flag_for_stage2), ONLY stage1_flag_marker has a recon_ledger writer (the single producer, flag_dedup.py:880); the other two are Mem0-only by design and are reaped by their own age-only sweeps (task_knowledge_sync.py:3012 and :3038). That sole ledger writer is gated at flag_dedup.py:750 by _is_valid_marker_task_id, which accepts ONLY `fp:<32 lowercase hex>`, a bare non-negative integer, or comma-joined non-negative integers — so a cross-project-qualified task_id like "dark_factory:1943" is rejected and writes NO ledger row at all. The guard landed 2026-06-05 (task 1656) and the ledger upsert 2026-07-09, so the writer has been gated since its first commit and no legacy colon-qualified ledger marker rows exist. Practical consequence: a colon-qualified stage1_flag_marker is always a legacy MEM0 record, collected by _sweep_stale_mem0_flag_markers (task_knowledge_sync.py:1274) on AGE ALONE (14 days, never task terminal-ness) — so before blaming ReconLedgerStore.gc()'s terminal-match arm for an unreaped marker, first check which store the marker actually lives in.

Stage 1 reconciliation write-counter policy: memory 711d2539 (content: 'Stage 1 flag marker: task=1139,1143,1145,1146,1148 type=human_operator_required from run=00ad627a') is a harness-level write generated by the flag deduplicator post-processor, NOT an LLM-generated write by Stage 1's consolidation logic. It is correctly excluded from Stage 1's memories_written_ids (which counts only LLM-initiated add_memory calls: 4422f48b, d55a5523, dfeceaf0 for run 00ad627a). The exclusion is intentional by design: harness-injected flag consolidation markers are infrastructure bookkeeping, separate from the LLM write budget. The memories_written counter MUST exclude harness-generated writes. This policy distinction was clarified in Stage 1 remediation run 62a9db11 (2026-05-04). Task 1146 tracking: implement atomic predecessor flag-marker deletion when a consolidated replacement is written.
Reconciliation flag deduplication involves Stage 1 and Stage 2 independently flagging the same issues

The reconciliation Stage-2 code (fused-memory/.../stages/task_knowledge_sync.py) has THREE distinct Mem0 marker channels, easily confused: (1) source=stage1_flag_marker — persistent Stage-1 dedup-state, GC'd only on dedup HIT plus age/cross-cycle sweep via _sweep_stale_flag_markers (task 1944 + task-2047 Gap 2); (2) metadata flag_for_stage2=true — ephemeral relay swept each cycle by _sweep_stale_fixc_markers; (3) source=stage2_persistence_marker — the per-flag persistence counter written by _track_flag_persistence (metadata {source, flag_id, run_id}, NO task_id/fp: key). Task 2095 added age-based GC for channel (3) via _sweep_stale_persistence_markers (constant STAGE2_PERSISTENCE_MARKER_MAX_AGE_DAYS=14, source tag stage2_persistence_marker_gc_sweep), wired into TaskKnowledgeSync.run() with stat report.stats['stale_persistence_markers_gc_swept']. So stage2_persistence_marker growth is now bounded — future recon cycles should NOT re-flag it as an orphan-growth anomaly. Task 1139's referenced plan.json (its GC design-decision record) no longer exists in the repo.

Constraints on reusing the task-3041 Mem0 deletion tombstone from a NEW delete path (verified 2026-08-15 on main eec91ee995, while planning task 3133). (1) There is deliberately NO "delete and stamp" helper: MemoryService.delete_memory contains zero tombstone/recon_ledger references, and the MCP delete_memory tool stamps nothing — so every new delete path must call the writer itself or it silently reproduces the recon-gate-165 audit dead-end. (2) You MUST capture the victim's metadata and created_at BEFORE the delete: record_mem0_deletion_tombstones takes victims as mappings with id/metadata/created_at, and there is no read path to a deleted point id (this is why _sweep_stale_mem0_pool keeps full member dicts, task_knowledge_sync.py:1273-1276). (3) The payload has NO survivor/canonical field — it is deleter, deleting_run_id, deleted_at, victim created_at, plus the identity-only projection _VICTIM_IDENTITY_KEYS = (kind, record_type, source, recon_pool, run_id). A consolidation-style reverse pointer needs a new arg on _build_tombstone_record (the single definition of the row shape); do not smuggle it through victim_metadata, which is documented as never carrying anything but the victim's own identity. (4) Ordering contract: stamp only from the confirmed-success branch — a pre-delete write false-positives on every failed delete, producing an audit trail claiming records are gone while they are alive. (5) By convention the SAME string is both the delete's _source and the tombstone's deleter (e.g. stage1_cycle_summary_trim), and deleting_run_id is passed as the delete's causation_id. (6) Prefer the batch form record_mem0_deletion_tombstones even for one victim (both prod callers use it): one upsert_many, one fsync, but all-or-nothing — a mid-batch error rolls back the whole audit trail. It is fail-safe (no recon_ledger wired returns 0 plus one WARNING, never raises), so a 0 return is NOT proof of success and should be surfaced to the caller rather than assumed.

(7) COVERAGE MAP, re-verified 2026-08-18 (recon run 72f6ea61-36ba-4390-bbdd-f1be428a1ecb). Tombstones are emitted from exactly TWO call sites in src/ — task_knowledge_sync.py:1366 (_sweep_stale_mem0_pool) and summary_pool.py:447 (enforce_summary_pool_cap) — covering FIVE named Python sweeps: stage1_flag_marker_gc_sweep, stage2_persistence_marker_gc_sweep, flag_for_stage2_gc_sweep, stage1_cycle_summary_trim, stage2_cycle_summary_trim. These Mem0 delete paths emit NOTHING: server/tools.py:4300 (the MCP delete_memory tool — i.e. EVERY LLM-issued delete, including Stage 2's own mandated flag-reaping deletes at prompts/stage2.py:596/:619/:654), memory_service.py:5091 (cascade child delete), task_knowledge_sync.py:2206 (_prune_task_count_snapshots), targeted.py:796 (stale echo-marker cleanup), harness.py:1638 (_delete_status_correction_memories), scope_freshness.py:344 (prior scope-freshness replacement). Confirmed first-hand on 2026-08-18: a consolidation delete issued through the MCP tool WITH an explicit replacement_memory_id left no tombstone — get_memory_by_id on the victim returned a bare {found:false}. The replacement_memory_id never crosses the service seam; tools.py:4279-4282 routes it to repoint_task_citations (citation_verifier.py:467), which writes a DIFFERENT citation tombstone into each citing TASK's metadata under x_memory_citation_tombstones (citation_verifier.py:67). So the survivor pointer is discoverable only by already knowing which tasks cited the dead id.

(8) DO NOT TRUST THE UNIVERSAL PHRASING IN THE SELF-MODEL. recon_self_model.py:520 asserts "Any recon-initiated Mem0 deletion now leaves a TOMBSTONE". Per (7) that is false for at least six paths. The hazard is the CONTRAPOSITIVE it licenses — "no tombstone, therefore not recon-deleted, therefore possible data loss" — which is invalid and fails in the direction that manufactures phantom data-loss incidents. That is precisely the recon-gate-165 / esc-165-1 dead-end (see memory 2d40d5d0-816a-41c3-84e6-2e05ad [cut]

claim: Reconciliation bookkeeping spans distinct stores, channels, and write paths, so trace the exact producer and lifecycle before interpreting cleanup, counters, or missing tombstones.

members.text: PEER NOTE (task 6714, S14 β, planned 2026-10-21; check whether 6714 is done before relying on it): the confirmed plan for task 6714 changes the session_registry.py bare-shell contract described in this topic. To make normalize_project_token come from shared.project_id.fold_project_token (the task's delivered check), session_registry.py gains a module-scope bootstrap. It appends `<checkout>/shared/src`, derived from Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3], to sys.path, never prepending, before `from shared.project_id import ...  # noqa: E402`. The contract becomes "stdlib plus this checkout's stdlib-only shared leaves". normalize_project_token and PROJECT_TOKEN_ALIASES are deleted; cockpit and scripts/sitting import fold_project_token from shared.project_id. TestStdlibOnlySelfContainment's sandbox mirrors shared/src, injects payloads after that import, and replaces the 'from shared import safe_io' payload with a pydantic-dependent shared module. Once 6714 lands, consequence 3 of this topic's canonical entry (the alias table must be a hand-maintained module constant) is superseded. Rationale and alternatives: escalation esc-6714-1.

Attention Rail hooks gotcha: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/session_registry.py (T3) is deliberately stdlib-only/self-contained so spawn-claude.sh can run it standalone by absolute path. A downstream module that imports it (e.g. the T6 session_hooks.py which does `from orchestrator import session_registry`) is NOT standalone — bash entrypoints invoking it must export PYTHONPATH="$REPO_ROOT/orchestrator/src" first (the same sys.path-insert trick tests/scripts/test_spawn_claude.py uses), or the package import fails with no venv/install.

scripts/tests/ (e.g. scripts/legibility/*.py) is verified via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/...` — this scopes execution to shared/pyproject.toml's own dependency set (pydantic, pydantic-settings, aiosqlite, pyyaml, python-dotenv only). Packages like jsonschema, ruamel.yaml, etc. that are only transitive deps of other workspace members (fused-memory, orchestrator, escalation per their uv.lock) are NOT importable there, even though they may appear available in an ambient/full-workspace venv. When writing a scripts/ module, verify package availability against `uv run --project shared python -c "import X"`, not the interactive dev shell's venv. This convention is load-bearing: see `_FALLBACK_UV_PROJECT = 'shared'` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py and the comment in shared/pyproject.toml (task 2070).

Gotcha: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/session_registry.py is deliberately stdlib-only and self-contained — its module docstring states it takes NO intra-orchestrator or workspace imports so skills/spawn/spawn-claude.sh can invoke it by absolute path with no venv/PYTHONPATH/install. Adding any non-stdlib import (e.g. `from shared import safe_io`) silently breaks the session hooks in production: the hook subprocess runs it under an interpreter without workspace packages, hits ModuleNotFoundError, exits fail-soft, and ~/.claude/fleet/sessions/<slug>/record.json is never written. The failure surfaces in orchestrator/tests/test_session_hooks.py (test_session_start_sh_then_notification_sh_flip_status and test_session_start_sh_converges_onto_pre_written_launching_record) as FileNotFoundError on record.json, NOT in test_session_registry.py — so a change can look green if you only run the touched module's own suite. Check the contract with: PYTHONPATH=<repo>/orchestrator/src /usr/bin/python3 -c "import orchestrator.session_registry" using a non-venv interpreter. Observed in task 3223, which had to revert this module from the shared atomic-writer consolidation and record it as a documented exception.

claim: Preserve standalone scripts’ minimal import and dependency contracts, and test them in the actual runtime environment rather than relying on an ambient workspace environment.

members.text:
Dark-factory convention: docstrings and comments should NOT cite source locations by line number (e.g. "see run_server:317-318", "see line ~96") — line references drift silently on every refactor to either file, including the SAME commit that adds them (task 3508 added ~89 lines to memory_service.py and thereby invalidated its own five citations, 2676-2689 -> 2755-2768 and 2984-2986 -> 3063-3068, before review even ran). Prefer symbolic/self-locating references instead: name the function/class/handler directly ("see WriteJournal fallback in run_server", "see app.py's paused_reason TODO"), cite by SYMBOL (`MemoryService.add_memory`, `GraphitiBackend.add_episode`) rather than `file.py:NNNN`, or refer to code blocks by name or content rather than position.

Applies especially to test docstrings and regression-test comments, where a stale pointer is easy to miss and no test covers it: task 3565 found three broken line-range citations in fused-memory/tests (test_merge_entities.py:980-1132, :1021-1131, and :154), two of which pointed past EOF or into unrelated code after task 3502's probe consolidation shifted lines.

In scripts/, this shows up as a SYMBOL-NAME convention specifically: scripts/_task_db_scan.py uses Sphinx refs (:func:`run_audit_cli`, :data:`AUDIT_EXIT_OK`) and contains zero bare line numbers; scripts/repair_wiped_metadata_files.py reserves `path/file.py:NNN` for cross-FILE refs only and records the lesson inline at :308 ("orchestrator/.../workflow.py:4550 — located by NAME; it moved once already"). Watch for the self-invalidating case: an edit that ADDS lines to a file shifts every anchor below it, so line numbers written into that same commit's docstring/comment are stale on write.

In dark-factory's warm-lane scripts and their tests, keep a divergence's full rationale in exactly one home (e.g. orchestrator/scripts/warm-lane/README.md's enumerated Deltas) and let the script comment/test docstring carry only the operative facts plus a symbolic pointer — do not embed base-commit SHAs or verbatim shell transcripts in test docstrings either.

Docstrings (especially on small test fixtures/helpers) should state the contract, not carry review/task lineage prose or call-site counts either — put the "why task N did this" narrative in the commit message and task record instead, and reference a convention by name ("the module's function-local-import convention") rather than by line number.

In dark-factory, hard-coded `file.py:NNN` line citations inside comments and docstrings rot silently and are a recurring source of reader misdirection — prefer naming the symbol or guard (e.g. "invoke_with_cap_retry's setdefault of backend under its `if invoke_fn is not None` check") over a line range. Concrete specimen found by task 4043: the SAME backend-forwarding site landed by task 2457 is cited by three different stale ranges — steward.py's `_invoke_agent_counted` docstring says cli_invoke.py:1079-1086, shared/tests/test_cli_invoke.py:4543's docstring says :895-896/:907/:928, and the actual code sits at cli_invoke.py:1509-1521. Note plans/*.md PRD citations are the deliberate exception: they are dated archaeology snapshots and should NOT be re-pointed when code moves.

CORRECTION to the "sanctioned STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out recorded in mem0 b80b78c4 (which cites tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py and its HTML-comment-marker convention as the approved way to pin a doc against live code). That carve-out is NOT reliably sanctioned and should not be planned as a safe pattern. On task 3465 an architect followed it exactly — bare `<!-- name:begin/end -->` marker spans in skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md and OPERATIONS.md, values derived from live producer constants via stdlib `ast` rather than hardcoded, loud-failing extractors that raise instead of returning empty, explicit STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline — and reviewer_comprehensive still blocked the whole 769-line module as a documentation/introspection meta-test and mandated deletion. That is the second such data point: task 3544 (mem0 3c294ce3) had a mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test deleted despite a live in-code oracle. Two independent blocks means the reviewer treats "derived from code at runtime" and "anchored on markers" as insufficient — what it keys on is that the ASSERTION TARGET is doc prose, a module-level/function-body string literal, or a parameter name recovered by introspection. Practical rule for architects: before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's OWN package already asserts those tokens against real produced OUTPUT; on 3465 fused-memory/tests/test_scope_violation_escalator.py already called the real report_rejection() and asserted category/agent_role/severity on the escalation JSON that landed on disk, so the entire guard was redundant with existing behaviour coverage. Same held for its two "premise guard" tests: escalation/tests/test_server.py, escalation/tests/test_queue.py and orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py already cover the granted_files grant end-to-end, so an introspection check on the parameter NAME was both redundant and strictly weaker. Also: when deleting such a guard, the doc-side marker spans and any prose sentence claiming the tokens are "pinned by <test file>" must be deleted with it — a SKILL.md is read verbatim as an LLM system prompt, so a dangling reference to a deleted test tells the executing agent a mechanism exists when it does not.

SPECIMEN (peer under topic `no-line-number-citations-norm`) — a distinct TRANSMISSION VECTOR for stale line pins: a task DESCRIPTION's `file.py:NNN` citations get copied verbatim by the implementer into the doc the task edits, laundering a stale pin out of an ephemeral task record into a durable, agent-read artifact.

Worked case, task 4659 (2026-08-24): the task description cited `GitOps.find_merge_marker` as `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py:7862-7905` and `_merge_subject` as `git_ops.py:1874`. The implementer reproduced both verbatim in a new "Deriving the landed sha" section in skills/unblock-low-risk/SKILL.md. Measured at HEAD: find_merge_marker is at git_ops.py:8524 (:7862 lands inside `release_lane_for_terminal_task`'s docstring) and _merge_subject is at git_ops.py:2315 (:1874 lands in a lane-flock inode comment) — drift of ~660 and ~440 lines. The same stale pair also sits on main in skills/merge-queue/SKILL.md and skills/unblock/SKILL.md, so the description most likely inherited it from those docs and then re-seeded it into a third — the rot is circulating between artifacts, not decaying in one place.

Why this vector is worth its own specimen: the existing specimens are all "author wrote a pin, code moved". Here the pin was never independently authored — it was transcribed from an upstream record that a diligent implementer had every reason to trust. So "don't author line pins" is not sufficient guidance; a task description's own citations must be RE-VERIFIED against HEAD before being copied into a doc, and the copy should be converted to a symbol citation even when the source used a line pin.

Extra force in skills/: a SKILL.md is read verbatim as an LLM system prompt, so a rotted pin does not merely misdirect — an agent that follows it lands on unrelated code and may conclude the whole skill is stale, discarding correct guidance. Fixed in 4659 commit 176e43c2cd by dropping the numbers and citing the symbols; the two pre-existing copies were left to a follow-up (ticket tkt_0RSTTQCYVJC2M8GD2XTV4TKNCC) because skills/unblock/SKILL.md had active claimants.

SPECIMEN (no-line-number-citations-norm), task 4116, commit 99354713c2 — a pin-entry VECTOR the other specimens do not show: the ARCHITECT's plan step cited a convention as "see memory_service.py:562 and :1002" as a navigation aid, and the implementer copied it verbatim into a production comment as "(see :562, :1002)". It went stale BEFORE the task merged: the esc-4116-9 refresh-from-main grew memory_service.py from ~2.7k to ~10.7k lines, landing both numbers in unrelated metadata-vocabulary docstring prose. Fixed by naming the enclosing symbols (_apply_memory_metadata_validation, _is_rate_limit_or_quota_error), each grepped before citing. PRACTICE for implementers: a plan's file:line pointers are for navigation at plan time — when a step asks you to cite one in a comment, translate it to the enclosing symbol as you write it; and after any refresh-from-main, scan your own added lines (git diff -U0 main..HEAD, '+' lines only) for ':NNN' before handing off.

claim: Avoid line-number citations in durable docs and comments; verify inherited pointers and replace them with symbolic references, since line pins drift and mislead.

members.text: Deleting a task-metadata key via scheduler.update_task REQUIRES metadata_mode='replace'. Popping the key from a read-modify-write payload is not enough: the default mode resolves to 'merge' (scheduler.py Scheduler.update_task), and the backend's merge is a shallow {**existing, **incoming} (sqlite_task_backend._merge_metadata) that PRESERVES keys omitted from the payload — so a mode-less "clear" logs a removal it never performs. Corollary: because 'replace' is a whole-blob overwrite where omission means deletion, the payload must be a backend-verified read; if the refreshing get_task fails, skip the write entirely rather than replacing with an in-memory-only dict, which would silently delete every backend-only key (e.g. memory_hints re-attached by Stage-2 reconciliation).

SCOPE CHANGE to topic metadata-mode-replace-key-retirement (task 3777, branch task/3777, pending merge as of 2026-10-01): once 3777 is merged AND the fused-memory server has restarted onto it, update_task(metadata_mode='replace') IS usable on a done/merged task, provided the payload carries the STORED metadata.done_provenance verbatim. Identity is JSON-value equality against the row read in the same transaction. Adding, changing or DROPPING done_provenance under replace is refused with error='done_provenance_via_update_task'. Omission counts as deletion, so a read-modify-write that loses the key is rejected rather than silently destroying it. Every other mode still refuses any payload carrying the key. Under enforce mode, a verbatim legacy (schema-invalid) done_provenance passthrough is not blamed on the write. The authority is fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/sqlite_task_backend.py::_assert_done_provenance_passthrough. Until the server restarts, the old presence-only floor still refuses any replace on a done task.

Retiring a task metadata key requires update_task metadata_mode='replace', NOT 'merge'. _merge_metadata (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/sqlite_task_backend.py:3301-3376) implements merge as a shallow {**old, **new} with no deletion sentinel, so a merge-mode write can ADD a renamed key but can never REMOVE the old spelling — both coexist and the code=unknown_key census line persists. The safe recipe (precedent: fused-memory/scripts/strip_leaked_control_keys.py) is read the full blob, transform it purely, write it back with metadata_mode='replace' carrying ONLY {id, project_root, metadata, metadata_mode}, then read back and diff every key plus the sha256 of description/details. That payload restriction is what keeps a replace from repeating the task-2180 hazard of wiping live data.

STAMPED PEER under topic `tasks-json-is-a-stale-mirror` (canonical 64ae84c2). Two updates the canonical does not carry.

(1) THE FILE IS GONE, NOT MERELY STALE. The canonical reads as though `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` still exists and is just old. As of 2026-08-30 it does NOT exist in /home/leo/src/dark-factory: `/bin/ls -la .taskmaster/tasks/` returns only `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-shm`, `tasks.db-wal`, and `test -e tasks.json` reports ABSENT. It was retired at the 2026-05-06 SQLite cutover and DELETED 2026-08-25 (date independently recorded at `.claude/skills/hotspot-survey/project.md`). Consequence for agents: a read of that path now FAILS LOUDLY instead of silently returning a 4-month-old answer — strictly better than the esc-4659-5 near-miss, where task 4659's architect read it, got a stale answer with NO error, and recorded a false "owned by no live task" claim. If such a file ever REAPPEARS it is a restored backup or a foreign artifact; do not read it and do not migrate from it.

(2) NEVER JUDGE tasks.db's FRESHNESS BY ITS OWN mtime. `tasks.db` runs in WAL mode. Committed writes land in `tasks.db-wal` and the main file's mtime is only touched at checkpoint, so it can lag live writes arbitrarily. Any code or eyeball comparing "which is newer, the db or some other file" must take max(mtime) across `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-wal` AND `tasks.db-shm`. A db-only stat will report an actively-written live store as older than a months-dead snapshot. This is not hypothetical: it is precisely the misread that would let `fused-memory/scripts/migrate_tasks_json_to_sqlite.py --replace` overwrite the live ~30 MB / 4600-row store with a 1152-task May snapshot (task 4682 adds the guard).

Per the canonical: quote no row counts as durable fact — measure them yourself. Open read-only (`file:...?mode=ro` URI). The two zero-byte decoys named in the canonical still apply.

GOTCHA (dark_factory, measured in source 2026-09-27, task 5771 planning): update_task(metadata_mode='replace') silently DELETES the scheduler wait anchor. SqliteTaskBackend.update_task strips pending_since/pending_since_backfilled from every caller-supplied blob (strip_machine_authored_metadata), then _merge_metadata(mode='replace') writes the blob verbatim, so the stored anchor is gone. This is intended for public callers ("design decision 8", task 3816). Any whole-blob metadata rewrite that must remove keys while keeping the anchor needs an interceptor-only privileged backend writer that carries _MACHINE_AUTHORED_METADATA_KEYS across (task 5771 plans SqliteTaskBackend.rewrite_audit_trail for audit-trail rotation). Separately, a replace blob containing done_provenance, even an unchanged one, is rejected by a presence-only floor.

claim: Retiring task metadata keys requires whole-blob replace, so verify the source payload and account for protected fields that may be rejected or stripped.

Python's `Path.exists()` is NOT a total fail-safe probe: `pathlib._abc._ignore_error` swallows only ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP/EINVAL, so EACCES **propagates**. An unreadable parent directory (chmod 0o000 on the path itself or ANY ancestor) makes a bare `if p.exists():` raise PermissionError. Verified on Python 3.13.9 against `shared/prompt_artifact.py` (task 4098). Consequence: wrapping only the subsequent read/JSON-load in `except OSError` does not make a "never raises" contract true — the stat probe that guards it must be wrapped too.

=== CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (curate-fused-memories batch sitting, gate 4414) — MEASURED, NOT VOTED ===
The errno set above is WRONG: it lists EINVAL. Measured directly on the interpreter this repo runs (CPython 3.13.9): pathlib._abc._IGNORED_ERRNOS == (2, 20, 9, 40) == {ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EBADF, ELOOP}. EINVAL (22) is NOT in it — the set has FOUR members, not five. This entry's 'Verified on Python 3.13.9' claim did not cover the errno list itself.
The entry's CENTRAL claim is UNAFFECTED and was re-confirmed empirically: EACCES is not ignored, so an unreadable path or ANY unreadable ancestor makes a bare exists() raise PermissionError (reproduced with chmod 0 on an ancestor directory).
ALSO CORRECTED: ENAMETOOLONG is NOT silently ignored by exists(). It RAISES — measured the same way. Any statement that exists() returns False for an over-long path is false.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 3790): in a production path that DEGRADES fail-safe on `except Exception`, a test double that violates its Protocol's RETURN SHAPE does not fail loudly — it makes tests pass VACUOUSLY, and neither pyright nor a green suite will tell you.

THE MECHANISM. `flake_ledger.py::_ensure_owner_task` does `statuses, statuses_error = await task_client.get_statuses([...])` inside a `try/except Exception` that degrades to "keep the stored owner, file nothing". A test double returned a bare `dict` instead of the Protocol's `(statuses, error)` pair, so the unpack raised `ValueError: not enough values to unpack` INTO that except, and every corroboration silently took the failed-read branch. The dedup test still passed: the degrade path also files nothing and also leaves exactly one debt row, so all three of its count assertions were satisfied while the live-owner branch its docstring documents never executed once. A regression re-filing against a LIVE owner would have stayed green.

WHY THE USUAL GATES MISS IT. pyright reported 0 errors because nothing statically related the double to the Protocol (the only references were docstring prose) — see the companion norm on pinning Protocol seams with a STATIC pyright-checked assignment, which is the structural fix. And a green suite is no evidence at all here, because the whole failure is a test that passes for the wrong reason.

THE DETECTION RULE, generalizable. When the success path and the degrade path have the SAME observable side effects (both file nothing, both leave one row), COUNT ASSERTIONS CANNOT DISTINGUISH THEM — so a passing count-based test does not pin the branch it names. Add one assertion that only the intended branch can satisfy: assert the degrade path's log line is ABSENT (`assert 'could not corroborate' not in caplog.text`). That is what converts the test from vacuous to load-bearing.

VERIFY BY MUTATION, not inspection. Reintroduce the wrong return shape and confirm the test now FAILS, then restore. Done for this one: it fails at exactly the new assertion with the `ValueError` traceback, and passes once restored. Without that step you cannot tell a fixed test from a still-vacuous one.

MIRROR-IMAGE COMPLEMENT to this topic's canonical (which says: exists()/is_dir() swallow only {ENOENT,ENOTDIR,EBADF,ELOOP} and re-raise the rest, so guard the PROBE too). The other half, measured 2026-08-25 on CPython 3.13.9 in .worktrees/4722: `Path.resolve()` RAISES exactly where those probes return False. `Path('/tmp/a\0b')` CONSTRUCTS fine; `.resolve()` -> ValueError('lstat: embedded null character in path'); `.exists()` and `.is_dir()` on the same path both return False without raising.

CONSEQUENCE for any fail-closed path pre-flight of the common shape `root = Path(root).resolve()` followed by `if not root.is_dir() or not (root/'.git').exists(): <structured refusal>`: the REFUSAL branch is fail-closed by construction, but the RESOLVE above it is not — a malformed path skips the refusal entirely and raises out of the function, landing in whatever generic `except` the caller has. That is the same half-fix shape as task 4098, arrived at from the opposite end: there the probe was unguarded ahead of a guarded read; here the resolve is unguarded ahead of a guarded probe. Wrap the resolve in `except (OSError, ValueError)` and return the refusal from there, i.e. put the resolve INSIDE the guard helper so the helper's fail-closed docstring covers the whole pre-flight.

This matters most when the refusal is a first-class AUDITED outcome and the exception is not: in fused-memory recon (task 4722, verify.py::_resolve_codebase_root) a refused codebase root writes `verify|codebase|agent_failed` with a census token, while an escaping ValueError writes an undifferentiated `verify|codebase|error` row instead — the diagnosis is erased, not merely relocated. Note also that a shape-only validator (require_project_root: non-empty + os.path.isabs) accepts '/tmp/a\0b', so such a path really does reach production code.

claim: Fail-safe behavior requires guarding every fallible step and testing that the intended branch ran, not merely checking outcomes shared by fallback paths.

In dark-factory agent sessions, `cat`/`head`/`sed` output through the Bash tool is SKIM-NORMALIZED (e.g. Python type annotations stripped: `def _lt(lock_depth: int = 2) -> ModuleLockTable:` renders as `def _lt(lock_depth = 2):`, and `def f(x: Path, y: list[str] | None) -> None:` renders as `def f(x, y):`), so it must never be used as the source text for an exact-match string replacement. The failure is SILENT: a python heredoc doing `s.replace(<text copied from cat output>, ...)` matches nothing, changes nothing, and still reports success — an Edit built the same way just returns replacement count 0.

AMENDMENT (confirmed dark-factory task 4559, 2026-08-23): the normalization ALSO strips a method's `self` parameter and collapses leading indentation, not just type annotations — a BROADER hazard than the exact-match-replacement failure above. One-command repro: `printf 'class T:\n    def test_a(self) -> None:\n        pass\n' > /tmp/p.py && cat /tmp/p.py` renders as ` def test_a():`. Never REWRITE a Python file wholesale (Write tool, or a heredoc) from what `cat` displayed — doing that to a pytest test class silently drops every `self`, and the class then fails at call time with `TypeError: TestX.test_a() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` raised from `_pytest/python.py`'s `testfunction(**testargs)` — a symptom that reads like a pytest-version quirk rather than a transcription loss, costing a debugging cycle.

WHAT TO USE INSTEAD for byte-exact content: the Read tool + Edit tool, or a python script that reads the file itself. `cat >> file <<'EOF'` for pure appends is safe (no exact-match required). Verify signatures with `git show HEAD:<path> | grep -n 'def '` or the Grep tool before concluding the on-disk source is unusual.

(Consolidated 2026-08-19 by recon Stage 1 run 25e9aaf2-201a-49f3-83dd-fea5a696e9a2 from near-duplicate memory dc8663bf-296e-4034-95e7-f73dc4a110b1, which is now deleted with this record as its replacement. Amendment folded in 2026-09-07 by recon-stage-memory_consolidator from memory 8c7a573b-cf8c-40f0-9a5d-c3654a9e99cf, itself now deleted with this record as its replacement — that entry was originally filed separately because content_amend on this record was restricted to recon-stage-*/curator-* agents at write time.)

GOTCHA (dark-factory agent sessions, measured 2026-09-07 in worktree 4829): `cat`/`sed` output rendered through the Bash tool can be LOSSILY SUMMARIZED — it silently drops tokens from source code. Do not read code you are about to copy or edit via `cat`.

MEASURED. `cat shared/tests/test_task_statuses.py` rendered every test method as `def test_is_str_enum():` — no `self` parameter — and omitted a `@pytest.mark.skip(...)` decorator entirely. Both are real, load-bearing text: `grep -n 'def test_is_str_enum'` on the same file returns `58:    def test_is_str_enum(self):`, and the skip decorator is at line 124. The lossy render was internally consistent enough to look correct (it even explained the 3 skips as "no skip marker in the file"), so nothing about the output flagged itself as truncated.

WHY IT MATTERS. Copying a precedent file's style is the standard way to write a new module here (see the `shared/src/shared/task_statuses.py` -> `merge_state.py` pattern). Copying from a lossy `cat` would have produced test methods with no `self`, which pytest fails to collect as a TypeError — a self-inflicted break attributed to the precedent.

PRACTICE. Use the `Read` tool for any source you will copy, cite, or edit — its output was verified faithful on the same file in the same session. `grep -n` for a specific construct is also reliable. Reserve `cat` for output you only need the gist of (config dumps, listings). When a `cat` reading and a test run disagree — e.g. tests pass that "should" fail given what you read — believe the test run and re-read with `Read`.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-07, esc-4821-5): never write a NEGATIVE existence claim ("there is no X", "the only X is at Y") from a grep whose output you truncated. A `| head` on a search is a display convenience, not a measurement, and treating it as one produces confidently-wrong absence claims that are then filed as structured evidence and believed.

WHAT HAPPENED. A code comment in fused-memory enumerated the uncategorized `EscalationQueue.has_open_l1` readers a level-0 write must be invisible to, asserting "That is the population this closes" and that the exclusions "were re-measured rather than assumed". An escalation then filed a structured evidence entry stating the uncategorized workflow.py site is in `TaskWorkflow._wait_for_resolution` "NOT `_await_steward_completion`", and that "No has_open_l1 occurs at :17262". Both were false. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py has TWO uncategorized readers — :14005 in `_wait_for_resolution` and :17262 in `_await_steward_completion`, the latter being exactly the requeue-diversion override the note claimed did not exist. The original reviewer had been right and the "correction" filed against them. Cost: one wrong escalate_info that a concurrent process had to correct.

RULED OUT, because it was the obvious excuse: this was NOT a stale-tree or different-HEAD artifact. The task worktree's workflow.py is byte-identical to main's (`git diff main --stat` empty) and contains :17262. A HEAD-drift hypothesis was offered in the note and does not survive contact with the measurement.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, and it is mundane: the search was truncated before the second match. `head`'s default is 10 lines and it truncates SILENTLY, with no marker in its output that anything was cut — a `grep -n 'has_open_l1(' orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py | head` returned exactly 10 lines, which looked like a complete result set and was not. I reproduced the same trap in the same session — my own first `grep -n has_open_l1` was piped through `head` and showed only 10 of the occurrences.

THE RULE: a BOUNDED read cannot establish an ABSENCE. Enumerating to prove "there are exactly N" or "there are none" requires an unbounded read — `grep -c` for the count first, or no `head`/`head_limit` at all, or `wc -l` on the raw result. The Grep tool's `head_limit` has the same hazard (it defaults to 250 and takes 0 for unlimited).

TELL: the danger sign is a truncated list whose length exactly equals the truncation limit. 10 results from `| head` is almost never 10 results.

THE RELIABLE SHAPE for "find every call site of X":
    grep -n "X(" <file> | grep -v "<kwarg you mean to exclude>=" | grep -vE ":\s*#"
with NO `head`, and read the count. To attribute each hit to its enclosing function without trusting line numbers:
    awk -v n=<line> 'NR<=n && /^    (async )?def /{f=$0} END{print f}' <file>

TWO DURABLE LESSONS.
1. Asymmetry of evidence: a positive claim ("X is at line N") is self-verifying — the reader looks and sees it. A negative claim ("X occurs nowhere else") is only as good as the completeness of the search behind it, and nothing in the output marks it as incomplete. Hold negative claims to a higher bar, and say which search established them.
2. An enumeration that ASSERTS COMPLETENESS is a different artifact from one that cites a location. Bare line pins in this repo are tolerated drift and must not be swept (CLAUDE.md). But a comment claiming "that is the population" is a load-bearing factual statement a future refactorer relies on — a missing member is a false statement, not cosmetic drift, and correcting it inside prose your own change introduced is expressly permitted. Know which of the two you are writing.

SECOND-ORDER LESSON, worth as much as the first: the false claim was laundered into durability. It went into an escalate_info AND into a code comment that presented itself as a re-measured COMPLETE population — the exact artifact a future refactorer would trust instead of  [cut]

claim: Treat command output as potentially lossy or truncated: verify source text and search completeness before copying, editing, or making claims of absence.

INVESTIGATIVE DISCIPLINE: never pipe `git status` / `git log` through `head` when you are scoping the BLAST RADIUS of an incident — and never let a truncated read become an asserted fact in an escalation.

MEASURED SELF-CORRECTION (dark-factory, 2026-08-31, esc-3949-14). While assessing a data-loss incident on main I ran `git status --porcelain | head -3`, saw ` M README.md` plus two `docs/prds/*.capability-manifest.yaml`, and filed a note stating that only README.md was involved in the working tree and that the other modified files were "someone else's WIP ... not part of this incident". The full status was NINE modified files. Three of them — plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json, plans/memory-metadata-census-report.md, plans/memory-metadata-coverage-history.json — were the OTHER three files damaged by the same incident, sitting just below the `head -3` cut. So the footgun I filed was four files wide, not one, and I had confidently mis-scoped it AND wrongly exonerated files that mattered.

WHY THIS SHAPE OF ERROR IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOPPY. A truncated listing does not look truncated. `head -3` returns exactly three plausible lines and no marker that more existed, so the output reads as a complete answer. The failure then compounds: the under-scoped observation gets written into an escalation as a positive claim about what is NOT affected ("unrelated WIP, leave it alone"), which is a claim the evidence never supported. A responder acting on it would have left three damaged files unrepaired.

THE RULE. For scoping questions — what is dirty, what changed, what is affected — read the WHOLE list, however long. Truncate only when you already know the shape of the answer and are sampling it, never when you are establishing its extent. If a listing really is too long to read, count it (`| wc -l`) and say so, rather than showing the first N and reasoning as though that were all.

THE COROLLARY, worth more than the rule. Distinguish, in your own writing, between what you MEASURED and what you INFERRED from an absence. "README.md is modified" was measured. "The other files are unrelated" was inferred from not seeing them — i.e. from a truncation artifact. Absence-of-evidence claims are exactly the ones to re-derive with an untruncated command before committing them to a record, because an escalation's negative claims ("X is not affected", "these are unrelated") are the ones a responder will act on without re-checking.

CHEAP HABIT THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: when a status listing is the basis of a scope claim, re-run it once without any pipe before you file. It costs one command. Here it turned a wrong four-file claim into a right one, and the correction had to be issued as a follow-up resolution rather than being right the first time.

NORM (dark-factory, 2026-08-05): piping a journalctl/grep evidence pull through `head -N` can TRUNCATE AWAY the very lines you are looking for and produce a false "not in the log" conclusion. Concretely: `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service --since ... | grep -i "markup\|<time>" | head -20` returned 20 lines of unrelated noisy `get_task error: INVALID_TASK_ID: non-numeric task id: markup-tripwire` entries (the escalation-watcher polling every 15 min), hiding the two markup_tripwire rejection lines further down. That briefly produced the wrong conclusion that the rejections had been served by a different fused-memory process. When testing an ABSENCE claim against logs, count matches (`grep -c`) or write the full match set to a file first, and only then head/tail for display. Pairs with the standing lesson that `| tail` masks a command's exit code.

NORM (task 3554, review-established): a guard/config test must never assert on comment or docstring PROSE in files it does not own. A ratchet in tests/scripts/ that required every entry of an exclusion set to still contain the literal 'skills/' made a cosmetic comment reword in scripts/tests/test_legibility_sampling.py red-wall a merge-blocking module config — measured as `1 failed, 5 passed` from a diff touching nothing the guard gated. Assert on RUNTIME state instead (discovered module-config prefixes, git ls-files/grep sweeps, parsed command targets, file existence). Do NOT "fix" such coupling with a word-boundary or regex variant: that keeps the identical cross-package prose dependency while hiding it. For a triage-style set (real-consumer inventory vs excluded mentions), gate only the ADD direction — an unmatched exclusion key is inert, since the untriaged check consults the triaged set for membership only, so a key matching no file cannot make any still-mentioning file pass. Prune stale exclusions opportunistically when the file is next touched.

claim: Base claims and tests on complete, authoritative evidence—not truncated output, inferred absences, or incidental prose.

members.text: Repo-root tests/scripts/ (e.g. deployment/config drift tests like test_orchestrator_service_files.py) is NOT covered by orchestrator/config.yaml's per-subproject test_command fan-out (which only runs shared|escalation|orchestrator|fused-memory|dashboard /tests). Instead, a changed root-level tests/scripts/test_*.py is run by verify.py's SCOPED fallback path (_build_fallback_config + _strip_leading_cd, docstring verify.py:228-234), which strips the leading `cd <subproject> &&` and runs the tool from the worktree root. So such a test only gates CI when the test file itself (or a mapped source file) is in the diff — placing a drift test there is a real gate, but it is not part of a bare full-suite run.

Tests under the repo-root `tests/scripts/` directory run via `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/` (scripts/orchestrator.yaml), so they can only import what `shared/pyproject.toml` declares — `escalation`, `dashboard`, and `fused_memory` are NOT importable there. When a scripts/ test needs a first-party package, put that test in a subproject whose pyproject already declares it (e.g. `dashboard/tests/` can import `escalation`, since dashboard/pyproject.toml has `escalation = { workspace = true }`) and load the hyphenated script by absolute path with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, rather than adding a test-only dependency to shared.

Two similarly-named test directories exist in dark-factory and only one is verified: the orchestrator fallback verify chain (dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml test_command) ends with `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/` — the REPO-ROOT tests/scripts/ directory. The separate scripts/tests/ directory (tests for scripts/*.py sweep and audit tools) is NOT in that chain, nor in lint_command, which only covers shared/escalation/fused-memory/orchestrator/dashboard. A green fleet verify therefore proves nothing about scripts/tests/. Run it explicitly: `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/ --timeout=300`.

members.text: jcodemunch-mcp 1.108.54 emits 3-segment MUNCH `__tables` specs (`prefix:table:cols`, e.g. `r:__rows__:file|specifier|match_type`) with the trailing type list OMITTED, and its `find_references` rows carry no `line` column at all. In reify-audit's `jcodemunch_client.rs`, a type-less spec decodes EVERY column as `ColType::Str`, so any wire adapter reading a numeric column with a bare `?.as_u64()` / `?.as_f64()` inside its `filter_map` silently drops the whole row — turning a grammar drift into a silently-empty `Vec` (an audit reporting a clean corpus) instead of a loud `LoadError::Protocol`. Read mandatory numeric columns through `row_u64` / `row_f64` (number-or-string-parse), and treat `line == 0` as the documented "wire did not report one" sentinel rather than a drop condition.

reify-audit's captured jcodemunch wire fixtures under crates/reify-audit/tests/fixtures/jcodemunch/ are jcodemunch-mcp 1.108.27-era and do NOT reflect the pinned 1.108.54 serve: 1.108.54 emits 3-segment MUNCH `__tables` specs (e.g. `r:__rows__:file|specifier|match_type`, per-column type list omitted) where the fixtures are all 4-segment. A green fixture suite is therefore NOT evidence the client decodes the live wire — that gap made every find_references call fail to decode for months (task #6447). A 3-segment spec also decodes every column as ColType::Str, so numeric columns like `line` arrive as JSON strings and a bare `.as_u64()?` inside a filter_map adapter silently drops the whole row.

In reify-audit's jcodemunch MUNCH decoder, accepting a TYPE-LESS 3-segment `__tables` spec makes every column decode as `ColType::Str`, which silently breaks any adapter that reads a numeric column with a bare `as_u64()`/`as_f64()` inside a `filter_map` — the row is dropped and the caller gets an empty Vec instead of a loud `LoadError::Protocol`. Widening the spec grammar therefore REQUIRES rewiring every mandatory numeric column through a number-or-string tolerant reader (`row_u64`/`row_f64` in crates/reify-audit/src/jcodemunch_client.rs). Optional numeric columns read with `unwrap_or_default()` are safe and deliberately left alone.

claim: When accepting type-less MUNCH specs, read mandatory numeric columns with number-or-string tolerant parsers to prevent silent row drops and empty results.

members.text: Committing even a docs-only file under plans/ in dark-factory triggers the FULL pre-commit hook (3× pyright over fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard), which exceeds the Bash tool's 2-min ceiling and gets SIGTERM'd (exit 143) mid-hook — the commit does NOT land. Fix: run it detached — `setsid bash -c 'git commit -F <msgfile> > <log> 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> <log>' &` then poll <log> for the EXIT= marker (pyright takes ~3-5 min total). Second gotcha observed this session: while the first (timed-out) commit sat blocked, the live merge queue landed an unrelated merge (task/2040) and advanced HEAD, leaving the staged file still staged (status `A`) — re-run `git add <file>` before the detached retry. Confirms and extends the feedback that the harness may ignore timeout/run_in_background for `git commit` and that pre-commit 3× pyright exceeds the 2-min ceiling; use -F for the message (heredocs get flattened).

Procedural note (2026-07-07): committing even a DOCS-ONLY change to plans/ on dark-factory's main still triggers the full pre-commit hook, which runs 3x pyright (fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard) over the whole repo — this exceeds the 2-min Bash-tool ceiling and kills the commit with exit 143. Run the commit detached (setsid + append to a logfile) and poll the log / git HEAD for the terminal marker instead of a foreground commit. Also: `git commit --only <path>` FAILS with 'pathspec did not match any file(s) known to git' for a NEW untracked file — you must `git add <path>` first (naming the exact paths, never `add -A`, to stay race-safe against concurrent sessions), then `git commit --only <path>`. The pre-commit itself passed cleanly (0 errors) once given time.

Shared main-checkout commit discipline (learned 2026-07-02): /home/leo/src/dark-factory's main working tree is used CONCURRENTLY by multiple live interactive sessions plus the orchestrator merge queue, so plain commits race. Observed failure shapes, all benign but confusing: (a) `fatal: cannot lock ref 'HEAD': is at X but expected Y` = another actor advanced main between your pre-commit hook and the ref write — just retry; (b) another session's mixed `git reset HEAD~1` (their commit-rework flow) UNSTAGES your `git add` mid-flight, so your retry says "nothing added to commit" and your file is back to untracked — re-add and retry; (c) the pre-commit hook runs pyright over 3 projects (~2 min) even for docs-only commits, which widens the race window substantially. Discipline: ALWAYS commit path-scoped — `git add <file> && git commit <file> ...` — which both survives concurrent index resets gracefully and never sweeps another session's staged WIP into your commit (found plans/interactive-warm-worktree-prd.md staged by a sibling session; a bare `git commit` would have stolen it). Also: the Bash tool flattens embedded newlines in `git commit -m "multi-line"` (not just heredocs) — commit message paragraphs collapse to one line; use `git commit -F <msgfile>` when the message matters.

Git gotcha (2026-07-06): to commit ONLY specific UNTRACKED files while leaving unrelated modified/staged files out (e.g. a PRD + manifest committed to main amid other sessions' live WIP), `git commit -F msg -- <path1> <path2>` FAILS on untracked paths with 'error: pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git' — git commit with a pathspec only sees tracked/staged paths. Correct sequence: `git add -- <paths>` FIRST, THEN `git commit -F msg -- <paths>` — the explicit pathspec still commits ONLY those paths (the --only default when paths are given), so other concurrently-staged content stays out of your commit. This composes with the existing df convention: run it as `setsid git commit ... &` + poll the log, because pre-commit runs the full 3× pyright (fused-memory/orchestrator/dashboard) and exceeds the 2-min Bash ceiling even for a docs-only commit.

claim: In dark-factory’s shared checkout, stage and commit only explicit paths, running commits detached because the full pre-commit hook exceeds the tool’s timeout.

members.text: SIGHTING (task 4374, 2026-09-06) of the lock-charter-drift-guard branch-staleness gotcha (topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth`): task/4374 (a single-file TTL-constant change, unrelated to lock-charter code) went red on test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script and test_every_tracked_extension_is_allowlisted[reify] for 'tombstones'. Confirmed via the documented 3-comparison recipe: `git show origin/main:.../lock_charter_guard.py` contains 'tombstones', `git show HEAD:` of the same path does not; mirror commit 3ab23ecd09 (cherry-picked from task-4804's 9b824da7db) is an ancestor of origin/main but not of HEAD; branch is 2 ahead / 1813 behind main (`git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main`). Disposition: escalate_blocker(category='infra_issue') rather than hand-edit the 4 out-of-scope allowlist files or cherry-pick — filed as a blocker on task 4374 rather than acted on unilaterally, consistent with task 5083's prior 'NO ACTION REQUIRED, rebase clears it' precedent. Task 3226 (the systemic hermeticity fix) is STILL status=blocked as of 2026-09-05, so this is at least the 4th recorded sighting (after 3134, 4412, 3388/5083) of the same false-positive costing debugger-cycle time — signal that 3226's priority may warrant revisiting.

GOTCHA — a bare-main health probe can report GREEN while every dark-factory worktree is RED, because fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py::test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script resolves the sibling repo by PATH ARITHMETIC: `_REIFY_GUARD_SCRIPT = Path(__file__).parents[5] / 'reify' / 'scripts' / 'lock-charter-guard.sh'` (test_lock_charter_guard.py:55), guarded by `skipif(not _REIFY_GUARD_SCRIPT.is_file())`.

From a PLAIN checkout (/home/leo/src/dark-factory/fused-memory/tests/) parents[5] == /home, so /home/reify/... is absent, the skipif fires, and the test SKIPS. From a WORKTREE (/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.worktrees/<n>/fused-memory/tests/) parents[5] == /home/leo/src, the script EXISTS, the test RUNS, and it asserts dark-factory's CODE_EXTENSIONS equals reify's live `--list-extensions` output.

CONSEQUENCE: whenever the reify allowlist and dark-factory's three copies diverge, the failure is invisible to any probe that runs in a plain checkout and unavoidable in every worktree on every branch. Diagnosed 2026-07-30 on task 3067, whose merge was blocked by this test although its diff (judge.py, test_judge.py, cli_invoke.py, test_build_claude_argv.py) touched none of the charter files — the real cause was reify commit 943978dd68 widening the allowlist 36 -> 58 on 2026-07-29, mirrored DF-side by task 3117.

WHEN YOU SEE test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script FAIL: do not treat it as a regression from the in-flight diff and do not edit the charter files to make your own branch green — they are typically inside another task's lock charter. Compare `bash /home/leo/src/reify/scripts/lock-charter-guard.sh --list-extensions | wc -l` against the DF copies, confirm your diff does not touch lock_charter_guard.py / shared/src/shared/locking.py / test_lock_charter_guard.py, and hold the merge until the mirroring task lands. There is NO gate-level escape: the merge lane's baseline machinery (orchestrator/verify.py diff_new_failures / main_baseline_failing_ids, merge_queue.py _classify_main_health_red) only re-attributes blame and enriches the reason string — the verdict is a hardcoded MergeOutcome('blocked'), there is no known-failures/quarantine config key, and merge_request exposes no force/skip_verify flag.

PEER of topic `worktree-stale-base-premise-verification` — a VERIFY/DEBUG-time variant, not a planning-time one. The 8 existing peers are all "base is stale, so landed work reads as MISSING and tempts a re-plan". This one inverts the consequence: the stale base makes a branch INHERIT main-side corruption, and the resulting test failures look like branch bugs.

MEASURED (task 3949, 2026-09-01/02). Verify on task/3949 failed 4 fused-memory tests that no task-3949 commit could reach: test_census_memory_metadata.py::TestCommittedParamsAreCheckoutIndependent::test_run_records_the_default_paths_repo_relative (CoverageHistoryError "schema_version None is not the 1 this build reads"), and 3 in test_memory_eval_retrieval_probe.py (2x KeyError 'grand_total', 1x missing 'census_topic'). Cause: on 2026-08-31 06:09 a census-timer test wrapper committed into the LIVE project_root instead of a sandbox, replacing 4 committed artifacts with 19B `{"baseline": true}` / 10B stubs (README.md, plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json, .md, plans/memory-metadata-coverage-history.json; stub commits 87ee297df8, 79397a78cc, bd092bab74, eec91ace00, all authored "Test"). task/3949's merge 08d649c745 took main at 4a34ca62d3 — inside the stub window — so the merge kept the STUB side even though its own parent 3ab23ecd09 held the full 917KB file. Main repaired all 4 in 38dc63ea42 "fix(4565): restore 4 artifacts a test harness stubbed onto main", which landed in 4a34ca62d3..main, i.e. AFTER the merge point.

THE TRAP, in 38dc63ea42's own words: the real content sat DIRTY in project_root's working tree while only the COMMITTED blob was stubbed — "so tests pass from the main checkout and fail in every merge worktree". A main-health probe that reads the working FILE returns a false green. This is the same `git show main:<path>` discipline the canonical index already preaches, but the failure mode it rescues here is a red verify, not a bad premise.

DIAGNOSTIC, when a merge worktree's verify fails on tests that read COMMITTED artifacts (fixtures, census/report JSON, registries) and nothing in the task's diff touches them:
  1. `git log --oneline main..HEAD -- <path>` — if only the merge commit lists, the branch never authored the state.
  2. `git cat-file -s HEAD:<path>` vs `git cat-file -s main:<path>` — a byte-size cliff (19B vs 1066848B) is the tell. Compare BLOBS, never the working file.
  3. `git log --oneline $(git merge-base HEAD main)..main -- <path>` — a repair commit here means main already fixed it and the branch merely predates the fix.
  4. Confirm the repair is byte-identical: `git rev-parse main:<path>` vs the last-good sha the repair commit names.
Remedy is a blob restore (`git checkout main -- <paths>`) or a merger merge of current main; because both sides then hold identical content, the restore introduces no later conflict. If the paths are outside plan scope, this is escalate_blocker(category='scope_violation') territory — filed as esc-3949-15.

STAMPED PEER under topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth` — what task 3226 ACTUALLY landed, correcting this topic's canonical prediction.

The canonical entry says "Task 3226 is the code fix that would make this whole gotcha class moot by making the guard hermetic." That is NOT what shipped, and the difference matters for triage.

WHAT 3226 DID (landed 2026-08-25, base main f38463508e):
1. Added `scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` — the cross-repo α/γ comparison run EXPLICITLY, out of suite. Three outcomes, NO skip state: EXIT_OK=0 / EXIT_DRIFT=1 / EXIT_UNAVAILABLE=2, so an absent or unrunnable sibling reports as loudly as real drift and can never read as a pass. Run it as `uv run --project shared python scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` (also `--reify-repo`, `$REIFY_ROOT`, `--json`). ATTRIBUTION: DRIFT is a cross-repo mirror gap owned by a mirror task, NEVER a fault in the dark-factory branch under test; UNAVAILABLE means nothing was compared. Documented in OPERATIONS.md §9a.
2. Closed the skip-vs-pass conflation IN THE PROBE, which is the general half of this gotcha. `verify._BASELINE_SKIPPED_IDS_CACHE` is a parallel per-main-SHA cache of SKIPPED test ids, seeded from the SAME single bare-main probe that seeds the failing baseline (a None `skipped_test_ids` seeds EMPTY, so the two caches never disagree about which shas were probed). `verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main`'s id-diff fast path now intersects its new ids with that cache and, on any hit, FALLS THROUGH to the (category, cause_hint) signature comparison instead of returning the confident task-fault `(False, '')` — one unattributable id invalidates the whole diff. `merge_queue._run_post_merge_verify` partitions the same way, so "N new failing test(s) not present on main" counts only tests main actually RAN, and skipped-on-main ids get their own clause. Both are CACHE-ONLY peeks (no probe on the critical path, G4/task 2564), so a cold cache degrades to the pre-3226 behaviour exactly.

WHAT 3226 DID NOT DO: it did not make the guard hermetic and did not delete the in-suite gates. As of this landing the real /home/leo/src/reify checkout is still executed during an ordinary dark-factory run by 5 gates in fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py and 4 in shared/tests/test_locking.py (plus TestReifyCheckoutPlantedLayout, ~250 lines whose purpose is to assert those gates are ARMED — task 4080). Deleting them would reverse tasks 3843/3978/3248/4080 and drop the coverage that catches real α/γ divergence, and 3226's own charter says "Do NOT simply delete the guard". So a reify-side allowlist change with no dark-factory change involved CAN STILL red this repo's suite. Recorded as esc-3226-5.

REVISED TRIAGE RULE: the parents[5] arithmetic that made bare-main and worktree disagree is gone (tasks 3843→3978 replaced it with a marker-bound nearest-ancestor walk single-sourced in shared/src/shared/reify_checkout.py; a fixed parents[N] index is now a REGRESSION, not a fix). Bare main and a worktree therefore reach the SAME reify root, so probe and branch agree and a drift failure classifies as MAIN_HEALTH_RED rather than blaming an innocent task. When you do hit one: run `scripts/check_lock_charter_drift.py` to get the answer without the full suite, and treat a DRIFT verdict as mirror work, not as the merging task's diff.

GOTCHA — a post_merge_verify failure in fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py::test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script is a PREEXISTING MAIN BREAK, not the merging task's fault (owner: dark_factory task 3117, the γ-mirror of reify #5726, which landed and widened the α lock-charter extension allowlist 36 -> 58 while all three dark-factory copies still pin 36).

Diagnostic that generalises beyond this one test: the Tier-2 guard's skipif keys on `Path(__file__).parents[5] / 'reify' / 'scripts' / 'lock-charter-guard.sh'`, so its visibility depends only on CHECKOUT DEPTH, never on the diff —
  <DF>/fused-memory/tests/            -> parents[5]=/home         -> absent  -> SKIPS
  <DF>/.worktrees/<n or _merge-* or _mainprobe-*>/fused-memory/tests/ -> parents[5]=/home/leo/src -> present -> RUNS and FAILS
Consequence: main looks GREEN from the plain project_root checkout and is RED in every worktree. Do not conclude "does not pre-exist on main" from a project_root-run probe. `main_baseline_failing_ids` mints its probe as `_mainprobe-<id>` under git_ops.worktree_base (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py ~:1049), i.e. depth 5, so the real probe DOES see it and should classify it wholly preexisting.

Cheap attribution recipe, no full suite needed: (1) `git diff main...HEAD -- fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/lock_charter_guard.py shared/src/shared/locking.py` — empty means the branch cannot be the cause; (2) compare `bash /home/leo/src/reify/scripts/lock-charter-guard.sh --list-extensions` (58) against main's CODE_EXTENSIONS literal (36) to evaluate the assertion directly against bare main.

Do NOT mirror the 22 extensions from inside an unrelated task: it spans four files outside any such task's charter (shared/src/shared/locking.py, shared/tests/test_locking.py, fused-memory/.../lock_charter_guard.py, fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py) and is a behavioural widening of the submit_task/scheduler lock-charter gate. Resolve the escalation as benign/preexisting and retry; if the same single failing id escalates again, land 3117 rather than re-verifying the innocent branch.

members.text: In reify capability manifests, `grep:` is a binding-KIND token in the evidence taxonomy, NOT a durability convention, and its trailing `wired` is a verdict word — not a greppable anchor. Per ~/.claude/skills/prd/references/gates.md and decompose-mode.md:48, `grep:file:line wired` / `producer:task-N upstream` / `grammar-fixture:path parses` / `floor:bound>X` are the same `<kind>:<locator> <verdict-word>` grammar, and grep:/producer: are two alternative PASS routes for the SAME anti-orphan check. So `grep:git_ops.py:789-809 wired` carries no anchor at all. The durable payload already sanctioned under that same kind is `grep:<file> <symbol> wired` (see warm-lane-pool-activation-seam.capability-manifest.md:59 and v0_6/differential-field-operators.capability-manifest.md:7). De-numbering a binding is gate-safe: the `binding` string is never machine-parsed (shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py takes it as free text) and the enforced artifact is the .yaml `delivered_check`, which is pattern-only and contractually forbidden from using file:line.

CAPABILITY MANIFESTS ARE FAILING IN A SPECIFIC, REPEATING WAY IN REIFY — two independent instances surfaced on 2026-08-07 alone, in unrelated subsystems. The failure is a row marked PASS on evidence that ROUTES AROUND the capability it claims. Instance 1, `docs/prds/v0_6/io-export-import-completion.capability-manifest.md:67`: `| version param reaches export | via δ driver (reads version off STEPOutput) | PASS (δ upstream) |` — a leaf's capability marked PASS on the strength of a SIBLING LEAF'S FUTURE WORK. The manifest also had NO row at all asserting the thing that actually broke ("demanded tolerance reaches OcctKernel::export()"), and its header dates all evidence to a pre-flight snapshot never re-checked after the leaves landed. Instance 2, the predecessor jcodemunch PRD: its live-serve bindings all route around the Rust client — `L-SERVE` binds a curl smoke, `L-CLIENT` a static decode of captured fixtures, `L-WIRE` a construction-site substitution — and the one binding that would have caught the real defect, `L-SMOKE`, names `scripts/smoke-jcodemunch-audit.sh` WHICH DOES NOT EXIST; what shipped instead is `#[ignore]`-gated AND graceful-skips on a bare TCP-connect probe. RULES THAT FOLLOW, for anyone authoring a manifest: (a) never mark a row PASS on a sibling leaf's future work — that is the phantom-completion vector in pure form; (b) never bind a row to a script or test that does not exist — verify the path; (c) a binding that exercises the seam from the OUTSIDE (curl, captured fixtures, a construction-site substitution) does not evidence that the PRODUCTION client works — bind to the production path or say the row is unevidenced; (d) beware bindings that graceful-skip, since a skip-erasing helper reads as PASS when the thing is broken. Also note the structural gap: NOTHING IN REIFY PARSES `*.capability-manifest.md` — only the `.yaml` sidecar's `delivered_check` rows are mechanically evaluated, and that happens downstream in dark-factory's merge queue, with `kind: manual` rows excluded. reify's own literature already names this: `docs/prds/prd-gate-executable-substrate-verification.md:19` — "it only converts free-text promises into tabulated promises that nothing executes".

reify-eval: never test "is a geometry kernel registered" via `Engine::default_kernel_name.is_none()` (or any registry-non-emptiness check) as a proxy for "this binary can tessellate". It is FALSE on every shipped binary. `crates/reify-kernel-manifold/src/register.rs` does its `inventory::submit!` UNCONDITIONALLY (no cfg gate — its manifold3d dep compiles its own C++ tree, so there is no "manifold absent" build), and `crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs`'s `extern crate reify_kernel_manifold as _;` states verbatim that the "manifold" key is always present in the binary's registry. `kernel_registry::pick_lexmin_brep_kernel` ends in `.or_else(|| registered.values().next())`, so even a stub-mode (no-OCCT) binary gets `default_kernel_name == Some("manifold")` — a Mesh-only kernel that cannot tessellate a B-rep subject. Only the `Engine::new(checker, None)` unit-test seam ever reaches an empty registry, so tests written against that shape pass green while the shipped behaviour is wrong.

Test CAPABILITY instead: `CapabilityDescriptor::supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep)` over the engine's own `geometry_kernels` names looked up in the static `kernel_registry`. OCCT is the only BRep producer in the workspace (its submit is `cfg(has_occt)`-gated; manifold declares Mesh, openvdb Voxel/Mesh), so that predicate is an exact test for "this binary was built with OCCT". `GeometryKernel` is a purely behavioural trait with no capability accessor — the descriptor lives on the `KernelRegistration` record — which is why the lookup goes through the registry rather than the kernel object. Reference implementation: `Engine::has_repr_capable_kernel` / `Engine::unmeasured_reason` in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_constraints.rs (task 6169, esc-6169-4).

Corollary for tests: a CLI/integration test whose expected wording differs by build mode must gate on `reify_kernel_occt::OCCT_AVAILABLE` (= `cfg!(has_occt)`, crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:20) — the same fact the engine keys on — or DERIVE the expectation from the registry. Hardcoding one mode's wording passes only because the local build has OCCT and silently breaks on a stub build, which per CLAUDE.md can arise from an OCCT SONAME move (task #6343). Related INV-SF-4 rule: when the engine cannot establish a cause, state the observable fact and point at an actionable remedy rather than blaming a component that is demonstrably present — a false "missing kernel" is the same misattribution sin as the original "operator undefined for these operand kinds", merely relocated.

CLARIFIED 2026-09-08 (curator sitting; verified against reify main @ efbc0932bd). The distinction that makes this rule bite is ENGINE-INSTANCE STATE vs LINKED-BINARY INVENTORY — two different things that `is_none()` is habitually misread as collapsing into one:
- The LINKED BINARY's inventory is the static `inventory::submit!` set. On any shipped CLI it is never empty (`crates/reify-kernel-manifold/src/register.rs:62-69` submits with no `#[cfg]`; `crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:20` links it unconditionally), so the empty-registry branch of `pick_lexmin_brep_kernel_in` (`crates/reify-eval/src/kernel_registry.rs:211-219`) is UNREACHABLE there and its `.or_else(|| registered.values().next())` fallback always yields `Some("manifold")` in stub mode.
- `Engine::default_kernel_name` is a field on the ENGINE INSTANCE (`crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs:455`), set only from what THAT instance was handed (`crates/reify-eval/src/engine_admin.rs:231-236`). `Engine::new(checker, None)` — production CLI code at `crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:947, 1100, 1983, 2127, 2287`, and the shape behind `make_simple_engine` (`crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs:106-108`) — leaves it `None` on a fully OCCT-equipped binary.
So the predicate is wrong in BOTH directions, not merely conservative: it is FALSE while the engine cannot tessellate a BRep (shipped stub mode, `Some("manifold")`), and TRUE while the binary is fully kernel-equipped (`Engine::new(_, None)`). It is neit [cut]

NORM for SATISFYING a capability-manifest `expect: absent` delivered_check: purge the forbidden literal from TEST FIXTURE INPUTS in the scoped paths too, not just production code — a mechanical grep cannot tell a live default from a test argument. Sighting 2026-08-21, task 6108 (jcodemunch gamma): the legacy leodearden/reify default was fully removed from production sites in crates/reify-audit/src/bin/reify-audit.rs, yet the manifest check (pattern leodearden/reify, paths crates/reify-audit/src, expect absent) still FAILED on one hit at jcodemunch_index.rs:561, where the literal was only the INPUT to an index_db_path slash-flattening assertion. Fix: substitute a neutral same-shaped literal (owner/project yields owner-project.db); behaviour under test unchanged. Corollary making an absence-guard TEST compatible with the manifest check rather than contradictory (raised as unachievable in esc-6108-3, dismissed): give the guard test a strictly SHORTER needle than the manifest pattern — the guard asserts help text lacks the bare owner token with no slash, which cannot match the manifest's slashed pattern. A non-matching-prefix needle is what lets both hold at once.

claim: Capability evidence and tests must verify the real production seam, not proxies, unrelated work, skipped checks, or misleading fixture artifacts.

[CORRECTED 2026-08-23 — see mem 48e2b53d-dc75-4f5a-83f4-4ce14ad504ea] The "STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out below is NOT reliably sanctioned: two independent review blocks (task 3465 — skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md + OPERATIONS.md marker spans, runtime-derived via stdlib ast, loud-failing extractors, STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline; and task 3544, mem0 3c294ce3 — mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test) were both blocked and mandated for deletion by reviewer_comprehensive despite following this carve-out exactly. The reviewer keys on the ASSERTION TARGET being doc prose, a string literal, or an introspected name — not on whether the value is runtime-derived or marker-anchored. Before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's own package already asserts those tokens against real produced output (often making the guard redundant with existing behavioural coverage). Treat the "sanctioned alternative" paragraph below as historical context, not current planning guidance.

---original content---
dark-factory enforces a repo-wide norm AGAINST pytest tests that pin documentation prose, and it is written into the test files themselves: tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_service_files.py:1263, tests/scripts/test_ruff_format_policy.py:48-51, tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py:38-40 and scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py:33-40 each carry a docstring forbidding extension into a wording pin, orchestrator/tests/test_roles_ancestry_check.py:21-36 rejects a proposed "grep skills/*/SKILL.md" test by name as a documentation meta-test, and one such prose pin was actually deleted in review (task 3802 remediation, recorded at test_design_invariants_consistency.py:1167-1170). The sanctioned alternative when a doc genuinely must not drift is a STRUCTURAL drift guard: derive the expected value from live code/config at runtime, anchor the doc side on an HTML-comment marker pair (the lint-command-mirror convention in CONTRIBUTING.md), unit-test the extractor against hand-written fixture markdown rather than the real doc, and make the extractor raise loudly instead of returning empty. Consequence for planning: a prose-only change to a skills/*/SKILL.md is correctly planned as impl-only with no test step — commits 0824cae7a3, 812e186780 and a322d65007 are all single-file, test-free SKILL.md amendments.

dark-factory has NO /prd project overlay (.claude/skills/prd/project.md does not exist) — the /prd skill runs in generic mode here. Writing the actual overlay file would let future /prd runs skip re-inferring this.

Process norm for dark_factory: the /prd skill runs in GENERIC mode — there is no .claude/skills/prd/project.md overlay for this repo. Conventions observed/used: PRD files live at plans/<slug>-prd.md; the capability manifest is committed beside the PRD as plans/<slug>-prd.capability-manifest.md; both are committed directly to main in the same skill turn (task agents run in worktrees branched from main and need the PRD on disk before decompose references it).
