members.text: scripts/tests/ (e.g. scripts/legibility/*.py) is verified via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/...` — this scopes execution to shared/pyproject.toml's own dependency set (pydantic, pydantic-settings, aiosqlite, pyyaml, python-dotenv only). Packages like jsonschema, ruamel.yaml, etc. that are only transitive deps of other workspace members (fused-memory, orchestrator, escalation per their uv.lock) are NOT importable there, even though they may appear available in an ambient/full-workspace venv. When writing a scripts/ module, verify package availability against `uv run --project shared python -c "import X"`, not the interactive dev shell's venv. This convention is load-bearing: see `_FALLBACK_UV_PROJECT = 'shared'` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py and the comment in shared/pyproject.toml (task 2070).

GOTCHA: a task whose only touched .py under a module prefix is a test file whose items are ALL marker-deselected by that module's pyproject addopts gets a scoped verify TEST leg that collects ZERO items -> pytest rc=5 "no tests ran" -> RED, even when the change is entirely correct.

Mechanism. verify_plan.py `_derive_module_runs`, the `elif collectable_tests:` branch, file-scopes the module's test_command to the touched test files. `classify_file` is purely PATH-based (name starts with `test_` => COLLECTABLE_TEST) and has no notion of marker deselection. Note the adjacent branch: a SOURCE-only diff at role='task' gets FULL_SUITE — it is specifically touching the deselected test file that narrows the leg to nothing.

Do NOT try to fix this in the classifier. verify_classify.py `_classify_opaque` pins it: "INVARIANT (task 1852): pytest rc=5 is intentionally classified RED here ... A real test target that unexpectedly collects zero tests must stay RED so the merge gate catches 'tests vanished' regressions — the data-module false-RED is fixed in the SCOPING layer, not here." Task 1852 already closed one instance of this class (test-data modules) at the scoping layer; marker deselection is a second instance the path-based predicate cannot see.

First live instance: orchestrator/pyproject.toml addopts gained `-m 'not warm_lane_bash'` (task 3349, 2026-08-01), moving the bucket to the offline warm-lane-bash lane. Task 3292 was the first task to touch orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py afterwards and redded on 0 items while its real coverage was green (214 passed / 0 failed standalone; 12/12 under `-m warm_lane_bash`; lint + type green). Escalated as esc-3292-1.

Diagnosing it: `uv run pytest <the touched test file> --collect-only -q` inside the module. "no tests collected (N deselected)" confirms it; compare against `uv run pytest tests/ --collect-only -q`. The verify log signature is `16 workers [0 items]` / `no tests ran`, categorised unknown_test_failure, with lint and type both green.

There is NO per-task or per-module scoping override — nothing in docs/task-authoring.md, nothing scope-related in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/defaults.yaml, and no rc=5 retry/widen anywhere in orchestrator/src or shared/src. So a dispatched agent cannot satisfy an obligation like the one at plans/warm-lane-infra-repatriation-prd.md:237 ("leaves must run `-m warm_lane_bash` explicitly on their own verify legs"). Escalate rather than improvising; re-enabling the bucket in addopts would break the addopts<->lane biconditional pinned by orchestrator/tests/test_warm_lane_bash_bucket_placement.py.

Gotcha: the scripts/tests/ directory (1228 tests, covering the sweep and audit scripts) is NOT exercised by any orchestrator verify chain. Both the root dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml test_command and the scoped scripts/orchestrator.yaml test_command run "uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/" — the repo-root tests/scripts/ directory, a DIFFERENT path that merely transposes the two segments. So a task scoped to scripts/ gets a green verify that never ran the tests for the files it changed. When working on anything under scripts/, run "uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/ -q --timeout=300" explicitly; a green fleet verify proves nothing about it. Verified 2026-08-01 by reading both yaml test_commands directly (task 3336).

claim: Scoped verification can miss real scripts or tests because of environment and selection boundaries, so validate the exact test command and dependencies rather than trusting a green verify.

members.text: Architect premise-verification must check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-commit> main`, NOT just read the file in its own worktree. Task 2778's worktree was based on a HEAD 9 days stale (5d07e3818b) that predated the fix, so the stale "Interim reality: hand-stamp" blockquote still appeared locally in skills/prd/references/decompose-mode.md even though it had been removed on main (02ee855dee, merged via 492f8bda2b "Merge task/2778 into main"). Reading the worktree file falsely CONFIRMS a stale premise and leads to re-planning already-landed work. Contradicts the older assumption that a new worktree's HEAD equals main — verify with `git rev-parse HEAD` vs `git rev-parse main` and inspect `git show main:<path>` / `git grep <token> main` before trusting local contents.

GOTCHA — a post_merge_verify failure in fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py::test_extension_drift_guard_vs_reify_script is a PREEXISTING MAIN BREAK, not the merging task's fault (owner: dark_factory task 3117, the γ-mirror of reify #5726, which landed and widened the α lock-charter extension allowlist 36 -> 58 while all three dark-factory copies still pin 36).

Diagnostic that generalises beyond this one test: the Tier-2 guard's skipif keys on `Path(__file__).parents[5] / 'reify' / 'scripts' / 'lock-charter-guard.sh'`, so its visibility depends only on CHECKOUT DEPTH, never on the diff —
  <DF>/fused-memory/tests/            -> parents[5]=/home         -> absent  -> SKIPS
  <DF>/.worktrees/<n or _merge-* or _mainprobe-*>/fused-memory/tests/ -> parents[5]=/home/leo/src -> present -> RUNS and FAILS
Consequence: main looks GREEN from the plain project_root checkout and is RED in every worktree. Do not conclude "does not pre-exist on main" from a project_root-run probe. `main_baseline_failing_ids` mints its probe as `_mainprobe-<id>` under git_ops.worktree_base (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py ~:1049), i.e. depth 5, so the real probe DOES see it and should classify it wholly preexisting.

Cheap attribution recipe, no full suite needed: (1) `git diff main...HEAD -- fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/lock_charter_guard.py shared/src/shared/locking.py` — empty means the branch cannot be the cause; (2) compare `bash /home/leo/src/reify/scripts/lock-charter-guard.sh --list-extensions` (58) against main's CODE_EXTENSIONS literal (36) to evaluate the assertion directly against bare main.

Do NOT mirror the 22 extensions from inside an unrelated task: it spans four files outside any such task's charter (shared/src/shared/locking.py, shared/tests/test_locking.py, fused-memory/.../lock_charter_guard.py, fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py) and is a behavioural widening of the submit_task/scheduler lock-charter gate. Resolve the escalation as benign/preexisting and retry; if the same single failing id escalates again, land 3117 rather than re-verifying the innocent branch.

Codebase gotcha (git_ops.py): `is_ancestor(HEAD, main)` returns True TRIVIALLY for a zero-commit branch whose tip equals the main HEAD at branch-create time — documented in find_task_citation_commit (git_ops.py:3331) and find_merge_marker (:3277). So it CANNOT distinguish a landed/merged branch from a freshly-created zero-commit one. To confirm a REAL landing, grep main's history for the canonical merge subject via `_merge_subject(branch, main)` (git_ops.py:578) with `git log <main> --fixed-strings --grep=... --format=%H` (the find_merge_marker pattern). The interactive-worktree reaper (task 2012) relies on this to avoid reaping a just-created _iact-* worktree mid-session.

claim: Verify repository state against main using context-aware history and diagnostics; local worktree contents or simple ancestry checks can mislead.

STAMPED PEER under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` — a FIFTH subcase, observed on dark_factory task 4115 (merge request mr-5b8a2168, landed 2026-08-21T12:21:47Z).

THE NEW SUBCASE: `merge_status` returns `state='done'` with NEITHER `merge_sha` NOR `kind`. This is the durable-tier (retention ring / event store) response shape, and it is what the /unblock runbook's polled-done branch calls the "re-derive from git" case. On a REBASE landing that re-derivation chain dead-ends: the runbook says to run `git log main --fixed-strings --grep="Merge task/<ID> into main"`, which returns EMPTY because no merge commit was created, and then to "fall back to {note: ...}" — i.e. record NO commit SHA at all. So the runbook's own fallback silently degrades a perfectly attributable landing into a note-only provenance stamp.

ALL THREE STANDARD SIGNALS READ "NOT LANDED" while the work WAS on main:
  - `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/4115 main` -> rc=1 (not rc=0, not rc=128)
  - branch ref task/4115 still existed at its pre-merge tip 95a16d6cc4
  - exact-subject marker search -> EMPTY

THE DECISIVE CHECK, and the one to reach for: diff the branch against main restricted to the task's DECLARED files.
    git diff main task/<ID> -- <declared file 1> <declared file 2>
An EMPTY result proves the landed content is byte-identical, which is a positive proof of landing rather than the absence of a ref signal. For 4115 this was empty for both declared files while a whole-tree `git diff main task/4115` showed only ONE file (docs/prds/claimant-invariant-enforcement.md, 400 deletions) — main having a newer unrelated commit the branch lacked, which is the expected asymmetry and NOT missing work. Cross-check it with subject matching: all 7 of 4115's commit subjects were findable on main under new SHAs.

STAMPING THE PROVENANCE: use kind='found_on_main' with commit=<the top commit of the branch's landed run on main> (for 4115: 14cfe63892786012b444221e3c4784258929dc7e, found by exact-subject search for the branch TIP's subject). This is legitimate and is NOT the runbook's forbidden "eyeball `git log main --oneline | head -5` and pick a SHA": the SHA is derived by exact-subject match to the branch's own tip commit AND corroborated by the byte-identical content check. The server's only backstop (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`) passes correctly here because that commit genuinely IS on main.

OPERATIONAL TELL: a background poller watching only `--is-ancestor` will run to its ceiling and look like a stall on a SUCCESSFUL landing. On 4115 a Monitor armed on ancestry-or-worker-quiet timed out at 40 minutes while the merge had in fact completed 15 minutes earlier.

DEEP-STALENESS ARM of the lock-charter drift-guard stale-lane variant: past ~a month of lane staleness, the "do not hand-port the allowlist" advice stops being about duplicating a commit and becomes about writing a symbol that NO LONGER EXISTS on main.

The existing peers (task 3134 / esc-3134-1, and the task-4412 entry) cover lanes 31 and 1251 commits behind, each with a delta of exactly {'tombstones'} (59 -> 60), and correctly prescribe: if main == reify's emitter and the lane does not, it is staleness — ask for a rebase, do not cherry-pick, do not hand-edit the 4-5 copies.

MEASURED 2026-09-11, task 2896 lane (HEAD=c267573b73, esc-2896-9). Same shape, an order of magnitude deeper: lane base 046947eb44 dated 2026-07-22, main tip 5b51fa970b dated 2026-09-11, `git rev-list --count base..main` = 11704. Lane vector 36 entries, reify's live `--list-extensions` 60, main's canonical vector extracted and diffed against that emitter = IDENTICAL 60 (main green). Mirror commit 9b824da7db an ancestor of main, not of the base. Branch-only diff touched neither guard file (empty `git diff base..HEAD` for both). Lint "All checks passed!", pyright "0 errors", suite 7891 passed / 1 failed — the guard was the only red.

THE NEW WRINKLE, and why it strengthens the no-hand-port rule rather than merely repeating it: at this depth main had also RENAMED the identifier. `git show main:fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/lock_charter_guard.py | grep CODE_EXTENSIONS` returns NOTHING — it is FILE_EXTENSIONS on main now, plus a new EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES vector, and main's test module resolves the reify checkout via shared.reify_checkout and carries an added corpus->allowlist guard. So hand-typing 60 entries into a stale lane's `CODE_EXTENSIONS` does not converge toward main at all; it authors a THIRD shape that conflicts on contact. Generalisation: the older the base, the more the hand-port target has itself moved — check `git show main:<path> | grep <symbol>` before assuming the symbol you are about to edit still exists upstream.

PRACTICAL NOTE for triage: the existing recipe's step "exec main's copy and sort FILE_EXTENSIONS" can fail silently on a deep-stale lane because main's module no longer defines a frozenset literal by that name. Fall back to extracting `_CANONICAL_EXTENSIONS` from `git show main:fused-memory/tests/test_lock_charter_guard.py` and diffing THAT against the emitter — it gave a clean identical-60 result here.

Peer under topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth`; the allowlist's own sync/count facts stay canonical under `lock-charter-extension-allowlist` (and per that entry, do not write down a fixed count as a durable fact — the counts above are dated measurements).

PEER of topic `worktree-stale-base-premise-verification`, direction (a) STALE BASE — the VERIFY/DEBUG-time variant, and the one-command diagnostic that settles it in seconds.

SHAPE. A task branch's verify goes red on a test the branch never touched, because the base predates a fix main already landed. Sibling peer 001acf5d records this for the scripts/ LINT gate (task 3614); this peer records it for a repo-wide META-TEST, where the mechanism is nastier: the test's verdict depends on the whole repo's content, not on the changed files, so "my diff doesn't touch that file" feels like a weak argument and agents talk themselves into hand-fixing it.

MEASURED (task 4286, debugger, 2026-09-09). `scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py::test_every_enumeration_site_is_pinned` failed: `docs/code-quality.md` restates 4+ invariant slugs but is not in PINNED_SITES. The branch's diff was 4 .py files, no markdown. merge-base 3470f61ae2 was 99 commits behind main; main (bf23ca33dd) ALREADY registered the file. Fix commit: d2459bd9a7 "fix(5230): register docs/code-quality.md in PINNED_SITES (fix-forward RED main)", landed 2026-09-08, i.e. the RED had been a genuine main-health event that main repaired forward.

THE DIAGNOSTIC, in order — each cheap, and the second one usually ends the investigation:
1. `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` — is the failing artifact even in your diff?
2. `git log --oneline $(git merge-base HEAD main)..main -- <failing-file>` — the killer. It lists exactly the main-side commits your base is missing FOR THAT FILE. A subject line containing "fix-forward", "RED main", or the test's own name is a confession; read the commit message, which often states which test it turned green.
3. `git show main:<path>` to confirm the repaired content, and `git rev-list --count <merge-base>..main` for the staleness magnitude.

DO NOT HAND-PORT THE FIX, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong. The upstream fix is often one step of a multi-commit chain, so the obvious-looking single commit is not self-contained. Here d2459bd9a7 (8 insertions — irresistibly cherry-pickable) only ADDS the registry entry; the pair-wise assertion that entry advertises lands separately in 1964555b6d (77 lines). Cherry-picking d2459bd9a7 alone would have registered a site with no actual pin — silencing the guard while hollowing it out, a strictly worse state than the red. Before cherry-picking anything, run `git log --oneline <merge-base>..main -- <file>` and look at how many commits the fix spans.

CORRECT EXIT: escalate for a BASE REFRESH (merge/rebase main), which brings the chain in as a coherent unit, and say so with the fix commit named. `git merge-tree --write-tree main <branch>` (peer ab747acb) prices the refresh without touching the tree.

COROLLARY for the same investigation: separate the deterministic red from the flakes before escalating. Two sibling failures in that run (`test_restart_all_orchestrators.py`, wall-clock bash-subprocess tests with a 15s cap) passed on isolated re-run — they had failed on an xdist worker while the sibling orchestrator suite burned 3438s of CPU. A verify attempt that fans out across two module prefixes is a load event, so timing-sensitive tests failing there are load flakes until an isolated re-run says otherwise.

claim: When Git signals or a stale branch mislead, verify against current main and refresh from it rather than infer status or hand-port changes.

[CORRECTED 2026-08-23 — see mem 48e2b53d-dc75-4f5a-83f4-4ce14ad504ea] The "STRUCTURAL drift guard" carve-out below is NOT reliably sanctioned: two independent review blocks (task 3465 — skills/escalation-watcher-auto/SKILL.md + OPERATIONS.md marker spans, runtime-derived via stdlib ast, loud-failing extractors, STRUCTURE-NEVER-WORDING discipline; and task 3544, mem0 3c294ce3 — mermaid-vs-TRANSITIONS parity test) were both blocked and mandated for deletion by reviewer_comprehensive despite following this carve-out exactly. The reviewer keys on the ASSERTION TARGET being doc prose, a string literal, or an introspected name — not on whether the value is runtime-derived or marker-anchored. Before planning any producer→consumer mirror guard, first check whether the producer's own package already asserts those tokens against real produced output (often making the guard redundant with existing behavioural coverage). Treat the "sanctioned alternative" paragraph below as historical context, not current planning guidance.

---original content---
dark-factory enforces a repo-wide norm AGAINST pytest tests that pin documentation prose, and it is written into the test files themselves: tests/scripts/test_orchestrator_service_files.py:1263, tests/scripts/test_ruff_format_policy.py:48-51, tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py:38-40 and scripts/tests/test_design_invariants_consistency.py:33-40 each carry a docstring forbidding extension into a wording pin, orchestrator/tests/test_roles_ancestry_check.py:21-36 rejects a proposed "grep skills/*/SKILL.md" test by name as a documentation meta-test, and one such prose pin was actually deleted in review (task 3802 remediation, recorded at test_design_invariants_consistency.py:1167-1170). The sanctioned alternative when a doc genuinely must not drift is a STRUCTURAL drift guard: derive the expected value from live code/config at runtime, anchor the doc side on an HTML-comment marker pair (the lint-command-mirror convention in CONTRIBUTING.md), unit-test the extractor against hand-written fixture markdown rather than the real doc, and make the extractor raise loudly instead of returning empty. Consequence for planning: a prose-only change to a skills/*/SKILL.md is correctly planned as impl-only with no test step — commits 0824cae7a3, 812e186780 and a322d65007 are all single-file, test-free SKILL.md amendments.

NORM (task 3554, review-established): a guard/config test must never assert on comment or docstring PROSE in files it does not own. A ratchet in tests/scripts/ that required every entry of an exclusion set to still contain the literal 'skills/' made a cosmetic comment reword in scripts/tests/test_legibility_sampling.py red-wall a merge-blocking module config — measured as `1 failed, 5 passed` from a diff touching nothing the guard gated. Assert on RUNTIME state instead (discovered module-config prefixes, git ls-files/grep sweeps, parsed command targets, file existence). Do NOT "fix" such coupling with a word-boundary or regex variant: that keeps the identical cross-package prose dependency while hiding it. For a triage-style set (real-consumer inventory vs excluded mentions), gate only the ADD direction — an unmatched exclusion key is inert, since the untriaged check consults the triaged set for membership only, so a key matching no file cannot make any still-mentioning file pass. Prune stale exclusions opportunistically when the file is next touched.

dark-factory has NO /prd project overlay: .claude/skills/prd/project.md does not exist (only .claude/skills/hotspot-survey/project.md does), so the /prd skill runs in GENERIC mode on this repo — it elicits path conventions rather than reading them. The de-facto conventions, inferable from plans/, are: PRDs at plans/<slug>-prd.md, capability manifests at plans/<slug>-prd.capability-manifest.md with a YAML sidecar twin plans/<slug>-prd.capability-manifest.yaml. Writing that overlay would be a cheap improvement — it would supply the PRD output path, the G2 signal vocabulary, the G3 substrate verifier, load-bearing seam names for G5, and exemplar pointers, none of which a generic-mode session gets.

claim: Keep repo-specific conventions explicit in owned configuration, and make tests verify runtime behavior rather than prose in files they don’t own.

A ratchet in tests/scripts/ that required every entry of an exclusion set to still contain the literal 'skills/' made a cosmetic comment reword in scripts/tests/test_legibility_sampling.py red-wall a merge-blocking module config — measured as `1 failed, 5 passed` from a diff touching nothing the guard gated. Assert on RUNTIME state instead (discovered module-config prefixes, git ls-files/grep sweeps, parsed command targets, file existence). Do NOT "fix" such coupling with a word-boundary or regex variant: that keeps the identical cross-package prose dependency while hiding it. For a triage-style set (real-consumer inventory vs excluded mentions), gate only the ADD direction — an unmatched exclusion key is inert, since the untriaged check consults the triaged set for membership only, so a key matching no file cannot make any still-mentioning file pass. Prune stale exclusions opportunistically when the file is next touched.

Do NOT build, keep, or HARDEN tests that assert on docstring/comment PROSE in dark-factory. Codified policy at three enforcement points, all introduced together in commit 7abff876d7, all verified verbatim in-repo on 2026-08-20:

1. ARCHITECT rule 5 "Test scope — skip documentation meta-tests" (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py): do NOT plan test steps that assert on __doc__ strings, docstring prose, comment contents, or module-level string literals, or that "Grep source files for 'did the author mention X' strings". "One-line `assert Foo.__doc__` existence checks inside an API-surface contract test are fine; 50-line substring/regex pins of prose are not."
2. REVIEWER_COMPREHENSIVE (same file): flag as `blocking` any test whose assertions target __doc__ strings, module-level string literals, comment contents, or the prose of another test file. Recommended fix: DELETE the meta-test; if documentation drift is a real concern, fix the source doc once and move on. Explicitly: 'Do NOT propose "harden the docstring-pin regex" as a follow-up — that just deepens the hole.'
3. TRIAGE SKIP rules (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/triage.py): documentation-only wording fixes, AND "Docstring-pin hardening suggestions" — any suggestion to strengthen a regex/substring/AST walk used to assert documentation wording. "The right fix is to delete the meta-test, not to harden it."

THE TRAP, recorded because a steward fell into it on task 4240 and had to reverse itself: when such a guard is found to have a coverage hole (there, a start-anchored regex that missed every path-qualified citation, seeing 45 citations where 64 existed), hardening the regex feels like the obviously-correct engineering fix — it is concrete, measurable and satisfying, and a reviewer's "just delete it" reads like an opinion to be weighed. It is the specifically-banned remedy. A coverage hole in a prose meta-test is evidence for DELETING it, not improving it: the policy's own rationale is that these "frequently ship subtle regex/substring bugs that let real regressions slip through", so finding exactly such a bug CONFIRMS the policy rather than creating an exception to it.

A SECOND ERROR FROM THE SAME EPISODE, worth generalising: do not argue from a NAME-pattern census to a claim about assertion content. "~281 test classes match Test*(Drift|SelfContainment|Completeness|Guard|Contract), therefore prose guards are conventional here" is invalid — those assert on structured config/import/AST drift, not prose. Two guards cited as precedent carry written prohibitions against extension to prose: tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py ("about surrounding prose, and must not be extended to") and tests/scripts/test_ruff_format_policy.py ("It asserts nothing about prose ... and must not be extended to"). main carries zero prose-asserting meta-tests in .py source, and several have been deleted (e.g. 099b1f25cd on task 4236, the near-duplicate sibling of 4240).

CORRECT RESPONSE to documentation drift here: fix the source doc once, at source, and move on — what task 4126 did. Do not build a guard; do not file a follow-up to harden one. Before defending any prose-asserting test against a reviewer, read these three policy sites first: the reviewer is executing codified policy, not offering a preference.

Dark-factory convention: docstrings and comments should NOT cite source locations by line number (e.g. "see run_server:317-318", "see line ~96") — line references drift silently on every refactor to either file, including the SAME commit that adds them (task 3508 added ~89 lines to memory_service.py and thereby invalidated its own five citations, 2676-2689 -> 2755-2768 and 2984-2986 -> 3063-3068, before review even ran). Prefer symbolic/self-locating references instead: name the function/class/handler directly ("see WriteJournal fallback in run_server", "see app.py's paused_reason TODO"), cite by SYMBOL (`MemoryService.add_memory`, `GraphitiBackend.add_episode`) rather than `file.py:NNNN`, or refer to code blocks by name or content rather than position.

Applies especially to test docstrings and regression-test comments, where a stale pointer is easy to miss and no test covers it: task 3565 found three broken line-range citations in fused-memory/tests (test_merge_entities.py:980-1132, :1021-1131, and :154), two of which pointed past EOF or into unrelated code after task 3502's probe consolidation shifted lines.

In scripts/, this shows up as a SYMBOL-NAME convention specifically: scripts/_task_db_scan.py uses Sphinx refs (:func:`run_audit_cli`, :data:`AUDIT_EXIT_OK`) and contains zero bare line numbers; scripts/repair_wiped_metadata_files.py reserves `path/file.py:NNN` for cross-FILE refs only and records the lesson inline at :308 ("orchestrator/.../workflow.py:4550 — located by NAME; it moved once already"). Watch for the self-invalidating case: an edit that ADDS lines to a file shifts every anchor below it, so line numbers written into that same commit's docstring/comment are stale on write.

In dark-factory's warm-lane scripts and their tests, keep a divergence's full rationale in exactly one home (e.g. orchestrator/scripts/warm-lane/README.md's enumerated Deltas) and let the script comment/test docstring carry only the operative facts plus a symbolic pointer — do not embed base-commit SHAs or verbatim shell transcripts in test docstrings either.

Docstrings (especially on small test fixtures/helpers) should state the contract, not carry review/task lineage prose or call-site counts either — put the "why task N did this" narrative in the commit message and task record instead, and reference a convention by name ("the module's function-local-import convention") rather than by line number.

claim: Keep tests and documentation resilient by asserting on runtime or structured behavior and using symbolic references, not brittle prose, line numbers, or embedded history.

PEER of topic `worktree-stale-base-premise-verification` — a VERIFY/DEBUG-time variant, not a planning-time one. The 8 existing peers are all "base is stale, so landed work reads as MISSING and tempts a re-plan". This one inverts the consequence: the stale base makes a branch INHERIT main-side corruption, and the resulting test failures look like branch bugs.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-13, worktree 3212): the Bash tool's rendering of `cat <file>` is NOT byte-faithful for Python source — it silently dropped every type annotation (`def _summarize_one(item: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:` rendered as `def _summarize_one(item):`) and collapsed the repo's double-space-after-period docstring style to single spaces. A scripted exact-string edit (python heredoc doing `assert src.count(old) == 1; src.replace(...)`) anchored on what `cat` showed therefore failed its assertion twice in a row on text that visibly matched.

PRACTICE: before writing any exact-match replacement, re-verify the anchor with `sed -n 'A,Bp' file` or `grep -n`, and for whitespace-sensitive anchors pipe through `cat -A`. Both of those rendered faithfully in the same session where plain `cat` did not. Keep the `assert src.count(old) == 1` guard — it is what turned a silent wrong-file-write into an immediate, cheap failure; the cost of the mismatch was two retries, not a corrupted file.

This matters most for the multi-hunk scripted edits agents use under bypass-permissions mode, where `cat` is the natural way to read a file first and the Edit tool's own "must Read first" bookkeeping is being bypassed.

Harness quirk confirmed 2026-07-12 (extends the known heredoc-flattening issue): the Bash tool's eval flattens ALL multi-line constructs, not just heredocs — a multi-line `for … do … done` loop collapses to one line and errors with "syntax error near unexpected token `do`". Also observed: a bare `cd <dir>` on its own line got joined with the next command ("cd: too many arguments"). RELIABLE workaround: write the whole sequence to a script file (scratchpad) and run `bash /path/to/script.sh`.

CORRECTED 2026-08-02 per esc-3249-1's resolution (canonical account: Mem0 8e09d0ea-9def-43e1-8d56-db654b7969af). The original claim that `git commit -F <file>` requires the message file to be INSIDE the repo tree was FALSE — `-F <file>` accepts any readable path regardless of location. The real constraint is ARGUMENT ORDER: `-F <file>` must appear BEFORE the `--` pathspec separator, or git parses the value as a pathspec and, if it resolves outside the repo, fails with `fatal: <path>: is outside repository at '<repo>'` — the error previously misattributed to file location. Also corrected: the claim that a docs-only commit still triggers the full pre-commit hook (~40s pyright) is stale — since task 2551, hooks/project-checks path-filters pyright to packages with staged .py changes, so a docs-only commit prints "pre-commit: pyright skipped (no Python changes)" and finishes in seconds. The working pattern `cp msg.txt <repo>/.commit-msg.txt; git commit --only -F .commit-msg.txt -- <paths>; rm .commit-msg.txt` still succeeds, but the in-repo-copy step is unnecessary cargo-cult, not a requirement — putting `-F <file>` before `--` is what actually matters.

members.text: Recon marker GC gotcha (task 2228, review finding regression-orphan-growth): when collapsing/replacing per-marker GC sweeps in reconciliation/stages/task_knowledge_sync.py, a collector must target the SAME store as its writer. ReconLedgerStore.gc() only deletes recon_ledger rows; it can never collect Mem0-resident markers. stage2_persistence_marker is written+counted in Mem0 by _track_flag_persistence (add_memory / count_memories_by_metadata) and is NEVER upserted into the ledger (only stage1_flag_marker and stage1_flag_suppression are, flag_dedup.py:635/800), so its Python sweep _sweep_stale_persistence_markers is its SOLE collector (per recon_self_model.MARKER_LIFECYCLE, deleter=DELETER_GC, unlike flag_for_stage2 which is also LLM-deleted by FIX C). Removing that sweep reopens unbounded Mem0 growth AND inflates the count driving STAGE2_FLAG_PERSISTENCE_THRESHOLD escalation. Before deleting any marker sweep, check the marker kind's writer store and MARKER_LIFECYCLE deleter.

GOTCHA — never pin a durable artifact reference to a commit sha created on your own task branch. The merge lane REBASES task/<id> before it lands, so any sha you record for a same-branch commit is an orphan by the time the work reaches main: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` says no, and `git show <sha>:<path>` fails outright once `git gc` prunes the dangling object. This is broken by construction, not bad luck — it is guaranteed for every same-branch sha, and it silently converts a documented recovery path into an unexecutable one.

Where it bites: any committed artifact (investigation report, provenance sidecar, recovery tracker) whose whole value is being auditable evidence. Task 3567's recovery-tracking.json hit exactly this — it pinned the only surviving copy of a deleted memory record to a pre-rebase orphan sha.

DO INSTEAD: pin by repo-relative path + sha256 over the referenced bytes. That survives rebase and is verifiable hermetically (file read + hashlib, no git subprocess), so a test can re-derive it in CI.

TESTING NOTE, the part that is easy to get wrong: a regex that checks a sha's SHAPE (e.g. 40-hex) is not an anti-fabrication gate. A fabricated or stale sha is exactly as well-shaped as a real one. Only re-deriving the digest from the committed bytes actually proves the reference resolves. If a commit sha is still wanted as commentary, label it explicitly non-authoritative and say what it is (run environment vs durability pin).

Reference implementation: fused-memory/tests/test_toolcall_xml_leak_sweep_artifacts.py::TestUnrepairedMutationsAreTracked::test_payload_digests_reproduce, which also rejects reintroduction of the old commit-sha field.

STEWARD DISPOSITION of the marker-deselected-test-file false-RED (esc-3292-1, 2026-08-01). Complements the diagnosis entry b1ee7610-5ef4-4639-8da4-84cc567221bf, which covers the mechanism and how to recognise the signature; this entry covers what to DO once recognised.

That escalation was resolved action='resume', resolution_class='benign' after the steward independently reproduced and confirmed the debugger's diagnosis. The signature — verify TEST leg reporting `[0 items]` / "no tests ran", categorised unknown_test_failure, with LINT and TYPE green — is an ACCEPTABLE false-RED when the checklist below passes. It is not a defect to chase, and the agent that hits it should escalate rather than reach outside its lock scope.

ACCEPT CHECKLIST (the reusable part):
1. Reproduce the empty collection: `uv run pytest <touched test file> --collect-only -q` inside the module, expecting "no tests collected (N deselected)". Contrast with the unscoped module command to show the suite itself is non-empty.
2. Confirm scope: `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` is confined to the task's declared metadata.files.
3. RUN THE TASK'S REAL COVERAGE DIRECTLY and record exact counts — the verify leg never ran it. For warm-lane that means the bash suites plus `uv run pytest -m warm_lane_bash`.
4. Accept on that evidence and send the branch to the merge queue with verified_green=True. Post-merge verify runs the module's UNSCOPED command, so it does not re-hit the empty-selection path that produced the escalation.

Worked example, task 3292: gc suite 214 passed / 0 failed (matching its own ASSERT_FLOORS bump 198->214, i.e. re-measured rather than padded to absorb a red), gc-sweep suite 86 passed / 0 failed, test_lane_state_lib.py 68 passed including the TestProtectGlobFallbackDrift INV-5 pin.

The structural fix is FILED, not dropped: ticket tkt_0RRZ7PP2M6DCRMG31Z20HZ8SXN (high) — widen the FILE_SCOPED pytest branch in verify_plan.py to the owning-module full suite when all targets would be marker-deselected, mirroring the shape task 1852 used for test-data modules, preserving both the rc=5-stays-RED invariant and the addopts<->lane biconditional. Its deferred design question: detect "all targets deselected" without paying for a --collect-only probe on every verify plan. Until it lands, expect the remaining warm-lane leaves (δ2, ε, and the task-3298 re-measurement) to red identically and handle them with the checklist above.

members.text: A script under fused-memory/scripts/ needs NO sys.path insert to import shared.* — fused-memory/pyproject.toml declares dark-factory-shared as a uv workspace dependency, so it resolves natively (this supersedes older notes suggesting shared/src conftest path inserts). Importing fused_memory.* also works directly (census_memory_metadata.py:101 precedents a module-level import). Repo-root scripts/ is the genuine exception: scripts/ and scripts/legibility/ contain no __init__.py and are installed nowhere, and fused-memory's pytest pythonpath is only ["src", "../orchestrator/src"], so importing legibility.* requires inserting <repo>/scripts on sys.path as a namespace package.

scripts/tests/ (e.g. scripts/legibility/*.py) is verified via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/...` — this scopes execution to shared/pyproject.toml's own dependency set (pydantic, pydantic-settings, aiosqlite, pyyaml, python-dotenv only). Packages like jsonschema, ruamel.yaml, etc. that are only transitive deps of other workspace members (fused-memory, orchestrator, escalation per their uv.lock) are NOT importable there, even though they may appear available in an ambient/full-workspace venv. When writing a scripts/ module, verify package availability against `uv run --project shared python -c "import X"`, not the interactive dev shell's venv. This convention is load-bearing: see `_FALLBACK_UV_PROJECT = 'shared'` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py and the comment in shared/pyproject.toml (task 2070).

Gotcha: the scripts/tests/ directory (1228 tests, covering the sweep and audit scripts) is NOT exercised by any orchestrator verify chain. Both the root dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml test_command and the scoped scripts/orchestrator.yaml test_command run "uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/" — the repo-root tests/scripts/ directory, a DIFFERENT path that merely transposes the two segments. So a task scoped to scripts/ gets a green verify that never ran the tests for the files it changed. When working on anything under scripts/, run "uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/ -q --timeout=300" explicitly; a green fleet verify proves nothing about it. Verified 2026-08-01 by reading both yaml test_commands directly (task 3336).

claim: Repo-root scripts are outside the workspace’s normal package and verification setup, so use the shared project explicitly and run scripts/tests directly.

STAMPED PEER under topic `tasks-json-is-a-stale-mirror` (canonical 64ae84c2). Two updates the canonical does not carry.

(1) THE FILE IS GONE, NOT MERELY STALE. The canonical reads as though `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` still exists and is just old. As of 2026-08-30 it does NOT exist in /home/leo/src/dark-factory: `/bin/ls -la .taskmaster/tasks/` returns only `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-shm`, `tasks.db-wal`, and `test -e tasks.json` reports ABSENT. It was retired at the 2026-05-06 SQLite cutover and DELETED 2026-08-25 (date independently recorded at `.claude/skills/hotspot-survey/project.md`). Consequence for agents: a read of that path now FAILS LOUDLY instead of silently returning a 4-month-old answer — strictly better than the esc-4659-5 near-miss, where task 4659's architect read it, got a stale answer with NO error, and recorded a false "owned by no live task" claim. If such a file ever REAPPEARS it is a restored backup or a foreign artifact; do not read it and do not migrate from it.

(2) NEVER JUDGE tasks.db's FRESHNESS BY ITS OWN mtime. `tasks.db` runs in WAL mode. Committed writes land in `tasks.db-wal` and the main file's mtime is only touched at checkpoint, so it can lag live writes arbitrarily. Any code or eyeball comparing "which is newer, the db or some other file" must take max(mtime) across `tasks.db`, `tasks.db-wal` AND `tasks.db-shm`. A db-only stat will report an actively-written live store as older than a months-dead snapshot. This is not hypothetical: it is precisely the misread that would let `fused-memory/scripts/migrate_tasks_json_to_sqlite.py --replace` overwrite the live ~30 MB / 4600-row store with a 1152-task May snapshot (task 4682 adds the guard).

Per the canonical: quote no row counts as durable fact — measure them yourself. Open read-only (`file:...?mode=ro` URI). The two zero-byte decoys named in the canonical still apply.

Reify testing technique — how to pin a constraint that GENUINELY must live in a trait body. The known gotcha (memories 06e35691, eea5b075, 10c6eb04) says a bare trait body is not dimension-checked, so rewrite the probe as a `structure`. For those, drop to EVAL level: `reify_test_support::check_source_with_stdlib` (needs reify-eval's existing `eval-helpers` dev-dep feature; no Cargo.toml change), declare the trait plus a conforming structure, and assert `reify_ir::Satisfaction::Satisfied` on every injected constraint result — plus a non-empty check so a conformer that injected nothing cannot pass vacuously, and a paired `Violated` case on a value that genuinely fails the bound. members.text: In reify-compiler, a `trait` body compiled with NO conformer is not dimension-checked at all. Inside a bare trait, `constraint material.density > 1m` (mismatched dimensions) and even `constraint material.no_such_field > 0` (undefined field) both compile with ZERO diagnostics; the same expressions inside a `structure` correctly emit DiagnosticCode::DimensionMismatch. Consequence: any compile-level "assert_no_error_diagnostics" probe written against a bare trait is VACUOUS and passes regardless of the behaviour it claims to pin. To pin trait-body semantics, either restate the shape as a `structure`, or use the eval-level signal (check_source_with_stdlib + assert the injected constraint's reify_ir::Satisfaction on a conforming structure). Measured on task 6038; the eval-level trait pins live in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_engine/polymorphic_zero_trait_eval.rs.

Reify runtime (eval-time) diagnostics flow: EvalContext (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:27-50) carries `diagnostics: Option<&RefCell<Vec<Diagnostic>>>`; emitters use `if let Some(sink)=ctx.diagnostics { sink.borrow_mut().push(diag) }` (see sampled.rs:94-101 FieldOutOfBounds, interp.rs). Engine::eval drains the sink into EvalResult.diagnostics (reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs ~2097). cmd_eval (reify-cli/src/main.rs:571-617) prints each diagnostic to stderr as `{severity}: {message}` and returns ExitCode::FAILURE if any is Severity::Error. Note: stdlib `eval_builtin(name,args)` does NOT receive EvalContext, so a builtin cannot emit diagnostics itself — emission must happen at the eval_expr call site (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:495). The compiler does NOT error on unknown free-function names (reify-compiler/src/expr.rs ~1261-1278 emits at most a Warning), so stdlib builtins like stackup_rss/contributor are callable from .ri without compiler registration.

Reify agent-harness idiom for waiting on a long cargo build WITHOUT a foreground `sleep` (blocked by the anti-polling guard), a busy-loop (SIGTERMed at the Bash timeout, losing all observations), or a reap-vulnerable background waiter: have the background job write a terminal sentinel to a log, then FOREGROUND-block on `timeout 600 tail -f -n +1 /tmp/<log> | grep -m1 -E "<SENTINEL>" >/dev/null` with the Bash `timeout` set above the `timeout(1)` value. `tail -f | grep -m1` exits ON ITS OWN the moment the sentinel appears, so it is a real blocking wait rather than polling; the `timeout(1)` cap bounds it so the call always returns a NEW TURN (resetting the idle watchdog) even if the build hangs, and you simply re-issue it. Emit the sentinel yourself — e.g. run the job as `{ cargo test ...; echo "EXIT1=$?"; cargo test ...; echo "EXIT3=$?"; } > /tmp/<log> 2>&1` — so one wait covers a whole sequence and the exit codes are in the log. Measured 2026-09-03 (task 5755 architect, cold warm lane `_lane-0`): a targeted `cargo test -p reify-compiler --lib <filter>` + `-p reify-eval --lib geometry_ops` + `-p reify-eval --test <one binary>` sequence finished in ~6 min this way, versus a bare `cargo test -p reify-compiler -p reify-eval` which was abandoned after 8 min still compiling because it must build and link ALL 236 top-level integration binaries under crates/reify-eval/tests/ (`ls crates/reify-eval/tests/*.rs | wc -l`). Always scope to `--lib <filter>` plus `--test <binary>` when confirming specific named tests.

claim: Reliable Reify validation requires checking the relevant execution path with focused tests and observing actual results, not relying on vacuous probes or unscoped builds.

STILL CORRECT AND USEFUL BELOW, unaffected by the falsification: the single-funnel dispatch analysis (all five queries bottom out in one `kernel_distance` call / `GeometryQuery::Distance`, with the booleans literally `d <= 0.0`), and the observation that pairing the boolean with the scalar adds no detection power for any positive tolerance (this remains true, it is just not evidence of a containment blind spot).

--- ORIGINAL TEXT AS WRITTEN 2026-08-12, PRESERVED VERBATIM AS A RECORD OF WHAT WAS BELIEVED AT THE TIME ---]

Reify's five interference/clearance queries all bottom out in ONE non-negative primitive — `kernel_distance` in crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs, issuing `GeometryQuery::Distance` (OCCT BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape): `distance`/`min_clearance` return it unchanged, while `intersects`, `interferes_with` and `interferes` are all literally `d <= 0.0` tests over it. Two consequences: (1) a solid fully NESTED inside another with no boundary contact has a positive boundary-to-boundary distance, so every one of the five reports "clear" — a real interference read as clearance, silently; (2) `constraint not intersects(a,b)` is logically implied by `constraint distance(a,b) > tol` for any positive tol, so pairing the boolean with the scalar adds no detection power anywhere and is not a remedy for the nested case. Tracked by the follow-up filed from task #5389 (ticket tkt_0RSCH02PV6MD6GHJ0S45T5ZDB2); pending task #5443's planned `no_undeclared_interference` ("every non-whitelisted body pair has distance > 0") inherits the same blind spot as specified.

In reify-eval, `Engine::default_kernel_name.is_none()` can be read as "this BINARY has no geometry kernel" — not merely "this engine instance has none" — but only on code paths reached via constraint dispatch. `Engine::eval()` never calls `dispatch_constraints` (only `check()`, `build()`, `check_snapshot`, `tessellate_snapshot`, `build_snapshot` do), so the CLI's deliberately kernel-free eval engines (`cmd_eval` plain branch, `cmd_bom`, `cmd_provenance`, all `Engine::new(checker, None)`) cannot reach constraint code. Every surface that both dispatches constraints and can carry a RepresentationWithin builds its engine with `Engine::with_registered_kernel` (`cmd_check`'s assertion branch, `cmd_build`, the GUI session), which yields `Some(..)` iff the binary was compiled with a kernel. This is what makes kernel-absence a safe discriminator for user-facing diagnostics that recommend building with OCCT.

Reify OCCT gotcha: `OcctKernel::DEFAULT_STL_TESSELLATION_TOLERANCE` (crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs) is `0.1` but the kernel works in SI METRES, so it is a 100 mm linear deflection — its own doc comment says "0.1 mm" and the correctly-scaled twin is `Engine::DEFAULT_TESSELLATION_TOLERANCE = 0.0001` (engine_build.rs). BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh emits NO triangulation for curved faces whose size is far below the deflection, so small curved parts export as 0-triangle STLs while planar faces (box) always triangulate. Measured on a guided sweep of circle(r) along a straight spine: r=0.003 m/len=0.02 m gives 0 triangles at tol=0.1 and 100 at tol=1e-4; r=0.02 m/len=0.1 m gives 28 at tol=0.1. The display/GUI path uses the 1e-4 constant, which is why such geometry renders fine but exports empty.

claim: In Reify, verify geometry behavior along the actual execution path, including kernel dispatch and units, rather than relying on API names or documentation.

PEER (topic reviewer-infrastructure-error-diagnosis) to b08ab18e — two NEW measured facts about the "reviewer verdict discarded" false infra error, from esc-6342-1 (task 6342, _lane-49, 2026-08-21).

FACT 1 — the reviews/ artifact is mechanically RECONSTRUCTIBLE from the sidecar, so the discard is repairable in place, not just diagnosable. On a HEALTHY lane, reviews/<role>.json compares EQUAL (python dict equality) to verdicts/<role>.json["verdict"] — verified on _lane-0. Both are {reviewer, verdict, issues[], summary}; the sidecar just wraps it as {role, schema_version, session_id, emitted_at, verdict:{...}}. So on a discarded lane the repair is a one-liner: write the sidecar's inner "verdict" object over reviews/<role>.json (back the original up as .error-bak first). Cheap, reversible, and harmless if the workflow later re-runs the reviewer and overwrites it. Whether the orchestrator actually re-reads a repaired reviews/ file on resume was NOT verified here — do the repair for the audit trail, but do not rely on it to make the workflow proceed; still go to the merge queue per b08ab18e.

FACT 2 — the discard is CONCURRENT across lanes, not a per-task fluke. At the same wall-clock, _lane-49 AND _lane-15 both showed reviews/=ERROR with 0 issues and the same "Reviewer emitted no/invalid verdict: Verdict submitted: **ISSUES_FOUND** ..." summary prefix, while both sidecars held complete verdicts (5 and 2 issues respectively). Both sidecars carried session_id "". If you find one discarded lane, check the siblings — other tasks are likely sitting on the same false escalation, and each will burn a reviewer lap if resumed.

TIMING SIGNATURE worth pattern-matching: on _lane-49 the sidecar was written 10:43:19Z, the ERROR reviews/ file 40s later at 10:43:59Z, and esc-6342-1 was filed in that SAME SECOND as the ERROR file. A sidecar that PREDATES the ERROR record proves the reviewer finished and was discarded — it did not crash and did not run out of turns (which is the OTHER, unrelated cause under this same escalation wording; see canonical index e2a6f1d4 and the transcript/runs.db routes c3cb28f3 / a94bc738).

PROCESS MISTAKE TO AVOID — I made it here: I resolved esc-6342-1 with action='resume' BEFORE searching memory, then found b08ab18e (which says use 'close_only', because 'resume' re-dispatches the reviewer into the same discard) and had to correct course by submitting the merge queue request separately. A resolve_issue call cannot be un-resolved. SEARCH MEMORY FOR THE ESCALATION WORDING BEFORE CALLING resolve_issue, not after. Recovery if you already resumed: check get_task_runtime_state — if the task's phase is DONE (as 6342's was), no reviewer is actually running, and submitting merge_request(verified_green=true) directly still lands the branch.

Handling a `review_issues` escalation: the escalation `detail` carries ONLY the severity=blocking review findings. Non-blocking suggestions are NOT in the record, so a steward reading `get_escalation` alone will silently triage zero of them and hand the task on with them unaddressed.

OBSERVED on esc-5467-16 (task 5467, 2026-08-24): summary said "2 blocking issue(s) and 9 suggestion(s)", and `detail` contained exactly the 2 blocking issues and none of the 9. The full 11-issue `submit_review_verdict` payload was recoverable from the reviewer's own transcript at `data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/<task_id>/<worktree-path-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl` (the resumed implementer found it on line 235 and dispositioned all 9 from there: 4 fixed inline, 5 filed as tickets).

WORKAROUND: when a `review_issues` summary advertises more issues than `detail` contains, pull the verdict payload from the reviewer transcript under `data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/<task_id>/` rather than assuming the suggestions were dropped or are unavailable. Alternatively hand the gap forward explicitly in the `resolve_issue` text so the resuming agent recovers them — that is what closed it here.

MECHANISM IS A HYPOTHESIS, not confirmed: the filing code was never read, so "the filer only serialises blocking items" is inferred from the one observed detail/summary mismatch, not verified. The OBSERVATION (detail held 2 of 11; transcript held 11) is what is measured.

Working recipe for a long cargo build/test — detach it from the tool's process group with a log + exit sentinel, then poll in sub-300s chunks:
  rm -f /tmp/X.log; setsid nohup bash -c 'command cargo test ... >> /tmp/X.log 2>&1; echo "SENTINEL_EXIT:$?" >> /tmp/X.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
  for i in $(seq 1 27); do grep -q '^SENTINEL_EXIT:' /tmp/X.log && break; sleep 10; done; grep -E '^SENTINEL_EXIT:|^test result:|^error' /tmp/X.log

As of mid-2026 it holds stackup/fea/geometry/dynamics/tolerancing. Classifiers that return `Vec<Diagnostic>` and/or fire on BOTH the success and Undef paths (dfm, flexure) get their own standalone `emit_*` fn called separately at the FunctionCall dispatch site. The `#[inline(never)]` extraction keeps owned-Diagnostic locals off every recursive eval_expr frame (2 MiB test-thread stack, pinned by eval_user_fn_recursion_depth_exceeded).

Reify agent-harness idiom for waiting on a long cargo build WITHOUT a foreground `sleep` (blocked by the anti-polling guard), a busy-loop (SIGTERMed at the Bash timeout, losing all observations), or a reap-vulnerable background waiter: have the background job write a terminal sentinel to a log, then FOREGROUND-block on `timeout 600 tail -f -n +1 /tmp/<log> | grep -m1 -E "<SENTINEL>" >/dev/null` with the Bash `timeout` set above the `timeout(1)` value. `tail -f | grep -m1` exits ON ITS OWN the moment the sentinel appears, so it is a real blocking wait rather than polling; the `timeout(1)` cap bounds it so the call always returns a NEW TURN (resetting the idle watchdog) even if the build hangs, and you simply re-issue it. Emit the sentinel yourself — e.g. run the job as `{ cargo test ...; echo "EXIT1=$?"; cargo test ...; echo "EXIT3=$?"; } > /tmp/<log> 2>&1` — so one wait covers a whole sequence and the exit codes are in the log. Measured 2026-09-03 (task 5755 architect, cold warm lane `_lane-0`): a targeted `cargo test -p reify-compiler --lib <filter>` + `-p reify-eval --lib geometry_ops` + `-p reify-eval --test <one binary>` sequence finished in ~6 min this way, versus a bare `cargo test -p reify-compiler -p reify-eval` which was abandoned after 8 min still compiling because it must build and link ALL 236 top-level integration binaries under crates/reify-eval/tests/ (`ls crates/reify-eval/tests/*.rs | wc -l`). Always scope to `--lib <filter>` plus `--test <binary>` when confirming specific named tests.

In reify-compiler, a `trait` body compiled with NO conformer is not dimension-checked at all. Inside a bare trait, `constraint material.density > 1m` (mismatched dimensions) and even `constraint material.no_such_field > 0` (undefined field) both compile with ZERO diagnostics; the same expressions inside a `structure` correctly emit DiagnosticCode::DimensionMismatch. Consequence: any compile-level "assert_no_error_diagnostics" probe written against a bare trait is VACUOUS and passes regardless of the behaviour it claims to pin. To pin trait-body semantics, either restate the shape as a `structure`, or use the eval-level signal (check_source_with_stdlib + assert the injected constraint's reify_ir::Satisfaction on a conforming structure). Measured on task 6038; the eval-level trait pins live in crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_engine/polymorphic_zero_trait_eval.rs.

claim: In reify, make diagnostics, tests, and build waits explicit about their triggers and scope so resource costs and behavioral blind spots are controlled.

members.text: CAPABILITY MANIFESTS ARE FAILING IN A SPECIFIC, REPEATING WAY IN REIFY — two independent instances surfaced on 2026-08-07 alone, in unrelated subsystems. The failure is a row marked PASS on evidence that ROUTES AROUND the capability it claims. Instance 1, `docs/prds/v0_6/io-export-import-completion.capability-manifest.md:67`: `| version param reaches export | via δ driver (reads version off STEPOutput) | PASS (δ upstream) |` — a leaf's capability marked PASS on the strength of a SIBLING LEAF'S FUTURE WORK. The manifest also had NO row at all asserting the thing that actually broke ("demanded tolerance reaches OcctKernel::export()"), and its header dates all evidence to a pre-flight snapshot never re-checked after the leaves landed. Instance 2, the predecessor jcodemunch PRD: its live-serve bindings all route around the Rust client — `L-SERVE` binds a curl smoke, `L-CLIENT` a static decode of captured fixtures, `L-WIRE` a construction-site substitution — and the one binding that would have caught the real defect, `L-SMOKE`, names `scripts/smoke-jcodemunch-audit.sh` WHICH DOES NOT EXIST; what shipped instead is `#[ignore]`-gated AND graceful-skips on a bare TCP-connect probe. RULES THAT FOLLOW, for anyone authoring a manifest: (a) never mark a row PASS on a sibling leaf's future work — that is the phantom-completion vector in pure form; (b) never bind a row to a script or test that does not exist — verify the path; (c) a binding that exercises the seam from the OUTSIDE (curl, captured fixtures, a construction-site substitution) does not evidence that the PRODUCTION client works — bind to the production path or say the row is unevidenced; (d) beware bindings that graceful-skip, since a skip-erasing helper reads as PASS when the thing is broken. Also note the structural gap: NOTHING IN REIFY PARSES `*.capability-manifest.md` — only the `.yaml` sidecar's `delivered_check` rows are mechanically evaluated, and that happens downstream in dark-factory's merge queue, with `kind: manual` rows excluded. reify's own literature already names this: `docs/prds/prd-gate-executable-substrate-verification.md:19` — "it only converts free-text promises into tabulated promises that nothing executes".

In reify, you cannot add a new standalone `tests/<name>.rs` integration-test binary to the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler — the `_HL_CRATES` array in tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh). tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh enforces that every top-level tests/*.rs is either a sanctioned `harness_<subsystem>.rs`, one of 7 named override binaries, or grandfathered in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest; anything else fails the merge gate with `HARNESS_KLOC_CAP FAIL ... reason=unsanctioned-standalone`. The reify-kernel-occt grandfather baseline is fully drained (zero entries), so ANY new standalone binary there fails. Per docs/prds/merge-gate-compile-cost.md an over-cap harness is resolved by SPLIT into another harness_*, never by raising CAP_LINES (currently 20000 raw lines). Consequence: "give this flaky test its own test binary for isolation" is not an available fix in these crates — fix the shared state instead. Verifying a Rust suite in a warm lane: `cargo test ... | tail -N` MASKS cargo's exit code (bash reports the last pipeline stage, i.e. tail), so an aborted run can look green — cargo halts at the first failing test binary and the "error: test failed" line can be scrolled past by the tail window. Capture the status explicitly (`cargo test ... > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"`) when the result gates a merge. Separately, a SIGKILLed cargo run (e.g. one hitting the 300s background-task ceiling) can leave `target/debug/deps/<test>-<hash>` missing while cargo still considers it fresh; the rerun then fails with exit status 127 / "No such file or directory" via `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh`. That is an artifact-integrity failure, NOT a test regression — re-run that single `--test <name>` target to rebuild it before diagnosing any code cause.

Reify, capability direction of the synthetic-kernel-key gotcha (task 6169, cost two review cycles): you cannot answer "does THIS engine hold a BRep-capable kernel?" by looking the engine's own `geometry_kernels` names up in the static inventory registry. Because `Engine::with_registered_kernel` (the constructor every production constraint-dispatching surface uses — reify-cli main.rs:604/999/1564, gui EngineSession) files its pick under the synthetic `Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME`, that lookup MISSES on every shipped binary and silently degrades to whatever the unregistered-kernel default is (a benefit-of-the-doubt `true` in 6169's case), making any arm gated on the answer dead code on exactly the surfaces it was written for. The fix shape that works: record the answer at CONSTRUCTION, where the `KernelRegistration` is still in hand (`(reg.descriptor)().supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep)` stored into an `Option<bool>` field), and keep the registry scan only as a fallback for `Engine::new(_, Some(stub))` test seams. Note the divergence is invisible on an OCCT build — both answers coincide — so the gate that makes it observable everywhere is a structural pin asserting the engine's own kernel names are ABSENT from the registry, not a behavioural test.

[CORRECTED 2026-08-26]: A prior append to this entry claimed "CONFIRMED 2026-08-26: task 6169 landed this fix as `Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>` (recorded at construction time from the `KernelRegistration`)." That claim was FALSE, verified this stage: a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `repr_capable_kernel` across the reify repo returns zero matches (the field does not exist in the codebase), and task 6169's live status is `pending`, not `done` — no fix has landed. Treat this gotcha as UNRESOLVED. Do not re-assert completion until task 6169 reaches status=done AND the field is confirmed present in the codebase via grep. This entry previously absorbed a same-day near-duplicate note (mem0 3ae219c3, deleted, consolidated here) that restated the same gotcha with less detail.

[RESOLVED 2026-09-09]: Both conditions the 2026-08-26 correction set are now MET, each re-verified first-hand this sitting rather than taken from another record. (1) Task 6169's live status is `done`, with `done_provenance.kind = merged`. (2) The field EXISTS: `Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>` is declared in crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs, and the wiring matches the fix shape prescribed above exactly. It is initialised to `None` in the plain constructor in `engine_admin.rs` — whose own comment says the caller-supplied-kernel seam "leaves it None and gets the benefit-of-the-doubt scan" — and overwritten with `Some(..)` by BOTH inventory-driven constructors in that same file: the single-pick path stores `picked.is_some_and(|reg| (reg.descriptor)().supports_any_repr(ReprKind::BRep))` right after `with_prelude`, and the multi-kernel path stores the `any(..)` of the same descriptor predicate across the registry. It is consumed by `Engine::has_repr_capable_kernel` in `engine_constraints.rs`, which returns the construction-recorded answer when present and falls back to the registry scan only when it is `None`; `engine_build.rs` destructures the field explicitly so a later field addition cannot silently skip it, and the structural pin lives in crates/reify-eval/tests/representation_within_assertion.rs. Reify's static interference/clearance oracle CANNOT detect full containment: `distance`, `min_clearance`, `intersects` and `interferes_with` all funnel through one `kernel_distance` call into a single `GeometryQuery::Distance` (OCCT `BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape`, non-negative by construction), and the two booleans are literally `Bool(d <= 0.0)`. So a solid fully nested inside another with no boundary contact yields a POSITIVE distance AND `false` from both booleans — all four report "clear" on the worst possible interference. Pairing the scalar with the boolean does NOT help; they are the same distance test read two ways. `contains` is NOT the fix: it is `contains(solid, point)` (args[1] goes through `resolve_point3_length_arg`), and since the compiler assigns only its result type (`"contains" => Type::Bool`) with no arg-slot check, `contains(solidA, solidB)` compiles clean and evaluates to a silent `undef`. No solid-solid containment predicate exists. The working idiom is the boolean-volume oracle, both calls let-bound: `let outside = difference(inner, outer)` then `let pokeout = volume(outside)`, contained iff `pokeout` is below a small positive floor (1e-9 m^3 is the established precedent) — never exact zero. Worked examples `examples/tolerancing/gdt_oracle_inside.ri`/` [cut]
